Guangdong was largely established for their benefit, in the tumultuous period after the war - and even if we feel that their actions are self-serving in the extreme, we can't risk running afoul of them and having them raise a ruckus. Fortunately, though they would do anything to protect their interests against the Cantonese-Japanese - and especially the Chinese - that same self-interest can be easily appealed to, and Suzuki is no stranger to wining and dining the elite.
strings.GNG_court_the_cantonese_japanese_desc: The 'Cantonese-Japanese', or Zhujin in the local Cantonese, are a myriad and diverse lot - a collection of local contractors, 'amenable' notables, popular entertainers and the salaried civil servants and police that form the backbone of Guangdong's government. They have all come to realize that working with the Japanese in the cause of Pan-Asianism is to their benefit, forming a class in between the Japanese expatriates and the Chinese poor that can be counted upon to support the government. Taking care of them - and reassuring them them that their livelihood will not be trampled on by the Japanese or endangered by the Chinese - is absolutely essential.
strings.GNG_motivate_the_chinese_workforce_desc:
The vast majority of Guangdong's population - even two decades after the establishment of the territory - is composed of poorer Chinese manual laborers and factory workers across both Guangdong's urban and rural regions. They are also, unsurprisingly, the most restive part of the population, and while most Japanese companies in Guangdong work them as hard as physically sustainable for meager pay, many find time to participate in the increasing number of dissident movements.

For the time being, at least, Suzuki will authorize motivational actions for the Chinese - shelving plans to shorten lunch hours, putting an extra rest day on for once every two months. If that isn't enough to keep them working without complaint, there are of course... alternative methods of motivation.
strings.GNG_the_security_situation_desc:
After observing the three ethnic groups of Guangdong, Chief Executive Suzuki now has enough data to compile a report summarizing the security situation. A holistic re-evaluation of the policies concerning local security will provide an indicative estimate of how best to assess and improve the security situation.

Or, at least, that's what we'll title the report to Tokyo, while Chief Executive Suzuki comes up with our next plan of action...
strings.GNG_update_tokyo_desc: With Chief Executive Suzuki's initial assessments of Guangdong's economic potential and security outlook complete, Suzuki prepares for a regular call with the Prime Minister in Tokyo to update him about his findings - and to seek authorization for his plan to stabilize the territory over the longer term.
strings.GNG_propose_the_revised_labor_standards_: Propose the Revised Labor Standards Ord.

Suzuki has surveyed both the economic and security situation of Guangdong and what he has found does not bode well for the future of our muddled nation. The Chief Executive has found that preserving Japan's long term rule over Guangdong will necessitate some form of compromise between the corporations and the people.

What Suzuki has identified is the growing threat of an ethnic timebomb, which is made worse by the day as companies relentlessly pursue quick profits above all else. Both the people and the firms Guangdong will need placating before this conflict is brought to the fore.

So the Chief Executive has determined the backlog of future dissent must promptly be drained by revising the current labor standards of the nation. This move will no doubt be unpopular with the businesses who rely on the cheap labor Guangdong's current, lax regulations allow; but change is needed now, before the rising tide of dissent washes all of Suzuki's work away.
strings.GNG_propose_RLSO_seek_support_from_two_f: We can seek support from two factions to vote for the £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Revised Labor Standards Ordinance.
strings.GNG_meet_with_the_maverick_desc:
Morita Akio, President of Sony, has done what so few Japanese businessmen have even been willing to even consider, namely making Guangdong the home of their companies. His confidence in our nation is certainly appreciated, however Morita holds substantial grudges against other members of the establishment of the Legislative Council, especially Ibuka Masaru who forced exile upon him all those years ago. Morita's simmering anger for the people who Suzuki will need to keep onside will somewhat take away from the amount the Chief Executive can openly support him.

Nevertheless, Morita is one of the only outspoken supporters of reform inside the Council, surely he will see merit in Suzuki's proposal.
strings.GNG_educate_the_engineer_desc:
On the surface Ibuka Masaru - the engineer genius and head of Fujitsu - represents the most immovable opposing force to Suzuki's reformist efforts. Ibuka has dedicated much of his time in Guangdong to squeezing every penny of profit he can out of the nation's lax labor costs, as well as encouraging more of his colleagues in Japan to join him in doing business in China. So whether the Chief Executive likes it or not, Ibuka, and his opposition to any and all reform, is here to stay for the foreseeable future.

Yet he could also be the key to passing the reform Guangdong's labor standards sorely need. Suzuki knows there must be something he can offer him in return, perhaps research subsidies or new facilities, maybe even a good word on his behalf to Tokyo.

Dealing with Ibuka will rile up other members of the Legislative Council, Morita Akio in particular, but if Ibuka can be brought over to the reformist side just this once, the rest of the reluctant opposition will surely follow.
strings.GNG_hold_court_with_the_heir_desc:
As heir to the prestigious electronic manufacturer Matsushita Electric, Matsushita Masaharu's voice carries great weight inside the Legislative Council and the wider Japanese community. His position has helped develop a persistent vigilance against movements that may negatively impact what will soon be his company, therefore Suzuki's reforms will, unfortunately, not be welcomed by Matsushita.

The position of an heir is highly precarious, no matter how hard Matsushita tries to cement his position he could always use some assistance; and who better to help than the Chief Executive himself? Yasuda may raise concerns over the future of their established relationship with Suzuki, though these qualms will have to be accepted if the support of the Heir is to be gained.
strings.GNG_confirm_the_bankers_credibility_desc:
If we are to make Guangdong an integral part of the Japanese sphere, we will need to work as closely as possible with Yasuda. The corporation is on the ins and outs of the Ino government back in the home islands, fostering relations with them would likely grant us substantially more influence than we currently hold.

We must remind those in charge of Yasuda that our partnership benefits both sides; in fact we should go further still and make sure that we are on the page in regards to our most recent initiative. This may cause some consternation with Matsushita, but he will have to accept being held out of the spotlight, for now this seems to be an acceptable cost for our regime.
strings.GNG_has_sought_support_from_less_than_tw: Has sought support from less than two factions.
strings.GNG_has_sought_support_from_two_factions: Has sought support from two factions.
strings.GNG_a_red_envelope_campaign_desc:
While we have expended significant political capital in acquiring the votes needed to pass the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance, there are still many who remain opposed to our initiative.

To shore up our position and ensure that nothing goes awry when our bill comes up in the Council, some... underhanded methods might be needed. An expensive gift, a new car, an all-expense-paid vacation to Okinawa, it's amazing how much more pliable people become once a little persuasion has been done.

This initiative, however, will not be cheap, and if we have failed to gather the necessary votes beforehand, the drain on our treasury will be... substantial.
strings.GNG_call_the_vote_desc:
Weeks of backroom meetings, politicking, and vote gathering has come to this; voting on the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance has finally begun in the Legislative Council. With it, we shall help ensure Guangdong's future stability and prosperity, no matter the grumblings of agitators or stubborn executives.

The die has been cast, and we have ensured that the game has been rigged from the start.
strings.GNG_an_invitation_to_hsinking_desc:
An invitation to Manchukuo's Chinese Economic Conference has recently been delivered to our government. In a feat of typical Manchurian perfidy, it arrived months late and has sent our diplomatic teams scrambling; the rats in Xinjing have even dared put the blame on us! For being late to put in an RSVP.

Despite their attempts to hinder us, we will not be made fools of. A delegation will be selected and dispatched in all due haste, and we will show the world Guangdong's finest.

Of course, this leaves the matter of who we are going to be accompanying to the conference-wide open, and we'll have to decide quickly.
strings.GNG_approach_the_chinese_desc:
While our northern neighbors have never been particularly... satisfied with the loss of Guangdong, we do need to play nice with the Chinese. A phone call to Nanjing and a few - hollow - promises should be enough to get them to parlay with us.

And with a population of several hundred million and some rather ambitious modernization plans, China could be quite a bountiful market in the near future, and it wouldn't do to let this opportunity go amiss.
strings.GNG_consult_with_the_japanese_desc:
Japan, the masters of Asia, and of us. While we are unquestionably tightly bound to our masters in Tokyo, we have few opportunities to meet with the Empire face to face. This golden opportunity cannot be squandered.

We shall meet with Japanese representatives and see what our masters wish of us. In exchange, we shall acquire the backing of the Empire of the Rising Sun, and support for us, and Guangdong's Japanese expatriates will be unquestionably valuable.
strings.GNG_parlay_with_the_manchurian_hosts_des:
The “Empire” of Manchuria are questionably our foremost rivals in the Co-Prosperity Sphere, competing with our products and our merchants for market share and influence with raw industrial might and slave labor. They look down on us at every turn, the representatives of their “Emperor” thumbing their noses down at our Chief Executive.

But, we ought to pay a visit to the hosts of this conference-a show of Pan-Asian unity-no matter our mutual animosity, and who knows, maybe these arrogant Manchus might be just let something valuable slip.
strings.GNG_guangdongs_place_in_the_sphere_desc:
After days of shuffling folders, collecting paperwork, and organizing scripts, the Chief Executive is finally scheduled to deliver his address in the closing moments of the Xinjing Economic Conference. There, he will speak directly to representatives from across the Co-Prosperity Sphere about the economic miracle beginning to emerge from the Pearl River Delta.

Whilst Suzuki is not particularly pleased about receiving the final allocated slot in the line-up speakers for the conference, he will use the time to the best of his ability. The clock strikes early morning hours, and people begin to leave, but Suzuki is here to tell the world that Guangdong is open for business.
strings.GNG_pacifying_the_pearl_river_delta_desc:
With the conclusion of the conference in Manchuria, our attention is diverted back to our plans for stabilizing the nation. Suzuki has been hard at work, negotiating his thoughts around stability in the Pearl River Delta, and finding a solution to remedy the surgence of agitators harassing local authorities.

His proposed labor bill will be a useful tool in settling unrest across the cities, and will help draw support for dissenters among the populace. We will have the tools to decouple the two, and begin identifying and cracking down on the dissenters themselves without punishing hard-working citizens going about their daily lives.
strings.GNG_the_cost_of_informants_desc:
To date, gathering intelligence on dissident activities has relied on a network of informants freckled across the delta. This web of respondents is maintained by the Kenpeitai, whose units keep a close eye on crime levels in Guangdong. Backed by our local police forces, the network is a tool often used in cracking down on the growing dissident activity across the nation.

However, we are confronted with an opportunity to break the ranks of the insurgents before they grow too large. Saving ourselves the risk of anarchy in the streets, we must consider the cost of investing in an intelligence network, backed by state resources, to vastly increase our capability to detect subversives.
strings.GNG_the_language_barrier_desc:
In such a nation that is Guangdong, there exists a very simple problem that plagues every level of the intelligence administration. The chatter in darkened street corners, damp evening markets, and rusting bus shelters is conducted in Cantonese - a language unintelligible to most Japanese.

We lose valuable time translating, confusing ourselves with cases, tenses, and characters - all costing us valuable time and resources. Until we address this gap within both the Kenpeitai and circles of trusted officers in the police force, we'll never be able to tell dissidents apart from the average citizen.
strings.GNG_gangsters_chasing_gangsters_desc:
The daily hurdle in gathering intelligence for our investigations is the public's lack of trust; our citizens do not have faith that the police - or the Kenpeitai - will treat them fairly as informants. The military brutality of the Kenpeitai, and their expansive jurisdiction, fills the average citizen with an exhausting dread. When the authorities are at the door, few have faith that anything good will come of the interaction.

Combined with the disorganized, impetuous state of our own police force, 'law enforcement' in Guangdong has become more of a brawl between two street gangs. This must change if we want to see any improvements in confronting dissent in the future.
strings.GNG_project_panopticon_desc:
It has been made clear to the administration that traditional methods of maintaining public order will not suffice in Guangdong. Too many slip under the radar and get away with all kinds of filthy acts and desperate crimes; the continuation of Japanese dominion over Southern China requires new thinking, and new solutions.

Our great inoculator is technology. An ear in every conversation; an eye in every room - with the use of technology, we can try to make our new surveillance state can be as invisible as possible, removing the human element entirely.

All it will cost is time and money, so we must hasten to make our proposal convincing enough to Tokyo.
strings.GNG_yasuda_crisis_economic_crisis: A disaster of this caliber has never hit the young State of Guangdong before.
strings.GNG_the_music_stops_desc:
The unthinkable has occurred - Yasuda, one of the cornerstones of the Japanese economy, has collapsed, and the Sphere's economy has been plunged into utter chaos. Orders are drying up, customers are hunkering down, and companies are racing to confirm whether they have enough cash to survive Yasuda's collapse.

And in Guangdong, Yasuda's position as one of the Four Companies means that worse is surely in store, unless we take action now.
strings.GNG_demand_answers_from_tokyo_desc:
There is no shortage of answers we need from Tokyo in response to Yasuda's collapse.

Why weren't we informed, given the central position Yasuda occupies in Guangdong? What is the status of talks, if any, to manage Yasuda's existing obligations? Have Japanese authorities extended any guarantees to Yasuda's creditors?

Most importantly - will Japan's budget support for Guangdong continue?
strings.GNG_revisit_the_budget_desc:
Of the revenue that Guangdong's government collects organically - that is, without reliance on customs levies or financial contributions from Tokyo - much of it comes from the taxes paid by the companies operating in the territory. Tax rates are low to begin with - in order to keep Guangdong favorably positioned against the rest of the Sphere - but Japan's continued economic growth, and the corresponding good performance of Guangdong's companies, meant that we came to expect fiscal stability.

But if Yasuda's financial troubles - and impending collapse - are as inevitable as recent news suggests, then our budget will have to be revisited - urgently.
strings.GNG_reassure_the_markets_desc:
If we're scared, the investors that make up the bulk of investment in Guangdong are absolutely petrified. Ever since that fateful day when Yasuda's stock price collapsed in Tokyo, Guangdong's markets have been in freefall, and the banks and investment houses in Honkon and Kōshū are frozen in place.

We need to get ahead of the news, and reassure investors and companies that we will have the situation under control shortly. Otherwise, the rumors of capital flight swirling through Guangdong could become reality - and that would surely be the kiss of death.
strings.GNG_a_fiscal_cliff_desc:
Our findings are bleak, the conclusion unavoidable. With funds from Tokyo drying up, our budget bleeding red ink, and investors running for the exits, we face a financial apocalypse that makes it impossible to sustain our current levels of spending.

Drastic action will be required.
strings.GNG_summon_the_tycoons_desc:
We need to fill the gaping hole in our budget, and the stark reality is that Guangdong has few sources of revenue aside from its corporations. The Chinese are too poor to tax, the Cantonese-Japanese fill critical positions in our government and in small business, and the Japanese expatriates would never open their wallets willingly.

Chief Executive Suzuki has come to the conclusion that we must call upon the largest companies - those sitting on the Legislative Council, and their tycoons, to do their part for the greater good. They will have to agree - their ability to continue operating in Guangdong, for Guangdong to exist at all, depends on it.
strings.GNG_summon_the_tycoons_tt: This will introduce the £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong Financial Stabilization Ordinance to the Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_suzuki_yasuda_has_picked_a_plan: We have hatched out an economic recovery plan for Guangdong together with the tycoons.
strings.GNG_stop_the_presses_desc: We have reached the worst-case scenario: the tycoons have turned against us. They have walked out of our meeting. The fallout will be immense. Even so, there are still means by which we can manage how much damage this causes. The first and most important: stopping the press. If word gets out that the tycoons have turned against us, there is no hope of salvaging the situation. Thus, we must clamp down on journalism - especially those we cannot control - until we are sufficiently prepared to deal with the consequences.
strings.GNG_a_rebuttal_desc:
Allegations have been spreading that we are failing to deal with the crisis, no doubt spread by our enemies in the tycoons. This is blatantly false, to the point where it is almost ridiculous to suggest such. Even so, letting this spread unimpeded is dangerous to our efforts, and so we must publish a rebuttal. In all of the newspapers and official news channels, we will make our defense heard.

And it would not hurt to slip in some lies of our own...
strings.GNG_increase_patrols_desc:
The streets and the halls of the government are two sides of the same coin, they say - one side plunges into hellfire, and the other is bound to follow.

Discontent from all sectors of civilian society is boiling over, right as we're busy handling the chaos ravaging our Legislative Council - and this cannot be allowed to stand. To this end we shall intensify deployment of our dutiful officers to the streets, even the Kenpeitai if necessary, and keep a watchful eye on any sign of civil unrest.

There will be no room left for the cries of the Chinese, the protests of underpayment of the Zhujin, or even the concerned chatters of the Japanese; for the sake of Guangdong's stability and future, no measure is too extreme.
strings.GNG_alternative_solutions_desc: The Guangdong Police Force is overstretched. Meant for upholding the law and dealing with smaller protests, the Chinese and their riots are too much for them to handle. Naturally, we have also sent the Kenpeitai to deal with the riots, but even their brutal efficiency cannot quell the delinquency of the rioters. It is time that we turn to a more... unconventional source of enforcement. Our friends in the Yakuza are willing to use their own methods to deal with the rioters, in exchange for various perks: less restrictions on their operations, appointing Yakuza members into important bureaucratic positions, and so on. Unfortunately, with our need for more enforcers to quell the riots, it's an offer we can't refuse.
strings.GNG_demand_yasudas_loyalty_desc: The Yasuda Zaibatsu and its involvement in the corruption within our government is what started this whole mess. Matsuzawa Takuji is the head of the Hong Kong branch of Yasuda Bank, the main financial operative of its Zaibatsu. Matsuzawa's situation within Guangdong is one of importance, since he represents one of our largest financial investors. While Matsuzawa has plenty to worry about and deal with, we need to make sure that he and his company will not abandon Guangdong.
strings.GNG_when_persuasion_fails_desc: Most of the investors and their Zaibatsu are willing to cooperate with us, and we thank them for their contribution. However, there are some investors who plan to abandon our industry, and their withdrawal from our economy will have deep repercussions on Guangdong. It is of the utmost importance that no company tries to leave our industry, lest they take us down with them. Luckily, most of these investors are heavily corrupt, and it won't take long to dig up dirt on them. We could also use our new Yakuza friends to persuade the investors. Some call these methods extortion, we call them survival.
strings.GNG_force_the_issue_desc: The Legislative Council: A cabal of politicians, investors, and businessmen that make up the closest thing to a government here in Guangdong. Their only purpose is to increase the benefits of Guangdong and the many companies that are invested in its industry. It is time to confront them, since they are our largest opponent to a Guangdong with us at the helm. We must demand that they stop interfering in our work, and to stop sabotaging our legislation. We demand their support in our regime, for the good of the Three Pearls!
strings.GNG_the_tsunami_of_chinese_anger_desc:
The consequences of the Yasuda Crisis have borne more deadly fruit for Guangdong. With the Sphere's economy in shambles, the hordes of Cantonese workers are fuming at the loss of their jobs, along with the claims of corruption within our government. Our police and the Kenpentei are doing what they can to suppress the former sweatshop workers, but the influx of job hunters from across the Sphere are starting to swell, further exasperating the protests. The laborers are demanding luxuries like paycheck bonuses, as well as food. This is a rather expensive demand, especially during an economic crisis, and one our investors will gawk at. However, If we don't do something to take care of the needs of our labor pool, we may have a revolt on our hands,

and revolts don't bode well for business...
strings.GNG_the_tsunami_of_chinese_anger_tt: The devil makes work for idle hands, it's said. The greatest danger facing Guangdong comes from the Chinese, and we must ensure that they remain occupied - with certain sweeteners, if needed.
strings.GNG_guarantee_deposits_desc: Guangdong, since its inception, has never needed financial safety nets, with a corporate official once stating that “The only safety nets Guangdong needs are for suicide prevention”. Unfortunately, it seems that the many banks of Guangdong are in dire need of some sort of financial backing in the form of a deposit insurance scheme. Desperate times call for desperate measures, and right now we are desperate to ensure that the deposits of the wealthier strata won't be considered worthless.
strings.GNG_lean_on_the_landlords_desc:
Guangdong is a heavily populated area, with millions living in the Three Pearls alone. Most of the workers reside in large urban apartment buildings, an inexpensive and effective method of housing them. With these buildings comes numerous landlords, many of them Japanese, collecting rent. However, with the economy temporarily paralyzed, our companies cannot afford to pay the laborers, keeping them from paying rent.

Our investors and bureaucracy have come up with a solution: order the landlords to stop collecting rent. The workers will be able to buy products and stay off the streets, preventing the spread of dissidence. Sure, the landlords will complain, but with some persuasion from the Kenpentei, they will see that their actions will be for the good of the Co-Prosperity Sphere.
strings.GNG_stop_excess_overtime_desc: The laborers of our country's industry work as hard as they can, only doing what they are told, as long as their wages are taken care of. We have taken advantage of this to churn out consumer goods for much of the Sphere. However, nobody is buying any consumer products thanks to the fallout of the Yasuda Crisis, and yet the workers keep working overtime. This is an obvious waste of money and resources, one which irks our investors. A solution to this problem would be to kick the workers out of the factories after hours. That way we could curb the production of excess goods and save money that would normally be used to pay overtime.
strings.GNG_daytime_work_only_desc: So far, the strategy of forcing workers out of the factories in order to prevent overtime has been a success. Unfortunately, our companies are still far from safe, and the workers still produce enormous amounts of goods that nobody is buying. What if we took this idea further? Let's restrict work hours to only daytime hours, that way less goods are produced, more excess is curbed and more money is saved.
strings.GNG_anything_for_security_desc: The Chinese outnumber the Japanese and the Cantonese-Japanese by such a margin we can't let their discontent reach critical mass. While Guangdong is not in the business of being nice to its workers - imagine the protests from the companies if their costs exploded - the Chinese need to be kept working for us, not against us.
strings.GNG_anything_for_security_tt: We will do anything to reassure the Chinese that they need not take up arms against the government...
strings.GNG_save_cantonese_japanese_suppliers_de:
If one were to call the hodgepodge of bureaucracy the vital organs of our economic body, and the factories and their products its veins and arteries, then our emerging Cantonese-Japanese class, otherwise known as the Zhujin - the embodiment of the Pan-Asian dream - would most certainly be the backbone that keeps the whole thing standing. Despite its relatively recent history and small numbers, already they've developed into such an inseparable part of our economy that any blow dealt upon them is guaranteed to fall tenfold upon the whole of Guangdong.

Promises, scrutiny, coercion, whatever it takes - under no circumstances shall we allow the Zhujin to be caught up in the seismic shock rippling across the Sphere, lest our economy fall into irrevocable, unsalvageable ruin.
strings.GNG_save_cantonese_japanese_suppliers_tt: The Zhujin represent the future of our economic model - a skilled workforce with the income to power a consumer economy. They must not be allowed to go under.
strings.GNG_provide_loan_forbearance_desc:
As much as we hate to admit it, up to this point most of Zhujin economic ventures have been pretty much fuelled by borrowed cash. Had times been better, bank loans would've been at the bottom of our priority list; but now at such a time of unprecedented crisis they may very well be the last straw that brings down our entire economy.

Contacts must be made with Tokyo, with local firms, with any bank we have one bit of leverage over to placate them and hopefully negotiate repayment delays, allowing the worthiest of our citizens at least some room left to make adjustments and brace for worse to come.
strings.GNG_offer_zero_interest_loans_desc: Bad news: our businesses are still losing money. While our current measures have stabilized their conditions, Japanese and Cantonese corporations are still on the verge of bankruptcy. With the banks all shut down, there is nobody that can lend money to corporations: except us. Our accountants have suggested that we lend our companies large sums of money with zero interest. While this measure will keep our companies afloat, it will drain our reserves and enrage our investors. With our current situation, however, this may be our best option.
strings.GNG_freeze_civil_service_cuts_desc: When it comes to the security and order of Guangdong, we rely on the civil service: policemen, bureaucrats, members of the Legislative Council, and many more in the intricate bureaucratic machine. Most of these civil servants are Cantonese-Japanese, who make up our “middle class”, and are the only thing separating us from the discontent of the Chinese laborers. In order to ensure that the Zhujin are loyal to our government and our investors, we must continue to keep them employed. This will further drain our reserves, which are draining by the minute, but the importance of the Zhujin and their work supersedes that of even our budget.
strings.GNG_guarantee_civil_service_pay_desc: Many of the Zhujin we promised to not lay off are grateful for our guarantee, as they should be. However some of them are still worried about putting food on the table. While this fear is laughable at best, thanks in part to the financial stability of our companies, we should take the guarantee one step further. We will promise the Zhujin that they will still receive pay. Our coffers will take a hit, but the Zhujin and their jobs are too important to jeopardize.
strings.GNG_the_worthy_few_desc: We've made our stance clear - we must ensure the survival of the Cantonese-Japanese, those worthy few who embody the spirit of enterprise and assimilation into the Japanese new order in Asia. This collapse wasn't their fault, they don't deserve to suffer for it - and for the sake of Guangdong's survival, we will see that they make it through.
strings.GNG_the_worthy_few_tt: We will do what we must to reassure the Zhujin that their interests will be taken care of...
strings.GNG_indemify_japanese_investors_desc: It is a fact of our existence that Guangdong was created to serve the whims of Japanese companies and investors. They are masters, and we are merely servants. Some have suggested that we do not provide compensation to them, in order to save much-needed capital. This is not a prudent idea, given our relationship with the Japanese. If we abandon them during this crisis, the consequences in the future will be dire. As such, we will provide bailouts to the Japanese in these tough times.
strings.GNG_indemify_japanese_investors_tt: The Japanese underwrite our entire operation in Guangdong, and losing their support would be catastrophic.
strings.GNG_ring_fence_yasuda_desc: Yasuda is about to collapse; no one can deny such a thing. But their collapse and its consequences will leave severe aftereffects. It is our job to limit the resulting damage to the economy as much as possible. We will see to it that no one but Yasuda will collapse. Their business partners will receive whatever they need to make it past this crisis - and cut our losses from Yasuda.
strings.GNG_deny_devaluation_desc:
We will not - we cannot - allow the Guangdong Yen to devalue like its Japanese counterpart. If such an event happens, a great majority of our investors will lose everything: a disaster for all. As such, we will reassure our investors that the Yen will not devalue, even during our greatest crisis.

Nevertheless, it will be quite expensive to keep our promises to our investors...
strings.GNG_enforce_margin_calls_desc: Lenders have been calling us day and night, demanding to know what we are going to do to protect them and their interests. Their main topic of concern are their loans that have been sent out - they fear that they may lose out on crucial payments, now more necessary than ever. We will help them collect on their loans, no matter how unpopular this move may be. Contracts must be enforced, even in the toughest of times.
strings.GNG_extra_security_desc: Unsurprisingly, there has been outcry over our moves to help Japanese investors collect on investments. From the smallest businesses to some of the largest companies, controversy over this move has intensified worries of violence towards the investors. As such, we are preparing to deploy guards to the homes of our investors to ensure their safety. Further, we will increase police patrols across the cities to dissuade certain... sections of society from rioting.
strings.GNG_sozai_igi_desc:
The initial instability seems to be coming to an end: events in Tokyo and the resolution of Yasuda's bankruptcy are indicating that the markets are bottoming out.

Now is not a time of rest. We have done much to address the immediate aftermath of the crash, but now we must assess overall damage and devise solutions to fix the situation. Our finances are beginning to stabilize with the generous help of our tycoons. Now, we must prioritize recovery and begin to re-establish our contacts in Tokyo.
strings.GNG_sozai_igi_tt: Guangdong is first and foremost a market for the Japanese to do business in - and this will remain unchanged!
strings.GNG_next_steps_desc:
As economic trajectory of Guangdong bottoms out on the back of Chief Executive Suzuki's confidence-building measures and economic assistance packages, Guangdong prepares to pick itself up and walk back towards the future it was always meant to have.

A future as the beating heart of the Co-Prosperity Sphere's economy, shining a light into the future under the watchful guidance of Chief Executive Suzuki, he who found Guangdong a warren of vice and avarice - and turned Guangdong into a paragon of industry and innovation. The tycoons may resent us for our bold undertakings, but Yasuda's troubles have shown that they cannot hope to survive alone - that strong leadership is the guiding force of profit.
strings.GNG_next_steps_tt: We've done what we can to put a floor in Guangdong's economic collapse... and now the hard work of rebuilding begins.
strings.GNG_subsidies_in_a_time_of_want: Subsidies in a Time of Want
strings.GNG_chief_executive_matsuzawa_desc: Matsuzawa Takuji, the representative director of the ill-fated Yasuda conglomerate's Guangdong operations, has been selected by his peers to serve as Chief Executive following Suzuki Teiichi's untimely return to Tokyo. With his patron gone and with his company on death's door, Matsuzawa has barely any capacity to pick up the task of administering a Guangdong spiraling into economic freefall - and that's just how the tycoons want it.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_matsuzawa_tt: We welcome our new Chief Executive - he who holds the poisoned chalice.
strings.GNG_an_accidental_appointment_desc:
The haste of Suzuki Teiichi's departure as Chief Executive has left a great deal of work unfinished, with hardly any process for handing over the responsibilities involved. The demands of the new Chief Executive's position present a steep learning curve - and although Matsuzawa was closer to Suzuki than anyone else of Guangdong's tycoons, the rumors have already started (perhaps from among the tycoons themselves) that he isn't up for the job.

That sometime down the line, a more permanent Chief Executive should preside over Guangdong's affairs.
strings.GNG_an_unenviable_position_desc: First Yasuda went underwater, imploding on itself and taking the entire Co-Prosperity Sphere's economy along with it. Then Chief Executive Suzuki fell from grace in Guangdong and was recalled to 'greener' political pastures in Tokyo, leaving behind a mountain of troubles for his hamstrung successor. It is a job that nobody wants - and thus Matsuzawa, already a dead man walking following the collapse of Yasuda, is the right man for the job. But even in his supremely weakened state, Matsuzawa still needs to find a way to convince people to work with him...
strings.GNG_guangdong_in_the_red_desc:
The most immediate pressing problem is that with our regular source of budget supply cut from Tokyo, Guangdong's fiscal situation is careening towards insolvency at a breakneck speed. The time lost from the removal of Suzuki from the Chief Executive position has only intensified these trends. Should the situation worsen any further, we could see a general investor rout from Guangdong - a death spiral from which we cannot recover.

We must choose who lives, and who dies in this new Guangdong. Not everyone can be saved, and we will simply have to demand the unlucky many suffer what they must. There is no other choice.
strings.GNG_guangdong_in_the_red_tt: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong is bleeding money. We need a plan...
strings.GNG_the_ibuka_plan_desc: Ibuka Masaru of Fujitsu has approached Matsuzawa with a plan to right Guangdong's finances - to go back to the roots of Guangdong as a place for Japanese entrepreneurs to do business. In his words, 'money is life' - and without taking emergency measures to stabilize investor confidence and correct Guangdong's budget, Guangdong is doomed. We will begin to do whatever is needed to keep Japanese investors and capitalists on our side - even if it means we earn resentment from the Cantonese-Japanese and the Chinese people.
strings.GNG_CRR_Ibuka_plan: We have chosen to go with £GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Ibuka Masaru's plan.
strings.GNG_prop_up_japanese_business_desc: If the fallout of the Yasuda collapse has shown us anything, it is that we flirt with the destruction of the Japanese firms that compromise our economic backbone at our own peril. While we were too late to do anything to save Yasuda from its own excesses, we must take care of those Japanese businesses and entrepreneurs in Guangdong and ensure that the damage does not spread any further than it already has.
strings.GNG_subsidies_in_a_time_of_want_desc:
Guangdong is a land of wealth and prosperity, but foremost it is the home of opportunity. For centuries, the Pearl River Delta has been the site of international investment and trade, and it is only desirable we keep it as such with our Japanese partners and patrons.

The best way to keep these companies in the nation is to make it as easy as possible for them to make a fortune here. We will advertise Guangdong to be a safe haven for Japanese investment, even in these turbulent times, where economic security is so scarcely found. Our future lies in the innumerable treasures flocking in from across Asia - it is only up to us to welcome it.
strings.GNG_subsidies_in_a_time_of_want_tt: Economists warn that our economy is not ready for wide-sweeping government intervention.
strings.GNG_rely_on_middle_class_investment_desc:
With our purse strings as stretched as they are, we need to gather as much investment and consumer confidence from the middle classes we rely upon to support the economy. Communities in Guangdong, as well as in Japan, have a significant stake in how our markets stay afloat, and we need them now more than ever.

We must focus our efforts in marketing Guangdong to be a beacon of economic security and stability in the East, even in these trying times. With the right know-how and execution, those fleeing market panic in Japan will land their resources in the Pearl River Delta, bringing their riches with them.
strings.GNG_prevent_a_capital_flight_desc: The other worst-case scenario imaginable for Guangdong is widespread capital flight - a catastrophic loss of confidence by Japanese investors who pull their funding back towards safer havens in Japan or elsewhere. While no country in the Sphere appears particularly economically 'safe' at the moment, Guangdong differs in that its industries will wither on the vine if foreign investors begin pulling their money out. We must reassure the investor community that we have their best interests at heart, even in difficult times.
strings.GNG_repeal_the_rlso_desc:
Suzuki's Revised Labor Standards Ordinance is and will be a millstone around the neck of both our current and future governments, making promises to the people that simply cannot be kept. The meticulous construction of the bill, and its intense optimism, will only constrict the administration of our future recovery measures.

Our patrons in the Japanese business lobby want the legislation repealed, for obvious reasons, and so it shall be done. If we want to even think about recovery, we must free ourselves some breathing room by issuing an annulment of the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance in its entirety.
strings.GNG_tried_and_true_desc:
What is Guangdong's place in the world? Our small state, at the foot of the Pearl River Delta, has been the forefront of international trade with Chinese markets for as long as we can remember. This is our destiny, as a people and as a nation.

Today, we are the conduit for wealthy Japanese investment into China, so that we can make use of the fruits of land and labor for the benefit of the Japanese companies operating there. With the initiative, determination, and expertise inherited from the rich merchant traditions of our ancestors, we will remain true to the founding spirit of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_suzukis_ill_timed_triumph_desc:
Chief Executive Suzuki spent much of his time in office attempting to pass legislation to enact working conditions reform. Although the bills broughts him great attention, they are now a burden for business as they operate in and throughout the Pearl River Delta.

Simply put, the costs are too high. It is undesirable that we hinder the performance of corporations hiring, manufacturing, and selling in Guangdong - lest they flee elsewhere in search of profits. Something must be done before we are reduced to rags because we idolised out-of-date laws and regulations.
strings.GNG_the_morita_plan_desc: Morita Akio of Sony has proposed that we rethink the circumstances we find ourselves in. In order to secure a Guangdong that can welcome back Japanese investment and orders at a rapid clip once the Yasuda Crisis ends, the government should focus its efforts on mitigating the harm of the current crisis on Guangdong's workers and smaller businesses. In other words - helping the Chinese and the Zhujin weather this storm. We can't save all of them - but we can convince them to grit their teeth and hang on with promises of a better future.
strings.GNG_CRR_Morita_plan: We have chosen to go forward with £GNG_Sony_texticon Morita Akio's plan.
strings.GNG_a_promise_for_the_future_desc:
In the midst of economic crises, times are going to be tough; there is no way around that. As difficult as it sounds, though, we can navigate around these complex problems to work and ensure the impact of the fallout doesn't punish our workers who keep Guangdong running, even as investors grow skittish and shy in the face of falling profits and flocking shareholders.

By no means will this be an easy task; where we must make cuts, we will promise they will only be temporary. There is a great reward for our workers at the end of the tunnel, they need only hold on and bare with us.
strings.GNG_delay_the_rlso_desc: Former Chief Executive Suzuki's magnum opus, the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance, was no doubt a great achievement of his time, and guaranteed the long-term continued stability of Guangdong's industries that was long overdue. Sadly, that time and case no longer applies to our current dire position. The RLSO would become an extra burden upon our already struggling finances if ever fully implemented, so it is necessary that it be delayed due to the current situation, as we do not wish for further strain to fall upon the existing Japanese and Zhujin businesses trying to meet its requirements. Of course, after we have moved past the Crisis, the RLSO shall be reimplemented accordingly, at least, that is what we will promise to the people.
strings.GNG_keep_the_workers_working_desc:
As we find ourselves occupied with a myriad of issues plaguing the nation, and the very last thing we would need right now is a horde of unemployed Chinese and Zhujin workers spilling into the streets and demanding their slice of the pie.

Our government is woefully under-prepared for the wild chaos of protesting and violence, and it is desirable that we avoid it in its entirety. We regard it as best for social stability across Guangdong that workers stay at their stations in some way, shape, or form. To keep the lights on for when business resumes, and to keep riots from breaking out across the cities - our assurances to the working class will have to do.
strings.GNG_slow_down_the_collapse_desc: The Yasuda Crisis has completely thrown the once functioning economy into freefall, the huge scale of its collapse has guaranteed the loss of capital and financial suffering, especially on the part of businesses. We need to reassure the populace and set a viable roadmap for future recovery, as well as start putting efforts into motion to at least try to halt the rapid pace of the collapse, even if it's at a monetary loss. The unemployed former workforce will benefit from these actions and gradually become aware of when recovery would allow them to return to their workplaces, as well as contributing to the protection of smaller Zhujin businesses, which make up the backbone of services towards our workforce. These measures are absolutely necessary to ensure that the people, the economy and the nation will survive through these arduous times.
strings.GNG_no_one_shall_go_hungry_desc: The ensurement that the needs of the populace and former workforce will be handled first is our best bet to surviving the horrible situation of the Yasuda Crisis. If we manage to guarantee enough supplies and opportunities to our people now, it would surely allow us to step out of the Crisis with an able and diligent workforce that would make our economy thrive and propel our nation to greater heights! Therefore, our most important obligation would be to attend to the basic sustenance of the people, even if it is at an immense cost to our finances, it would surely put us in a great position for an expeditious and guaranteed recovery.
strings.GNG_no_one_shall_go_hungry_warning: Putting pressure on our economy during a crisis can be damaging.
strings.GNG_suzukis_legacy_desc: Suzuki Teiichi was, and still is a complicated figure for Guangdong. He had resigned in shame and disgrace after news of his failures broke loose, but that does not mean that he was completely defunct in his thoughts and ideas. Guangdong had for a very long time, focused on meeting the satisfactions and desires of shareholders and investors, granting it temporary benefits, at the expense of neglecting and undermining the needs and interests of the territory, Guangdong itself. Ultimately, Chief Executive Suzuki would be a divisive figure for quite a long time, but it is better to retain some of his legacy, to guarantee prosperity, harmony and growth in the years ahead.
strings.GNG_breaking_even_desc:
We've staved off the worst - for now. The economic freefall has ground to somewhat of a halt, thanks to our swift and timely decisions on which sectors of society to prioritize salvaging, and on the future of the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance.

It is natural to feel tempted to breathe a sigh of relief; yet all is not well, far from it. Prospects of our fiscal recovery remain out of sight, with the most cynical of our benefactors already drafting up plans of escape. Phantoms both old and new arise from their slumber, their screeches echoing across the urban skylines and through slums and shantytowns, and their haunting presence seeping through the fabric of society we have so meticulously woven together. And amidst all the burning wreckage lies Yasuda's rotting carcass, laid bare on the streets for vultures circling on all sides to sweep down and dine on.

Suzuki Teiichi left behind him a freighter collapsing under its own weight and riddled with gaping holes, and it is up to us to funnel all that we have into patching it up. Guangdong shall never sink into oblivion, as long as there is one man still standing at its helm.
strings.GNG_auction_off_yasudas_assets_desc: Yasuda's collapse has left our government with an important question: What to do with the remains? Since the Zaibatsu's assets in Guangdong were entrusted with us, the creditors circle our government like carrion vultures, eyeing the assets hungrily. Unfortunately, we can't keep these pieces of Yasuda much longer, with their maintenance costs draining our already dwindling reserves. A solution has been put forth, to auction off the Yasuda assets to willing buyers. We could kill multiple birds with one stone; selling the assets would fill our reserves again, eliminate the cost of maintaining the assets, and get the creditors off of our back.
strings.GNG_auction_off_yasudas_assets_tt: The spoils of £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's demise shall be partitioned to the highest bidder...
strings.GNG_taking_inventory_desc: In order to sell Yasuda's old assets, we should determine what assets we hold, and how much they are worth. The bureaucracy will organize a comprehensive list of factories, subsidiaries, and properties formerly owned by Yasuda, and determine their respective values.
strings.GNG_taking_inventory_tt: We need to know what we're selling, and what it is worth...
strings.GNG_top_it_off_desc: Our control over the value of several Yasuda assets means we could set their values as high or low as we want, and no one would be the wiser. Of course, if this is discovered, our government would be in a scandal of epic proportions, but as they say, nothing ventured nothing gained. And there is much to be gained here.
strings.GNG_top_it_off_tt: If we say the assets are worth more than they are... then they are worth exactly what we say they are. £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong needs the money.
strings.GNG_no_more_no_less_desc: As the owner of Yasuda's former assets, it is our responsibility to determine the value of each asset as accurately as possible. Any manipulation of the values would be unfair and corrupt, which are attributes we cannot be affiliated with as of now.
strings.GNG_no_more_no_less_tt: To lie about £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's true value, from the mouth of Guangdong's Chief Executive, would be an insult on top of injury.
strings.GNG_going_once_desc: The value of the assets have been determined and the auctioneers are restless. The auction is about to begin, and with it the growth of our coffers. It is time to start the bidding!
strings.GNG_playing_favorites_desc: Most of the assets of Yasuda will most likely be bought up by companies here in Guangdong. As many of the companies have members on the Legislative Council, we have an opportunity to get them on our side. We could simply play favorites with the companies on the Council, selling them the assets, in return for a few favors from the Council members.
strings.GNG_playing_favorites_requirement: The price of the £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda assets have been set.
strings.GNG_playing_favorites_tt: Nobody said an auction has to be fair, after all...
strings.GNG_a_fair_game_desc: As beneficial as it may be to give Guangdong companies priority as auctioneers over other companies for favors from the Legislative Council, it would be unprofitable in the long run. Since the Yasuda Crisis was caused by deep corruption involving much of the Japanese government, armed forces, and industry, any sort of corruption in our dealings would spell certain death and disgrace for our administration. The auction must remain as fair as possible.
strings.GNG_a_fair_game_tt: ...but we respect the spirit of fairness, as Ibuka Masaru insists we do.
strings.GNG_matsushitas_offer_desc: The Matsushita Electric Company has approached us with an intriguing offer; If we were to sell the assets of Yasuda to Masushita Electric, the company would also take on Yasuda's liabilities as well. Their price is our full support within the Legislative Council when they need it. This deal would not only bring in money for our government, it would also rid us of any debt or interest we inherited from Yasuda.
strings.GNG_matsushitas_offer_tt: ...and Matsushita Masaharu has a proposal to ease £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's throes.
strings.GNG_sonys_appeal_desc: In the wake of the Yasuda collapse, Sony has risen to take on its aftereffects. It has magnanimously offered to employ former Yasuda employees and find places for them in its workforce. While many have pointed out that Yasuda and Sony operated in very different industries, the latter has reasoned that these employees are no less useful, even if they may be out of their depth. There is an additional benefit to Sony's offer: discontent and unemployment would be significantly lessened. Of course, if we accept their bargain, they expect political backing in return - but surely that can be resolved later?
strings.GNG_sonys_appeal_tt: ...Morita sees the big picture, and it's time we do as well.
strings.GNG_going_twice_desc: All bids have been set over Yasuda's assets. Many, especially from the remains of Yasuda, are decrying this as opportunism. While we cannot deny such accusations, the fact remains that this is the best way to make use of the resources now that the company has collapsed.
strings.GNG_going_twice_tt: We have made the necessary phone calls...
strings.GNG_sold_desc:
Yasuda is gone.

It has been swept into the dustbin of corporate history, remembered only as the instigator of corruption and the crumbling of economies across Asia. The effects of Yasuda's collapse are still being felt, but the company itself is no more. Guangdong waits for no man or corporation - least of all a dead one. This is but a new beginning for our state.
strings.GNG_limiting_collateral_damage_desc:
It seems the Yasuda collapse has singlehandedly brought our domestic tensions to a boiling point. Across the East China Sea, thousands of displaced Home Islands aristocrats, businessmen and residents alike flock to us every day for any semblance of normal life, a certain burden on our infrastructure; meanwhile on our own streets, our attempts at economic first-aid have inevitably provoked backlash in the form of worsening dissident activity, paralyzing government institutions and bringing financial recovery to a standstill.

The longer we let this stand, the less likely we'll survive the eventual fallout. It is imperative that we immediately begin formulating our approach to the issues at hand, so as to deliver our people - both within and outside our borders - a satisfactory solution, whatever the costs may be.
strings.GNG_limiting_collateral_damage_tt: The chaos in the streets and on our shores must be contained.
strings.GNG_the_tsunami_desc: In the wake of Yasuda's collapse, hundreds of thousands of workers in Japan have been thrown into economic desperation. This, unsurprisingly, has launched a new migration of businessmen and their families into Guangdong. Many are fleeing the consequences of the collapse, whether that is debt payments, jilted lovers, political enemies, or simply the shame that they have lost everything. While we are taking in as many as we can, we are still in recovery from the economic crisis - it is putting a strain on our coffers to take care of them. As more settle, we have no choice but to take action upon these settlers.
strings.GNG_the_tsunami_tt: Hundreds, maybe more, of destitute £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese wash up on our shores. Their misery only threatens to compound our own.
strings.GNG_a_safe_port_desc: What kind of businesspeople are we if we turn away new investors? What are we if we turn away new blood? There is precisely no reason why we should turn these new, Japanese, migrants away. Many of them are ready to take up positions in the leading companies at any time. As such, we will give these new migrants all they need to adjust to Cantonese life; employment assistance, new housing, and most importantly, safe haven.
strings.GNG_displace_cantonese_japanese_desc: There is only so much space available for new managers or senior specialists amid this crisis. If we are to fulfill our promises to the Japanese, we must displace the existing ones wherever possible. This will affect the Zhujin the most, for they are the primary demographic for middle management - but they are a worthwhile sacrifice in return for continued economic support.
strings.GNG_cast_them_adrift_desc: Many may criticize us for this move, but it must be done. We simply cannot welcome these new migrants, no matter how useful they may be. Our hands are already full with numerous problems - the existing Japanese expatriates who want their money back, the Zhujin who fear poverty, and the Chinese struggling to live day by day. In this climate, it is an illogical choice to take these migrants in.
strings.GNG_stoke_national_sentiment_desc: The Japanese are obviously displeased by our decision to turn away the migrants from the Home Islands. While this will be hard to deal with in the future, our informants among the population have noticed something interesting. The Chinese and Zhujin populations seem to be broadly supportive of our move, as we have prioritized their interests over those of the Japanese. This is the perfect opportunity to gain support from the population. As such, we will continue to emphasize the interests of the residents of Guangdong before foreigners.
strings.GNG_maintaining_public_order_desc:
The street and the government hall are two sides of the same coin, they say - and all it takes is the hellfire of economic turmoil to devour it all.

All the intensification of police deployment, all the authorization of Kenpeitai operations - it just isn't enough. With every passing day, for every hundred people thrown out of their jobs or apartments, a hundred more are swayed over to the subversive elements slipping through our fingers and running rampant across the map. The sight of demonstrators and protestors at the doorsteps of government buildings has degraded into an irritating regularity, a nuisance distracting loyal officials from performing their actual duties for the sake of our recovery.

What we've been doing isn't enough - but it's still not too late to catch up. We have to begin drafting up plans of action and take matters firmly into our own hands, before the Kenpeitai can take them into their own; otherwise, the credibility of our government will suffer.
strings.GNG_maintaining_public_order_tt: Our workers have become unemployed malcontents, and our police a demoralized mob. A dangerous combination on £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's streets...
strings.GNG_round_up_the_agitators_desc:
As a matter of fact, we do have a rough list on our hands of the most prominent faces of the dissenters, from radicals advocating workplace reforms, to Chinese nationalist rabble-rousers, to Nanjing sympathizers demanding “retrocession of Guangdong to the legitimate government” - we simply chose to turn a blind eye to those people who amounted to little significance in the past.

But extreme times call for extreme measures. Every one of them will be tracked down and put under custody, to prevent them from fanning the flames already burning away what little left of our domestic stability. We're well aware this won't be a silver bullet to the unrest; all we need is get the message out, warn the antsy populace against stepping out of line, and buy ourselves enough time to decide on our next course of action.
strings.GNG_crack_down_on_organized_crime_desc:
We have let the underworld run amok for too long - the Triads, the Yakuza, those who cheer at our woes and take their spoils from the rubble with glee. Reports from past weeks have indicated a drastic uptick in recruitment operations, smuggling ring activities, as well as extortion and kidnapping of innocent citizens; worse still, rumor has it that a growing number of officers within our own ranks have already been compromised, apparently desperate for any source of cash to make ends meet.

Our tolerance ends here. We will put our foot down and make our stance clear, even if it's for a lost cause. We will employ whatever we have at hand to muster up at least some semblance of resistance against such blatant violations of social order, and make it clear to all that Guangdong's essence lies in its integrity, not in shady dealings.
strings.GNG_enforce_a_curfew_desc:
As a matter of fact, we do have a rough list on our hands of the most prominent faces of the dissenters - but closing in on them risks tanking whatever left of our reputation in the eyes of the masses. Certain figures in the police department have instead proposed a curfew, a certainly viable alternative.

On one hand, nightly mass gatherings are to be prohibited, preventing formation of supersized demonstrations and thus ensuring that nighttime businesses remain undisrupted; on the other, our ability to impose law and order will be examined, verified, and employed as a means to regain civilians' faith in law enforcement, curtailing popular discontent and hopefully opening up channels for cooperative discourse.

Dissenters will remain an annoyance, but it is advisable for now to show some restraint and cultivate a trustworthy image around ourselves.
strings.GNG_turn_a_blind_eye_desc:
We have let the underworld run amok for too long, its machinations having grown well beyond our control. The Triads, the Yakuza - those who cheer at our woes and take their spoils from the rubble with glee - have recently taken it upon themselves to take to the streets, ruthlessly expanding recruitment and enforcing their peculiar brand of “justice” upon faction rivals, civilians, and everyone else they deem uncooperative.

With our police force already overstretched from domestic unrest, it is best not to tempt the rogue beast for now, lest it wedge its sharpened fangs into our throat; we will have to wait until the economic shock has subsided before we get back on our feet, ready our whips, and put the brute back in its place - sooner or later.
strings.GNG_weather_the_storm_desc:
Despite our doubts, despite the overwhelming strain on our law enforcement, everything worked out fine - the fates of our Japanese compatriots have been decided upon, popular unrest has been quelled somewhat, and we have stabilized our domestic situation enough for us to set connections back up, brave the waters once more, and survive the raging maelstrom that barely weeks ago threatened to tear us asunder.

A few more finishing touches, and Guangdong shall sail on.
strings.GNG_weather_the_storm_tt: We have done all we can, at least under Chief Executive Matsuzawa.
strings.GNG_the_empty_throne_desc: The companies and the Legislative Council have been the foundation of the government and economy of Guangdong ever since its conception, colossal pillars holding up the sky. With the collapse of Yasuda Holdings, one of those pillars came crashing down, leaving a vacuum, requiring a suitable replacement. Now that the question of social instability and the remnants of Yasuda's assets has been resolved, it is time we look towards the missing pillar. It is clear that the might of Sony, Fujitsu, and Matsushita alone isn't enough to sustain dominance and control over the economy of Guangdong, and with Yasuda nothing but scattered and gone, someone else would have to be chosen to reside upon the vacant throne in the Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_hail_hitachi_desc: An interesting proposal has been offered by Ibuka Masaru of Fujitsu Limited, to fill the vacant seat in the Legislative Council with the Hitachi Limited of Manchukuo, the electronics subsidiary of the Mangyō Industrial Concern. Many objections have been raised to the fact that Hitachi originates from Manchukuo, and therefore is a direct rival to Guangdong's economic growth and projection, which makes it unfit for entry into the Council. Ibuka however, has assured us plentifully that Hitachi would only be of use to us, that they are too weak to act against us but would help obstruct Sony's political influence, ensuring a political scene dominated by Matsushita and Fujitsu. Whether Ibuka's words are correct, we will have to see.
strings.GNG_hail_hitachi_tt:
We will summon £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi, the subsidiary of the £GFX_MAN_mangyo_texticon Mangyō conglomerate of £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Manchuria, to take £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's seat.
This will give them a better start upon the formation of the new£GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_contact_cheung_kong_desc: A suggestion has been raised by representatives of Sony in the Legislative Council on the matter of the succession of Yasuda's spot in the Council. Sony cites that the collapse of Yasuda has openly demonstrated to the populace, especially the Zhujin population of Guangdong that having the Legislative Council dominated by solely foreign Japanese companies had an exceeding amount of limitations. They claim that the stability issues faced by former Chief Executive Suzuki would only be exacerbated by continuing this unsustainable model of governance, and that the only succinct solution would be to give the Zhujin population more representation in the higher echelons of Guangdong, especially the Council. Therefore, the obvious choice would be to invite Li Ka-shing and the Cheung Kong conglomerate to take the former place of Yasuda, which would fulfill all of the previously mentioned goals and balance against the dominance of Matsushita and Fujitsu.
strings.GNG_contact_cheung_kong_tt:
We shall invite£GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong, the largest local conglomerate in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong, to take £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's seat.
This will give them a better start upon the formation of the new£GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_guangdong_in_the_black_desc: With the collapse of Yasuda Holdings still ravaging the economy and society of Guangdong, Chief Executive Matsuzawa has done all he could to ensure that the people and the state of Guangdong survive through these desperate times. As the assurances and worries of the past fade through the sands of time, everyone's eyes and focuses are centered towards one direction, the future. Now that it is completely certain that Yasuda has gone entirely defunct, Matsuzawa knows that the days where he is to remain in his position are very much numbered, his successor would likely be picked soon directly from Tokyo. In the final moments where Matsuzawa remains at the center of the limelight, he would leave his last mark on deciding the future of Guangdong, recommending a possible successor.
strings.GNG_tax_relief_for_the_lower_income: Tax Relief for the Lower Income
strings.GNG_a_helping_hand_from_the_government: A Helping Hand From the Government
strings.GNG_the_new_face_of_pan_asian_industry: The New Face of Pan-Asian Industry
strings.GNG_a_stable_economy_for_a_stable_nation: A Stable Economy for a Stable Nation
strings.GNG_chief_executive_morita_desc:
After over a decade as the perennial underdog in Guangdong's corporate politics, Morita Akio now reigns as Chief Executive - alongside his second-in-command and longtime ally, Li Ka-shing, the richest Zhujin man in Guangdong. For years, the two have built an empire in the shadow of the Japanese Zaibatsu - fighting as hard as they dared for the survival of Sony and Cheung Kong, and for the livelihoods of the Chinese and Zhujin working for them.

The scars of the Yasuda Crisis are plain to see from Sony's headquarters in Honkon - the jobless, the poor, and the hungry rule the streets of Guangdong, bound together by a creeping helplessness. But Morita and Li believe that in every crisis lies an opportunity - both for their business and for the people.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_morita_tt: We salute our new Chief Executive, Morita Akio - and his partner in arms, Li Ka-shing!
strings.GNG_lis_ambition_desc:
Few would have expected an unassuming factory owner with nothing more than an elementary education to have climbed out of poverty to become the leader of Cheung Kong, the only local conglomerate with the scale to join the Five Companies - with interests in property, retail, distribution, and light manufacturing.

To be rich is not enough - Li will not stop until he is the richest man in Guangdong, capable of ensuring that the people of Guangdong do not suffer the same poverty he once did - preferably by eating out of his hand.
strings.GNG_moritas_dream_desc:
Driven from Japan in 1952, Morita Akio has seen much since he washed ashore in Guangdong, penniless and abandoned. Years of backbreaking effort have earned him more local respect than he ever found in Japan, as 'The Man Who Fought The Zaibatsu' in spite of their overwhelming material advantages.

Now, as he holds the future of Guangdong in his hands, Morita knows he has no time to waste to ensure that Sony can turn its moment in the spotlight into everlasting glory - to reward the many backers of Guangdong's homegrown champion by taking it from one of many, to the one and only.
strings.GNG_more_than_just_survival_desc: The New Guangdong will not simply be a playground for the corporations to do as they will, while leaving broken bodies and discarded dreams in their wake. For Morita and Li, even as they receive their official mandate from Tokyo to surpass Manchukuo and usurp their position in the Co-Prosperity Sphere, they dream of something else - to make life in Guangdong about more than just survival, and to get rich while doing it.
strings.GNG_more_than_just_survival_tt: Morita and Li will do everything to see that the people of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong will come to see it as they do: their home, first by necessity, and then by choice.
strings.GNG_maintaining_our_solvency_desc:
If the Yasuda collapse taught us anything, it is that we cannot be overly reliant on Japan for the means of our government's survival. When the flow of money from Japan stopped, Guangdong nearly lost everything - and we are still picking up the pieces today.

More worryingly, for the vision of Morita and Li have for Guangdong to become reality, the government's expenditures are certain to grow still further. Exploring options for financing the government without the assistance of Tokyo is more than just a 'good idea' - it is of utmost necessity.
strings.GNG_maintaining_our_solvency_effect_tool: Our envisioned program to turn £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong into something more than a glorified factory floor will not come cheap. The government's finances must be made bulletproof.
strings.GNG_our_dues_with_the_japanese_desc:
We need to recognize that the Japanese still hold the lion's share of the capital and political power in Guangdong - and our eventual reforms elsewhere will no doubt leave many of them very annoyed with us.

In the interests of winning their goodwill, the government has the option of selling off the remaining insolvent assets left over from the Yasuda collapse to the Japanese corporations. That way, we can signal to them that we understand that their contribution to Guangdong is highly valued, and that they can invest in Guangdong safely, just as they would in Tokyo.
strings.GNG_our_dues_with_the_japanese_effect_to: We will give the £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese investors a bone - because if they will not respect our vision, then they will at least respect cold cash.
strings.GNG_open_the_auctions_desc:
The land has a price, and we've been sitting on it all along.

We will establish a series of auctions to gradually parcel off Guangdong's state lands to willing corporate developers, granting them the right to develop land as they see fit in exchange for a hefty sum paid to the government. We would be consenting to a far more rapid pace of development in Guangdong, largely led by the Japanese, outside of the projects we have planned for the state - potentially with destabilizing impacts on local Chinese and Zhujin populations - but we will surely reap the benefits in the short-term.
strings.GNG_our_debts_with_zhujin_desc:
There still remains the issue of resolving the leftover insolvencies from the Yasuda collapse - those firms that came into state receivership during the crisis and remain on our books.

Selling these off to willing buyers would provide a quick injection of funds into Guangdong's coffers - but more importantly, if we sell these valuable assets to the Zhujin businessmen of Guangdong, we can kickstart the foundations of a local economy that will undoubtedly be far stronger than those tied to foreign capital.
strings.GNG_our_debts_with_zhujin_effect_tooltip: We will reward our £GNG_zhujin_texticon Zhujin backers with the spoils of what remains of £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's empire, so they can support us in turn.
strings.GNG_contracts_for_sale_desc:
One of the greatest resources available to the government is the sheer amount of land available as a public asset - which we can sell in parcels to willing corporate bidders looking to participate in public construction and industrial development projects. There is far more land than the government can feasibly develop on its own - but the private sector could certainly provide a helping hand, for a price.

However, we have no interest in a free-for-all bidding war that will lock out the general public from enjoying the fruits of said development. We will invite companies to bid on sets of contracts for public-private partnership projects - while this will likely be a less rapid way to raise funds for the government, but at least we can direct the flow of investment and project practices to reduce any harm to the local Chinese and Zhujin populace.
strings.GNG_financial_solvency_and_liquidity_ord:
While the Chief Executive might have the authority to dispose with some amount of public land as he sees fit, this will only be a solution on the margins. Any plans to solicit private bidding for large tracts of undeveloped public lands will need to be authorized by the Legislative Council, if only for the sake of avoiding the inevitable accusations of corruption and conflict of interest.

We will thus seek the Legislative Council's approval to create an annual schedule of private lands to be put up for auction to the private sector, as a way of ensuring transparency and keeping potential participants in the know. Surely, nobody objects to how we raise money for the state, especially if state assets are being parceled off to willing private buyers?
strings.GNG_plumbing_in_the_tax_system_desc:
Codifying arrangements to quickly sell off insolvent companies and auction off state lands will only be viable for so long. In good times, the number of bankruptcies falls; eventually, we will sell all our unneeded land.

For Guangdong to truly stand on its own, we must take a deep look at its tax system - even if doing so would upset the corporate and Japanese pillars of our economy. It is the only feasible way we can grow the recurring revenue streams that keep our government afloat in the timeframe necessary to support Morita and Li's other objectives.
strings.GNG_plumbing_in_the_tax_system_effect_to: Our tax system is plagued by exceptions, loopholes, and underreporting - and we would do well to plug these leaks.
strings.GNG_new_pipes_of_revenue_desc:
Simply filling in the gaps in our current tax system will not be enough to fund the programs we need to turn Guangdong into something resembling a home for its people. We will approach the issue of tax reform by expressly widening the tax base - even if it means that we anger corporate donors, wealthy Japanese, the Zhujin businesses, or the Chinese masses.

They will understand, in time, that we do this for the good of all. It is the price we all must pay to live in something resembles a civilized society.
strings.GNG_new_pipes_of_revenue_effect_tooltip: It's not enough to fix the plumbing. We need new pipes - and that means new taxes. For the greater good, as £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong will it.
strings.GNG_raise_taxes_on_estate_desc:
Proposing to openly tax wealth would court political disaster from the Japanese expatriate population, and proposals to raise taxes on the corporations are equally a nonstarter in the Legislative Council - Suzuki's demise makes that painfully clear.

But it is true that Guangdong currently has no form of tax analogous to the estate tax - and if we want to incentivize the wealthy to pay their fair share to everyone else, then we might simply have to wait until they are dead. Literally. If needed, we can structure the incentives so that the rich are encouraged to indulge in their more... philanthropic interests in life.

Everyone wins, right?
strings.GNG_tax_relief_for_the_lower_income_desc:
To our critics: yes, Chief Executive Morita plans to cut income taxes for the poor. They don't make enough, in most cases, to be taxed anyway, and the visits from our tax collector often collect nothing but resentment and nothing else.

But everybody needs to spend to eat, to buy clothing, to buy amenities, and for the odd luxury or two.

To be absolutely clear: we will not tax incomes. We do not believe in depriving the populace of the means to survive. But we will tax spending - at a lower rate than what we would tax their income, but taxed nonetheless. This will no doubt prove more stable a source of income to the government than increasing the government's cut of a fluctuating wage bill.
strings.GNG_national_tax_rationalization_ordinan:
Any permanent changes to Guangdong's tax laws - and any hope of actually getting a broad swathe of Guangdong's society to agree to pay - rests on our ability to pass our proposed raft of tax legislation through the Legislative Council.

Nobody expects the vote to be easy - nobody likes paying the taxman, and our corporate enemies even less so - but we must not stop here.
strings.GNG_sealing_the_cracks_desc:
To actually institute new taxes would be a bridge too far, a political gamble we could not take without destabilizing the delicate political and social situation in Guangdong already. The Japanese would object and withdraw their support; the Chinese already struggle to make do as it is; and the Zhujin need every advantage they can get.

We would be better served looking into our existing tax structures and filling in any cracks and loopholes that we discover. It's much easier to sell our reforms as ensuring everyone has to pay their fair share under the law - without discussing how fair the law itself is...
