strings.GNG_sealing_the_cracks_effect_tooltip: Raising taxes would raise alarms from the investor community, threatening a loss of confidence. Better that we plug the leaks, and rely on our economic growth to do the rest.
strings.GNG_unleash_the_watchdogs_desc:
The signs of tax evasion aren't too difficult to miss in most cases, so long as you know where to look and have good people doing the searching. An overly gaudy vase here, frequent trips to Okinawa there, too many receipts from expensive restaurants in an errant suit pocket; for most, the temptation to use the immediate gains from tax evasion is too powerful to resist.

Unfortunately, unlike our counterparts in the National Tax Agency in Japan, the Guangdong revenue authorities are perennially understaffed, and what investigations they do undertake are frequently stonewalled by backrooms political dealings and corruption. No more. The tax collectors and the auditors will have the resources and authority to do what must be done.
strings.GNG_amnesty_for_repayment_desc:
Over the past decade of chronic underfunding and corruption, we are aware that many individuals - across all of society, but with some truly egregious examples among the wealthy Japanese and Zhujin - have 'misfiled' or 'forgotten' their tax payments to the state, for the services we all enjoy.

Unfortunately, we also rely on these individuals to provide the necessary political and business acumen to implement our policies and run Sony and Cheung Kong on a daily basis.

Even as we strengthen the authority of the tax agencies to go after future offenders, we will extend a forgiving hand for these individuals, so long as they find a way to cough up some of the money they owe the government. We will leave the writing on the wall, and they can draw their own conclusions.
strings.GNG_financial_supervision_and_regulation:
The authority of the Chief Executive to order tax audits and temporarily shifting resources from other accounting departments in the government to the tax offices only goes so far.

For the Guangdong government to have the lasting authority and resources needed to assess dues, collect taxes, and curtail tax evasion across Guangdong's financial system, we will need to broadly expand the powers of Guangdong's monetary and financial regulatory bodies - vested in the Financial Secretary, his secretariat, and the Guangdong Monetary Authority.

If the Legislative Council agrees, of course...
strings.GNG_fiscal_independence_desc:
The work may be thankless and tiring, but it is done.

Guangdong's revenue system has been entirely revamped and rebuilt from the ground up to provide a tax base that can support our vision of the state. Not as a simple caretaker for a corporate largess, but as a provider of much-needed public services within the framework of Guangdong's capitalist economy.

Nobody likes paying more to the authorities, of course. We can only hope that Chief Executive Morita's plans for the economy and social issues can convince the populace that it's all worth it...
strings.GNG_fiscal_independence_effect_tooltip: We have done what we can to secure £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's fiscal health.
strings.GNG_the_guangdong_spirit_desc: From the ashes of Yasuda, a new Guangdong must rise. Where the old Guangdong focused on profitability at the expense of long-term stability, Chief Executive Morita now faces a question of how to redefine Guangdong's economic model for his term in office. If we want to be as transformational a leader as we aspire to be, then this decision will have momentous consequences.
strings.GNG_the_guangdong_spirit_tt: The future of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong shall be defined by how we build our economy, and the place of our £GNG_zhujin_texticon Zhujin businesses and £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese workers are given within it...
strings.GNG_of_excellence_desc:
Though Morita Akio and Li Ka-shing were the voice of a heterodox faction in Guangdong's politics, arguing for a greater emphasis on equity for employees (and now, residents) in addition to stakeholders and investors, the position of Chief Executive comes with an altogether... wider perspective. Morita now nominally also answers to the powers that be in the Japanese government - which have made clear that they expect continued growth and success from Guangdong.

Answering the expectations of Tokyo, while continuing a commitment to reshape Guangdong into something resembling a home for its people, constitutes a challenge of monumental scale. For Morita, Guangdong will need to emphasize its traditional strengths - its culture of innovation, efficient business, and productivity - in order to generate the returns needed to ensure that both Tokyo and the people receive their dues.
strings.GNG_of_excellence_effect_tt: We will adopt Morita Akio's vision of the future of our economy, and propose a bill in the£GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council to this effect.
strings.GNG_a_helping_hand_from_the_government_d:
There can be no room for error or wasted time if Chief Executive Morita is to guide Guangdong successfully into the breakneck economic growth needed to accomplish his vision. Guangdong must always be two steps ahead of the world at large - to see the needs of the public, to know what the people want intuitively before they even know they need it.

As an electronics pioneer in his own right, Morita is adamant that the government will direct privileged access to capital and funding behind those firms that are best positioned to shape the future. Importantly, Zhujin - and Chinese - entrepreneurs will be considered as potential recipients for government support. Doing otherwise would be an unjustifiable waste of the enormous reservoir of talent at Guangdong's disposal.
strings.GNG_encouraging_horizontal_integration_d:
A perennial problem encountered by Sony and Cheung Kong in their early years was the problem of scale - to find ways to compete against the financial and industrial resources of the Japanese behemoths in the playground. While the relative underdevelopment of Guangdong - and the support of the Zhujin and Chinese community - helped Morita and Li through the tumultuous 50s, the game has changed in the decade since.

For the Zhujin and Chinese businesses to have any shot at repeating the meteoric rise of Sony and Cheung Kong, they will need to grow rapidly - to integrate horizontally. In doing so, Morita hopes to steer the creation of local conglomerates under Sony's guidance, with the depth of financial and human resources to meet their Japanese competition head-on.
strings.GNG_the_new_face_of_pan_asian_industry_d:
If the Japanese led the way in creating industrial behemoths that are the economic light of Asia, then Guangdong will prove that this model is by no means unique to Japan - that the peoples of Asia, with adequate access to capital, government guidance, and economies of scale, are more than capable of ascending to the commanding heights of Asian industry.

As Sony wills it, so shall it be!
strings.GNG_the_new_face_of_pan_asian_industry_t: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong stands for productivity first, solidarity second.
strings.GNG_of_stability_desc:
While Guangdong has longstanding obligations to its shareholders and to the corporations that comprise the inner circle of its government, the fragility of its wholesale commitment to profits was laid bare by the Yasuda Crisis. Both Morita Akio and Li Ka-shing had questioned the status quo as the vanguard of a new line of thinking - of prioritizing the interests of the employees (and now, the residents) of Guangdong at equal level as those of the boardroom.

Now that they occupy the heights of power in Guangdong, Li is keen to put their new theory of paternalistic capitalism into action - even if that means accepting slower growth in the name of social stability.
strings.GNG_of_stability_effect_tt: We will adopt Li Ka-shing's vision of the future of our economy, and propose a bill in the£GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council to this effect.
strings.GNG_a_mutual_partnership_desc:
The reality is that Guangdong's economy is buttressed by a vast array of small-to-medium sized businesses, often run by Zhujin entrepreneurs alongside smaller Japanese subcontractors. Cheung Kong was no different in the 1950's - only that its alliance with a similarly-sized Sony, and good fortune, helped propel the two to prominence by 1962.

Li aims to replicate Cheung Kong's success by replicating its alliance with Sony in a multitude of industrial sectors, creating corporate alliances that allow resource sharing and amplifying negotiating power against the larger Japanese conglomerates. While this loose arrangement of alliances will cause redundancies and inefficient distribution of capital in the economy, Li hopes that this initiative - with Cheung Kong's financial help - will open the door for more Zhujin and Chinese businessmen to build their fortunes.
strings.GNG_unfettered_access_to_financial_capit:
If money is the lifeblood of a modern economy, then it stands to reason that the only way to ensure that businesses thrive is to make sure they have the seed capital to get off the ground. For Li's vision of the new Guangdong economy to succeed, we have to ensure that the local businesses that have led a hand-to-mouth existence to date have the funds needed to begin expanding.

And where the Japanese financial houses see Zhujin or Chinese businesses as 'too risky' to lend to, Morita and Li will step in - through specialised government financial institutions and calling on the leading lights of the Zhujin community to enter the financial industry.

With some assurances, we can convince everyone - save the major Japanese banks - that there's an opportunity here for everyone.
strings.GNG_a_stable_economy_for_a_stable_nation:
Future generations must know that Guangdong turns a corner today - turning away from the monopolization of profit by those companies with means, to providing the means of opportunity to those with ambition. The new Guangdong will derive its economic vitality from the diversity of its industrial structure - regardless of ethnic background.

Some would call Li's vision irrational, sacrificing efficient organization out of sentimentality. They do not realize that Li and Morita would happily trade efficiency for stability, if the cost is simply one of ensuring greater access to opportunity to as many as are willing to seize it. It's simply good business.
£GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong stands for solidarity first. Productivity is important - but not all-important.
strings.GNG_the_industrial_organization_ordinanc:
The programs established by Chief Executive Morita and Li Ka-shing have had a limited effect on restructuring Guangdong's competitive landscape their own, but for them to truly have an impact in Guangdong, we must secure backing to roll out these programs in a formal capacity across Guangdong within the Legislative Council.

There surely are ways of designing the future of Guangdong's economic framework in a way that gains political support, to show that these changes are not as threatening to the Five Companies as they might otherwise fear... but can we convince them, and if we do, would we be working against our own goals?
strings.GNG_the_land_we_stand_on_desc: The foundation of Guangdong's electronics economy lies in the land - in its resources, its people, and the networks that link them both together. But the usage and development of this land - and the treatment of the people who live here - has been done too haphazardly over the decades, without thought for sustainability or justice. That must change.
strings.GNG_the_land_we_stand_on_tt: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong sits on a wealth of natural resources, which have been haphazardly and hazardously developed in the past, at great cost to local residents. We will be different.
strings.GNG_guangdong_untapped_potential_desc:
Guangdong sits on a treasure trove of untapped mineral wealth - rare earths and minerals that can easily be extracted and processed into the wafers and transistors that are the lifeblood of the economy of tomorrow. Yet the pressing question of how to treat the Chinese villages and townships that often sit atop these vital resource deposits has never been answered in any satisfactory fashion by our predecessors - and all too often at the expense of the local residents, who have been uprooted at gunpoint to settle in the Three Pearls.

For Guangdong's future, both economic and political, we have to get this right.
strings.GNG_guangdong_untapped_potential_effect_: We must decide how best to employ those people who live on top of resources we require...
strings.GNG_offer_employment_desc:
Li Ka-shing's answer to the land usage issue is simple - get the people who live on the land, to work the land. We will solve the longstanding issue of land evictions and forced relocations by not relocating anybody, and pay them for working the land that we need to make use of.

Our engineers are not exactly fans of the idea - construction, excavation, and processing work have advanced well beyond the point you can tell any person on the street to grab a pickaxe and get to work - but Li reckons that the people are willing to learn, if it means keeping their lands.
strings.GNG_resettlement_packages_desc:
As tragic as it is, we simply cannot leave the specialized work of land development, resource extraction, and metals refining to amateurs - we will need to bring in specialists to do the work at the quality we require, without the locals nearby to pose a distraction.

The transition does not need to be needlessly painful. Morita knows he will be asking the people to sacrifice their homes for the name of economic development; we must ensure they are compensated appropriately for their loss, and given the help they need to settle into their new lives in the cities without being harassed, cheated, or robbed.
strings.GNG_the_rural_development_ordinance_desc: We have taken the initiative to present a new way to develop the rural regions of Guangdong in a manner that we believe is both humane and efficient - now we have to make sure that everyone else is held to the same standard we are. We will approach the Legislative Council with a bill codifying best practices in rural resource development projects, and seek the agreement of the other corporations in the interests of Guangdong's long-term stability.
strings.GNG_constructing_the_arteries_desc: The arteries of modern commerce is infrastructure - roads, rail, and the electricity needed to harness all the energies of the people and the land to maximum economic efficiency. Despite a high level of development being restored in the cities via Japanese aid after the war, much of the countryside remains ill-served by modern infrastructure - an easy criticism and source of resentment against the Guangdong government. This must change if Guangdong is to become all that Morita and Li want it to become.
strings.GNG_constructing_the_arteries_effect_too: The foundations of growth are in infrastructure, and we must lay them well.
strings.GNG_efficient_transport_infrastructure_d:
Morita has watched endless debates over piecemeal road and rail projects that do little more than connect each corporation's pet projects together on the map. The benefits delivered by the whole package of an efficiently designed transportation network - roads, bridges, railways, and waterways - is far more than those of its individual parts.

As the centerpiece of this new network, Morita will construct a new international airport in Shinsen - an undeveloped region located between the Three Pearls - with more than enough passenger and cargo capacity to keep Guangdong open for business and wow investors for decades to come.
strings.GNG_electrifying_guangdong_desc:
Li knows firsthand the drawbacks and perils of a life without electricity - fumbling in the dying light for a dropped tool next to an activated metal lathe, or settling the account books to the light of a flickering oil lamp. Without electricity, a human cannot work or relax to the full extent that modern civilization makes possible.

Mammoth power plants, hydroelectric dams, transmission networks, and power lines stretching across the countryside - these are the symbols of modernity! If Guangdong is to advance into the future, we cannot leave our people behind in darkness.
strings.GNG_the_public_works_and_infrastructure_: The Chief Executive can only greenlight so many projects on the margins of the annual budget debated in the Legislative Council. Infrastructure projects and public works are measured in years to completion, not months, and if any of our most ambitious plans for Guangdong are to be realized in full, we will need to ask the Legislative Council to authorize multi-year development plans. That way, even if Morita and Li should fall from grace, their successors will still be required to work within the development blueprint left behind - a valuable form of institutional memory.
strings.GNG_remaking_human_geography_desc: Much of Guangdong's populace remains in rural villages and towns, over land of no material value, living with minimal interference from the Guangdong government - except when the Kenpeitai conduct one of their infamous sweeps of the countryside. Unsurprisingly, these villages and townships do not contribute to Guangdong's economy or government revenue - and worse, serve as hubs for dissident activity. For the sake of economic advancement - and just for knowing what's going on in our territory - the government must find a way to incorporate these settlements into Morita's new society.
strings.GNG_remaking_human_geography_effect_tool: Even where no resources exist, we must do something with the people.
strings.GNG_incorporate_the_villages_desc: Li's approach to the issue of unincorporated townships is simple - simply incorporate them by fiat of the government! We will dispatch a contingent of census takers and bureaucrats - escorted by the police, not the Kenpeitai - to these villages and take inventory. By the time we are done, we will know who lives there, who is in charge, and - most importantly - we will have reminded the villages of their obligations to the government. If they begin doing the work that Guangdong requests of them - to host factories, provide police, collect tax - then the state can begin providing services to them to improve the lives of their people.
strings.GNG_new_industrial_communities_desc: Morita's preferred approach to the unincorporated villages and townships is a bit more imaginative - find ways to make them more useful than they are otherwise. If these townships were unrecorded and not in usable or valuable areas before, the government could propose to relocate willing townships, or a portion of their residents therein, closer to key resource or factory zones along the Pearl River - at the state's expense. If they agree - and we emphasize, unlike our predecessors, their consent - they'll have jobs, electricity, and modern civilization, all in a new community of their own. Surely, it's not such a bad deal?
strings.GNG_the_industrial_development_ordinance: We must codify our new approach to the unincorporated villages and towns into Guangdong's laws, so that we don't face an avalanche of criticism from the other corporations - like so many vultures circling their next source of disposable bodies for their sweltering factories. By passing our approach into law through the Legislative Council, we can hopefully end the practice of undocumented 'evictions' and wholescale 'relocations' of entire villages - and the periodic cleanup required - while still ensuring that we maximize the use of our labor force in the name of industrial development.
strings.GNG_investing_in_our_future_desc:
As our industries come up to full speed with the willing contribution of the people, and as our corporations reap the profits - in spite of the new restrictions they face - we now face the question of what Guangdong should do with its profits. How shall we make use of the fruits of our labor today to ensure continued prosperity tomorrow?

There are a number of proposals on the table on how best to reinvest our wealth to ensure that the flow of riches never stops...
strings.GNG_investing_in_our_future_effect_toolt: You need money to make money, or so they say. How best should we prepare for £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's future?
strings.GNG_debt_taxes_desc:
To keep Guangdong at the cutting edge of the rapid changes in information technology, continued investments in research, industrial machinery, and human capital will be required - potentially at scales dwarfing anything we have done to date.

In order to pursue these activities, the government will bank on its record of good stewardship to push investors to recognize that Guangdong's future will need to be funded somehow - either through accepting increased taxes, or acknowledging a certain level of government debt that we pledge to honor. We can only hope that our promises of good governance are enough not to spook stability-seeking investors, both in Guangdong and in Tokyo.
strings.GNG_debt_taxes_effect_tooltip: To spend money we must raise money - from those who have the means to pay. This may be controversial, for little benefit if we fail. Think carefully about our next choices...
strings.GNG_the_public_finance_ordinance_desc:
Even as we put our proposal before investors, we have to remember that Guangdong has not been mandated to run recurring government debts - investors have historically demanded Guangdong run surpluses and to erase its debts when possible, so that the corporations don't have to foot the bill for ruinous government spending.

But it is equally true that, in order to prepare for the future, companies must sometimes go into debt. Why should Guangdong be any different? It's time the Legislative Council saw things our way.
strings.GNG_the_guangdong_future_fund_desc:
The proper way to use our accrued fiscal surpluses is to put them to use in the markets, growing a 'rainy day' fund for when the economic cycle inevitably turns against us. We will create an asset management fund with the express mandate of managing and growing our accumulated surpluses so that emergency funds can be available to the government when needed, subject to the oversight of the Legislative Council.

This concept - a sovereign wealth fund - might rankle some of the corporates the wrong way, as it gives the government an independent source of financial power that they cannot directly control - but it is conceptually sound and unlikely to impose any incremental burden to them, either.
strings.GNG_the_guangdong_future_fund_effect_too: We must grow our financial resources, so that we may have plenty in a future time of need.
strings.GNG_an_investment_in_its_people_desc: Given that the government has some discretion to do what it wants with the money in the Future Fund, we choose to invest in the people of Guangdong - to improve the lives of the populace through means-tested, return-generating programs that will ensure Guangdong is prepared for the challenges of tomorrow. To improve the lives of the people is to lay the foundations for a stronger, more resilient workforce in the future - and to address the desperation and poverty that so often draws them to radicalism.
strings.GNG_our_corporate_benefactors_desc:
Guangdong remains a state where the major corporations control the levers of economic power, much as we have tried to expand the role of the state in the lives of the people. To ask something that would dilute the power of the corporations in financial matters by creating an independent source of wealth - or credit - to the government would face stiff opposition.

Though it would necessarily be of a smaller scale than anything we would hope for, we could curry favor with the corporates and their delegates in the Legislative Council by giving them a larger role to play in the future of Guangdong and the economy - to lend their wallets, as it were, for the benefit of future generations.
strings.GNG_our_corporate_benefactors_tooltip: Those with the means should be reminded of their obligations to the public...
strings.GNG_through_soup_kitchens_and_schools_de:
Even if the corporates sit in the driver's seat on what goes into any financial contributions for Guangdong's future, the state has its own way of ensuring a quid pro quo is in effect.

In order for the corporations' contributions to at least look as generous as they are being marketed as, we will require a portion of the corporate contributions to any future development fund will be devoted to improving the lives of our citizens - to demonstrate a common bond between corporation and citizen.
strings.GNG_an_economy_of_opportunity_desc:
The sun rises on the new Guangdong economy - one where success is not measured by your fortune of being Japanese or wealthy Zhujin, but defined by how one takes advantage of the opportunities afforded to them, regardless of ethnic origin.

Guangdong is open for business, for one and for all, and Morita and Li wouldn't have it any other way - especially, they would add, when they have profited handsomely from the whole affair.
strings.GNG_an_economy_of_opportunity_effect_too: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong used to work for the £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese. Now £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong works for its native sons - with £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong at their head.
strings.GNG_reformed_security_desc:
So goes an old joke run 'round the pubs at Central: “A man at work with ten yen must pay the Three Tithes before he comes back home: three to the Shirokiya Hotel, three to the Kenpeitai, and three to the Commissioner of Police. By dinnertime all our poor hero has left for his house and lady is half a yen.”

“What about the other half?” one would then ask. “Why,” the other would reply, “to the lady mistress in Wan Chai of course.”

“Then why are there Three Tithes and not Four?”

“Because half a yen's no tithe in Wan Chai; it's a dowry!”

Everyone laughs because it is true, but that doesn't mean it should remain so.
strings.GNG_reformed_security_effect_tooltip: Corruption, police weakness, crime, and vice. All must be addressed head-on, so that £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong may wake up to a more secure future.
strings.GNG_rooting_out_corruption_desc:
Corruption in Guangdong isn't detested or reviled so much as it is accepted as an immutable fact of life, like loan sharks, opium addicts, and the stench of piss behind Causeway Bay Depot. It melts into the drab-grey concrete and infuses itself rebar-deep, always part of the background but never the facade itself - except perhaps in price tags with extra zeroes, and gentlemen in tacky suits with an open palm on one hand and a gun in the other. The Commissioner can talk all he want, but as long as the boys in blue talk shop with gangsters in broad daylight 1 Arsenal Street's talk is just that: talk.

To its credit, hard-boiled cynicism was what kept Guangdong alive since 1945. But for the Three Pearls to thrive within his lifetime, the Chief Executive knows it must make do without. Somehow.
strings.GNG_rooting_out_corruption_tt: We will attempt to excise £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon corruption from £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong as best we can...
strings.GNG_into_the_ranks_desc:
The first thing that separated the Guangdong Police Force from the Triads, they said, was that the citizenry paid taxes so the former can rob them out of house and home. Second was that they wore blue khaki shorts; Stanley Ho's boys dressed themselves smarter, see.

Under Sony's spanking-new management however, Commissioner Ōmori will have to decide if the “bonuses” his men skim off LegCo's coffers is worth the people's (lack of) trust. And maybe get rid of the stupid shorts while he's at it.
strings.GNG_a_hotline_for_petty_corruption_desc:
The uphill battle Chief Executive Morita faces in his anti-corruption drive stems in large part from the people's effort themselves - or rather, its absence. They're no ignorant sheep; they've seen the faces in Government House come and go. Yet they've seen nothing out of the promises LegCo bandies out either, so why bother putting any work themselves? It is a prophecy that fulfills itself seemingly from government to government.

Enter his novel solution: 25-266-366. Dial on your phones and report the dodgy clerk from Central to Morita himself. Maybe it won't make a dent on the more clandestine networks the Yakuza fall back on - but it will assure your jaded officeman that he had made a difference, no matter how minor.
strings.GNG_audit_senior_officers_desc:
“A KHK journalist was writing a fluff piece on how Honkon transformed after being liberated from the imperialist British. For this she interviewed an old man in Diamond Hill. After some sumai and lemon tea she asked, 'Da ren, what was life like in Honkon before the Civil Authority?'

'Back then things were nice and simple,' said the man as he chewed on a toothpick. 'We paid taxes to Government House and kept the streets clean. The gwailou paid no taxes and left their horseshit on the sidewalk.'

'Then has anything changed when Japan drove the British out of Honkon?'

'Certainly; now we pay the riben so they can sell us their horseshit!'”

As the saying goes: the more things change, the more they stay the same. Chief Executive Morita plans to prohibit such double standards within the government's upper echelons by bringing their financial records under close scrutiny, though it will undoubtedly invite the ire of their friends in the Home Islands.
strings.GNG_adjust_incentives_desc:
Punishing the corrupt has ever been popular among the people, else Morita wouldn't have campaigned so hard for it. More than proving that justice is still alive in Guangdong, public displays of contrition from men of ill-gotten wealth satisfies their supposed lessers on a visceral level. Retribution only deters men from error however; the desires which lead them to it will still remain. For their part, our public servants desire financial security in a city with more expenses than anywhere else.

As such, the Chief Executive believes a review of the Civil Authority's pay scales is long overdue. For the sated wallet is less inclined to seek dirty money - and a lot of wallets will leave Government House sated once the review concludes.
strings.GNG_reward_workforce_dedication_desc:
“A man from North Point composed a letter to his parents in the city outskirts, asking for financial aid. He appealed, 'Baba, life in Shenzhen is terrible. I leave home at six in the morning and come back at ten in the evening; I clean messes people leave behind; and I get paid trinkets for honest work while Boss smokes opium and pockets bribes in his office.'

After paying the mailman's tea money, he cut open the brown envelope containing their reply. Out spilled bank notes worth several thousand yen and a letter. Flipping it open he read, 'Get a better job; we didn't raise a street sweeper!'

'Baba,' he wrote in his own response later that month, 'I'm a clerk in Government House. At least they pay street sweepers pensions!'”

Our civil servants, overworked and underpaid, and so jaded they make punchlines out of themselves in private. Is it any wonder they become inside men for corporations willing to pay their rent? This must change, says the Chief Executive.
strings.GNG_extend_senior_bonuses_desc:
It is the sort of counterintuitive logic that would make the Chief Executive's more zealous allies balk out of both principle and thrift: let the senior executives pocket more of the government's money, and they might not pocket the Companies' in exchange for favors. Many expect little change from men with long histories of scandal and grift.

Morita thinks otherwise. Loyalty is the pulse that drives Guangdong; money stimulates it like jolts of electricity. Carefully applied money, in conjunction with punishments unto the worst examples, will signal to the government's privileged that their employer desires their loyalty more than Matsushita, Hitachi or... Fujitsu.
strings.GNG_an_independent_commission_desc:
To borrow an old saying, men will want to make a quick yen for far longer than other men will resist it. And Sony's continued preeminence in the Legislation Council is by no means a certainty; disaster may strike the Chief Executive, or other circumstances may align so he leaves the office earlier than his due. As his crusade screeches to a halt, man's persistence will nip at its edges, render it impotent through a thousand cuts, until Morita's successor dismantles it entirely.

Men independent of the Chief Executive's decree are not so vulnerable. In fact a commission mandated to investigate government corruption will perpetuate themselves in a place so rife with it as Guangdong. There they will spot the grime in cracks neither Morita nor Li can spot, part misdoers from their money without the Chief Executive ever lifting a finger. When feared by many and answerable to none, an Independent Commission is the most resilient weapon the government will ever have against human nature.

Which begs one question: do dogs ever bite the hand that feeds them?
strings.GNG_an_independent_commission_effect_too:
Tactical measures aren't enough to root out £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon corruption on a prolonged basis. We must take some action to institutionalize anti-corruption measures in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong.
The vote will be held soon after this foci is taken. Ensure that we have enough support in the£GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council, or suffer the consequences...
strings.GNG_a_night_with_stanley_ho_desc:
While the Triads have a well-deserved reputation for criminality and brutality, Morita and Li have pinned their hopes on bringing the underworld of Guangdong to heel via their longtime acquaintance - Stanley Ho, the Macanese smuggler, industrialist, and 'fixer' with ties of his own to the Triads.

While Stanley woos the hearts and courts the checkbooks of Guangdong's Japanese elite in Macau, he squares off against his rival, the Japanese vulture capitalist Yokoi Hideki, in a war in the shadows of Guangdong. Beneath the watch of the Guangdong police, Stanley and Yokoi fight a merciless battle where lives are cheap, money is king, and everything is at stake.

If we were to help Stanley win and go 'legitimate', we would have a powerful ally in maintaining control over Guangdong. Stanley has just such a proposal - an exclusive contract for gambling rights within his home territory of Macau, to make it a shining light of 'tourism' in the Sphere. But the Yakuza will surely not go quietly...
strings.GNG_a_night_with_stanley_ho_tt: Instead of browbeating the underworld into submission, we may be able to use the £GNG_triads_texticon Triads to our advantage - and Stanley Ho has a plan by which we might do just that...
strings.GNG_replace_yakuza_bonus_decisions_with_: Replaces our bonus £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza decisions with bonus £GNG_triads_texticon Triad decisions.
strings.GNG_has_not_confronted_hideki_yet_tt: Has not confronted Yokoi Hideki yet.
strings.GNG_tolerate_some_vices_desc:
No matter how much we try, crime and vice will never truly be eradicated - the question is simply controlling it, and making sure that the consequences do not infect society at large.

The businesses and 'leisure' facilitated by Stanley Ho's contacts are not unique - but he does promise a means to make sure that they don't spiral out of control, or begin to work against our interests. Opium dens and Yakuza-affiliated loan sharks will be outed so long as we turn a blind eye to the soaplands, topless bars, and 'other establishments' in the Three Pearls.

Better the devil we know, after all...
strings.GNG_raid_the_yakuza_warehouses_desc:
The other element of Guangdong's underworld - the Yakuza, and their own 'respectable' representative, Yokoi Hideki - are firmly in the pocket of the seedier parts of the Japanese expatriate population in Guangdong, and are not at all amenable to what we propose as the future of Guangdong.

Thankfully, we can give Stanley Ho - and his Triad contacts - a leg up in their war in the shadows by tipping the scales of law and order against the Yakuza's businesses and warehouses along the Pearl River. We will not stand idly by and allow the Yakuza's siren song of drugs and easy money enthrall Guangdong - not while we have something to say about it.
strings.GNG_wave_the_trucks_through_desc:
Stanley Ho's primary business is 'trading' - including in illicit goods, sourced from Japan and moved over the border into China, or purchased in China and imported back into Guangdong at marked-up prices. Beyond moving 'goods', the practice services as an easy way for Stanley and his associates to launder their proceeds from other activities via 'generous' invoices between associated businesses.

To the extent that the goods being smuggled will not actively be turned against the Chief Executive, the government, or the people, we have reached an understanding with the Triads. Apart from some truly dangerous controlled substances - weapons, opium, or other narcotics - we will give Stanley Ho's trucks more lenient checks, so that he may build his warchest for cornering the underworld.
strings.GNG_audit_the_shell_companies_desc:
In recent years - and in line with Yokoi Hideki's own background as a quasi-legitimate industrialist and financier - the Yakuza have begun to diversify their operations, engaging in money laundering and white-collar fraud through a network of shell companies and financing bodies that operate within Guangdong's freewheeling economy.

While we remain dedicated to the principles of competitive capitalism, we are not so accommodative of criminality masquerading as capitalism, and we will tighten the noose around these conduits of misconduct.
strings.GNG_confront_yokoi_hideki_desc:
For Stanley Ho to decisively seize control of the underworld, we will need to eliminate or otherwise isolate his nemesis in the Japanese underworld - Yokoi Hideki, the vulture capitalist and 'fixer' for the Yakuza. We can only pray that we have strengthened Stanley's associates - and weakened Yokoi's - enough that our attempt to box Yokoi in for good will not be disrupted.

It's time to call in Yokoi for a little 'conversation'...
strings.GNG_confront_yokoi_hideki_effect_tooltip: Let's hope we've done enough to weaken Yokoi and his £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza friends before we call him in...
strings.GNG_the_casino_license_desc:
Even as we have worked to influence the war between Stanley Ho and Yokoi Hideki behind the scenes, the Legislative Council has been drawing up plans for establishing and auctioning off the rights to operate all legitimate gambling activity in Guangdong.

It will be one of the most lucrative business contracts tendered in Guangdong's history, and now the long-awaited day to bid for the casino contract has arrived.

Going once, going twice...
strings.GNG_has_dealt_with_yokoi_hideki_tt: We have met up with Yokoi Hideki.
strings.GNG_casino_license_needs_to_be_prepared_: Our meeting with Yokoi Hideki will determine the future of the Makao casino license.
strings.GNG_professionalize_the_police_desc:
“They say in Guangdong you have three people to turn to when your neighbor's making a ruckus. The first is the Kenpeitai, who will charge an unwashed Chinese an arm and a leg for breaking the public peace.

The second is your loan shark, who will charge you an arm and a leg so he'll send his goons to break your neighbor's.

If you have neither Kenpeitai nor loan sharks, only then will you call the Police Force. Because a cop will charge your arm and leg so he'll visit your neighbor, then charge him his arm and leg so he'll do nothing and leave!”

Jokes aren't made out of the police's expense for no good reason - and what good is a force they say is used only as a useless last resort? Trust between the uniform and the people it's sworn to protect must be established before the Kenpeitai get too accustomed to enforcing Guangdong's laws as they interpret it.
strings.GNG_professionalize_the_police_effect_to: The Guangdong Police Force must be brought up to standard, or the £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese will forever have an excuse to interfere in our affairs.
strings.GNG_new_rules_of_engagement_desc:
Cops patrol the streets in ones and not in twos because past experience taught them that shakedowns are easier without a second witness. Cops detain people longer than legal because the sergeant said it's the best way to get what they want to hear. Much of the petty corruption within the Guangdong Police Force is embedded into its procedures and precedents like so, hence why you'll barely get more than a helpless shrug when you ask an officer why they keep “misplacing” evidence, why they keep beating helpless suspects up - because to them, “It's how it's always been, and it's always paid the bills.”

Change their protocols - mandate two brothers per beat, define strict limits on use of force, enforce appropriate custody durations for every felony, offense and misdemeanor - and corruption in the ranks will plummet. Not completely, but appreciably.
strings.GNG_police_boxes_desc:
A man is shot in Tin Chiu Street in broad daylight. Crowds scatter and scream as the victim dies atop a pool of his own blood. Police arrive an hour later, spend half that hunting for the suspect, then head back to the precinct for drinks: cold beer for a cold case. Days later the superintendent lambasts reporters in a press conference for suggesting that the men in uniform are anything but diligent.

Guangdong's jaded citizenry have personally seen this song and dance at least once in their lives. Small wonder why they expect the worst from their tax money at work. We can bring confidence to them by bringing their beat cops from air-conditioned offices to small outposts closer to crime scenes within their bailiwick.
strings.GNG_language_training_desc:
As has been observed in multilingual societies throughout history, the people who matter speak one language while the people who... matter slightly less, speak another. Complications arise when both comprise their law enforcement agencies. Such divide has caused officer and civilian both tragedy and grief in Guangdong; more than one plea for help was left unheeded because the officer on duty understood no Cantonese, and native policemen were often dispatched to the wrong locations because their orders were written and told in Japanese.

To remedy the divide, Chief Executive Morita has authorized extensive bilingual training programs for all policemen regardless of rank. The usual suspects hem and haw over its costs; as usual, Sony's CEO tunes them out.
strings.GNG_do_small_things_right_desc:
Men often compare their achievements to mountain peaks: tall, ginormous and distant, nevertheless conquered. The Chief Executive sees in the Police Force a bottomless pit, dug over the course of decades. Until the more high-profile crimes are convicted, all he has to make a mountain of are fluff pieces - stolen goods returned to their owners, schoolchildren reunited with their parents, lost pets rescued to the local pound. Pebbles snuck as far back as page 14 of the South China Morning Post.

As the saying goes: it takes ten years to establish a reputation and ten seconds to ruin it. In ten years Guangdong's law enforcement will have either built a mountain out of pebbles or remained stuck in its own pit. There's no harm in trying either way.
strings.GNG_the_organized_crime_bureau_desc:
A popular joke among the cadets in 18 Ocean Park goes like this: “Guangdong is the sterling example of pan-Asian harmony. Every man of every race lives and does in accordance with the other - the Yakuza pretend their opium is medicine, the Triads pretend their migrants are legal, the businessmen pretend their money is clean, and we pretend to arrest them all!”

Even if bringing them to task were popular, however, the Guangdong Police Force is ill-equipped to do so. Curtailing organized crime requires a certain acumen and experience - and both had been steadily weeded out from the ranks ever since their refashionment into the Kenpeitai's glorified auxiliaries.

Change in this regard begins by bringing certain retirees back into the Force: those promising once-recruits dismissed or sidelined after burrowing their noses “where they shouldn't”. With them the new Commissioner promises a reckoning for the high-class misfits Guangdong's lowly underbelly.
strings.GNG_demand_jurisdiction_from_the_kenpeit:
After seeing the old colonial police and found wanting, the Kenpeitai had shouldered the final authority over Guangdong's laws since its founding. For the time being, they reassured, until its reorganized officers are deemed fit to exercise their responsibilities on their own.

These twenty years have proved that nothing is more permanent than temporary measures - and with the GPF's disappointing state, not everyone begrudged our overstayed guests either. Such opinions have begun changing since LegCo introduced its motley reforms. When before the Kenpeitai were grudgingly seen doing what the Police clearly could not, now they are becoming cold, aloof, out-of-touch foreigners intruding unfairly into our own detectives' work.

Perhaps now's the time to exchange pleasantries with Colonel Miyazaki. Even a rock like him will budge with enough push.

We will demand Colonel Miyazaki withdraw the £GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai to their barracks and let the £GNG_police_texticon GPF be the main security organ of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong. He will, of course, demand proof that the £GNG_police_texticon GPF is ready to take over their responsibilities...
strings.GNG_has_not_demanded_jurisdiction_from_k: Has not demanded jurisdiction fron the £GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai.
strings.GNG_the_public_order_ordinance_desc:
We have illuminated the path forward for public safety in Guangdong, with new practices and procedures instituted in the Guangdong Police Force and our new modus vivendi with the Kenpeitai. But in case anyone wasn't fully aware and compliant with the new face of law enforcement in Guangdong, we must formally legislate our program into law.

We must know whether the assembled corporations of Guangdong will stand with the future and the rule of law, or stand defiantly on the side of bending laws?
strings.GNG_a_clean_start_desc:
Our civil servants work for the people. The police protect them in the sun; and we can only hope that Stanley Ho's associates will protect them in the dark.

While we must preserve some freedom of action for ourselves - and the power games and boardroom politics surrounding the Chief Executive's office will never truly disappear - we have built a security apparatus in Guangdong that we can trust will fulfill its public duties long after we are gone.
strings.GNG_a_clean_start_effect_tooltip: We have torn down the old, and started anew. Only time will tell if this was enough to make a meaningful impact on £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's security situation...
strings.GNG_capitalism_with_a_human_face_desc:
We are bystanders to a culture of unchecked corporate predation and exploitation, which treats its employees as disposable as a ballpoint pen or a scrap of paper. The social ills caused by this culture are as starkly visible as the nets stretched out from the factory rooftops, a mesh of fibers and struts cutting into the sky.

For all of his faults, Suzuki Teiichi was not wrong in his assessment that this state of affairs would cause problems: Guangdong's capitalist model, in its current form, generates far too much resentment to be sustainable. But where Suzuki saw the problem through the lens of ensuring a docile populace, we aim for something more.

Let it be known that Chief Executive Morita and Li Ka-shing believe in capitalism with a human face. We believe in this not just because it is a more ethical way of doing business - but also because only through the power of the state can we compel our competition to do the right thing without crippling ourselves.
strings.GNG_capitalism_with_a_human_face_effect_: For people to begin developing a sense of loyalty to £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong beyond their paycheck, it would help as a first step by not working them to early graves...
strings.GNG_the_malaises_of_today_desc:
The social ills afflicting Guangdong's populace are impossible to ignore: widespread poverty, rampant workplace deaths, suicide nets, all amidst a haze of industrial smog and smoke that increasingly poisons the air we breathe.

The most visible sign of our commitment to make Guangdong something more than a factory line with disposable people, to make good on our promise to do better, we must take action on the malaises of today.
strings.GNG_the_malaises_of_today_effect_tooltip: Dignity in work and health in life - these are the two most pressing concerns that we can take action to address, today.
strings.GNG_the_meaning_of_work_desc:
To live in Guangdong is to work - and it is a bleak existence for those who toil on the factory floors or in the masses of office cubicles in the name of the corporations. The corporations demand the clerks work past midnight for no recompense, while children work alongside the elderly in triple shifts on cluttered factory floors.

Even the sympathetic Zhujin and Japanese - what few exist - can do little for the Chinese underclass, for fear of being undercut by their more cutthroat competitors. While Sony and Cheung Kong have done their level best to try to present a better deal for their Chinese and Zhujin blue-collar workers, the competitive realities of Guangdong simply made altruism a losing proposition in the face of the Zaibatsu. But now, with Morita and Li in the driver's seat, we can force everyone onto the same playing field.
strings.GNG_buying_dignity_desc:
How do you reward someone who gives their body, time, and freedom to their job? Li Ka-shing believes that the answer is simple: pay them more. To give people the recognition for their labor, and in doing so, to give them the first means to their self-emancipation.

Li acknowledges that his meteoric rise in Guangdong's corporate politics, clawing his way out of poverty, was the product of sharing in the profits eked out by his partnership with Morita. Even if the majority of workers will never become capitalists themselves, it's not unreasonable to ensure that the masses are able to live off of the labor they provide - to clothe themselves in the dignity of work.
strings.GNG_the_question_of_work_hours_desc:
During normal times in Guangdong's factories, laborers work ten hour shifts across two shifts; in busy periods, people work eight hour shifts across three shifts. Without breaks.

In our offices, workers are effectively on call at all hours, holding back from returning home for fear of earning the ire of their manager after a missed call.

It's clear that this is exhausting, contributing both to worker dissatisfaction and to greater workplace accident rates - neither of which do anything for productivity. We will introduce the novel concept of taking breaks and limiting work hours to allow both machines and people to rest and recuperate.
strings.GNG_the_minimum_wage_question_desc:
While Suzuki's attempt to improve working conditions via the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance was commendable, extreme poverty remains a fact of life for countless thousands across Guangdong despite their laborious toil. The simple fact of life is that wages are far beneath the rising cost of living and basic necessities in Guangdong's expanding cities, while dwindling opportunities in the rural areas - that aren't linked to the closed economies of corporate towns or mining settlements - consign thousands to mere subsistence.

Both for the people's sake - and for leveling the playing field among the corporations in terms of cost - we will formally propose and institute a minimum wage in Guangdong, enough so that the survival of the masses is no longer in doubt, if not a good life.
strings.GNG_disability_insurance_desc:
With the rate of workplace accidents in Guangdong, all it takes is one stroke of misfortune to wipe out one's savings and condemn them to a life of poverty on the streets. The disabled eke out a truly wretched existence as beggars on the streets of the Three Pearls, their knees and foreheads bloodied from scraping asphalt, groveling for change from an increasingly desensitized populace.

For our workers' sake, and as a business opportunity, we should encourage the sale of disability insurance contracts in factories and workplaces across Guangdong. An accident need not spell the end of a person's life - for while even a maimed man may provide value, a dead man provides none.
strings.GNG_safety_first_desc:
Morita believes it is far more reasonable to assume that the dissatisfaction of the Chinese and Zhujin workers in Guangdong stems from the mortal danger they face on a daily basis. Our workplaces more often resemble houses of horror, where unsecured equipment and 'space economization' mean that a simple misstep or a freak accident result in death or crippling injury.

By drafting and instituting basic safety restrictions, we can credibly claim to be improving the lot of workers to the standard Sony and Cheung Kong aim to provide, while forcing our competitors to be held accountable to the same level. We can claim the rationale of improving productivity and an obligation to provide for workers' safety against our detractors - for surely they must recognize that they would benefit from the continued survival of a skilled workforce.
strings.GNG_overhauling_the_building_code_desc:
The haphazard, uncoordinated state of construction and urban planning across much of Guangdong and the Three Pearls has left our factories and residential neighborhoods a literal tinderbox, an architectural nightmare prone to total and catastrophic failure in adverse conditions.

Improved ventilation, fire escapes, flame-resistant materials, proper concrete - addressing even some of these would make workplaces and tenements much safer, giving some much needed reassurance to the Chinese and Zhujin who toil without knowing if an errant spark or rusty rivet will be the death of them.

And we might be able to take some of the renovation work ourselves...
strings.GNG_a_standard_for_workers_safety_desc:
Even if Sony and Cheung Kong take pains to ensure that their offices and factories are not literal deathtraps for their employees, the lack of a standardized safety and workplace environment standard for laborers and office workers alike means that the other corporations have all the leeway they need to treat their employees as disposable cogs and not humans.

And Sony and Cheung Kong have to play down to their level! If we have the power to do something about it, then we can use this opportunity to make Matsushtia, Fujitsu, and Hitachi play on our level for once. If their investors have a problem with it, we can simply ask them: would they be willing to subject their employees on the Home Islands to the same conditions they require of those in Guangdong?

No matter how they reply, the people will know that we are right.
strings.GNG_an_amendment_to_the_labor_standards_:
To declare our commitment to improved workers' rights is one thing, but to follow through to completion is quite another. We can only take ad-hoc executive action via the understaffed and overworked Labor Bureau for so long. For our reforms to have any chance of being carried out in a comprehensive manner, we must win the approval of the Legislative Council.

The proposed measures are nowhere near enough to be ideal for workers, but it is a good first step. Such is the reality of politics in Guangdong, where we cannot let the perfect become the enemy of the good.
strings.GNG_has_not_started_amended_labor_standa: Has not started voting on the £GNG_Sony_texticon Amended Labor Standards Ordinance.
strings.GNG_the_health_crisis_desc:
The deplorable working and living conditions in Guangdong's slums and factories have given rise to the two grave maladies of life in Guangdong - respiratory illness, and despair. What society can be said to be a 'good' one while its people choke on smog thicker than water, walking underneath a lattice of suicide nets, so normal that the shade cast by a decaying body is treated the same as a passing cloud?

Where Matsushita or Ibuka might assert that caring for the health of the public is a costly exercise in 'preserving human resources,' we would beg to differ. It is an ethical obligation, a cornerstone of the renewed contract between labor and capital. We share the same fate; why should employees suffer unduly the consequences of management's excesses?
strings.GNG_the_bodies_we_see_desc:
It is impossible to ignore the nets strung above the Pearl River, to 'catch' those who would prefer the release of death over the pain of life. Every life lost from despair in Guangdong is one bright light for the future snuffed out well before its prime - and the numbers only continue to increase, while those who remain sink deeper into misery as the retrieval crews navigate the urban spiderweb.

Li Ka-shing has had enough - something must be done. We surely cannot save everyone - but we owe it to everyone to try to save as many as we can.
strings.GNG_reach_out_and_listen_desc:
The breakneck pace of urbanization in Guangdong has uprooted countless communities into cramped, airless tenements in unfamiliar territory, before packing them into deafening factory floors as cogs in a mammoth machine. It is no wonder that the populace feels their issues are insurmountable, surrounded as they are by strangers on every side.

If nobody else will listen to them, we will. We will direct the health authorities to establish hotlines and social outreach programs to rebuild something resembling organic communities in our growing megacities. We have to give people someone who will listen to them today, so that they may live tomorrow.
strings.GNG_the_value_of_life_desc: We must emphasize to the corporations that the people who work for them are not an inexhaustible resource. They aren't a resource at all, to be completely honest, but small steps must be taken before large ones. Every person who is able to come into work tomorrow is another person who gets better at their job, and can be more productive and efficient than they were yesterday. Experience is key to success, and time is needed to develop experience.
strings.GNG_the_air_we_breathe_desc: It is no wonder why the workers are often distracted from their tasks. How can anyone be expected to focus when they're busy coughing up noxious fumes drifting over from the factories on the pearl river, and spitting up tainted water from that very same body of water polluted by those very same factories? Distracted people with shortened life spans bring in less profit. Therefore, instead of trying to convince the other corporations to treat the symptoms of despair, we will get them to agree to the easier and more effective solution of treating the problem at its source.
strings.GNG_water_purity_control_desc: Countless pollutants are being unnecessarily dumped into the upstream of the Pearl River by industry without any regard for the residents downstream. With this in mind, it should come as no surprise that waterborne illnesses and toxic contamination are a shockingly common part of the lives of everyday people in the poorest regions of the Three Pearls. We will direct the corporations- with state funds if needed- to treat contaminants when it is possible and to safely dispose of them when it is not. Together, we will clear the water table we all rely on of toxic elements, so that we might all lead healthy lives.
strings.GNG_the_smokestacks_quit_smoking_desc: In the modern day, the primary issues of industrial smog are quite simple to mitigate using the right technology, filters, and efficient design. All of these are, however, quite expensive- and in the past corporations have preferred to be cheap instead of clean. That ends now. We will set new standards for all others to follow, requiring them to purchase the necessary equipment and keep the air their employees breathe clean and healthy.
strings.GNG_the_public_health_ordinance_desc: Stopgap efforts to combat the various health crises in Guangdong simply cannot increase the overall quality of health without a concerted and focused effort across multiple governmental departments. However, the only way to expand the powers of the government enough to accomplish this- and to contract dedicated companies to address the issue if necessary- lies through the Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_has_not_started_public_health_ordina: Has not started voting on the £GNG_Sony_texticon Public Health Ordinance.
strings.GNG_the_quagmires_of_tomorrow_desc:
What good is a man who believes is true only that which his eyes can see? Task him with a compromised apartment, sure; he'll doubtless list the broken stairways, the faulty fire alarms, the crumbling wallpaper. Ask them why a simpleminded clerk's numbers don't add up and they will be quick to point at their mistaken sums, their sloppy assumptions. But what of the marshy ground holding aloft ten stories of rusted rebar and crackleted concrete? What if the clerk were no clerk but a child who never learned his sums - students who never learned accounting because their schools never bothered? If the complex collapses like pancakes and the universities report their own dismal numbers, when the inquiries are shouted and fingers pointed - who else is to blame but the man with more sight than foresight?

Companies are no less immune to such a failing than men. Many expect it from them, even. That may apply to our peers - but not to Sony. Nor to Cheung Kong. We've come too far to repeat their mistakes; if Guangdong expects foresight from their government, then foresight we good businessmen shall provide in generous rates.
strings.GNG_the_quagmires_of_tomorrow_effect_too: It is not enough to address the crises of today. For £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong's leadership to be fully accepted, we must be one step ahead of the social issues of tomorrow.
strings.GNG_investing_in_human_capital_desc:
Husbands and wives spend twenty and more years of wealth and time on their children for good reason. For all that a machine can lift heavier weights and faster crunch numbers, it is ultimately men who design machines and guide them towards their purpose. Properly fed, properly raised and properly taught, man given machine will solve the world's ails and better their families' lot through ingenuity and drive.

If even dictators acknowledge that man is the most precious capital, what should preclude a capitalist from doing likewise? Quarterly profit margins? Hidebound foolery. For Morita and Li, Guangdong's future rests not in cheap metal knick-knacks made by unthinking slaves, but in silicon wares crafted by artisans who dream. Sony and Cheung Kong will make it so.
strings.GNG_investing_in_human_capital_effect_to: People, not machines or mineral deposits, are £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's greatest resource.
strings.GNG_the_housing_crisis_desc:
Stray away from Chai Wan's lamplights at night and you'll find yourself a tourist of the Guangdong undergrowth, hidden beneath its neon billboards and glitzy high-rises. Here the poor and desperate huddle in ramshackle rooms the size of cabinets clustered to one another like aggregate tumors, not because they can but because they can't anywhere else. What trickles down from corporate offices to its shoulder-wide streets is paper trash rather than paper money. Nobody spares any hope for the island's hundred thousand souls. No, they scrape their hope themselves from wherever they can find it: whorehouses, opium dens, pachinko machines.

Skinflints would balk at the upfront cost of bringing hope to settlements like Chai Wan. Chief Secretary Li sees no costs - only the young ones playing marbles and hopscotch, faces besmirched with dirt yet pearlescent, as their parents look on and wonder if their paper-thin walls will suffice against the frigid winter chill. He was one of them once.
strings.GNG_the_housing_crisis_effect_tooltip: Li argues that without homes, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong will fester in crime and iniquity.
strings.GNG_build_the_bed_towns_desc: Space in the Three Pearls' urban areas is limited by design, and architecture can only build so high without posing a safety risk. The best solution is to find land close to the cities and develop them into commuter towns: residential districts connected by rail with the main city, so that the throngs of workers will have somewhere to sleep other than the miserable tenements in the city slums. They may not be pretty, but these new towns will be a huge step up from the rat warrens these masses live in at the moment, and will free up valuable real estate within the city proper.
strings.GNG_plumbing_power_progress_desc: We have started building new communities for the people of Guangdong, but those communities lack the basic creature comforts of a productive life - proper plumbing and electricity, for a start. By ensuring our people can bathe and stay warm in winter in their own houses, we can save the time they would otherwise spend going to communal baths or taking trips to the well, and maybe even put a smile on their face while we're at it.
strings.GNG_the_schooling_shortage_desc: Between their low literacy rates and even lower levels of technical competence, much of our large population are simply unproductive. For Morita, ensuring that the populace becomes educated and literate is an absolute requirement in order for Guangdong -along with Sony and Cheung Kong- to grow to their full potential.
strings.GNG_the_schooling_shortage_effect_toolti: Morita argues that without education, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong will be forever condemned to poverty.
strings.GNG_a_literate_workforce_desc: Literacy is not just the ability to read and write - it is an understanding of the signals used to live a civilized life. Think of how much time is spent explaining to our workers what a lathe is, or simply how to use a typewriter. Wasted time means wasted money: basic literacy across Guangdong will make our lives infinitely easier in the long run, even if educating the populace will be costly.
strings.GNG_engineering_scholarships_desc:
There is a name for men who detest waste while ignoring wasted talent, extol the virtues of hard work while telling subordinates and aspirants their hard work just won't cut it. The court of public opinion can't decide the better between “hypocrite” and “plaster saint”, but they unanimously agree Guangdong is full of them. Especially in the halls where licenses and diplomas are made.

Sony and Cheung Kong have their own work and money cut out for them if Guangdong's literati refuse to seek out the brightest among the Zhujin and native Chinese. But that just means they get more of these bright young men working for them when they graduate, no?
strings.GNG_human_capital_advancement_ordinance_:
The Office of the Chief Executive has done much to better the fortunes of Guangdong's people since Morita's accession. Minimum wage, work hours, safety standards and healthcare - all these and more were bettered under the Sony CEO's fastidious watch, monumental change enacted with an effortless signature. Progress came relatively easy thanks to his position's wide-ranging powers... and yet the very same powers can undo his work just as easily once wielded by an unscrupulous successor. Once, not if.

At the end of things, Morita is only a man with dreams. Guangdong is adept at grinding both to nothing. Consortiums of men on the other hand, equal parts wealth and political acumen, are costlier to uproot. Thus he shall assign such men as stewards - Secretaries - of his many legacies in Health, Welfare, Housing, Education, and others, that they and their new offices will maintain them long after he no longer can.
strings.GNG_reforming_the_civil_service_desc:
Guangdong's government has often been accused of being a colonial administration in all but name, dominated at its top and middle levels by Japanese and Japanese-trained bureaucrats who answer to boardrooms in Tokyo and Kōshū. No matter how many Zhujin - or the rare, educated Chinese - patrol the streets and file papers as lowly patrolmen and clerks, we will never earn the trust of the population so long as they see the Japanese as masters of Guangdong.

Both to show to our backers in the Zhujin and Chinese communities that our promises will be kept - and to ensure that our new policies are directed as effectively as possible - we must turn our eye to addressing the composition of Guangdong's civil service, our public face to the world and a prominent means of social advancement for those Zhujin and Chinese with means.
strings.GNG_the_cantonese_question_desc:
The simple fact of the matter is that while Japanese is the lingua franca of the Co-Prosperity Sphere and the language of business, the vast majority of the people of Guangdong speak Cantonese.

The government of Guangdong has, until now, remained firmly on the side of Japanese in all official transactions, as expected of the governing authorities in the Sphere - but it has done little to bring the government closer and make it more relatable to the people. It also has created opportunities for communities and criminals to slip through the cracks of our administration, with the particularly unscrupulous among them using their language expertise to manipulate and extort the people ostensibly under their care.

To officially recognize Cantonese as a language of the state would not only allow us to bring these groups under the eye of our government and serve as a powerful symbol of our commitment to a more 'local' government, but it would also serve as a powerful distinction with the neighboring Republic of China - that is, if the Japanese don't throw a fit first...
strings.GNG_the_cantonese_question_effect_toolti: Our choice for the language of government will be heavily scrutinized, from within and without. Choose carefully...
strings.GNG_full_localization_desc:
Li Ka-shing argues that if we are to fully unlock the potential of Guangdong's people - and win their trust and loyalty - we must give them a substantive say in how their affairs are governed.

It will not be instant, nor will it be grand in scope. But we will commit to opening the most senior positions in our civil service to all backgrounds - including native Chinese and Zhujin - and build our own institutional expertise without relying on Tokyo.

The Japanese expatriates and senior mandarins will detest us for this, no doubt. But the journey to a better future begins with a single step... and we must be the ones to take it.
strings.GNG_full_localization_effect_tooltip: We will make the necessary adjustments to make £GNG_zhujin_texticon Cantonese an official working language of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong.
strings.GNG_a_trusted_core_desc:
While fully opening the ranks of the civil service - including its highest positions - to locals and the Zhujin would be a powerful political symbol, it would also alienate the Japanese investors who pay for the programs we seek to institute.

Morita argues that Guangdong should adopt a more gradual approach to localizing the Civil Service. The government will allow competitive advancement into the middle ranks regardless of ethnic background, but remain reliant on a core of Japanese and trusted Zhujin administrators educated in Tokyo. The connections will surely allow us to remain abreast of any drastic developments in Tokyo while smoothing over any ruffled feathers with investors - even if the slow pace of change will frustrate reformists and dissidents alike.
strings.GNG_a_trusted_core_effect_tooltip: To maintain the quality of public services, we must maintain a trusted core of £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese-trained civil servants. That's what we will say publicly, anyway.
strings.GNG_the_civil_service_ordinance_desc:
Life in Guangdong is not easy, despite our best efforts. In an atmosphere where profit is prioritized above all else, there is only so much we can ask from collective effort at the highest levels, where competition is a way of life.

But we have taken the first step, to show to the people that their government can and will provide an opportunity for a better life. As we show solidarity with the people of this erstwhile nation, we now call upon the people to persevere, to direct their energies from simple survival to prosperity. To take ownership - however partial - of your home is to commit yourself to its survival, and we must ask the same of the Zhujin and Chinese.
strings.GNG_the_lion_rock_spirit_desc: Life in Guangdong is not easy, despite our best efforts. In an atmosphere where profit is prioritized above all else, there is only so much we can ask from collective effort at the highest levels, where competition is a way of life. But we have taken the first step, to show to the people that their government can and will provide an opportunity for a better life. Where we offer solidarity with the people of this erstwhile nation, we now call upon the people to persevere, to direct their energies from simple survival to prosperity.
strings.GNG_the_lion_rock_spirit_effect_tooltip: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong does not simply survive - it endures, and so do its people, under £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong's tutelage.
strings.GNG_dare_to_dream_desc:
Today, the people of Guangdong wake up to something new - a sense of safety, of belonging. For the first time in years, Guangdong's people march to work not as the indentured servants of the Five Companies, but as members of something greater - a fledgling society and culture, taking root in the Pearl River Delta.

More importantly, they know who to thank - and who to pay. In their gratitude, they live in Cheung Kong properties, buy food from Cheung Kong supermarkets, use technologies developed by Sony Electronics, while borrowing money from Sony's bankers to pay for utilities provided by Sony power plants. They eat from Morita and Li's hands, and thank us for it.

All is as we once dreamed it, and we will not see this dream taken away from the people - and from us.
strings.GNG_dare_to_dream_effect_tooltip: A new day dawns in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong...
strings.GNG_if_we_make_it_they_will_buy_it: If We Make It, They Will Buy It
strings.GNG_call_in_a_favor_from_stanley_ho: Call in a Favor From Stanley Ho
strings.GNG_morita_personal_crisis_events: More pressure will be put on £GNG_Sony_texticon Morita Akio.
strings.GNG_LKS_personal_crisis_events: More pressure will be put on £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Li Ka-shing.
strings.GNG_shock_to_the_system_desc:
The rug has been pulled out from under us. Tokyo has once again disconnected one of our vital streams of capital and once again pushed us from the nest that was the Co-Prosperity Sphere, the only vital tool Morita needed to continue his experiment of enlightened self-interest.

The economy has been sent into a state of panic. Prices on most goods, especially raw materials and consumer goods, have soared to previously unfathomable heights unseen in Guangdong beforehand, already having an impact as citizens and companies alike choose to limit their spendings and save up cash.

The productivity, economy, and government of Guangdong has faltered. But Morita has already come this far.
strings.GNG_shock_to_the_system_tt: As £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong convulses, the world looks to Morita to walk the talk...
strings.GNG_once_again_alone_desc:
It seems that the crisis has affected our Japanese benefactor in much the same way as us. Communications have been cut, much like our precious funding, and it seems we will have to make do with the tools currently at our disposal.

Our issues are plenty; the government itself must be sustained at all costs, but the private sector must be maintained too. Most companies are currently unable to adjust to our price-inflated economy and as it stands, are begging for government intervention. We will not leave them out to dry.
strings.GNG_once_again_alone_tt: We call - and £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Tokyo does not answer.
strings.GNG_our_promises_desc:
Social spending helped our struggling people, from the Chinese in the rural parts of our nation to the Zhujin and Japanese expatriates of our cities. It wouldn't be a stretch to say that without these policies, much of the nation would slide back into the poverty that gripped it before Morita's rise to power.

The funding handed out to us by the Japanese that in turn was used to fuel this social welfare has evaporated, and with that fact comes a choice: we can continue our social spending policy in these trying times or attempt to cut loose ends. No matter what the future may reveal, the present is already crystal clear: it will not be an easy choice.
strings.GNG_our_promises_tt: It's easy to be generous in times of plenty. But when times are hard...
strings.GNG_maintain_government_projects_desc:
Even though Guangdong faces its second economic crisis in a decade, that is no excuse to fall back into old, dangerous habits. Despite the calls for fiscal rectitude by our investors, the best way to get the economy back in shape when times are hard is not by closing the government pursestrings. Our creditors might benefit from such an approach, but we would be paying our debts on the back of popular penury.

The government will continue to spend - to keep people at work and to pay them for doing so. In a time when private spending is depressed, keeping government infrastructure spending up will be a valuable way to put money in people's pockets - and the people will surely appreciate having food on their tables in tough times.
strings.GNG_maintain_government_projects_econ_tt: To fund our social and administrative programs, we will at minimum have to spend 25% on the social and administrative bars.
strings.GNG_review_government_contracts_desc:
Guangdong has long been a nation of, if not useless projects, less profitable projects. A slightly underused train station here, a half capacity apartment block there, all of it made sense when cash was plentiful and the economy needed boosting. If only we could go back to days like those...

Non-priority projects are no longer viable. Let us void the contracts for these projects and only push vital projects desperately needed by the people. Our money is our most vital tool, and slashing a few projects will aid us in saving it.
strings.GNG_an_opportunity_desc:
Hard times are simply another name for an opportunity; acquisitions made on the cheap, deals made in desperate circumstances. As the Japanese economy and its corporate appendages in Guangdong restructure themselves in the face of the Oil Crisis, we should play a coordinating role in pooling the resources of our Zhujin businesses to undertake public works projects on behalf of the government - at cheaper prices than the Japanese. The government will still save money, while delivering services the Japanese can no longer provide satisfactorily.
