If the Zhujin expand their share of Guangdong's economy in the process, so much the better - though the Japanese business community will no doubt be displeased.
strings.GNG_draw_a_red_line_desc:
Fairness. Such is the lifeline and the ultimate virtue of the businessman - doubly so in times of crisis when his clients call out to him in desperate want. As the shockwave of the Oil Crisis ripples on from the Home Islands, the Japanese business community, already skeptical of our expenditure programs thus far, grows warier still of perceived unfairness; to “concede” to the Zhujin and Chinese once more, therefore, is to invite Japanese investors' vitriol, unfortunate a reality as that may be.

Public works projects will have to be distributed strictly according to established procedures and expenditures is to remain largely as planned, with whatever overt favors for the Zhujin and Chinese restricted to a bare minimum. Fairness is what our compatriots demand, so fairness is what we will deliver - at least on the surface.
strings.GNG_freeze_hiring_desc:
For any organization, one of the single largest and most consistent expenses will be that of personnel, whether it be in wages paid or in the myriad of benefits meant to encourage would-be employees. As the Oil Crisis rocks the world, it is clear Guangdong cannot afford any additional expenses.

While shrinking of our labor force and cutting down on employment would be attractive in other circumstances, the political consequences have thus far preempted any such moves. However, we can freeze hiring so that we aren't actively adding costs when we can least afford it. The wider Zhujin population looking to enter the civil service will be disappointed, but our finances will thank us.
strings.GNG_chase_economies_of_scale_desc:
As we grapple with the Oil Crisis's impact, our battered finances have received some much-needed relief. Japanese firms, themselves reeling from the repercussions of the crisis, have offered to take over several of our infrastructure programs at prices far cheaper than we would've had otherwise. Offers which, when coupled with their support in the Legislative Council, would do much to alleviate our financial and political woes.

Yet, the economics of scale offered by these companies cannot be matched by local firms, and by cutting out Chinese and Zhujin businesses from government contracts, we are, to borrow a Yankee expression, “selling them down the river.” A state of affairs that would not only draw howls of protest from our northern neighbors but also pour gasoline on our already volatile domestic situation.
strings.GNG_prime_the_pump_desc: The primary lesson of Guangdong's response to the Yasuda Crisis was that scaling back spending in a crisis, even if reassuring to our investors, wreaks havoc on the economy - and the general populace. We have to ensure that our people have the money to spend and to keep the economy moving - even if it means spending putting money in the pockets of the people from our own accounts. Our creditors may protest, but we would rather see every yen go to reviving the economy rather than to paying off our debts.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_spare_desc:
Our initiatives to bolster the socio-economic positions of the Zhujin and the Chinese population of Guangdong, while well-intentioned and vital to the continued existence of the nation, cannot be sustained. The similarities to the Yasuda Crisis that brought down the Suzuki administration cannot be ignored, yet unlike our ill-fated predecessor, our economic and political positions remain stable. A state of affairs that we cannot compromise with further social spending.

For the coming months, we must be frugal, lest we be caught off guard by the same sort of machinations which brought down our predecessors. For now, at least, we will have to let the markets take care of the rest.
strings.GNG_we_shall_provide_desc: It is not enough to provide minimum assurances and token payouts to the unemployed - in the face of the second major economic dislocation in a decade, we must ensure that those who are worst affected have what they need to stay secure until times improve. The Japanese might call this unfair redistribution, but the unemployed and the homeless neither work nor spend; and without their labor or their wallets, soon even the Japanese will feel the pinch.
strings.GNG_hold_this_line_desc: We have stated our commitment to extend support to local workers remains in place - but the fact remains that we don't have the room to do much more. Both for the future of our own programs and in order to retain investor confidence that is the lifeblood of the Five Companies, we must husband our resources carefully - and this means we yet again cannot save everyone. We can try to keep people at work - provide some kind of minimum assistance to ensure people don't starve or become homeless - but our largesse cannot be infinite in size or duration.
strings.GNG_reduce_payments_desc:
The most effective and direct way to reduce our expenditure is to cut spending. Publicly funded social programs, investments, and utilities all must find ways to save on money if we are to stabilize our finances. Of course, we must endeavor the wrath of the Chinese population, who depend the most on government services.

A series of minor cuts across a broad range of programs should accomplish this goal, maintaining our commitment to support all of Guangdong while at the same time reducing costs. Some in the Japanese expat community would surely wish we would go further, but they will be pleased that we are lessening the 'distorting elements' in the economy.
strings.GNG_tighten_eligibility_desc:
One of the more effective ways to slash spending without reducing government benefits is to tighten who can, and can't, receive compensation. Tightening eligibility would do much to save on our expenditure, cutting out large swaths of the population from accessing public benefits.

The boon to our finances, however, will be matched tenfold by the outrage amidst the Chinese and Zhujin populations who depend the most on these programs. Further worsening an already precarious security situation.
strings.GNG_tap_additional_resources_desc:
The people must keep spending. Our commitment to social welfare has aided them in doing so, but the reserves for the welfare net are finally reaching their limits.

To keep funds flowing, the pink porcelain pig must be shattered. All the savings, reserves and sovereign wealth funds, everything we built up over the years, all must be collected now, every single penny. The people of Guangdong sacrificed these reserves for their future, and the future is now.
strings.GNG_tap_additional_resources_tt: Whatever the people require in a time of hardship, we will provide with the economic resources we set aside during the Silicon Years.
strings.GNG_proclaim_our_solvency_desc:
Guangdong stands a lighthouse amidst the swirling seas caused by the Oil Crisis, a solvent, stable beacon of prosperity built upon the sound foundations of a solvent economy and a healthy balanced budget. The people are content, business is booming, and investors have nothing to fear and everything to gain, or at least, that is how the official line goes.

We have done everything we can to right the ship of state in these turbulent waters. It is time to see how much influence and money the world sees fit to bring to our decks.
strings.GNG_proclaim_our_solvency_tt: We will court new investor funds by guaranteeing £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's solvency to the world... though they may not take us at face value.
strings.GNG_kept_desc:
The scales have finally been balanced. While we have cut funds from almost every government program under the sun, the economists and professional budget managers have come to an agreement: the government's finances are once again in the black.

While the people have certainly suffered, we must always remember that old programs can be renewed, and cash-strippen organisations can easily be replaced later on. Guangdong is stable, and we have kept our word. That is all that matters to us now.
strings.GNG_kept_tt: We can only hope the people understand the choices we have made to save them from the Oil Crisis.
strings.GNG_our_companies_desc:
The bread and butter of Guangdong and her economy, our many electronics companies, have suffered much from the global spike in oil prices and the drastic decrease in consumer spending power. The lifeblood of our nation is under threat, and we must take action quickly.

Sony and Cheung Kong, two of the most prominent electronics companies in Guangdong, must adapt to these new times with innovative business practices and new manufacturing techniques. Our electronics must be sold, else these two vital companies will fall into irrelevance like so many before.
strings.GNG_our_companies_tt: We must adapt, or die. Such is the way of business.
strings.GNG_morita_like_no_other_trigger: Chief Executive Morita must choose his own plan to maintain £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's state-of-the-art quality.
strings.GNG_like_no_other_desc:
Morita Akio, ever the patron of verifiable commerce integrity, has made his preference clear: Sony and Cheung Kong will not compromise on perfecting our commodities' quality, even if it means racking up the price tags to cover for our expenditures.

Our people, the Zhujin, the Chinese, the Japanese, they deserve the best we have to offer. Such has been our modus operandi, the foundation upon which our stellar reputation has solidified itself over the five years of our tenure thus far - and with the crucial aid of our allies in the Legislative Council we have the financial capability and the incentive to make sure it stays this way, to entrench the brilliance of our craft within the Guangdong market and the Guangdong psyche once more. We are an enterprise like no other, and the freshly stoked demands coursing through our nation will serve as its greatest testament.
strings.GNG_morita_we_only_do_everything_trigger: Chief Executive Morita must choose Li's plan to diversify the assets of £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong, while maintaining the companies' level of quality.
strings.GNG_we_only_do_everything_desc: In times of crisis and disaster, the leadership must respond with decisiveness and drive, it is certainly not the time for ineffective solutions bound by restrictions; our moves must be bold, we must reach for the stars. Li Ka-shing has always been a man of innovation at heart, and while he may take careful and precise steps in the game of politics, he is certainly willing to take large strides in the field of engineering and product development. We will upkeep our image of quality, but also deliver our commodities to our consumers at less cost. We acknowledge the issues that will come with this approach, including the financial consequences that will arrive and the possible controversy it may cause, but we maintain hope that the sacrifices of today will bear fruit tomorrow. Furthermore, in order for this initiative to truly succeed, we will have to be precise on the matter of spending, our funds must not be wasted.
strings.GNG_we_only_do_everything_mech: To succeed in Li's plan, we must allocate sufficient funds for innovation.
strings.GNG_OC_Sony_Spending_Point_tt: More money will be allocated to innovation.
strings.GNG_OC_Sony_Spending_Point_big_tt: A ton of money will be allocated to innovation.
strings.GNG_accept_customer_needs_desc: One of the surest outcomes of a recession is that customers tighten their purse strings - which leaves them able to pay less exactly when we are pouring money into product development. For the sake of Sony and Cheung Kong's brand, and for our loyal customers, we cannot pass on the costs to them - we will continue to provide our products at previous cost, and accept the hit to our bottom lines instead. Goodwill, afterall, is priceless.
strings.GNG_we_know_what_they_want_desc:
Our decision to continue to pursue quality and excellence is nothing more than an extension than one of Chief Executive Morita's key beliefs when it comes to engineering, if not politics: that the public may not know what is possible, but we do.

It is only natural, therefore, to ask them to pay their fair share. A product that is revolutionary will sell itself, and this will keep us afloat to continue delivering future revolutions to come. Messaging this will be difficult, of course, but we hopefully can convince those with means - the Japanese expatriates - to keep one eye on the future that Morita envisions.
strings.GNG_compact_design_desc:
Our products remain at the center of the situation, for they will determine whether we rise from the ashes in triumph and increased vigor. As of current, there are many things which could be done to increase efficiency in production and marketing to the consumer, the most obvious of which are the designs themselves.

Matsushita Electric has honed this aspect of production intensively: refined, simple designs. By delivering new commodities to the markets with compact and simplified designs, we reduce the costs of manufacturing while also increasing the speed of production, ensuring that we are able to provide consistency to our populace. However, it is undeniable that risks to this approach do certainly exist, as it does not tackle the issue of quality.
strings.GNG_overclocked_design_desc:
Heeding Morita Akio's wishes of increased quality in our products, we shall further invest our time and funds into the development and pursuit of newer and better approaches to production, at the expense of our already constrained budget.

It is certain that this approach to the matter is of the specialty of Fujitsu, a corporation that strives for excellence and quality. Although we acknowledge the fact that this would be a slight detriment to our monetary reserves in this time of need, it is necessary to ensure that our populace's faith in our products is retained and that we emerge from this time of need basking in the glorious golden light of success.
strings.GNG_match_reduced_demand_desc: Unsold inventory is the bane of any company's existence - emblematic of costs paid that are simply not being recouped. Whatever we have chosen to do on the question of price or quality, we must make sure to match our overall production to the reduced demand from our customers. We will ask our production lines and our partners to reduce production of their goods and to reduce their shifts - which may help give some respite to our workers while protecting Sony and Cheung Kong's bottom line at the same time.
strings.GNG_if_we_make_it_they_will_buy_it_desc: Speed and innovation are key in our pursuit of recovery on the matter of production, two factors that may either propel our numbers into new heights or jeopardize our entire operation. However, Chief Executive Morita is aware of the situation at hand, this is not the time for costly and stagnant market research, it would be an extra weight upon our shoulders, a weight which is entirely unnecessary. Sony has always branded itself as a pioneering force in innovation, a corporation whose products outshine others due to the virtues and uniqueness in their designs. As such, we see no reason to drastically reduce the output of our efforts in manufacturing and jeopardize our reputation, as our products themselves shall continue to draw customers to the stores.
strings.GNG_always_be_closing_desc:
Bankruptcies and closures have occurred all across the nation. From retailers to manufacturers, companies have been forced to lay off employees and shut stores, leaving a once in a lifetime opportunity for just the right rival company...

Cheung Kong shall replace the void that our weakened competitors have left behind. While they consolidate what little resources are left to them, we shall spread our many tentacles and grasp every corner of the nation. Unfortunately, Cheung Kong will be less able to influence the Legislative Council, but our massive expansion will secure Cheung Kong's future in Guangdong forevermore.
strings.GNG_consolidate_sales_networks_desc: The people just won't spend, no matter how much funds we throw at them. To ensure the continued profitability of Cheung Kong, adjustments must be made. Retraining and rearrangement of our staff plus the consolidation of low demand sales offices will allow us to continue treading water, and most importantly, allow us to continually influence the Legislative Council.
strings.GNG_iteration_desc: As we continue to strive for an effective and smooth recovery and recuperation, we need to take the issue of production into account. As we are in a tenuous time of crisis where rash decisions may lead to further disaster and catastrophe, we shall engage in extensive market research and development on iterations of our preexisting products, to fully ensure that our manufacturing efforts are ultimately successful and that our products get taken off the shelves. This method of approaching production is cost-effective and rather inexpensive in comparison to our other options, although it does not necessarily capture the sense of innovation and imagination we are known for.
strings.GNG_revolution_desc: When our entire product lineup is under question, the answer should not be focused on incremental improvements. If we want to come out of the Oil Crisis stronger than ever, then we need to ensure that our products are completely revamped, utterly optimized for the post-Oil Crisis world. We will accept no substitutes, no half-measures, no piecemeal additions - for Guangdong, we will show the public the future they want, no matter how much it costs us.
strings.GNG_please_understand_desc:
In these dire times of need and distress, we have achieved and attempted much in our efforts to recuperate the ailing economy of Guangdong. We have engaged in restructuring and consolidation, act upon act dedicated to the betterment of Guangdong, its citizens and its businesses, so that we all may emerge from the debris and return to an era of economic prosperity once more. However, we must not neglect the entity which our endeavors impact the most: the public.

Throughout all of our efforts and achievements, we have done much to ensure that the workforce and populace of Guangdong do not suffer, this, however, does not free us from the obligation of transparency. We must appeal to the public, our actions have to be explained and their support has to be guaranteed; it is of the utmost importance that the citizenry grasps the intent of our decisions, so that they may understand that their faith in us has not been misplaced.
strings.GNG_please_understand_tt: Whatever difficult decisions we have made, they will be worthless if we do not make the case to the masses. We can only hope they understand...
strings.GNG_seek_additional_financing_desc:
The one issue with trying to do everything is that it costs an arm, a leg, and then some besides. Our own cash reserves, accumulated over years of profits, are straining under the burden of our mammoth investments in research and development.

We are trying to complete remake the world of consumer electronics in our image, and we just need a little more to take us over the finish line. Surely the banks and our investors would understand if we ask them to contribute their fair share?
strings.GNG_resurgent_desc: Capitalism is a harsh, merciless master, and those who cannot adapt with the times will invariably be consumed at the hands of the competition. But Sony and Cheung Kong will not fall! We will harness the shifting tides of our present condition and make it the engine of our future success.
strings.GNG_resurgent_tt: Never bet against £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong.
strings.GNG_resurgent_2_tt: Our prior choices will determine the effects of this focus.
strings.GNG_our_streets_our_borders_desc:
To the economists and financiers of our nation, there are only a few similarities between the Yasuda Collapse of the sixties and the Oil Crisis of our current year. To everybody else, it may very well seem like the death of Guangdong itself.

The fear is palpable, but we cannot succumb to it. Let us show our will and power to the world, that Guangdong is strong and stable, for the sake of our own people and the Japanese and Chinese watching from abroad.
strings.GNG_our_streets_our_borders_tt: Beyond GDP figures and revenue targets, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong churns under pressure - from both within and without.
strings.GNG_reinforce_the_police_presence_desc:
Our efforts to strengthen and professionalize Guangdong's security forces are bearing fruit now, especially when we need them to do their jobs more than ever to prove that the Kenpeitai are unnecessary. As Guangdong buckles under economic hardship and murmurs of social unrest, we will ensure that the Police will have everything they need to maintain order and hunt down dissidents and troublemakers.

No matter the costs it will entail.
strings.GNG_reinforce_the_police_presence_tt: What do we pay the £GNG_police_texticon police for? And more importantly: we're willing to pay for overtime...
strings.GNG_buckle_down_desc:
Suzuki's failure during the Yasuda crash was his inability to maintain a steady hand during the crisis, his failure, and that of his administration to uphold a facade of stability and calm not only panicked investors but worried the public and emboldened dissidents. We shall make no such mistake.

We will not stand idly by, but not will not give in to temptations of panic or alarm. There is no need for dramatic action or public theatrics, but merely a guiding light to steer Guangdong through these troubled waters.
strings.GNG_buckle_down_tt: Crisis management is first and foremost an exercise in prioritization - and some say we must manage affairs close to home...
strings.GNG_call_in_a_favor_from_stanley_ho_desc:
Stanley Ho's network of “associates” and “partners” runs deep through Guangdong's underworld, and should we be able to enlist their support, it will help greatly in preventing the worst from reaching Guangdong's streets. Enlisting the support of Guangdog's most notable socialite, however, is easier said than done.

Ho's willingness to bargain will depend entirely on the goodwill we have managed to engender with him throughout our administration. Should we have done too little, his support will be... tepid at best.
strings.GNG_call_in_a_favor_from_stanley_ho_tt: £GNG_Triad_texticon Stanley Ho owes us for all the backroom dealings - let's see what he can do for us.
strings.GNG_the_brain_drain_desc:
Guangdong has had no problem finding labor to fuel our economy; that is until now. Once a hub of immigration from our northern neighbor, as workers moved south to partake in the Silicon Dream, this trend has been reversing in recent years. Slowly at first, the Oil Crisis badly battered our trade dependent economy and has led many in Guangdong to move back to the burgeoning industries of the RGOC.

This phenomenon poses a grave risk to Guangdong's economic standing, as once plentiful labor grows increasingly scarce, threatening the very bedrock of our economy. We must find ways to address this “brain drain” before it's too late.
strings.GNG_the_brain_drain_tt: We must address the outflow of our £GNG_zhujin_texticon Zhujin and £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese labor to the £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon Republic of China.
strings.GNG_the_second_japanese_wave_desc:
As shockwaves from the Middle East reach Asian shores, Japanese companies across the Sphere find themselves reeling from the twin blows of the Oil Crisis and surging Chinese competition. As stock markets plunge for the second time this decade, many conglomerates and companies are left looking for a safe harbor and space to rebuild their operations.

Guangdong is this harbor; by advertising ourselves as a port amidst the storm, we can attract valuable talent and capital as companies flock to establish themselves on the Pearl River. Our Zhujin backers, however, many business owners themselves, will be less than pleased should we take this Japanese wave yet again.
strings.GNG_the_second_japanese_wave_tt: We must address the second influx of £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese migrants from £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China, seeking new pastures in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong.
strings.GNG_insert_ourselves_into_the_vacuum_des:
Exactly why should our ambitions stop at the borders of Guangdong? If our workers are fleeing to China, and Japanese capital is fleeing China, then there is one easy solution. All we need to do is take our capital, invest in China, and employ our people in the places where we invest. Out of everything we have dealt with this, this is not a crisis, far from it; it is instead an unprecedented opportunity for Guangdong to enter into and stake out a commanding position in China's largest market.

All opportunities, however, carry an inherent risk, and this is the case here too. The risk is that the rapidly-industrializing Chinese government and our Japanese corporate backers may be irritated if we make too many gains at their expense.
strings.GNG_insert_ourselves_into_the_vacuum_tt: £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese capital is fleeing £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China; our £GNG_zhujin_texticon workers are running into £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China. This is an opportunity, not a curse.
strings.GNG_allow_open_borders_desc:
It is self-evident that closing the border to one of our largest trade partners is out of the question. It is just as self-evident that the reforms needed to improve Chinese perceptions of Guangdong towards making them consider it more attractive than China as a place in which to live is politically infeasible. That is because all Five Companies will torpedo even the slightest suggestion thereof.

Our failure to act will force us to face the prospect of a constant stream of resources and growth leaving Guangdong for China. But this will be the new reality with which we must contend; the only solution we have is to innovate past this problem as we have done with every problem that preceded it.
strings.GNG_allow_open_borders_tt: We must accept that there will be a largely open border with £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China, even if the £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese cooperate on updating some visa regulations.
strings.GNG_demand_corporate_accountability_desc:
It is self-evident that closing the border to one of our largest trade partners is out of the question. But we must make some kind of gesture that will make clear to the people of Guangdong that they have more to gain from staying here rather than running for any open exit door they find. Only a grand and decisive gesture will suffice to make this point; fortunately, we have figured out the one to make.

We will demand that the labor abuses that have plagued Guangdong be immediately and publicly addressed in the Legislative Council. Though this runs the very great risk of costing us the LegCo's support, it will make our point for us that Guangdong is indeed a better place to live in.
strings.GNG_demand_corporate_accountability_tt: In exchange for controlling the flow of migrants across the border, the £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon Republic of China has demanded we take binding action against labor abuses...
strings.GNG_demand_corporate_accountability_tt_2: This ordinance will be an almost impossible sell to anyone outside of £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong, so be adequately prepared.
strings.GNG_welcome_them_in_desc:
Japanese capital is fleeing China in the millions and billions of yen, and a large portion of it hopes to set up shop in Guangdong instead. There is exactly no reason to prevent them from finding a new home in the Three Pearls or anywhere else in our fair state; accordingly, we will throw the door open as wide as is humanly possible. As we are beginning to face a major and increasing brain-drain, the resources offered by these fleeing entities will help make up the difference.

Unfortunately, it has been brought to our attention that favoring the Japanese to such an extent may disadvantage the Chinese and Zhujin businesses already present. Though this prospect saddens us greatly, we deem it to be a worthy cost to help stabilize our situation.
strings.GNG_welcome_them_in_tt: £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese capital is always welcome in £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - especially if they place it at our disposal...
strings.GNG_they_knew_the_risks_desc:
Japanese capital is fleeing China in the millions and billions of yen, and a large portion of it hopes to set up shop in Guangdong instead. But investing overseas is a terribly risky business, and the Japanese companies knew that risk very well when they entered China. Whatever suffering they are going through now is an outworking of their unpreparedness, and there is exactly no reason why Guangdong should displace its own industrial capacities and resources to help companies subordinate to Tokyo and not Kōshū.

Now putting our foot down like this is not without risk; the Japanese government might have something to say about our defense of our own interests. On the other hand, Stanley Ho tells us there is a distinct chance that the Chinese might think differently of us for our oblique refusal to protect Tokyo's interests.
strings.GNG_they_knew_the_risks_tt: Every businessman knows the maxim: buyer beware. And it seems the £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese forgot...
strings.GNG_secure_desc:
The protests that have recently bedevilled the streets of our cities are now contained. Guangdong's various official and unofficial authorities know what they need to do if and when things get out of hand. The twin crises on our borders, caused by the effects of the Oil Crisis on the Japanese sphere, have at last been addressed and contained, for the most part. We now know what to do, but our plans may be affected by the way in which the Chinese and Japanese react.

For now, however, Guangdong at last knows a semblance of peace. All we need to do now is hold the line, watch the situation, and wait for the economic cycle to begin trending upwards again, as it always does.
strings.GNG_secure_tt: We have battened down the hatches; now all that remains is to ride out the storm.
strings.GNG_the_pearls_ablaze_desc:
Hitachi's debacle during the factory strike crisis has exploded into a nationwide catastrophe. Guangdong stands united in protests and not a single city street has remained silent since that dreadful day. Their voices chant for reparations, and a delivery on promises made by the Chief Executive.

If the people screaming in our ears weren't bad enough, the structures of the government themselves are being bent and twisted. Corporations, unwilling to see their profit margins decrease by even miniscule amounts, are pressuring us to let these protests die out naturally without ceding an inch to the people. With the two interest groups Morita tried so damn hard to placate at each other's throats, none can tell whether the Executive's dream will die before it even leaves the crib.
strings.GNG_the_pearls_ablaze_tt:
If £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong burns to ashes - so do we.
Not every focus needs to be taken, if we believe the situation is under control...
strings.GNG_walk_the_talk_desc:
We've been saying we'll make life better for the regular Chinese and Zhujin people in Guangdong, but there were always pockets where our efforts did not reach - mainly controlled at the behest of the other corporations which, legally required or not, often took our policies as 'suggestions' rather than 'requirements'.

The indignities inflicted by the other corporates - nothing new, but festering over time in the face of our promises - have now exploded in a storm of rage, a spark lighting the tinder laid by the Oil Crisis. We have promised the residents of Guangdong a semblance of justice and dignity, under Sony and Cheung Kong's leadership - and now Guangdong asks us to walk the talk.
strings.GNG_walk_the_talk_tt: We have promised change. The people ask where it is - and we must have an answer.
strings.GNG_listen_to_the_street_desc: The overwhelming ethnicities of our nation, the Chinese and Zhujin, have united and railed against the great crimes done against them by Hitachi. We have sided with the people before, and taken in their concerns as a solution previously. We must do so again now, when everything is on the table.
strings.GNG_listen_to_the_street_tt:
The grievances of the people must be heard, or else our claim to represent them dies.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism, at the expense of £GNG_japanese_frustration_texticon Japanese frustration, are unlocked.
strings.GNG_invite_the_leadership_desc: Over the course of the riots that have come in the wake of the Oil Crisis, two major factions have emerged which lead the rioters, the Guangdong Federation of Tradesmen and the Committee of Chinese Labor. The leadership of both organisations will be invited to meet with the Chief Executive and Chief Secretary. We must hope that they are willing to be cooperative with us, or else this situation will only continue to spiral downwards.
strings.GNG_snap_factory_inspections_desc: As discontent spreads amongst the workers, it is important that we remind them that we have always been, and will remain, on their side. Using the mounting tension caused by the riots as our justification, snap inspections will be ordered for factories across Guangdong to ensure that the existing policies, which we so vigorously championed, are enforced.
strings.GNG_let_them_vent_desc: Some of the more reckless corporate leaders have been keen to call for a blanket clamp down on the dissent which has emerged, following this course of action would no doubt be misguided. The grievances of the people must be aired, after all, their outrage against the Hitachi disaster is perfectly understandable. We can not push too hard against them, or else they will snap and turn their rage from Hitachi to us.
strings.GNG_let_them_vent_effect: Reduces £GNG_riot_strength_texticon rioter strength increase by 1.5% for 150 days.
strings.GNG_discontent_is_no_excuse_desc: Although we hold the utmost sympathies for the pain and anger of the protestors on the street, we must preserve the rich and prosperous fabric of Guangdong for the future. Their misguided strikes against the police and the state, which only seeks to protect them, must not go unpunished. Certain limits are necessary to keep the protests safe and manageable to ensure that Guangdong as a whole does not perish.
strings.GNG_discontent_is_no_excuse_tt:
Whatever the grievances of the people, disorder is not the way forward.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_insist_on_permits_desc: It has forever been a fact of life in Guangdong that the security forces - be they Police or Kenpeitai - are far outnumbered by the Chinese locals. Were all these locals to flood the streets at once, there would be no way to preserve order on the streets. Thankfully, in these early stages there have signs that some demonstrators will heed our calls to request permissions and follow good order in the expression of their discontent - a measure that will ease the burden on the Police and allow us to more quickly identify troublemakers.
strings.GNG_peacefully_desc: Discontent is one thing; anarchy is another. We must insist that even as the Chinese and Zhujin residents of Guangdong have the right to voice long-suppressed grievances, that they do so in as peaceful and non-disruptive a manner as possible. Violence and disorder only serves the purposes of Morita's political rivals - to those who say that violence is the language of the oppressed, we counter that they would see results, if they would only stop giving their enemies more ammunition.
strings.GNG_wait_until_nightfall_desc: We are fully aware that bad faith motivates a select few of the protesters on the streets - looking for any excuse to cast the first stone to plunge Guangdong into anarchy, whether out of radicalized frustration or as an appendage of more malign powers. In order to keep these dissident elements from radicalizing the protests further, we must isolate and detain any identified troublemakers without provoking public fury as Hitachi did. We will direct our police direct action teams to wait until nightfall before conducting intrusive searches and arrests of radical ringleaders, far away from the public eye.
strings.GNG_normal_is_not_enough_desc:
Just as we thought that the situation could not get any worse, it did. We expected the riots to slowly dissipate as time went by, but it seems the reverse is true, and that the riots grow both in strength and radicalism for each passing day. This situation has far gone what we call “normal,” and it has to be sorted out quickly and return to normalcy.

As priorly stated, the “normal” effort that we put into containment is no longer adequate. In order to sort this situation as rapidly as possible, more state resources must be focused into taking control of the situation, more police, security, and riot control must be unleashed to put down the riot. We will be willing to take far more drastic measures to stop the riots, at any cost.
strings.GNG_normal_is_not_enough_tt: If normal means are insufficient, then we must dig deeper - in either mercy or resolve.
strings.GNG_find_our_allies_desc:
The demonstrators are many in numbers, and with their numbers come the diversity of each and every protestor's different beliefs and ideals. The protestors have as many different views as there are grains of sands on the beaches, and with that many clinging to different ideals, there has to be several that we can ally and exploit to our own benefit.

Even if we can't fulfill everyone's demands, we can give many promises and enticements to those that we can. Promise those whose ideals align the closest to ours with anything that is necessary to get them off the streets of Guangdong, we expect this blow to the strength of the protests to cut down the size and strength of the protests slowly but surely, and those that are convinced might just march with us into the future.
strings.GNG_find_our_allies_tt:
As the battle lines harden, we must identify those who are most willing to work with us.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism, at the expense of £GNG_japanese_frustration_texticon Japanese frustration, are unlocked.
strings.GNG_incorporate_the_manifestos_desc:
We have previously given the protestors the promises that they wanted to hear, but unfortunately, they have started to demand the fulfilment of those promises sooner than we predicted them to. The protestors now demand that we incorporate everything that we have said into our current policy programs in the near future. Doing this is a very reliable way to end the protests once and for all and further our goals of returning Guangdong to the world stage, but we must tread very carefully.

The main problem that we are facing is that while indeed there are protestors whose goals align with ours, a larger portion of the protestors' goals and demands do not meet with our vision of the future. Conceding to the latter may spark the fury of our Japanese overlords and the corporates that come with them. The matter has become more complicated than we've ever imagined it to become, and we must be very careful of our actions from this point on.
strings.GNG_serve_the_changes_desc:
It is a regrettable truth of our country that many of the state's factory owners, overseers, and bureaucrats very oftenly abuse their powers and mistreat many of their subordinates, seeing them as nothing more than just a capital, leading to a lot of unnecessary suffering for the workers. Regrettably as well, this debacle has gone for years, even decades, and there may be no way for the people to calm themselves after this many years of unreleased frustration.

The charges must be served, and justice must be enforced to those who abuse their powers with impunity. This may damage the structure of our economy, as the people that we rely on are given their fair share of justice, but our priority is contenting the people no matter the price. Only then might we be able to calm the people down.
strings.GNG_limited_coordination_desc:
The protests are still growing as they have been since this entire debacle started, but we must still push on working to eliminate the protests off the streets. As we have dealt with in the past, there are more than a few groups of protestors that are aligned to our goals more than others, and we have given them the promises of marching together with us to the future. It is to our best interests to press on harder on this initiative to further break apart the protests.

There will be new measures to further this goal, such as having the police give them a better timing preference for their protest permits so as to have them off the streets when we start our clearance operations. This also has the side effects of giving the protestors less and less opportunities to coordinate, breaking their strength even more.
strings.GNG_limited_coordination_effect: Reduces £GNG_riot_strength_texticon rioter strength increase by 1.5% for 150 days.
strings.GNG_isolate_the_troublemakers_desc:
As we have taken into account on several occasions during this crisis, the protestors are very diverse in terms of their beliefs and goals. While most simply wish to express their discontent with the circumstances that they are in, there are some that are more unsavory than the rest of them. These are the people that don't want to express their displeasure, instead looking to cause anarchy, stir trouble, and in general destabilize the state of Guangdong.

They are people that we cannot reason with, and treating them in the same way as we treat the rest of the protestors is simply a mistake. Instead, they must be eliminated from the picture as soon as possible. The police will focus on isolating their influence from spreading, so as to not attract any more people to their cause.
strings.GNG_isolate_the_troublemakers_tt:
The most inveterate troublemakers will be taken out of the picture.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_screen_public_transport_desc:
Most of the demonstrators cannot afford their own means of transport, and it just so happens to be that we ourselves provide the means of gathering for these troublemakers. Public transportation systems have been observed to be utilized by demonstrators looking to either reach their intended protest location, or to organize with their fellow demonstrators. Services such as public buses and train systems have been reported to carry passengers possessing questionable gear with them.

To prevent them from gathering strength or further organizing, we will take measures to screen the public transportation system. Anyone carrying stones, homemade explosives, or anything that may be used to disrupt peace on the streets shall be detained before they can group up with the masses. Divide and conquer.
strings.GNG_raise_the_black_flag_desc:
Since the beginning of the demonstrations, we have enacted a policy of tolerance towards the demonstrators, the protesters are already encouraged to engage in peaceful acts of demonstration instead of violence, and we had hoped that the situation would not escalate any further. We have been proven wrong.

The protesters have started to become more violent and destructive, far exceeding what we - or our investors - consider the limit. More and more destruction and disruption has erupted on the streets of Guangdong, and the country is inching closer into anarchy for every second it is not addressed.

Enough is enough. They have been warned, and yet they remain ignorant. Bring out the teargas, raise the black flags! Guangdong must be saved from these vandals.
strings.GNG_daylight_raids_desc: Despite all efforts by security forces to quietly and carefully suppress the radicals that have thrown Guangdong into chaos, it is clear this strategy is not working. Now we must attempt a policy of deterrence. Daylight raids and investigations in hotspots of radical activity will be approved, both to arrest as many of the subversives as we can as well as to show the people that we will not tolerate revolutionaries in our midst.
strings.GNG_remove_the_limiters_desc:
Just as we were thinking that the situation could not ever deteriorate further, we received more and more reports from the streets of anarchy and destruction. It seems that our previous measures were not enough to deter the protests from intensifying, and instead, the protests have even amplified in intensity. There is no work, yet the people are not satisfied. Even worse off, our investors and the Tokyo government has started to demand results of the de-escalation of the situation, and we have little to nothing to show in that regards.

The circumstances are desperate, and desperate times call for desperate measures. Anything that we have been holding back from doing in the past, we do today. The limiters must be removed, and the streets must be pacified.

By any means necessary.
strings.GNG_remove_the_limiters_tt: The crisis on the streets must be brought under control - even if the means shake us to our core.
strings.GNG_with_us_desc: The riots are dragging on for far too long, and the only remaining viable way to end this is to make it clear once and for all to the protestors that they can walk alongside us into the future if they wish- but only if they accept the fact that we will remain in power in this new future. Those who cannot will remain enemies of Guangdong and be treated accordingly.
strings.GNG_with_us_tt: Radical £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism, at the expense of Japanese frustration, are unlocked.
strings.GNG_accelerate_integration_desc: The protestors themselves have made it clear that there is no acceptable outcome where they do not have a seat at the table and a say in the making of Guangdong's future. Japanese transplants dominate the bureaucracy, the police, and obviously much of the government. It would be fair to say that many of them serve Tokyo rather than the Chief Executive. To counteract this we will accelerate the integration of Zhujin and Chinese into the government and public services, to ensure a fairer treatment of the people and stronger loyalty to Guangdong.
strings.GNG_hold_them_accountable_desc:
We have been on the backfoot ever since we decided to give concessions to the rioters in order to satisfy them, but they ask for more, unthinkable amounts of concessions to be handed to them. But alas, we cannot stop now. In order to succeed in pacifying the country, we will have to give in to those demands even more.

Those in control, factory owners, bureaucrats, foremen, and anyone else holding great responsibilities, must be held accountable. In the past, we have gone after second-rate players of the Japanese and corporate elite, but now, those measures are no longer enough. None shall be missed by the ever-vigilant eye of the state, and everyone will be held accountable.
strings.GNG_selective_enforcement_desc: At the current rate, it is quickly becoming impossible to keep rioters off the streets. We must conserve our resources to change the situation, and to accomplish this we will soften police activity towards protest groups who have indicated a willingness to negotiate with us. For as long as they are willing to talk, they can expect this moderated treatment to continue.
strings.GNG_selective_enforcement_tt:
We can use the £GNG_rioters_texticon rioters to accelerate our own agenda.
Unlocks a new £decision_icon_small decision to use the £GNG_rioters_texticon rioters to weaken£GNG_legco_texticon LegCo opposition.
strings.GNG_or_against_us_desc:
Call them extremists, radicals, or even terrorists. Those groups of people have made it clear to us that their priorities lie not for the sake of the future. They have made it clear that they will not, in any way or form, join us in marching to the future of Guangdong, and instead hellbent on wreaking havoc and destruction of their homeland rather than preserving it. We must make sure that they cannot destroy or threaten the wellbeing of anyone else, other than themselves.

Actions have consequences, and although they may be misguided, worthy of pity, or simply had things differently from us, the truth is, they know very well of what they are doing, and chose to press on with their meaningless campaign. Their actions will grant them consequences, and they shall not be spared from our wrath.
strings.GNG_or_against_us_tt: Desperate £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_advise_against_movement_desc:
The time for half-measures are over, and we must commit to protecting the innocent and our own interests. Regrettably, screening public transport requires significant resources, and coupled with us having to deal with the protests themselves, we are easily overwhelmed, and permits have long since stopped being useful as a means to control public movement and activity. For the sake of the safety of all, we must declare curfew.

General restrictions of movement will be declared after sundown, to keep the law-abiding citizens of Guangdong safe from the dangers outside. This can also help us pinpoint those who do not abide by the law, for they will be the only ones outside at late hours. They will be swept off the streets while the innocent will be safe indoors.
strings.GNG_deploy_armor_desc:
Deaths and injuries have increased exponentially on the anarchic streets of Guangdong, and the police force is slowly but surely getting pushed back by the chaos. It is clear that the regular means of containing the violence on the streets are no longer sufficient in deterring the protesters, or protecting the innocent, and that more resources and equipment must be allocated into the effort to pacify the streets.

Fortunately enough, we are in the possession of equipment that cannot be damaged by the roughly made tools used by the protesters. Armored cars and vehicles will be deployed to protect our men from the savage protesters. Some may call this unnecessary intimidation and use of brute force, but the alternative is much worse.
strings.GNG_unlimited_detention_desc:
A concerning cycle has begun to develop within this crisis. A radical protester or leader of a group gets imprisoned and brought before the court only to be released into the streets due to overcrowding, and what do they do? Return to protesting on the streets. This has gone unaddressed since the start of the protests, and it is about time that we do something about it.

The law is no longer enough, but the people will cease illegal activity, it matters not what actions we must take to do this. Those detained will be detained indefinitely, at least, until the entire situation is resolved. The situation is too desperate for us not to do this, and we are going to have to put aside the dubiousness of this measure's legality.
strings.GNG_everything_for_guangdong_desc:
Morita Akio and Li Ka-shing have staked everything on making Guangdong a place where they can have a chance at succeeding - hand in hand with those who envision a Guangdong that is more than just a factory floor for the Japanese Zaibatsu and the tycoons. To give up now would be a betrayal not only of our mission, but of the tens of thousands who look to us to provide a model for a better future under Sony and Cheung Kong's aegis.

Even as the Three Pearls and the outlying provinces are consumed in days of rage and plumes of teargas, and as the rumbles of discontent in Tokyo grow louder, we have no choice but to walk our path to its bitter end.
strings.GNG_everything_for_guangdong_tt: There is no price too great to be paid to save £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong's £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong.
strings.GNG_our_home_our_way_of_life: Our Home, Our Way of Life
strings.GNG_the_smoke_clears_desc:
As the sun rises above the fading columns of smoke over Kōshū, Honkon, and Makao, Guangdong endures. The vision of Morita Akio and Li Ka-shing endures, as the corporate sigils of Sony and Cheung Kong shine down on the cityscape and settlements dotting the countryside.

The dissidents have been bought off, or forced underground once more. The IJA is standing down. The other corporates, whose folly and disregard invited Guangdong's greatest crisis, have been cowed into silence. We - and only we - claim to represent the interests of the people, our loyal employees from which Guangdong's prosperity derives.
strings.GNG_the_smoke_clears_tt: We clear the streets of rubble and ruin - cleaning the ash from the pyre of progress.
strings.GNG_the_peoples_faces_desc:
Guangdong has become far more humane, far more 'nice' than it once was. The worst of the discrimnation is gone; people are being paid. Deaths by 'karoshi' and overwork are a thing of the past. The people, far from merely surviving, live. With a brief vignette of peace they are now freed to look forward, not at their beaten feet.

Best of all for us, they know very well just who has brought them all this bounty. They rely on us - to Sony, to Cheung Kong - to provide for them and their families. They look to us at all times, and we most willingly provide, as is our right and duty.
strings.GNG_our_new_economy_desc:
This great state of Guangdong will recover, as it has done many times before. We use adversity to gain ever-greater triumphs for ourselves. Powered by the energetic labor of a loyal, dedicated workforce, and backed by the brilliance of engineers in Sony and Cheung Kong, those among the Chinese, Zhujin, and Japanese expatriates who choose to join their hands with us shall propel the Sphere, nay, the whole world into a new future.

We of Sony and Cheung Kong shall guide and guard them in this endeavour. It is elevated and correct, our right and our duty, to do so.
strings.GNG_stand_down_the_reserves_desc:
As the world-historical disaster that has been the Oil Crisis slows down, and recovery continues, regular life in Guangdong - crime not least among its many facets - reasserts itself. Petty crime, vices, smuggling, all these things remain much the same as they once were. Things have changed, true: the Kenpeitai are more or less driven out, and the Police run far better than they once did. But for all that the crime doesn't really seem to have gone away.

Looking at this we question whether the criminals are just criminals, or in fact the desperate who are possessed of no other choice in Guangdong's hyper-competitive economy.
strings.GNG_stand_down_the_reserves_tt: ...with only a nominal amount of force...
strings.GNG_our_home_our_way_of_life_desc:
Morita and Li promised themselves a decade ago that Guangdong would become more than just a place to survive - it would be a place that they, cast adrift from Japan and caught in the grinding gears of poverty, could call their home.

Now, their way of life is now that of an entire nation. Capitalism and enterprise will be the means by which the Chinese - and especially the growing Zhujin professional classes - will make a home of Guangdong, despite being caught up in historical happenstance. The Japanese will adapt, as Morita did so many years ago, or the new Guangdong will pass them by.

Guangdong will be more than farms, a foundry, or a harbor - it will be a nation, under Sony and Cheung Kong's trademark.
strings.GNG_our_home_our_way_of_life_tt: ...and soon you forget you live in a world of £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong's design.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_the_horizon_desc:
With the immediate needs of the Guangdong Riots met it is time for us to look beyond Guangdong's borders. We are at last free to get back to what we were doing before everything went to hell in a handbasket faster than Li Ka-shing could say “ham gaa caan”.

As such, let's return to what we do best - selling, selling, and selling (not to mention selling). It is time for us to make the rounds in Tokyo, Nanjing, and hopefully further afield; surely this next decade will be better than the last. We, uh, hope it will be, anyway.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_the_horizon_tt: When we look upon the future, we look through lenses tinted by the past...
strings.GNG_beyond_manchukuo_desc:
Let us proclaim an end to the old, outdated industrial paradigm. For all that Sejima Ryūzō or Kishi Nobusuke might protest otherwise, the industry of the future will have little and less to do with steel, chemicals, or machinery. The Manchurians are welcome to cling to their rusting behemoths and creaking factories if they want to. But we have seen the right path, and it is paved in silicon.

Electronics truly are the way and the wave of the future; the demand for them is universal and transcends all immutable characteristics. It is time for us to take on the world, as is our right.
strings.GNG_beyond_manchukuo_tt: Let £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Manchuria recline on a throne of wrought steel and blackened soot! We have seen the future - a world defined by silicon transistors and microchips.
strings.GNG_the_getyear_tokyo_meetings_desc:
It has been a good long while since we last updated Tokyo. In fact it's been a good long while since they even checked in on us. Though we do like not being bothered by bureaucratic annoyances who have to have everything explained to them, this can't be sustained forever.

So Chief Executive Morita will pack his bags and return to Japan for the first time in a long time. Having departed in shame and ignominy he shall return in glory, the shining light and example of the Great East Asian Co-Prosperity Sphere. Or at least that's what we hope our esteemed overlords will say.
strings.GNG_the_getyear_tokyo_meetings_tt: Surely, £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Tokyo will be eager to hear of our success...
strings.GNG_business_in_nanjing_desc:
During the same time period, Li Ka-shing will go to Nanjing for business, with a view on representing Guangdong in the heartland of the Republic of China. It stands to reason that everyone will recognize that Guangdong is destined to remain firmly in place, since Cheung Kong and Sony sell just as much in China as they do anywhere else.

To ensure continued prosperity, Li will meet with his various business partners and contacts in Nanjing with a view on working out a better relationship. As China grows, Li thinks Guangdong can surely help it accelerate its progress, and gain something for itself in the meantime.
strings.GNG_business_in_nanjing_tt: ...and it would be wise to cultivate new prospects in £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China.
strings.GNG_the_coming_storm_desc:
So much can change in a decade. Such is true outside Guangdong's borders as within them.

Beyond the borders of Guangdong, transforming itself into the Pearl of the Sphere, Japan and China eye each other warily. Tokyo remains consumed with internal politics, paying less heed to our triumph than the latest crisis engulfing the Sphere at large. Our connections in China tell of furtive plans, meetings we are not invited to, that speak to larger ambitions behind China's economic revival - a political awakening, a call to arms.

As the new decade beckons and the horizon darkens, Morita and Li must make ready to meet the future - or Guangdong will be swept away by history.
strings.GNG_the_coming_storm_tt:
A new decade calls - of limitless opportunity...
...and existential crisis.
strings.GNG_steady_steps_on_an_uncertain_path: Steady Steps on an Uncertain Path
strings.GNG_a_good_workman_and_his_tools: A Good Workman and His Tools
strings.GNG_give_space_to_the_other_corporations: Give Space to the Other Corporations
strings.GNG_turn_a_blind_eye_to_our_own: Turn a Blind Eye To Our Own
strings.GNG_make_it_stable_keep_it_safe: Make It Stable, Keep It Safe
strings.GNG_chief_executive_matsushita_desc:
It is often said that men who are in possession of vast amounts of intellect prefer to avoid the glaring limelight, never taking on the reins of responsibility and authority directly, fearing the sword of Damocles, continually dangling overhead. This saying, though widely applicable, is far from gospel, as evidently demonstrated by Matsushita Masaharu.

Cunning and resourceful, and an exceptionally astute businessman, his entry into power via the puissant Matsushita family may seem like blatant nepotism to the unaware, but his calculating demeanor and pragmatic tendencies have assisted greatly in cementing his position.

Now, as the strife of the Yasuda Crisis casts its ominous and looming shadow over Guangdong, its penumbra extending far and wide, the responsibility of recuperating the shattered ruins of Guangdong's economy and workforce falls squarely on the shoulders of newly minted Chief Executive Matsushita. Visions of an efficient industrial powerhouse that was once Guangdong, a never ending upward struggle to place benefit above all else. Leaving and establishing a stable and illustrious legacy for the success of Guangdong and its everlasting institutions.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_matsushita_tt: Under Chief Executive Matsushita, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong breathes easy...
strings.GNG_becoming_a_worthy_successor_desc: The position of Chief Executive is by no means an inconsequential position, and therefore, it is naturally an extremely unstable one. In order for the Chief Executive to be able to conduct his performance assiduously and with efficiency, we first absolutely need to demonstrate to the Legislative Council that the man who currently holds the position is no weak-willed Lepidus. As such, Matsushita has planned to address the Legislative Council personally, making sure that we cement and reinforce our reputation within the administration.
strings.GNG_assessing_the_situation_desc: It is extremely apparent to everybody that Guangdong has not been faring adequately for quite some time, and the responsibility of handling the problems smoothly now falls into the hands of Chief Executive Matsushita. As such, we require clear reports and assessments of the current state of Guangdong, to determine just how deep Guangdong's issues lay. No matter what, it is necessary that this matter be elucidated before any direct action takes place in order to ensure maximum efficiency and swiftness in eliminating any trouble towards a smooth recovery.
strings.GNG_steady_steps_on_an_uncertain_path_de: The key to a stable career is a good image, something that will forge you a legacy in the annals of history. Nobody is more aware of this than Chief Executive Matsushita. In order to secure our position in the present and our memory in the future, we need to take measures for our reputation, mainly, the handling of problems, whether they are concrete or invisible. The first few years of your tenure are crucial for Matsushita, as it determines how the populace remembers him, how history remembers him, how the world remembers him.
strings.GNG_steady_steps_on_an_uncertain_path_tt: ...and Matsushita eyes a future of his own design.
strings.GNG_release_guangdongs_potential_desc:
Guangdong, before the Yasuda Crisis, was a shining star. As the nexus of corporate interests, it boasted one of the fastest growing economies in the Sphere, rivaling that of co-equal Sphere members. Alas, the Crisis struck us down from the sky, like a hunter shoots down a bird. But Guangdong is no ordinary bird: it is a Phoenix, born again in the ashes of strife, more majestic than ever. Our economy, with the right guidance, could reach newfound heights in value and growth than ever seen before.

Matsushita, our new chairman will be that guiding hand. With his control of one of the five largest companies here in Guangdong, and his connections with the rest of the corporations, Matsushita will tap into the nation's potential, and usher us into a golden age of prosperity and profit!
strings.GNG_release_guangdongs_potential_tt: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong still has so much left to offer the world - and Matsushita will leave his mark on every face of the Silicon Delta's economy.
strings.GNG_pack_them_into_the_cities_desc: The cities of Guangdong are the industrial heart of our economy, and our nation as a whole. Matsushita has ordered the government to move civilians from the countryside to urban areas, dubbing the policy “Mandatory Urbanization”. Mandatory Urbanization should increase the output of our industry to the extreme, and gives companies the chance to grow in size. Many are forced to relocate to cities against their will, and many more are outraged about seeing their friends and countrymen hauled away to work in factories. Their opinions are irrelevant, as if we would listen to the cries of a bunch of barbaric backwater peasant farmers.
strings.GNG_pack_them_into_the_cities_tt: To achieve true economies of scale, the Three Pearls will need more workers than ever before.
strings.GNG_promises_of_an_easier_life_desc: In order to encourage further immigration into the cities and keep existing residents from bewailing, we need to advertise and offer some support. Although funds are always scarce and need to be treasured, the support we'll be offering won't be substantial. Of course, news of this generosity would need to be broadcasted and showcased to the populace, the media would certainly prove to be useful in that aspect, while also not putting immense strain on the budget.
strings.GNG_on_their_own_desc: With the new influx of immigrants into the cities of Guangdong, their living conditions need to be considered. It is objectively a wiser decision to allow the workers to sustain their own livelihoods and dwellings, as not doing so will drain valuable limited resources that could easily be spent on much more important matters at hand.
strings.GNG_feed_the_extra_mouths_desc: Mandatory Urbanization has created a new problem for us: we will have fewer farmers to grow food to feed our people. Since many will be sent to work in factories, there will be less people to grow food to feed everyone. In order to make up for this loss, we have set the food quotas higher than before. Normally, this would be something that would put the financial safety of our agricultural sector at risk, but given that our farmers will use the abandoned plots and farms left by the factory workers, they can manage these new quotas. We will even help modernize and mechanize the equipment of the farmers to make their jobs even easier, but this would have to be kept quiet.
strings.GNG_feed_the_extra_mouths_tt: To keep our cities fed, we must mechanize rural agriculture into more efficient agribusinesses, even if it upends local farmers. A hungry man is both unproductive - and resentful.
strings.GNG_a_good_workman_and_his_tools_desc: Our factories here are some of the most productive in the Sphere, as they need to provide goods for much of East Asia. However, the potential of their workers is not at its full potential, since they use rudimentary tools and equipment. Modernization of factory equipment should be out top priority, since it holds the key that unlocks our full economic potential.
strings.GNG_a_good_workman_and_his_tools_tt: Our workers shall be trained in the latest tools and methods to maximize productivity.
strings.GNG_remove_restrictions_desc: The new workers being shipped in to the factories will be a great economic success. However, with all of these new laborers, we don't have enough homes for them, and with such large numbers of people we will send to the cities, we could have a real homeless crisis on our hands. The solution to this problem is rather simple: Remove regulations on construction to encourage businesses to build housing and apartments for the new workers. Our economy would benefit, and our laborers would have homes. Sure, this means the houses aren't as safe as they used to be, but living in a house that could hurt you is much better than living on the streets.
strings.GNG_remove_restrictions_tt: When we build the apartments of the future, efficiency must always be the first and foremost in our minds.
strings.GNG_urban_housing_ordinance_desc:
It is time to take our proposals to the Legislation Council. The Urban Housing Ordinance will begin Mandatory Urbanization, and also loosen housing and construction regulations to promote the building of houses for the new workers. Compiled with this bill are new quotas to be set as soon as Mandatory Urbanization starts, as well as programs that will modernize both farming and factory equipment.

If this bill passes, it will be a huge victory for the Masushita administration; If not, it may be a sign that Matsushita's plans for Guangdong will end before they even start.
strings.GNG_polish_each_pearl_desc: The Three Pearls are Guangdong's largest cities, and its most important cities too. Centers of industry, finance, and luxury (for the Japanese), the three Pearls, Honkon, Makao, and the capital Kōshū. However, as prosperous as our cities are, Matsushita sees that their glory could be taken to greater heights than ever before. Matsushita has a plan: Develop and specialize the Pearls. Kōshū's factories wil be grown to twice their sizes, and turn the capital into a center of manufacturing that could rival five cities. Honkon will be made into a hotbed of bureaucracy and financial planning, transforming it into Guangdong's nerve center. And Makao, with its luxury casinos and hotels, will become the Las Vegas of the Co-Prosperity Sphere, a businessman's paradise, and a gambling oasis the likes of which the world has never seen!
strings.GNG_assist_the_sprawling_surroundings_de: The Three Pearls are undoubtedly our greatest and sincerest pride. Brilliant, radiant cities that serve as a glowing and continuous example of economic prosperity and Guangdong's prowess in the Sphere. However, the cities certainly have issues. The poorly planned and maintained residential urban sprawl that has been allowed to spread house millions of citizens and workers, though not exactly a liability as it provides living spaces for men serving in the industry, certainly needs assistance to prevent the brewing of discontent.
strings.GNG_assist_the_sprawling_surroundings_tt: We will make token efforts to alleviate the overcrowding outside the urban centers.
strings.GNG_all_efforts_inward_desc: It is necessary for us to address the hideous blot which stains the Three Pearls, the uncontrolled and ravenous spread of the unorganized and chaotic urban sprawl. While it is too late to attempt to exterminate these sectors, as they do house millions of workers, they shall receive no resources or support from us. The funding could very easily be used alternatively in further development of the city centers, allocating it to the suburbs would be an inefficient and unnecessary waste.
strings.GNG_all_efforts_inward_tt: The future of £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong is in its cities and the urban elite - our attention will not be diverted elsewhere.
strings.GNG_efficiency_investment_ordinance_desc: Now comes the time for Matsushita to present his second bill to the legislation Council. The Efficiency Investment Ordinance Bill will secure funds for Matsushita's development of Guangdong, funds that have to be justified to the Council. The Legislation Council will need much convincing if we are to obtain the money and grants needed for Matsushita's plans. If the money we need is secured and used effectively, we will have gained the trust of many of Guangdong's industry and political leaders. If we fail, it will be all the more difficult for Matsushita to carry out his plan for the country.
strings.GNG_relentless_innovation_desc: What Guangdong needs most is innovation. Everywhere and everything has room for improvement - and we must close that gap as much as possible, whenever possible. To that end, our methods and equipment must be constantly assessed for any flaws, any inefficiencies that can be resolved. Further, we must improve our research facilities in order to maximize the potential for new innovations.
strings.GNG_relentless_innovation_tt: The future belongs to £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita, and we will brook no expense to make it so.
strings.GNG_adopt_new_subcontractors_desc: Matsushita needs to run as efficiently as possible. To this end, we have begun hiring several subcontractors to help us. However, we find ourselves at an impasse: we must choose between our current course of hiring Japanese companies, or allow select Zhujin companies in. Such a matter must be solved before we can begin collaboration with them.
strings.GNG_adopt_new_subcontractors_tt: In the pursuit of excellence, we may need to choose between local firms and outside contractors.
strings.GNG_monitor_japanese_universities_desc: Admitting Japanese students into Guangdong would surely bring many advantages that our administration needs to survive. The pace at which our technologies would develop would be increased. In addition, the arrival of these students will almost certainly shore up our approval with the Japanese elite of Guangdong - something we desperately need to be consistent at all times.
strings.GNG_evaluate_local_graduates_desc: We will choose to admit local graduates from our own universities. While many question our decision, there are many advantages to sticking to our own for future researchers. Chiefly, the quality of our research equipment will improve much more rapidly, which in turn will allow for faster advances in technology. Further, our approval with the Zhujin population will increase, for they will be the chief beneficiaries of this policy.
strings.GNG_establish_greater_connectivity_desc: The most important aspect of any business is connection. It allows for streamlined communications and transportation of goods and services, therefore, it is absolutely necessary that we invest into improving Guangdong's current infrastructure. The old dirt and stone paved roads of a bygone era simply no longer suffices for the required connections of today. These investments, though it may be costly, will surely ensure that we eventually catapult our progress above our rivals and provide us with long term profitability.
strings.GNG_a_new_sales_network_desc: It is necessary to connect to a market's consumers; as such, we must be making our products seem palatable and conducive to their needs as much as possible. To this end, we will embark on an advertisement campaign across all corners of Guangdong. Posters will line the streets, films dominate the television screens, and so much more. A hefty investment will be required at first, though our projections state that should this be successful, it will inevitably lead to higher spending and economic growth.
strings.GNG_a_new_sales_network_tt: As the economy's fortunes go, so do £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's...
strings.GNG_give_space_to_the_other_corporations: Ultimately, the benefits associated with letting the other firms profit outweigh the costs that Matsushita may miss out on. While our plans are temporarily set back with our decision, it is worth remembering that we are still in a strong position. Keeping this opportunity away from the others is needless antagonism that will cost us votes in the Legislative Council and galvanize the leaders against us.
strings.GNG_a_matsushita_appliance_in_every_home: The costs associated with letting other corporations participate in our investment are too large compared to any benefit that could be gained. Matsushita cannot afford to let other firms use this opportunity to compete - it must only be used for it, and it alone. While they may send letters of protest and frustrate our efforts wherever possible, this initiative will cement Matsushita as the leading company in Guangdong.
strings.GNG_open_up_our_natural_riches_desc: Guangdong is a land of potential and opportunities, and nowhere is that more clear than directly beneath its surface. Endless deposits of tungsten, iron and coal are stretched all across the nation, untapped riches simply waiting for adequate exploitation. It is to no doubt that the corporations of Guangdong must be approved to utilise these natural riches accordingly, and soon.
strings.GNG_keep_the_cogs_turning_desc: The economy of the nation appears to be in a consistent pattern, surge after surge, rocketing towards success. As such, it is necessary that we provide sufficient oversight, as to ensure that this new economic paradigm be allowed to continue to prosper and retain its upward course. If the economy continues to progress, we may soon begin to satisfy our ambitions of industrial growth.
strings.GNG_keep_the_cogs_turning_tt: The march of progress - and £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's corporate behemoth - stops for no one.
strings.GNG_lean_into_our_greatest_partner_desc: It is very apparent that Guangdong has been struggling monetarily for quite awhile now, to the point where in order to stabilize the budget, we need to look towards external sources of support. Japan had always nurtured us in the state's infancy, we may have to look for a bailout from our greatest partner. Undoubtedly, Japan will not be pleased initially by our request, but them accepting it is essential for the prosperity of the state, even if it means we are forced to resort to begging.
strings.GNG_lean_into_our_greatest_partner_tt: Even if £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong has righted its own ship, additional support from our backers in £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japan would make our position bulletproof.
strings.GNG_demolition_of_the_old_order_desc: The aftermath of the Yasuda Crisis had impacted everyone in Guangdong in one way or the other, and it is imperative that we safeguard the nation from ever having to suffer from a similar situation. The pre-Crisis Guangdong was very much extremely inefficient, its byzantine bureaucracy and useless legislation contributing to the anguish of the Crisis. We need to begin ridding ourselves of the structures of the past and begin anew. The process of the disposure and sale of unproductive and fruitless assets shall begin soon.
strings.GNG_demolition_of_the_old_order_tt: Round 2, and this time it will most benefit £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita. The fat and excess of the Crisis shall not prevail under our watchful eye.
strings.GNG_seizing_dead_firms_assets_desc: The Crisis left many struggling firms and businesses unable to continue under the stressful and devastating situation, and their husks now litter the streets and records of Guangdong. We will begin the confiscation of abandoned and discarded properties in order to prepare them for sale in the near future in order to raise money and keep the market in circulation.
strings.GNG_keep_control_desc: The auction for the assets is one that many have their eyes on. It has been suggested that we favor the Japanese, as it may regain support and respect lost in previous affairs.
