However, favoring them would unbalance the stability of Guangdong severely as it would remove a sizable portion of control of Guangdong's rebuilding economy from the existing Guangdong corporations.
strings.GNG_keep_control_tt:
£GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's assets are £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - and £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's - own.
This makes the £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda Auction more risky, which influences the result.
strings.GNG_favor_the_japanese_desc: Our struggle through these hardships wouldn't have lasted if not for the guidance and support of Japan. We desperately need to regain favor and respect from powers within our partner, and providing them with an advantage in the upcoming auction may be a surefire way to achieve that goal. After all, most investors are Japanese.
strings.GNG_favor_the_japanese_tt: We do the £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese a favor, and their investment in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong will multiple tenfold.
strings.GNG_manipulate_the_process_desc:
The process of righting Guangdong's finances is to be conducted via a fair and transparent bidding process, in accordance with the free market principles that have served as the foundation of Guangdong's economy since its inception. Chief Executive Matsushita is well aware of the obligations that come with his position, his own interests as CEO of Matsushita Electric in Guangdong notwithstanding.

It also has always been true that the bending of the public interest to serve private ends is a firmly established practice in Guangdong - allowing Yasuda's political and economic influence to grow like a cancerous growth in the years preceding its collapse. While Matsushita is eager to avoid the steps of Yasuda's downfall, he is not so devoted to principles to easily forgo an opportunity to shore up his political and competitive position by making sure Matsushita holds the best assets at the end of the auction...
strings.GNG_avoid_unnecessary_risks_desc: If we decide to engage in the 'local tradition' of Guangdong's politics, then we must assume that our enemies - our esteemed competition - will do the same to us. They will be watching our every move, and tipping the scales of our first major initiative as Chief Executive to our advantage will not go unnoticed. We would be risking our political position, so tenuous to begin with in the face of Sony and Fujitsu, when we will undoubtedly have better opportunities in the future - and we will not tempt fate. We will maintain a level playing field for the auction, aside from taking advantage of any easy opportunities that present themselves.
strings.GNG_avoid_unnecessary_risks_tt: Better to take our share than be caught being too greedy.
strings.GNG_take_all_we_can_desc: Our position in Guangdong's executive gives us myriad opportunities to tip the balance of the seized asset auction in our favor - a full accounting of the assets' value, their operations, and what synergies they could present for Matsushita Electric. All that needs to be done is to feed this information from the government back to the directors at Matsushita, while directing the auctioneers to prioritize Matsushita's access to the juiciest of assets available at the 'best' price. Where the other corporations see a junkyard filled with the rusting scrap of dying firms, we see boundless opportunities to turn lead into gold - all beneath our competition's notice.
strings.GNG_take_all_we_can_tt:
It's only natural to take what we can - anyone else would do so in our position. Unless we fail...
This makes the £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda Auction more risky, which influences the result.
strings.GNG_sell_sell_sell_desc: All the investigative accounting has been completed, the legal paperwork for the title transfers complete. We will open the bidding for the assets seized in the aftermath of the Yasuda Collapse, taking the expense of maintaining the dead embers of Yasuda off of the state's books and allowing the corporations best positioned to make use of them to breathe life back into the economy. It is the truest expression of the capitalist metabolism, the lifecycle of capital, and it is time for it to take its course - and Guangdong's coffers will receive a much-needed shot in the arm.
strings.GNG_sell_sell_sell_tt: We shall sell what remains of £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda's empire - and hope that £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita comes out on top.
strings.GNG_resolving_future_insolvencies_desc: If the devastation left in the wake of Yasuda's collapse has made one thing clear, it is that the laws and regulations governing the resolution of bankrupt companies are dangerously outdated, leaving the carcasses of dead firms rotting in Guangdong's economic ecosystem for months on end. Every day an insolvent firm clings to life without recourse to restructuring or a financial bailout is a day that capital is diverted from the most productive sectors of the economy, and our bankruptcies must be rewritten to this end.
strings.GNG_resolving_future_insolvencies_tt: A cleaner bankruptcy code will benefit everyone - and allow us to collect our share as quickly as possible.
strings.GNG_leniency_towards_the_people_desc: Statistically speaking, the small and medium-sized enterprises in Guangdong are the most likely to face bankruptcy when faced with difficult times - often without access to legal advice or adequate protections when creditors come calling. Though it may not be the most 'efficient' in terms of promoting economies of scale with the largest corporations in Guangdong, we will ensure that the voices of the smaller entrepreneurs are heard as we draft our new insolvency regulations.
strings.GNG_leniency_towards_the_people_tt: We will give smaller businesses their say in how business should be run.
strings.GNG_ensure_corporate_interests_are_heard: The largest and most influential voices in Guangdong have, and always will be, the largest of its corporate titans. They alone have the economic and legal expertise to ensure that the rewriting of Guangdong's insolvency regulations are efficient and maximally effective in keeping business moving. For the sake of the economy - and our continued working relationship with the business titans of Guangdong - we will cooperate with the major corporations on insolvency regulations, even if the smaller business owners suffer for it.
The interest of the Five Companies must always come first.
strings.GNG_pass_the_amendments_desc: The draft amendments to Guangdong's archaic insolvency legislation are ready for debate in the Legislative Council. Nobody would disagree with the need for some kind of amendment to these laws, and Matsushita has made sure to canvass the business community beforehand to secure their support. Passing this legislation will be an early signal of how capable we are of bending the Legislative Council to our will.
strings.GNG_pass_the_amendments_tt: Matsushita isn't the only actor with an interest in insolvency legislation...
strings.GNG_toward_financial_independence_desc:
For all the benefits of our close relationship with Tokyo, the recent crisis has made it quite clear that our close association with Japan can be as much a curse as it is a blessing. The struggle to procure the needed financing to make up for our budget shortfalls being but the most prominent example.

Now in power, Matsushita will ensure that such embarrassments will never again come to trouble Guangdong. The first step in this long road will be asserting our financial independence. The task will not be easy, but failure is not an option if we are to see Guangdong prosper.
strings.GNG_ensure_a_healthy_budget_desc:
A balanced budget is a healthy budget. While Suzuki and his cronies may have thought it wise to spend Yen like water, it is up to us to clean the mess they have created.

It will not be an easy task. Years of deficit spending has left everyone with their own golden gooses and sacred cows, and we will need to tread carefully to keep our majority and balance the budget. Cut too many cows, and raise too many taxes, and may we yet find ourselves in a rather similar position to our former Chief Executive.
strings.GNG_ensure_a_healthy_budget_tt: Everyone will be pleased with a balanced budget - and we will never repeat Suzuki's follies.
strings.GNG_cut_wasteful_spending_desc:
Our predecessors have seen fit to commit government funding to many unnecessary programs, especially initiatives designed to assist Guangdong's working-class. Such programs may have been defensible in better fiscal times but are prime examples of the sort of frivolous spending which got into this mess in the first place.

Funding for these programs will have to be cut if our budgetary shortfalls are to be resolved. We must tread carefully to avoid provoking too much unrest among Guangdong's workers, while also taking crucial steps to bring our budget back into the black.
strings.GNG_find_new_income_sources_desc:
An enormous amount of capital is produced and exchanged in Guangdong every single day, but the government receives little of the wealth it helps create. While this may have been tolerable in better times, it remains a wholly unsatisfactory state of affairs.

If we are to bring our budget back into balance certain - unpopular - steps will have to be taken. Taxes will have to be raised to generate badly needed revenue.
strings.GNG_settling_up_to_the_zaibatsu_desc: It is well known that we have been struggling to find acceptable deals with the Japanese government directly, and so, it is necessary for us to conduct an alternative path that may better serve our interests. We have arranged meetings with several Japanese bankers, representatives of the Zaibatsu, in hopes of establishing suitable agreements about possible investments in Guangdong that would be a boon to our budget.
strings.GNG_settling_up_to_the_zaibatsu_tt: If consistent support from the £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese government is too much to ask for, then we better get as much as we can from the £GNG_expats_texticon bankers, instead.
strings.GNG_appropriate_stakeholder_returns_desc: With the influx of investors attracted to Guangdong, we need to ensure that they are satisfied with their decisions. Therefore, we need to guarantee their profits, convincing them that their investments were fruitful, which may make them consider more beneficial long term investments. The issue is squarely on where the profits will be gathered from, currently we can only scrounge up excess funds from whatever opportunity appears, but at least the investors are happy.
strings.GNG_appropriate_stakeholder_returns_tt: We will ensure our £GNG_expats_texticon investors are paid what they are owed, even if it means dipping into our pockets elsewhere...
strings.GNG_paying_their_fair_share_desc:
Guangdong's Corporations are undoubtedly some of the biggest beneficiaries of our vibrant markets, yet we receive little in the way of revenues from these Corporate Giants. Tapping into this source of wealth would go a long way towards bringing our budget back in a solvent state, if at a cost.

Certain... steps will be taken to encourage the Corporations to pay their share, lest they find their business impeded by regulatory oversights and overzealous inspectors. It goes without saying that this will not go over well with the Corporations, and our support in the Council will surely suffer.
strings.GNG_paying_their_fair_share_tt: Ultimately, we will ask the other corporations to put in their fair share. Why should £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita bear all the costs of governance?
strings.GNG_matsushita_payingfairshare_trigger: We have decided that the Five Companies must pay their dues for our shared prosperity.
strings.GNG_guarantee_their_investment_desc: No matter what, we need to ensure that the investors receive their profits. It is the only hope Guangdong has to recover the budget. It may signal direct interference with the economy and the market, but we should do all that is necessary to back up their investments. Eventually, all of Guangdong will benefit from the long term prosperity despite short term harms that will result from this endeavor.
strings.GNG_guarantee_their_investment_tt: We will guarantee investors more control over their investments in £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - on the condition they support our political endeavors, even if they hold more sway over the economy.
strings.GNG_go_all_in_desc:
We have made significant progress in wooing investors back to Guangdong, but there are still... ways we can further lure investors to Guangdong's shores.

While certainly underhanded, we can quietly divert additional funds from our banks towards enticing investors and offering increased returns on their investments. After all, the better the dividends, the more investors. Of course, if our indiscretions were somehow discovered and publicized, the blowback will be... immense.
strings.GNG_matsushita_goallin_trigger: We have chosen to ensure Guangdong's fiscal balance through less transparent means.
strings.GNG_starting_to_separate_desc: Though we have developed past the need for reliance on the Japanese government in Tokyo, we now find ourselves entangled in a web of loans and investments from our Japanese banking benefactors. In order for us to be able to develop our economy and fill the treasury, we must cooperate with the banks, who hopefully will be more equitable and candid than our previous backers.
strings.GNG_starting_to_separate_tt: £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's finances are secure - one way or another.
strings.GNG_addressing_the_legislative_council_d: The Legislative Council, the glistening gilded pillar upon which the state is held, the bedrock of authority that guides and supports Guangdong, is something that is absolutely not to be ignored or neglected. Though it is evident that we, Matsushita, hold a copious amount of sway and are the dominating corporation, the other corporations of the Council are nevertheless present in Guangdong's administration and economy. It is required that we take notice of the concerns and issues of the other corporations, as this act will further seal Matsushita's position as the center of the Council, something we imperatively need to prove.
strings.GNG_ensure_matsushita_dominance_desc: No matter how critical or important the roles of the other corporations in the Legislative Council may be, it is essential that we remain the undisputed central force. Therefore, it is crucial that we begin to expand our extensive influence even further. The acquisition of vacated properties, expansion of production into other markets and a robust and vigorous show of force in the Council itself may all be necessary steps towards the entrenchment of Matsushita's dominance on the ever-competitive economic stage of Guangdong. While the other corporations are engaging in trifling squabbles, we shall seize the advantage. It is best for us not to delay and waste precious time, as it is the key to our success.
strings.GNG_ensure_matsushita_dominance_tt: ...and you can never have too much of it.
strings.GNG_monitoring_the_councils_corruption_d: Corruption. An abominable, heinous blot in Guangdong's administration, running rampant throughout the Legislative Council ever since the tenureship of Suzuki Teiichi. It has thoroughly integrated itself into the Council through the years, cash finding its way into the pockets, wallets and coffers of the most unremarkable secretary to the highest echelons of corporate offices. With such an integrated cancer, it is impossible to rid ourselves of it at once, but we can begin to monitor its spread and begin minor attempts to eventually stamp it out. Increased penalties for noticed corruption and the rooting out of certain persons known for corruption would serve as a fine beginning, as it would benefit our budget by making governance cheaper in general, and it would affect the other companies a lot more than ours...
strings.GNG_monitoring_the_councils_corruption_t: A show of decency, to make the world go round.
strings.GNG_turn_a_blind_eye_to_our_own_desc: Although corruption is undoubtedly a detestable and terrible vice that grips the offices and chambers of the Legislative Council, it has become severely ingrained into the culture of the Council and its daily affairs. If we were to indeed move against all corruption, it would be a futile task that would continuously drain our already strained monetary reserves. It would also appear that many employees of Matsushita also indulge in the dreadful act, but striking against our own men would only serve to destabilize the central authority and unity of Guangdong. It is therefore best to set the issue of our own men aside and focus on more efficient methods of destroying the plague, Matsushita needs to endure.
strings.GNG_turn_a_blind_eye_to_our_own_tt: No holds barred, for power is its own reward.
strings.GNG_placate_the_opposition_desc: Though our goals ultimately include absolute control and domination of the Legislative Council, it would remain quite a challenging feat. Currently, the corporations of the Council still hold increasing amounts of influence, and directly challenging the bloc of opposition would be a foolish and disastrous decision. In order to maintain our current position, we'll have to appease the other corporations, or at least do so on paper. We will grant them limited leverage and powers in the Council, surely enough to comfort much of the representatives. Rest assured, these minor concessions are temporary measures to ensure that resistance doesn't stiffen against us, and can and will be changed accordingly.
strings.GNG_placate_the_opposition_tt: ...having too much paints a target on your back.
strings.GNG_promises_for_the_moderate_executives: Within the mire of opinions and ideologies of the Legislative Council, a growing passel of corporate executives have developed viewpoints that are foreign to a sizable portion of Guangdong's existing corporate realm. These “moderates”, who have adopted beliefs contradictory to the prevailing status quo, rallying against what they deem “exploitation”, most of whom are part of or linger around Morita Akio and Sony. Though they may seem like overly-sentimental bleeding hearts, their support would be a great asset towards ensuring that our position as head of the Council is maintained, and to keep them satisfied as to not cause any unnecessary agitation. Chief Executive Matsushita will personally arrange a meeting with them, hopefully some promises and honeyed words will do.
To acknowledge frustrations is no weakness.
strings.GNG_adherence_to_the_status_quo_desc: Though it may seem that reform is very much necessary to maintain the turning of the cogs of Guangdong's economy, it is hardly the whole truth. Reform requires a considerable amount of invested time and desired funds, with the outcome usually being unsatisfactory and benefits minimal. It is therefore apparent that large scale reform is unnecessary and not advantageous to our current position, the clear path forward is to adhere to the established status quo, a significantly less daunting and simpler task that would sufficiently benefit our standings in the Legislative Council, dominated by conservatives. We shall ensure that the existing circumstances are upheld, with full assurances granted to the conservative executives in the Council.
strings.GNG_an_independent_body_desc: It is time to address the long overdue issue of corruption, the tumor that festers in the deepest sections of Guangdong's core apparatus, draining it of vital funds and workplace efficacy. After much deliberation, it is apparent that the wiser option would be to assemble an anti-corruption body free of the influence of any of the corporations of Guangdong, an assembly that will determine each case with equal judgment. This system would be impartial and efficient, but also cleanses us of any potential accusations of controlling a marionette. Though this will impact Matsushita correspondingly, it doesn't mean that once the issue is over and exterminated, we won't be the ultimate beneficiaries, it is a blow we must endure.
strings.GNG_an_independent_body_tt: Long-term trust is built through equal and consistent application of the law - such as it exists.
strings.GNG_maintain_our_influence_desc: Corruption is a disease that saps and tarnishes every corporation equally, it knows nothing of justice or discipline. For the benefit of all of Guangdong, we must assume the mantle of the battle against this vile beast, a body of professionals selected precariously and painstakingly by Matsushita, to ensure maximum efficiency in their labors. The opposition may cry and rant that this is merely a ploy to extend our own influence over the Council, that the body will not be impartial and judge without bias, which may perhaps be true, but for the greater good of the livelihoods of millions of Guangdong's citizens and the economic stability of the state, it is best we proceed with the arrangements.
strings.GNG_maintain_our_influence_tt: The law is a tool - and we trust nobody to wield it but Ourselves.
strings.GNG_corruption_investigation_ordinance_d: After enduring through the several onerous and arduous objectives involved, we've finally reached the discussion of pivotal and of the utmost importance. The previous arrangements and procedures currently are nothing but a series of unreinforced proposals, and in order to truly initiate the struggle against nefarious practices and compose the anti-corruption body, our designs must be realized through a simple vote. If we manage to secure the vote in our favor, this will guarantee a substantial shift in Guangdong's administrative structure, and as we hope, a shift to our benefit.
strings.GNG_initiate_executive_reinforcement_des: A satisfied worker is a productive worker, one of the essential tenets of human resources management and necessary for an efficient workforce. This fact has been recognized by us and certain predecessors, leading to an array of legislated workers' rights, rights being strictly defined, of course. Though they are officially legislation, they are barely recognized or even acknowledged by a sizable portion of the operating businesses and industries of Guangdong. Not only is this a blow to worker productivity, it perceives our administration as weak and incapable of enforcement of our own policies, which is unacceptable. Matsushita, with his position as Chief Executive, will begin to crack down on non-compliers, largely with hefty fines. Compliance is obligatory.
strings.GNG_initiate_executive_reinforcement_tt: The push for a safer - and more productive - workforce must come from the top down, regardless of political costs. If we bring everyone down to our level, then the playing field is leveled regardless.
strings.GNG_clamp_down_on_the_loopholes_desc: The rampant disregard for the policies laid down by the Legislative Council and Matsushita is unquestionably and utterly unacceptable and needs an appropriate and decisive response. Necessary enforcement and crackdowns have to be executed in order for the image of administrative and Matsushita control to retain its weight. Punishments akin to fines and governmental embargoes will be issued if continued resistance against the law is documented, making it impossible for the corporations to ignore our presence and legislation for any longer, no matter the nature of the response.
strings.GNG_the_corporations_know_best_desc: As much as we would like to be able to exercise complete authority over the various corporations of Guangdong, we have to accept that they are independent entities with their own bases of power, it is impossible for us to demand too much from them, not to mention that they are ultimately our centers of support. Undoubtedly, if we push too far with demands, they will fiercely defend their commitment to profit, and would only serve to diminish the influence of our faction and the Chief Executive.
strings.GNG_the_corporations_know_best_tt: Without the other corporations' buy in, any push to trade safety for productivity will come to a dead halt, and leave £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Electronics at a disadvantage.
strings.GNG_legislate_corporate_self_regulation_: It is abundantly clear the many corporations across Guangdong do not consent to our so-called “meddling” in their workplace priorities, to that, we say so be it. We shall pass legislation that will force the corporations to regulate themselves without the constant inspection of government agents. We also have to acknowledge that our extent of influence is limited, with the amount of factories and businesses residing in the economic market of Guangdong, imposing self-regulation would be a step towards exercising efficient government authority.
strings.GNG_our_sense_of_duty_desc: The media of Guangdong is a power that is to be harnessed and exploited, its exposure of messaging is unrivalled in the urban jungles of the Three Pearls and beyond. In order for our administration to be respected, we must spread the word about our innate benevolence and the gifts that we have brought onto the populace of Guangdong, however true that may be. We can coerce the media into displaying policy that we have enforced that may contribute to the betterment of working conditions, let the word of our consideration be known across the factories and workplaces of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_the_least_we_can_offer_desc: Reform on the matter of the satisfaction of workers has been circulating around in the administration for quite awhile now, but has never been put to practice. As much as we doubt the necessity of such reforms and changes, it is clear that there is a sizable force backing it. Matsushita will pass reforms, though they will be minor and guaranteed to not affect the sustainability of the corporations and industries of Guangdong that thrive on the current conditions of the workforce. Undoubtedly, workers will be somewhat content with the privileges granted to them and give our administration their partial support, as well as retaining popularity within the corporate executive circles of the Council, or at least not severely damaging it.
strings.GNG_the_least_we_can_offer_tt: Will add the Least We Can Offer amendment when we will introduce the £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Limited Labor Standards Ordinance, which grants following effects for the ordinance:
strings.GNG_honest_pay_for_honest_work_desc: As often discussed within Matsushita's inner circles, reform is not a necessity in order for an economy and nation to survive. As such, we see no reason to instate unnecessary burdens upon our reputation in the Council, especially to the conservative executives. Instead of unwanted and unneeded workplace reform, we shall simply offer the workers extra beneficial pay if they voluntarily work longer hours. This will obviously satisfy the executives, as well as please the workers, at least, hopefully.
strings.GNG_honest_pay_for_honest_work_tt: Will add the Honest Pay amendment when we will introduce the £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Limited Labor Standards Ordinance., which will grant following effects for the ordinance:
strings.GNG_limited_labor_standards_ordinance_de: A few short years ago, Chief Executive Suzuki Teiichi implemented and successfully passed the magnum opus of his tenureship, the Revised Labor Standards Ordinance, an ambitious piece of legislation that would bring sweeping change to the workplace environments and standards of the manufacturing plants of Guangdong. As we can see now, the RLSO was incredibly over-lenient, and far too extensive for what it's trying to accomplish, which rightfully led to the man's downfall. We shall not make such a naive mistake. Our reform bill would be limited in its changes, but still contain enough to be called such, and it needs to be at least demonstrated and shown in front of the Legislative Council, for the sake of our image and longevity.
strings.GNG_ease_the_tensions_desc:
The longstanding tensions between the Japanese, the Zhujin, and the Chinese have expectedly escalated over time, with the self-proclaimed “downtrodden” demanding increased rights to educational resources and political representation. While never dramatically exacerbated by our policies, such matters nonetheless require our immediate attention, lest ethnic conflicts arise and critically disrupt Guangdong's day-to-day operations.

Naturally, any issue involving our fundamental societal structure warrants close deliberation. We can choose to maintain our current course, or we can attempt to placate the marginalized ethnic groups with at least minimal reforms. Neither is expected to incur drastic consequences in the short term, but we must display commitment to our common citizenry all the same.
strings.GNG_ease_the_tensions_tt: We will address the timebomb of ethnic discord with the means that are available and feasible...
strings.GNG_keep_them_in_their_place_desc:
Who is to say our administrative model will not retain its efficiency and serve us well for the foreseeable future, when it has already wonderfully done so since Guangdong's inception?

The Chinese were excluded from government halls back then; it certainly would not be overly detrimental to exclude them now, and petty squabbles aren't enough justification for upsetting the established administrative order and agitating our benefactors from the Home Islands. The “downtrodden” can expect us to grant them certain token positions with utmost generosity, and nothing more.
strings.GNG_keep_them_in_their_place_tt: ...but at a time at our choosing, and for the sake of good governance and profit, that time is not now.
strings.GNG_open_up_the_bureaucracy_desc:
While we may feel tempted to disregard recent reports, we cannot deny they have indeed brought to light certain regrettable deficiencies within our administrative model - deficiencies regarding ethnic inequalities which are susceptible to exploitation by dissidents, ever the threat to our domestic stability.

We shall make a gesture of “answering” the calls of our citizens and begin gradually lifting restrictions from Chinese entry into existing institutions, ground-level and no higher, if only as a publicity maneuver. We can only hope our appeasement will satiate the greed of the lowly for the time being.
strings.GNG_open_up_the_bureaucracy_tt: ...and if we open up the lower levels of the bureaucracy to the £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese, they won't be as eager to burn it to the ground.
strings.GNG_extend_education_desc: Recent discourse has alerted us to yet another noteworthy issue: Guangdong's schools have been somewhat lacking in inclusivity, potentially resulting in the shrinkage and eventual exhaustion of professor and student pools. Regardless of our stance on previous related matters, an expansion and total renovation of Guangdong's educational institutions is in order, if we truly wish to nurture a new generation of innovators who may assist in the expansion of our manufacturing capabilities and the maintenance of our unmatched technological prowess in the foreseeable future.
strings.GNG_extend_education_tt: A smart worker is a productive worker. It just makes economic sense.
strings.GNG_manipulate_the_government_desc: As of now, there are no laws that separate a corporation and the state. This means that members of companies can be public officials and still work for a corporation. Matsushita technically can appoint members of the Matsushita Electric Company on his cabinet and other roles within the government, granting the company enormous amounts of power. While it is not illegal to do this, many in the Legislative Council would protest and fight this move to the bitter end, considering how it gives one corporation a major advantage over all the others.
strings.GNG_manipulate_the_government_tt: £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita sits in the highest seat of government. Why can't £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita men sit in all the seats below him?
strings.GNG_fuse_with_the_state_desc:
The fate of our great nation depends on how well we can govern over it, and with our economy in desperate need of recovery, there remains only one option left - to merge the Matsushita firm with the government at all available opportunities.

In doing this, our scope in the administration over the Pearl River Delta will expand significantly, as we integrate the private army of bureaucrats and secretaries to manage and regulate the country's resources.

There is no doubt, once we usher in this new economic order, that we will be making grim enemies with the opposition. However, as rival hatred turns ever-bitter, our grasp over Guangdong will tighten, and prospects of recovery will shine over the horizon.
strings.GNG_fuse_with_the_state_tt: £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita is the state; both in person, and in body.
strings.GNG_overcome_the_temptation_desc:
The cards are on the table, and with the best interests of the nation in mind, the only rational way forward is to keep from merging state ties to the firm. Whilst it may immediately seem to benefit our administration, it would only be a shot in the foot, making enemies of virtually everyone else in the Legislative Council.

Some would call it a missed opportunity, but what's done is done; the firm will stay some distance from our administration, whilst we bide our time and find other ways to secure our position.
strings.GNG_make_it_stable_keep_it_safe_desc:
Although the government and the Legislative Council has full authority over Guangdong, there are forces throughout the Pearl River Delta with dark motives and desires. Lurking in the shadows, often in places one would least expect, these unknown forces are likely to try and damage our authority over the nation.

It's a tough challenge, trying to tackle these risks, but they will be much easier to face with a stable and loyal government under our control. Underground crime and malevolent influences constantly redefine how we are to manage governance, but with a determined cabinet and loyal bureaucracy, no challenge can be too great.
strings.GNG_make_it_stable_keep_it_safe_tt: The interests of £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita are the interests of the £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon state. Nobody can tell us otherwise, and we will do anything to make sure it stays that way.
strings.GNG_treat_the_epidemic_desc:
Every year since the birth of Guangdong, hundreds of dissatisfied salarymen and wage laborers would opt to terminate their own lives, leaping off skyscrapers or hanging themselves on chandeliers. Some may have come to dismiss such a sight as negligible normalcy; this is, unquestionably, a dangerous misconception. It is imperative that our administration truthfully recognize the so-called “suicide epidemic” as a persistent blight upon our society, having only intensified in its contamination and erosion of our financial and industrial institutions whilst we grew preoccupied with other matters.

Token construction of suicide nets around high-risk areas will suffice no longer. More drastic measures with regard to worker suicides have already been slated for approval, and Chief Executive Matsushita shall lead in the excision of this cancerous tumor once and for all.
strings.GNG_treat_the_epidemic_tt: Dying workers - by their own hand, no less - is a catastrophe for the bottom line and for optics. To the extent it does not unduly burden our companies, we will request this be corrected.
strings.GNG_dont_worry_desc:
As per the principles of pathology, it is the root of a particular disease, not its superficial symptoms, that requires precise identification and elimination; and the crux of Guangdong's cancer, it appears, is the blatant lack of household safety provisions, with substantially greater numbers of open balconies and open courtyards than acceptable - practically encouraging demotivated workers to engage in suicidal behaviors.

And deliver the remedy we will. We shall channel the planning and construction expertise of our corporations and commence comprehensive urban renovation projects, which will entail total elimination of building openings as well as expansion of suicide net systems. If only those supposedly depressed “rejects” from our society would understand we are doing this for their own good, and that of Guangdong as a whole.
strings.GNG_dont_worry_tt: The easiest solution is to secure the factory windows - and we will pay to make sure this happens.
strings.GNG_be_happy_desc:
As per the principles of pathology, physiological immune deficiencies weakens the body against even the most trivial of ailments; and Guangdong's mental immunity, it appears, has been long compromised by the unrestricted circulation of narcotics and depressants both within and between various social strata, rendering our citizens excessively vulnerable to psychological disturbances and resulting suicidal tendencies.

Our vaccine for Guangdong's disease, therefore, shall be the total isolation of its populace from such harmful substances, realized via direct supervision and regulation of pharmaceutical manufacturers and retailers. Such measures will effectively eradicate the crippling negativity infecting the workforce, and finally steer Guangdong one degree closer towards diligence and prosperity.
strings.GNG_be_happy_tt: We should not let our workers have the choice to sleep forever; much can be done while awake, and our doctors are just as good as medicine.
strings.GNG_environmental_standards_desc:
It would appear that our struggle against one of Guangdong's worst maladies has enlightened us to the severity of another - the immense deterioration of overall environmental quality as evidenced by increases in toxic materials within Guangdong's air and water supply, a natural consequence of unsupervised industrial outpour.

Chief Executive Matsushita shall contact the worst offenders in this regard and initiate negotiations on emission regulation, as a reiteration of our preference for a sustainable production model capable of elevating environmental standards and therefore Guangdong's quality of life, rather than degrade them to the point of irreparability.
strings.GNG_environmental_standards_tt: There is no need for us to be actively harming our workers through emissions - only the bare minimum required.
strings.GNG_safe_and_sound_desc:
Guangdong is the land of freedom of prosperity, but if we are to take pride in a stable society in which our citizenry can enjoy these natural rights, it is of the utmost importance that we organize a strong security presence throughout the Delta.

From dissidents recruiting in the city backstreets, to officials taking bribes in the shadows of government buildings, the state must wield the authority to regiment the disorderly and pacify the rebellious so that law and order can guarantee the peace and security so desirable in our great nation. If we are to be fair, and if we are to be free, we must punish the wicked so that wealth may flow down the lifeline of our great nation.
strings.GNG_safe_and_sound_tt: Stabilizing the security situation - in £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's own image and style - will be critical for ensuring our own survival.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_hide_desc:
Under-the-table dealing, the 'disappearance of funds', shady favors - corruption is deeply ingrained in almost every practice in Guangdong. From the colossal business interests operating in the country, to the shady bureaucrats working in every tier of government, there is always someone paying another for a way around the law.

This great web of corruption makes governance extremely expensive, and at times ineffective. It is in our best interests to attack this culture of corruption wherever it is found, in the hopes we can build up our power for an even stronger administrative influence.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_hide_tt: Those guilty of £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon corruption have nothing to fear...
strings.GNG_unmask_the_worst_offenders_desc:
With the corrosive influence of corruption spilling over our efforts of administration, rotting the very institutions that guide our citizenry to prosperity, we cannot hope to truly remove corruption unless we strike at its source - from the wealthiest, most influential echelons of society.

As such, we deem it necessary that we employ a top-down approach to managing our investigation into corruption charges. Let us set an example, by cutting the head off the snake and eliminating the most corrupt of our society first.
strings.GNG_unmask_the_worst_offenders_tt: ...but we will make an example of the worst offenders, to be replaced by our loyal company men.
strings.GNG_bribe_our_way_in_desc:
If we are to be successful in uprooting the most secretive criminals in Guangdong from their shadowy practices, we too must get our hands dirty. Bribing is not only comparatively cheap, it is also consistently effective, as a means of forcing our way into criminal circles.

It is a necessary evil to some, but one that will not compromise our determination to uncover the extent of corruption across the Pearl River Delta. Dirt and blood under Guangdong's nails is by no means a new occurrence, but perhaps this is the last time we plunge our hands into the fraudulent muck of public malfeasance.
strings.GNG_bribe_our_way_in_tt:
The remaining have proven their loyalties can be bought - £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita simply needs to offer them a better deal.
This doctrine will impact our investigation on £GNG_triads_texticon Stanley Ho and £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yokoi Hideki.
strings.GNG_authorize_kenpeitai_raids_desc: Under a variety of circumstances, the most efficient, undemanding and viable solution to an issue is not with careful management or arrangements, but simply the insurmountable and vigorous power of forceful authority. Of the many assets we have access to, the Kenpeitai is a particularly formidable one, and one that we can certainly utilise to eliminate the problem of corruption. We will direct the Kenpeitai to several locations where marked suspects of sizable scale corruption were recorded to dwell or operate in, offices, homes, warehouses, and attempt to locate tangible and definitive proof of their undoubtedly vile corrupt acts.
strings.GNG_authorize_kenpeitai_raids_tt:
And for the rest, the £GNG_police_texticon Police and the £GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai can have them.
This doctrine will impact our investigation on £GNG_triads_texticon Stanley Ho and £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yokoi Hideki.
strings.GNG_spring_the_trap_desc:
Our efforts to uncover evidence of corruption in the highest levels of government have turned out to be very fruitful. We now have more than enough evidence to implicate two very prominent, and dangerous, members of Guangdong's criminal underworld. Stanley Ho and Yokoi Hideki have been nothing more than scourges on our internal security, there is little doubt that many will be glad to see them taken down a peg or two.

However, they both still hold on to enough power to make any attempt at capturing them incredibly dangerous. If they are to be caught, we must act carefully to limit the chaos they obviously want to cause.
strings.GNG_spring_the_trap_tt: No man shall stand above Matsushita - not even Stanley Ho or Yokoi Hideki.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_the_other_corporations_desc:
We must now turn our attention on to the other corporations, who are just as guilty of widespread corruption as the criminal underworld. These are powerful men, but one way or another our vigilant oversight must be felt by them there will be no room for their harmful practices.

This corporate corruption crisis has gone on for too long and ends now. Their power over our government will be removed.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_the_other_corporations_tt: The other corporations will fall in line under our watchful eye, even if our own men protest at being watched like hawks.
strings.GNG_start_at_the_roots_desc:
Barging in, head-first, on the criminal business practices of some of the most powerful men in Guangdong is not only an ineffective strategy, but also has the potential to damage our own legitimacy and even endanger officials throughout the nation.

Instead, it is in our best interests to focus on discouraging, investigating, and rooting-out corruption on the ground by chasing down those in the open. Not only will this make some aspects of administration more efficient in the long term, but also implicitly let the more influential criminals know that their days are numbered.
strings.GNG_start_at_the_roots_tt: £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon Corruption is a swamp - it festers if even one drop remains, and it must be drained entirely.
strings.GNG_anti_vice_supervisors_in_the_police_:
Some believe that every policeman in Guangdong can be bought, if you have the money. In fact the root of most of the police's inefficiency and unreliability can be found in the extent of corruption amongst the officers. None of them can be deemed innocent for certain.

The culture of corruption amidst the security forces will have to end if we are to maintain control of the people, and an extension of surveillance over the force will no doubt achieve this.
£GNG_police_texticon The police - and our own men within it - must be beyond reproach.
strings.GNG_monitor_low_ranking_bureaucracts_des:
Corruption has of course been a problem throughout the government, from the highest minister to the lowest bureaucrat. It is so wide spread that dealing with the entirety of the system at once is simply out of the question.

Instead we must target our resources at the lower levels of the government's structure, the rest will have to be dealt with at some other time.
strings.GNG_monitor_low_ranking_bureaucracts_tt: £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon Corruption may be a 'petty' crime at the lower levels - and we must eradicate this notion if we ever want a clean government.
strings.GNG_admonish_the_perpetrators_desc: Those within the government who have been found guilty of accepting bribes will be condemned in as servere a manner as possible. All those who work for us must be made aware of what happens to corrupt officials and that they are no longer tolerated. The harsher the condemnation of these perpetrators, the less likely the rest will follow and the cleaner our government will become.
strings.GNG_expand_the_punishments_desc:
Words alone will not remove the worst of the bureaucrats' culture. More repercussions will have to face any corrupt members of the establishment. Anything from large fines to imprisonment must be considered to dissuade them.

These measures are severe, but they will need to be if we are to change such a deeply ingrained part of the bureaucracy.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_fear_desc:
An adequate and skillful police force is the cornerstone of enforcement and maintenance in a truly successful nation, it is an ambition that many strive for, but alas, it is easier said than done, and this task will be extremely burdensome and demanding. The current police force of Guangdong is an affront to and a demonstration against the authority of the administration. Dating back to before the Yasuda Crisis, and only being exacerbated by the event, the police force had been and still undeniably is woefully under-equipped and undermanned, and absolutely unsuitable for its exacting task of the pacification of the clutter and chaos of Guangdong's ever busy streets.

In order for the police force to truly become a capable tool of imposition and pacification, plenty of effort and funds will be required, as to change the pitiful reality of our current “protectors of the nation”.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_fear_tt: We cannot rely on £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon incentives and the underworld alone to do our job for us. The £GNG_police_texticon police - and £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's grip on the institution - must be strengthened.
strings.GNG_strongly_built_desc:
A building with a lackluster foundation, no matter how opulent or magnificent it becomes, will eventually and inevitably collapse. The police force will have to be utterly ripped apart and retrained from the bottom up, its officers will be drilled and worked intensely as to ensure that they proficiently understand and are able to recount as well as perform the procedures for the enforcement of policies and laws and methods of handling dissent and violence.

Before the training is able to begin however, we must first address the decadent excess that has gathered around the police force, completely incapable personnel leaching off of the resources of the administration. These elements will be assuredly and swiftly eliminated, as there is no room for incompetence in an efficient and productive force.
strings.GNG_promote_corporate_security_firms_des: The state of Guangdong operates from the willpower and desires of its populace, the millions of consumers who allow the economy to fluctuate and function. With the abundance of buyers, various unique markets have appeared throughout the Three Pearls. One type of these firms dedicated to satiating the needs of the population are the independent security services, benefiting off of the general fear rampant throughout the streets. The security services are well-equipped and trained, and certainly would be more than willing to lend us their support for a feasible price, which would provide considerable assistance to our currently waning and lackluster police force. Though this may help bolster our forces, we have to acknowledge that these services are operated by private corporations, and would only contribute to our dependency upon them.
strings.GNG_enforce_higher_standards_desc: Due to a prolonged period of neglect from our predecessors, the Guangdong Police Force has grown apathetic and dilatory. Though we have implemented significantly more demanding and stringent standards, it is apparent that many lackadaisical personnel have quietly dismissed the newly raised bar and fully intend to disobey our commands. This is utterly unacceptable. Many of the punishments set in place to prevent disobedience have been found to be overly lenient, and as such will be extended and expanded upon, ranging from severe wage cuts to direct apprehension. The amendments to the punishments shall be transmitted to all police force personnel, perhaps repercussions will allow them to understand that yielding to the standards is mandatory.
strings.GNG_expand_recruitment_desc: Technological superiority and strategic dominance may all be essential aspects of a powerful force, but the true extent of their advantages cannot be reached unless it possesses the necessity of manpower. Now that we have ensured adjustments to the system, we shall fill the ranks of our police force with suitable men, but particularly an abundant source of manpower, the Chinese. The promise of sufficient wages will surely attract expendable Chinese men with fitting skills, who could easily be deployed upon the streets of Guangdong to overwhelm any feasible or mounted opposition. We expect the recruitment campaign to bear bountiful fruit which will undoubtedly aid in our efforts to combat resistance.
strings.GNG_train_the_next_generation_desc: The wave of men in the current police force are the embodiment of the neglectful rule of our predecessors, an inadequate disgrace brimming with corruption and decadence, incapable of performing its duty with efficacy. The next generation of the police force shall not and will not be condemned to the same state as the previous generation, it must be guaranteed that they are to be competent and skillful, vigorous and productive. The necessary preparations and arrangements to ensure this are to be laid, various examinations and drills shall be performed on a weekly basis to harden their spirits, they shall be proponents of a well-oiled machine, a machine that keeps the residents of the state manageable and allows Guangdong to continue flourishing.
strings.GNG_merciful_heart_desc: The existing Japanese elements present and residing within our police force is a variable we have to handle with the utmost caution. It has been noted that several Japanese personnel in the police force have been engaged in corruption and financial improprieties, such behavior would under normal circumstances warrant immediate expulsion, but it is best not to infuriate them in order to maintain a semblance of harmony within our ranks. We will show the Japanese officers and their associates a degree of leniency, the extent of which will be decided.
strings.GNG_merciful_heart_tt: When it comes to the core staff of the £GNG_police_texticon Police, we will remind them that £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon once-tolerated activities will be tolerated no longer.
strings.GNG_uphold_japanese_dominance_desc: While it is abundantly and absolutely evident that the police force has a plethora of glaring issues in its system and performance, this certainly does not equate to faults with the established order of the force. A substantial amount of the current order of the police force is dominated by the Japanese personnel present, who have proven themselves to be capable in leadership, and clearly skillful in maintaining some semblance of order. As we can place our firm trust in the Japanese officers managing and watching over the force, it is plainly unnecessary to adjust the present arrangements of the established order. After all, what is the purpose in correcting something that is perfectly serviceable? The Japanese officers will be undoubtedly suitable if we are to retain them.
strings.GNG_uphold_japanese_dominance_tt: The resources of the £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese are too valuable to be discarded and rebuilt from scratch. Our £GNG_police_texticon Police will be stronger with £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese assistance.
strings.GNG_beginnings_of_an_intelligence_networ: Alongside the myriad of problems present within the police force, the established order has certainly been a protruding issue, comparable to a beam of wood that has failed to petrify, instead rotting away. The current order is needlessly rigid, almost entirely being hegemonized by bands of Japanese officers. To distance ourselves away from the poorly managed order, we shall begin the establishment of several separate departments and agencies within the police force, to hopefully diversify and decentralize their future efforts. A clear option would be the establishment of an expansive and flexible intelligence network, further increasing our influence in Guangdong and creating a more specialized and tenable outlet for exercising control.
The danger of “overly relying” on £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese assistance is that we only see what they want us to see - and not what is most useful to £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita.
strings.GNG_updating_our_surveillance_desc: The streets and neighborhoods of Guangdong are brimming with hostile dissent, a vexing pest lurking and present in every lusterless crevice. We must be made aware of any presence of resistance to our administration, as to be able to exterminate a threat it first must be known by us. The creation of the “Special Branch” shall be a remedy to cure the lingering malaise of ignorance, a force that will shine our lights upon the darkest of shadows, a looming pair of eyes surveilling the inundated maelstrom of fluorescent lights that are the Three Pearls. The “Special Branch” forces exacerbate our grip upon the security apparatus of Guangdong, allowing us to prevent any form of insurrection from occurring.
strings.GNG_updating_our_surveillance_tt: Thorough surveillance and £GNG_police_texticon pre-emptive action we shall attempt to block any dissenters against £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's reign.
strings.GNG_favor_the_special_branch_desc: With the creation of the Special Branch, we have secured our presence on the chaotic surface of Guangdong's cities. The Special Branch will be utilized with efficiency and ferocity, an efficate tool that ensures we hold sway over the streets. Now that we are able to retain the Three Pearls under our cautious and precise watch, they shall surely greatly improve and become a stark contrast to their current state, a beacon of safety and security that radiates waves of prosperity. We shall begin to eliminate petty crime and storm underground strongholds, no person shall hide away from the ever watchful eyes of Matsushita.
strings.GNG_favor_the_special_branch_tt: Beware the unassuming salaryman with a camera - for £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita is watching you.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_see_desc: One of the most corrupt parts of our country is the Yakuza. The crime organizations of Japan, while extremely powerful in the home country, have insurmountable power here in Guangdong. They're everywhere: The streets, the casinos, the police departments, and, thanks to the shady dealings of Matsushita's predecessor, even within the government. Matsushita sees the Yakuza as a danger to both his power, and the efficiency of the nation. In order for Matsushita's plans to work without disruption, he must first eliminate his criminal rivals.
strings.GNG_nothing_to_see_tt: We will cast light on the shadows of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's underworld, and illuminate it with the light of £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita ingenuity.
strings.GNG_contacts_in_the_underworld_desc: Matsushita has determined that the best way to get rid of the Yakuza is from within. The use of moles within the Yakuza could provide us with information that could be used to take them down. Of course, this is extremely risky, given that there are Yakuza members within the government itself. However, if we do not plant the informers within the Yakuza, we will have no idea what criminal dealings they perform, and that could hurt Guangdong's efficiency very badly.
strings.GNG_contacts_in_the_underworld_tt: It is easier to have the rats do the job for us. We will begin seeking contact with the £GNG_triads_texticon Triads and the £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza to that end.
strings.GNG_provide_adequate_funding_desc: The best way to deal with the Yakuza is to make use of our already available asset: the police. Guangdong's police force, while useful, is woefully unprepared for dealing with the Yakuza. As such, Masushita plans to allocate funds for the police, so that they can be more readily prepared to deal with and suppress the Yakuza. However, while this is a tried and true method of dealing with crime, it has several issues. The Yakuza will be more secretive in their dealings and operations, the bureaucracy is a nightmare, and the police force has no guarantee of being uncorrupt.
strings.GNG_provide_adequate_funding_tt: In the end, the only men we can trust are our own - even if it takes years to get them up to standard.
strings.GNG_an_enticing_approach_desc: A new development within the situation with organized crime has revealed itself. Matsushita and his administration have been contacted by two members of prominent organized crime groups, Stanley Ho and Yokoi Hideki, about possible collaboration. Stanley Ho is the President of SJM Holdings, a mostly Chinese-run casino and hotel company based in Makao, and has several links to the Triads here in Guangdong. Yokoi Hideki is the owner of Shirokiya Hotel, and is deeply tied to the Yakuza. Both men represent factions within the Guangdong underworld that want to get rid of any criminal rivals and contenders. With access to men within the Yakuza, and valuable assets here in Guangdong and abroad, having one of these two men as an ally would benefit us greatly. However, dealing with men like Ho and Yokoi is like making a deal with a demon: In the end, the price is paid with your soul, and the demon will usually cheat you.
strings.GNG_an_enticing_approach_tt: Do we crush the £GNG_triads_texticon Triads, the £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza - or both?
strings.GNG_finding_an_ally_desc: With enemies as powerful as the Guangdong criminal underworld, Matsushita's administration needs all the help it can get. Now that an alliance has been formed with Ho and Yokoi, Matsushita must make a decision, for in the end only one faction can be chosen to work with the administration. Stanley Ho and his connections to the Chinese Triad would help deal with criminal organizations in the casinos and hotels, and Ho's ideas for improving the economy based on gambling, as well as his ambitions to go legitimate once all competition has been snuffed out, makes him a candidate that represents a more independent and native-oriented Guangdong, that still promotes the nation's ruthless capitalism. Yokoi on the other hand, would use his connections within the Yakuza to root out corruption within the IJA, and the Kenpeitai, along with his connections to both organizations, Yokoi would represent a more Japanese-orientated Guangdong. However, no matter who Matsushita sides with, one thing is for sure: Matsushita will be greatly indebted to one of these men, and a debt to a criminal is never a good sign.
strings.GNG_finding_an_ally_trigger: We have chained ourselves to one of the factions in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's criminal underworld.
strings.GNG_begin_the_offensive_desc: Guangdong's scandalous and crooked underworld is a pandora's box that is not to be opened under any circumstances. The participants in the underhanded dealings and affairs of the vile criminal strongholds below the surface are callous thugs who trade with dirty money and illicit contraband, working directly with them is akin to engaging in their trivial conflicts and is absolutely contradictory to the nature of our institutions. The issue of the gangs of the ever-shifting and repugnant underworld will be handled accordingly, and unquestionably, with our own police force's manpower and arms.
strings.GNG_begin_the_offensive_trigger: We have decided to attack both groups of the underworld simultaneously.
strings.GNG_changing_the_culture_desc: The despicable deed of corruption has haunted the offices and halls of Guangdong's corporate and civil administration ever since its original conception, it had been thoroughly ingrained into the core apparatus of the state and slowly fused with its societal culture. Though the cancer is still prevalent in life in Guangdong, efforts to slowly and gradually an expunge it have been effective. Noticeable trends have formed with the decrease of accounts of open corruption, as well as harsher enforcement of existing anti-corruption laws, all pointing to the conclusion that the pervasiveness of corruption among the populace of Guangdong is diminishing, and though we are far from eliminating this menace, it is assuring to be aware that progress is being made.
strings.GNG_choke_out_dissent_desc: Our newly brandished and revitalized police forces are to be put to use with the utmost productivity. They shall be deployed en masse across the state, spreading the influence and control of our administration from the disorderly din of the Three Pearls to the agrarian hinterlands that once lay beyond our reach. The omnipresent threat of opposition remains and lingers in the cities and countryside, having been allowed to fester while we were incapable of effective action, this current order of matters must not remain. We are to immediately begin the process of extermination, our forces acting as a coursing flame against the pernicious weeds of resistance, the citizens must be assured of their safety, and the dissidents their destruction.
strings.GNG_sleeping_soundly_desc: Although the neon signs still gleam with vivacious colors overhead, and the air still tainted with the unmistakable odor of diesel fuel, an unprecedented change has befallen the streets of Guangdong. The concrete sidewalks appear to be orderly, the underground trading sessions are no longer present, the derelict tenements overlooking the traffic, once a staple of criminal activity, now lay silent and abandoned. An uncharacteristic yet desirable calm has descended, the once bustling hub of illicit and criminal activity of Kōshū extinguished by the crackle of bullets and the stomping of boots. Men in uniforms patrol the alleyways, their eyes scanning the place where criminals and thugs once stood, no longer harboring their presence. This Guangdong would be alien to the Guangdong of a few years back, this Guangdong has shed a portion of its identity, an identity that was inherited by Matsushita, and has now been cleansed by the same hand. While the issue may have been silenced, we have yet to reach the stage of total pacification, the prospect of re-emergence is up to time.
strings.GNG_sleeping_soundly_tt: Now that the £GNG_police_texticon Police are safely under £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's thumb, we can turn our attention to other pressing matters, safe in their loyalty to the corporate state.
strings.GNG_the_man_of_the_hour_desc:
The nation is akin to a canvas, painted and dyed by the ambitions and abilities of men, displaying the traces and remains of the eminence of figures and organizations, their legacies forever imprinted. On the canvas of Guangdong, Matsushita Masaharu overshadows all else.

The Guangdong inherited by Matsushita was a state of immense opportunity, a land thoroughly mismanaged by his predecessors, riddled with inessential excess and decadence, its colossal potential never harnessed. Through years of vast struggle, Matsushita has transformed Guangdong into the epitome of economic prosperity, a state that was diligent, adaptable, and above all, efficient. Through the abundance of adversity faced by the Chief Executive, the omnipresent light of growth persisted, and it continues to do so, never dimming. Guangdong has advanced into a new era of opulence and success, yet the cogs of the machine do not cease, the zenith of potential has yet to be reached, and with Matsushita residing rightfully upon the seat of power, the canvas shall fill to his desire.
strings.GNG_the_man_of_the_hour_tt: Can a nation be shaped in the image of a man, a company? When we behold £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita, we see that the answer is yes - it can.
strings.GNG_Matsushita_Morita_Point_tt: £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's Morita Akio will gain more sway over £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Masaharu's decisionmaking.
strings.GNG_Matsushita_Great_Morita_Point_tt: £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's Morita Akio will gain tremendous sway over £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Masaharu's decisionmaking.
strings.GNG_Matsushita_Morita_Point_subtract_tt: £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's Morita Akio will gain less sway over £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Masaharu's decisionmaking.
strings.GNG_Matsushita_Ibuka_Point_tt: £GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Fujitsu's Ibuka Masaru will gain more sway over £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Masaharu's decisionmaking.
strings.GNG_Matsushita_Morita_Ibuka_Point_tt: £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony's Morita Akio and£GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Fujitsu's Ibuka Masaru will gain more sway over £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita Masaharu's decisionmaking.
strings.GNG_the_rising_tide_desc:
The world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis has at last arrived on the shores of Guangdong. Aside from resource shortages and trade disruptions, it also brings a more urgent risk. There is a distinct chance that all Chief Executive Matsushita Masaharu's hard work for the prosperity and stability of Guangdong will be swept away as if in a Nankai tsunami.

This demands swift, decisive action. We will need to move quickly to protect the economy; the pandemonium in the Legislative Council must be put to an end and the flow of workers and capital out of our borders must be stanched at the earliest possible opportunity. Let all that must be done be done quickly for the welfare of the people of Guangdong and the continued longevity of the Chief Executive's benevolent rule!
strings.GNG_the_rising_tide_tt: Matsushita Masaharu scrambles to place £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong on higher ground...
strings.GNG_facing_the_storm_alone_desc:
Alas, all the protestations of the members of the Co-Prosperity Sphere that we are a “rising star” and “critically important to the triumph of Pan-Asianism” were for naught. In our time of need, our so-called 'allies' left us to hang, and we are now forced to fight alone.

But Matsushita has not been caught off guard by this crisis. Though Guangdong's situation has turned out worse than even the most pessimistic official in the state could have thought it would, our Chief Executive remains unfazed. On our own initiative, trusting in Matsushita's wise leadership, the state of Guangdong and its people and corporations will rise out of this chaos stronger and more experienced than ever before.
strings.GNG_facing_the_storm_alone_tt: We thought the £GNG_Yasuda_texticon Yasuda Crisis would be the last example of £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japan's fickle ways. It was not - and now £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita feels the weight of the world on his shoulders.
strings.GNG_claw_a_way_back_desc:
We exist because of the command of the Emperor and the might of his armies; otherwise we would be but a province of China. Our existence is ultimately in service to the Great Japanese Empire and its political and economic aims. Accordingly, we must go to Tokyo and seek as much aid as we can possibly hope to get from them. No one denies that this is a humiliating option to even consider. But everyone with a brain knows that it is the only option we have.

The powers-that-be in Guangdong, led by Chief Executive Matsushita, will exercise whatever influence they can to draw out funding from Tokyo. Though they are unlikely to give us much, what little they do allow us to take will probably suffice to reduce the damage that we are likely to suffer by a significant amount.
strings.GNG_claw_a_way_back_tt: Even with all our efforts, only £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japan - and its investor class - has the resources to plug the economic gap £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong faces again. It's the only way to be sure.
strings.GNG_plug_the_gap_desc:
It would be an act of humiliation, desperation, and stupidity, not to mention a faux pas of historical proportions, for us to go begging to our overlords in Tokyo for whatever financial scraps they can spare us. The loss of face is not worth whatever supposed benefits it might yield; accordingly, we must look elsewhere for a source of funds to cover the growing shortfall in our budget.

The Chief Executive has therefore decided to proclaim an emergency tax increase to plug the gap for the time being. But as we implement this program we must be mindful of the severity of our situation. This crisis has had a terrible impact upon our budget; this plus the emergency tax increase will no doubt inflict further grave damage on our economy.
strings.GNG_plug_the_gap_tt: A company cannot be dependent on its creditors - why should £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong be any different?
strings.GNG_conserve_our_funds_desc:
Some people are suggesting that Guangdong spare expenses to prop up either established, dominant firms or the recently-rising competition. That is folly piled upon folly. We simply do not have the ability to simultaneously keep ourselves solvent and engage in charitable handouts to struggling corporations. If we now commit to doing one, we will neglect the other; since solvency is indispensable while charity is an optional extra, the choice is obvious.

This being the case, we will not issue extra funds to any company under any circumstances. We need to keep ourselves as financially balanced as humanly possible, no matter what blow this insistence might deal to our reputation among other interests within Guangdong's economy.
strings.GNG_conserve_our_funds_tt: To drive ourselves bankrupt to save the many is to throw the baby out with the bathwater. We will spend - but only to save those most important to £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita.
strings.GNG_relief_to_small_firms_desc:
It is a well-known fact dating back to the inception of Guangdong that smaller firms and corporations in the country have traditionally been given the short end of the stick over and over again. In contracts, resource distribution, tax credits, whatever they have always been ignored in favor of larger, more established companies that are often closely connected to the Five Companies.
This unjust paradigm cannot be allowed to continue, especially if we want the support of the Zhujin.

The support of the burgeoning Zhujin community will be indispensable to our state during this crisis; if we can somehow make room for them in the new order, we will certainly reap the benefits.
strings.GNG_relief_to_small_firms_tt: Our contractors are the backbone of the economy - or so Morita says.
strings.GNG_restore_the_corporations_confidence_:
Everyone and their mother-in-law knows full well that Guangdong relies on the major corporations - the Big Five and their assorted tributaries. If Chief Executive Matsushita lacks the confidence of the major corporations, it stands to reason that he will be thrown out by the Legislative Council or the Japanese Diet before the day is out.

That outcome is more likely at the moment due to the Oil Crisis giving people impetus to question the Chief Executive's leadership. Financial support will be given to all the dominant firms in order to keep them solvent and ensure their loyalty to the current regime.
We shall spend our funds ensuring that the great engines of the economy - the corporations - continue to operate smoothly.
strings.GNG_reassure_the_workers_desc:
The Japanese influence and power in Guangdong is self-evident; the firm hand of Japan and its people on the tiller are why Guangdong is what it is today. But the local population of Guangdong - the workers, secretaries, cooks, and so on - are just as important, and just as (if not even more) potentially threatening to our state during this terribly volatile time. We cannot afford to enrage them, lest they come and drown the Police, the Kenpeitai, and the army garrison in a sea of angry humanity and put an end to our glorious experiment.

To placate the common folk (and protect ourselves from them), we will ensure that the welfare payments given to rank-and-file workers are protected. Though this will meet with suspicion from the Japanese section of society, it is worth it to ensure that the commoners are kept docile and do not cause us any trouble.
strings.GNG_reassure_the_workers_tt: It will mean nothing if we have no workers at the end of this crisis. We must keep them in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - by maintaining all previous incentives we have offered.
strings.GNG_guarantees_to_japanese_stakeholders_:
Without the investment and expertise that Japanese expatriates have brought to Guangdong from their homes across the Home Islands, Guangdong will fall still closer to economic ruin. If we want to prevent such a disaster, we need to reassure them.

Measures of reassurance of various shapes and styles, financed by a general cut in welfare, will have to be made to all the Japanese with a presence of some kind in Guangdong. This conservative approach to the crisis will ensure that the Japanese remain behind us the whole way, and cement the established, well-deserved dominance the Japanese corporations of our state hold over the population.
We shall do what is necessary to shore up the confidence of £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese investors - and keep them in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong long-term.
strings.GNG_freeze_the_budget_desc:
The economic crisis brought about by the conflagration in the Middle East swirls with ever-greater instability and violence; economic confidence remains at best lackluster, with corporations and entrepreneurs simply unwilling to consider any major measures. Chief Executive Matsushita is therefore left with no choice but to resort to increasingly desperate means, such as decreeing a budget freeze.

Freezing the budget and thereby drastically limiting future spending may well provide the economic certainty that Guangdong needs to get back to normal again. We must be cautious, however. This is certain to be a terrible handicap to us if a major future expense becomes unavoidable. So we should keep an open mind to the concept of not pursuing this measure.
strings.GNG_freeze_the_budget_tt: The greatest signal of our fiscal responsibility would be freezing the budget... assuming, of course, that the£GNG_legco_texticon LegCo and the populace would be happy with it.
strings.GNG_an_eye_on_the_executives_desc:
Both Morita Akio and Ibuka Masaru hold considerable power and influence in powerful sectors of the Guangdong ruling class. Despite Matsushita's meteoric rise to dominance after the fall of Suzuki Teiichi, that influence has still eluded him. But, fortunately, both of them are still willing to hear their fellow tycoon out.

Actions can be taken to gain their favor and support in the Legislative Council. But we must be careful about the way in which we make such a major decision; it will come at a steep price, starting with the expansion of either Morita or Ibuka's influence in Guangdong and possibly going downhill from there.
strings.GNG_an_eye_on_the_executives_tt: The£GNG_legco_texticon LegCo, a chamber of squabbling corporate potentates at the best of times, is coming apart at the seams. Whatever happens, £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita must remain on top.
strings.GNG_bring_in_the_outsiders_desc:
For all that Morita and his reformist allies Li and Ho go a bridge too far with their over-concern for the welfare of the common folk and others that Guangdong neither can nor should worry about, they have been raising some fairly good points, and Matsushita knows that very well.

Accordingly, to benefit from their wisdom, Matsushita will invite Morita and his reformist allies into more influential positions within the government in exchange for their confidence and supply. While this comes at the cost of Matsushita's influence, it will increase the chance that Morita and his delegates will be willing to give our proposals fair hearing.
strings.GNG_bring_in_the_outsiders_tt: If the times demand something different, then they will have something different. £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita is, after all, a man attuned to shifting tides.
strings.GNG_listen_to_ibukas_concerns_desc:
Ibuka and Fujitsu, to Matsushita's view, are a bit too hyper-focused on their precious 'efficiency' and 'meritocracy', going on and on about 'innovation' to the detriment of anything else. Nonetheless, as Matsushita knows, a focus on things like that is conducive to catching more errors and making good points.

To benefit from Ibuka's wisdom, Matsushita will invite him into the government in exchange for his confidence and supply. This comes at the cost of Matsushita's influence but increases the chance that Ibuka will be willing to give our proposals fair hearing.
strings.GNG_listen_to_ibukas_concerns_tt: The most valuable advisor is the one who will tell you what you need to hear, and not what they think the masses want to hear - and that man is Ibuka Masaru.
strings.GNG_offer_morita_relief_desc:
The world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis has inflicted grievous wounds of one sort or the other on all companies in Guangdong, particularly the Big Five. One of the worst-affected of them is Sony, partly due to its charitable insistence on better conditions for its workers.
