The Chief Executive is of the mind that such goodness ought to be rewarded not just in the Pure Land but in this life too.

Accordingly, Matsushita has directed that an emergency grant be offered to the firm; this will show what the Chief Executive thinks about worker rights, and also further cement Morita's support for the government.
strings.GNG_emergency_research_and_development_g:
The world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis has inflicted grievous wounds of one sort or the other on all companies in Guangdong, particularly the Big Five. Yet among this maelstrom of social, financial, and economic ruination the Fujitsu Limited continues to pursue the cutting-edge of Japanese electronic innovation. The Chief Executive is of the mind that such a pursuit of excellence ought to be held up as an example to the Sphere and to all in the world that are willing to be advised on such a matter.

Accordingly, Matsushita has directed that an emergency grant be offered to the firm. This will clearly show the Chief Executive's approval of technological innovation and also further cement Ibuka's support for the government. He will be particularly appreciative of this since it will partly relieve the current squeeze on his firm's profits.
strings.GNG_legislate_japanese_corporate_suprema:
As the Oil Crisis roils the old Japanese corporate establishment and lays low companies that had weathered civil strife and the Yasuda Crisis without trouble, it is entirely within the realm of possibility that Zhujin firms may be able to fill the hole they left behind if action is not taken. This cannot be borne; only Japanese firms are fit to represent and dominate Guangdong.

Accordingly, the Japanese firms that remain have petitioned the Chief Executive to put his influence to use to defend the current order against these Zhujin-come-latelys and assorted upstarts. The Chief Executive sees the value in this; he will see it done.
strings.GNG_new_employment_standards_ordinance_d:
For years now Morita Akio has campaigned incessantly for stronger enforcement and better labor standards for the common workers of Guangdong. He considers a decision of this kind to be an investment in the very future of Guangdong, as a happy, healthy worker works harder and better. Our Chief Executive cannot help but see the merit in this proposal; all the more since he has seen it mesh with his own experience.

Accordingly, with the backing of Morita's reformist faction, the Chief Executive shall introduce a new bill to the Legislative Council with a view on improving the current rights of Guangdong workers.
strings.GNG_new_employment_standards_ordinance_t: What is a country without its workers?
strings.GNG_revert_to_the_old_ways_desc:
The 'Old Ways', also known as the Envelope System, is a euphemism for bribery. This system, like any other functional system, is versatile and can be used for various purposes, be those gaining power, wealth, influence, or reputation. As luminaries such as the esteemed Adhemar de Barros of Brazil have proven, it is of special use in convincing politicians to dance to one's tune.

This being the case, we will now make good use of it to get the various members of the Legislative Council on our side. This will of course fly in the face of our prior, massive anti-corruption efforts, but desperate times call for desperate measures.
strings.GNG_revert_to_the_old_ways_tt: Through £GNG_corruption_yen_texticon deals and favors, £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita always comes out on top.
strings.GNG_the_greatest_crime_desc:
As the world descends into yet another iron hell of instability, the economy of Guangdong - once of the great examples of the Co-Prosperity Sphere - is faltering and on the edge of collapse. The profits of every corporation in Guangdong are threatened; they cannot be allowed to fold. If all the corporations began to lose money, it would throw Matsushita's leadership into question and ruin his reputation. This cannot be borne.

Matsushita Kōnosuke once said, “If we cannot make a profit, that means that we are committing a sort of crime against society.” His adopted son and heir Masaharu remembers those words and agrees with them 100 percent. In the name of Guangdong, of filial piety, and of saving his own hide, Masaharu will 'play the crime fighter' by saving as many corporations as he can.
strings.GNG_the_greatest_crime_tt: Politics is politics, but profit is a matter of life and death. We must ensure £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita remains steadfast in this storm.
strings.GNG_scale_back_production_desc:
Amidst the current economic crisis, demand for goods produced in Guangdong has collapsed; nobody has the money required to buy any of them. This is self-evident to anyone with eyes to see and ears to hear, and can by no means be ignored or dismissed.

Some suggest that production should continue on as it did before the Oil Crisis began; this suggestion must be rejected as foolhardy. There is no point for us to maintain our previous high levels of production if no one can afford to buy our goods; accordingly, we will scale back our operations in order to reduce our costs. Laying off workers and cutting costs will greatly help our bottom line.
strings.GNG_scale_back_production_tt: If demand will not recover, then supply must adjust.
strings.GNG_preserve_our_innovative_momentum_des:
Amidst the current economic crisis, demand for goods produced in Guangdong has collapsed; nobody has the money required to buy any of them. Be that as it may, our production must continue on unabated lest we worsen our already grave situation.

Some suggest that production should be cut down to reduce our costs; this suggestion must be rejected as foolhardy. We simply cannot afford the risk of long-term damage to our production because of unwise, poorly thought-out cuts. Accordingly, production will continue at current levels in order to protect our past adaptations and innovations.
strings.GNG_preserve_our_innovative_momentum_tt: People are an investment for a better future that will come - even if it strains us now.
strings.GNG_efficiency_through_technology_desc:
Incessantly shilling our old products will only take us so far; the question of the people of Guangdong and of the Sphere losing interest in the Matsushita and other products currently on the market is a matter of when and not of if. Repeated advertisement was not what made Guangdong as great as it is today. No, it was our repeated and sustained technological advancements that grabbed the attention of all humanity and made Guangdong a force to reckon with.

If we wish to survive and thrive in the aftermath of the Oil Crisis, we must take decisive action to promote this behaviour once again. If we are successful in that, we will be able to make our recovery swifter and more effective.
strings.GNG_efficiency_through_technology_tt:
Yes, people tighten the purse strings when times are hard.
But people still want novelty and excitement in their life - and if £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita can provide, then they will pay.
strings.GNG_we_know_what_they_want_matsushita_de:
It is well and good to cut down on inefficiencies or promote efficiency through new technology, but it is just as effective to promote sales of the already perfectly good products we are making. We will want to put our previously-built sales networks to use, putting them to their absolute highest potential, to drive up domestic demand for the products our corporations make.

In the past we considered an advertisement campaign bringing a Matsushita appliance to every home. Whether or not that succeeded, let us use the infrastructure developed therein to promote our products and make sure that any and all deserving corporations receive a fair share of what profits are able to be obtained.
strings.GNG_we_know_what_they_want_matsushita_tt:
What are our sales networks for if not to convince the masses that they still need our wares, even in meager times?
Assuming, of course, we built those networks in the first place...
strings.GNG_a_matsushita_appliance_in_every_home: Because we took the focus “A Matsushita Appliance in Every Home” during the Silicon Years, we get following effects:
Because we did not take the focus “A Matsushita Appliance in Every Home” during the Silicon Years, we get following effects:
strings.GNG_focus_on_streamlining_desc:
One possible methodology we can use to improve our profits to a more stable level is the concept of streamlining and increasing product efficiency through the concept of “lean manufacturing”. By focusing on our production processes with a view on reducing wastes and non-value-adding components from them, we can easily make more goods from less materials. It will also make things safer, reduce quality defects, cut the manufacturing costs, and improve worker morale and retention.

This program will reduce the amount of materials we need to purchase, which will increase our profit and make industrial technology research easier.
strings.GNG_focus_on_streamlining_tt: It's not cutting corners; it's making sure our customers can afford our products.
strings.GNG_their_aspiration_desc:
It is known that Heaven and the will of the corporations of Guangdong have entrusted us with the control of the Land of the Three Pearls. It is self-evident that we and not the reformists or Fujitsu and Hitachi are Guangdong's sole guarantor of progress and prosperity. But despite these facts, our position does not rely on us alone, and we cannot hope to preserve our position without the support of our customers. They are as much a part of this recovery as we are.

If we wish to heal the crisis-battered economy of Guangdong, we must recuperate their confidence and make them want to buy our products once more. Let us set about doing it.
strings.GNG_their_aspiration_tt: ...and £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong, at least, shall be bedecked in £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita wares.
strings.GNG_our_vision_desc:
Heaven and the will of the august corporations of Guangdong have entrusted us with the control of the Land of the Three Pearls. We - not the overly charitable reformists of the State Faction, nor the 'meritocrats' and tech-fiddlers of Fujitsu, nor indeed the 'proud Manchuria enjoyers' over at Hitachi - are the sole guarantor of progress and prosperity for this state and its people. We must prove ourselves worthy of this duty, and we have every intention of doing so.

In order to preserve our power and bring prosperity to this land, we will keep production costs low and prices and the appropriate level required for us to turn a healthy profit. Let no one presume to stand in our way or stop us from doing so. If they try, we will push them aside, all for Guangdong and the will of our Chief Executive.
strings.GNG_our_vision_tt: £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita stands for something - a better, automated, convenient future...
strings.GNG_our_vision_effect: Grants us a free level increase in £GNG_household_electronics_texticon Household Electronics £GNG_research_texticon research
strings.GNG_going_all_in_desc:
The corporations of Guangdong must make a profit, or they will be betraying the society that has allowed them to exist. As the Chief Executive cannot bear such a prospect, we have taken decisive action to try to make them profit.
We have moved to improve the sales and production efficiency of our products. We have promoted our vision for Guangdong but tried our best to keep the aspirations of our citizens and customers in mind. All that is well and good, but we can do more.

Let us start doing more by making additional investments in our economy to bolster its strength during this trying time. Anything we can spare now will be returned to us sevenfold and more as growth is restored and prosperity resumes.
strings.GNG_going_all_in_tt: No expense shall be spared to secure £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's continued dominance.
strings.GNG_weathering_the_storm_desc:
Thanks to our adept response in the areas of finance, cooperation with other Big Five executives, and the issue of production, we have successfully brought an end to the worst of the Oil Crisis' terrible effects. Progress has been made, and the recovery has begun in earnest.

But the chaos is not yet over. There is terrible instability and collapse still ongoing both within Guangdong's borders and outside of them. The next few months will be absolutely critical; we must be extremely cautious in the way we go about things. If not, there is a risk that the hard work of our esteemed Chief Executive will all be thrown out of a window like briefcases were during the hellish time that was the Yasuda Crisis.
strings.GNG_weathering_the_storm_tt: When it seems like we have time to take a breather...
strings.GNG_back_on_the_main_stage_desc:
As we look up from containing the effects of the Oil Crisis in our own territories, we are astounded and worried at what we see around us. The chaos was by no means limited to the State of Guangdong. There is turmoil across the Co-Prosperity Sphere and in the entire world more generally. There are many things that give us cause for anxiety... and just as many opportunities that pique our curiosity.

We have no small amount of problems to deal with. First, we need to address the fact that Chinese laborers, angry at their situation, are leaving Guangdong en masse. Second, we need to take action about the rumors of Japanese companies withdrawing from Guangdong. Finally, more familiarly, we need to deal with the ever-present squabbles of the LegCo.

Our work is cut out for us.
strings.GNG_back_on_the_main_stage_tt: ...we realize that the world beyond our borders has not been idle either.
strings.GNG_our_own_initiative_desc:
We could certainly call upon potential allies in the Guangdong Legislative Council, or lean on some of our underhanded allies among the '100% legitimate businessmen' of the Guangdong underworld to solve our current problems. But we have no need to pursue either option in light of the strength of our Chief Executive and his well-known ability and acumen.

Our Chief Executive is a prudent, cautious man; he trusts his own abilities and views those of others with well-merited scepticism and suspicion. In these turbulent times, he thinks, it is elevated and correct to concentrate power where he can effectively control and distribute it, rather than running the risk of ambitious potential rivals causing any trouble. We agree with him.
strings.GNG_our_own_initiative_tt: £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita will carve a solitary path into the future - against the tide, if need be.
strings.GNG_friends_in_the_legislative_council_d:
We could certainly rely upon our Chief Executive's well-known initiative and political might or call upon some of our underhanded allies among the '100% legitimate businessmen' of the Guangdong underworld to solve our current problems. But we have no need to pursue either option if we have friends in the Legislative Council who we can rely upon.

Let us call upon our various allies and sympathizers in the LegCo and obtain their support to enact the policies necessary to stabilize Guangdong. We will promise to keep their concerns front-and-centre at all times; this assurance will free us from some of their obstruction as we try to pass ordinances in the immediate future.
strings.GNG_friends_in_the_legislative_council_t: The greatest problem is the £GNG_expats_texticon Japanese pulling capital out of the £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon Chinese mainland - we must convince them to stay, by any means at our disposal.
strings.GNG_call_on_our_underhanded_allies_desc:
We could certainly call upon potential allies in the Guangdong Legislative Council, or rely upon the Chief Executive's well-known ability and acumen. But we have no need to pursue either option in light of the dividends that reaching a fair and honorable agreement with the noble members of the Guangdong underworld has brought us.

Calling in the faction of the corps of '100% legitimate businessmen' of the underworld with which we previously allied ourselves will allow us to put its considerable influence to use without straining Chief Executive Matsushita or bothering the Legislative Council overmuch.
strings.GNG_call_on_our_underhanded_allies_avail: We found an underworld ally in the Silicon Years.
strings.GNG_call_on_our_underhanded_allies_tt: If we chose to give one of our underworld 'friends' a lease on life if they cooperated with us... then we must demand their cooperation now.
strings.GNG_matsushita_yakuza_ally_tt: Because we allied the £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza, we get following effects:
strings.GNG_matsushita_triad_ally_tt: Because we allied the £GNG_triads_texticon Triads, we get following effects:
strings.GNG_too_big_to_fail_desc:
Everyone and their mother-in-law knows full well that Guangdong relies on the major corporations - the Big Five and their assorted tributaries. During this recent crisis, we have repeated this time and again as we have more-or-less successfully attempted to restabilize the situation. But now the time comes for us to back our statements with action.

Chief Executive Matsushita has reached a decision on the final course of action for us to take. We will reward the esteemed factory owners for their kindness to us during this time of crisis by cutting them some slack on the matter of labor standards. As adherence to labor standards is a major financial burden for most corporations, lifting that burden from them will make sure that they do not fail anytime soon.
strings.GNG_too_big_to_fail_tt: We will not leave the engines of our economy to gather dust and idle needlessly. They will be kept alive - if they cut costs, of course.
strings.GNG_addressing_the_capital_flight_desc:
Japanese entrepreneurs representing financial portfolios valued in the millions and billions of yen are threatening to leave Guangdong, and that puts our economy in grave peril indeed. They say that if we do not put our money where our mouth is as regards prioritizing their concerns over coddling rank-and-file Zhujin and Chinese workers, they will leave for a place that is more friendly to their money.

Fortunately, that problem is not too difficult to solve. We can simply continue with our prior decision to limit the rights of workers. That will more than suffice to reassure them about our focus on their freedom to profit and innovate in this country.
strings.GNG_addressing_the_capital_flight_tt: If the £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Japanese investors are fleeing £GNG_chinese_nation_texticon China because they see no commercial opportunities, then changing their mind should be simple... assuming, of course, we are willing to pay the cost, both in money and in reputation.
strings.GNG_trouble_on_the_border_desc:
Our border with China has always been a source of trouble, but never to the extent of the present day as the chaos in China - the revival of their formerly-docile national spirit and will to modernize and 'expel the foreign oppressors' - spreads to our borders. Masses of Chinese and even Zhujin workers, understandably angry about our focus on entrepreneurs and investors over them, have begun to stream across the border in search of better deals than they can find here.

We will need to take a very close look at our policy on the maintenance of the frontier and decide what action if any we are going to take about these emigrants. Let us be careful lest our decision have a destabilizing effect on the economy.
strings.GNG_trouble_on_the_border_tt: There is no greater challenge than the flow of economic migrants across the border - both in terms of workers and capital lost. £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita's decisions may have far-reaching consequences...
strings.GNG_incentives_to_stay_desc:
Masses of Chinese and even Zhujin workers, understandably angry about our focus on entrepreneurs and investors over them, have begun to stream across the border in search of better deals than they can find here. The corporations try their best to keep them in place, but all reports indicate that it is insufficient in the vast majority of cases.
This is a matter of grave concern and must be resolved as soon as possible.

Though it displeases us and runs the risk of irritating the entrepreneurs and factory owners, we must increase worker benefits if we wish to bring the situation under control.
strings.GNG_incentives_to_stay_bypass: We passed the £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Budget Freeze Order.
strings.GNG_incentives_to_stay_tt: If our workers are leaving for greener pastures, then perhaps it's time to make the garden look nicer... assuming, of course, that£GNG_legco_texticon LegCo hasn't tied our hands on this matter.
strings.GNG_keep_the_people_docile_desc:
Reaching a fair and honorable agreement with the noble members of the Guangdong underworld has brought us great dividends. We should by all means continue to avail ourselves of the benefits of this great partnership.

Accordingly, let us grant free rein to the segments of organized crime with which we have allied ourselves in order to keep the Chinese populace docile through a combination of bread-and-circus (such as gambling and bars) and carrot-and-stick tactics (such as bribery and the violent suppression of potential union activity). This has worked before, and it will work again. We are more than capable of withstanding any negative consequences this might have.
strings.GNG_keep_the_people_docile_tt: A facade of normality will eventually become the real thing - and until then, we must keep the malcontents off the streets.
strings.GNG_matsushita_leads_desc:
The will of the august corporations of Guangdong has entrusted Chief Executive Matsushita Masaharu with the welfare of the Land of the Three Pearls. As Matsushita leads Guangdong and the company that bears his family name through the world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis, he remains on top of it all, with his hand on the tiller fully in control over the direction that the state takes.

As a result, Matsushita leadership has begun to be seen as a fact of life. That a man called “Suzuki Teiichi” was once Chief Executive a decade back is known only to historians, some Japanese, and the LegCo itself; virtually everyone else acts as if 'Matsushita-dono' was always the Chief Executive. This attitude is indicative of the fact that Matsushita Masaharu has become an inseparable part of Guangdong's structure and way of governing.
strings.GNG_matsushita_leads_tt: £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Chief Executive Matsushita sits upon his throne...
strings.GNG_guangdong_follows_desc:
As time has gone on under the rule of Chief Executive Matsushita, the formerly artificial state that supported and controlled this land of Guangdong has proven surprisingly resilient. It has managed to withstand internecine conflict between corporations, power struggles, riots, police disputes, gang warfare, and a myriad other problems. It has even managed to persist through both Yasuda and this present Oil Crisis more or less unbowed and unbroken.

Having at last somewhat recovered from the most recent storm to batter its shores, Guangdong looks to Matsushita Masaharu to lead it into the next age of global history.
strings.GNG_an_island_of_stabillity_desc:
For all our efforts in rallying the executives, stabilizing our finances, maintaining production integrity, controlling the flow of Chinese workers, and preventing Japanese entrepreneurs from fleeing en masse, one terrible constant remains: that of uncertainty. For all his power, intellect, and merits, Chief Executive Matsushita Masaharu is of exactly zero use in suppressing the unstoppable tide of conflict that now threatens the whole of Greater East Asia.

All we can do is prepare what defenses we can muster, hold things together, keep innovating, and hope and pray to any heavenly power that will listen that Guangdong will be spared the worst of what the next few years will nearly certain bring.
strings.GNG_an_island_of_stabillity_tt: When the Oil Crisis passes - as all crises do - £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong will be stronger than ever before. Woe to those who wrote off £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong as a lost cause!
strings.GNG_strike_while_the_iron_is_hot: Strike While the Iron is Hot
strings.GNG_the_concerns_of_the_legislative_coun: The Concerns of the Legislative Council
strings.GNG_rout_them_to_the_last_man: Rout Them to the Last Man
strings.GNG_a_shattered_illusion_desc:
At this moment of time, one can be forgiven for thinking that Matsushita's actions have finally brought peace to Guangdong. But the truth could not be further from that. His solution was only momentary; now, workers and laborers have taken to the streets in the wake of Hitachi's disastrous mishandling of its factories in Kōshū. Tens of thousands roam the streets of Guangdong in protest of the recent events. The illusion of peace in Guangdong is shattered, perhaps for good.

This is our time to regroup and reorganize our forces to respond to this threat. True, this is going to be a monumental task; the country has never seen protests of this scale before. It will take a lot of resources and commitment from the state to bring the masses back to heel. But we must push on, for Guangdong and the Co-Prosperity Sphere.
strings.GNG_a_shattered_illusion_tt: And we may never put back the pieces...
strings.GNG_picking_up_the_pieces_desc:
For every day that we take no action, a hundred more laborers take to the streets of Guangdong in protest, further escalating the already-grave situation. If left unchecked, their numbers will grow uncontrollably; with enough time, Guangdong may be overrun by protesters, causing anarchy to descend upon the Three Pearls. We cannot allow these terrorists and ingrates to rule the streets for long. Something must be done to clamp down upon this movement.

There is no time to waste, no seconds for us to spare. The riots will end, and the police force will make sure they do. We have no choice but to stop this before the situation worsens.
strings.GNG_picking_up_the_pieces_tt:
... and to prevent this we must act swiftly.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_gather_our_strength_desc:
Of course, charging aimlessly without proper preparation into crowds of rioters is at best foolhardy. Before we strike them, we must first make sure that we make each and every strike hit and hurt. At this point, our police force is in disarray and in panic due to the situation unfolding so rapidly, and at this shape, we stand no chance against the rioters on the streets.

We must take decisive action, but not without watching our steps. We will consolidate all our strength into a coherent and organized force, planning and preparing the necessary steps to counter the people on the streets. When we are ready, we will strike hard and fast. Hopefully, our efforts will pay off.
strings.GNG_lure_them_out_desc:
Though they are a large, unwieldy group, the rioters still have something resembling organization and make use of minimal but effective tactics. On seeing a force that they think they cannot fight, they retreat to areas of cities where the streets are narrow and the architecture obstruct our passage, and continue their disruption from there. Given the layout of the major cities within Guangdong, particularly Kōshū itself, this means that they can avoid us easily.

To effectively reduce their strength, we must first be able to fight them. The riot control forces will make use of methods that can lure them out into areas where they can be more easily combatted. In a matter of time they will have nowhere to run but into our embrace.
strings.GNG_strike_while_the_iron_is_hot_desc:
There is no time for us to be patient and slowly chip away at the rioters' strength without achieving anything. Where we previously showed restraint in combating the rioters, this time we will not. The best method of ending this crisis is to strike once, but strike as hard as we can. This action will ensure a rapid return to normalcy on the streets, and the return of order to the country.

Everything we have, every man, every armored vehicle, and every equipment we have in our stockpile will be unleashed in one devastating blow to the rioters. They will fall, and Guangdong will return to the norm, and they will go back to the factories, whether they want to or not.
strings.GNG_strike_while_the_iron_is_hot_tt: One lethal strike, to destroy the tumors known as the £GNG_CCL_texticon CCL and £GNG_GFT_texticon GFT.
strings.GNG_a_change_in_course_desc:
We seem to have miscalculated our moves, and we have done nothing but make the situation worse. Our supposed strategy of striking while the iron is hot has failed, and the heavy crackdown has only strengthened the resolve of the workers, and in turn, radicalized their motives. This is bad, really bad.

It is now up in the air, especially up to Matsushita to show us the way forward. A new tactic towards the situation will have to be adopted, and at the moment, we have two options to choose from. The first option is to continue what we were doing and grind the rioters down to submission with our superior strength. The alternative approach is to attempt to open talks with the rioters to reconcile and cease hostility. Our choice will determine how the situation will unfold.
strings.GNG_a_change_in_course_tt: Only fools would insist blindly on staying on a mistaken course - but fewer still are those who know the correct path forward.
strings.GNG_out_of_harms_way_desc:
We have chosen to approach the rioters with a reconciling manner, and we must waste no time on getting to work to bring order back on the streets. Our focus is to deradicalize the troublemakers on the streets to the point that they may be drastically easier to handle and control, at least until a permanent and peaceful solution to the crisis can be found.

Sometimes, we have to know to concede to some of their demands, this will surely calm the rioters down. But we must practice caution, as the integrity of the state cannot be compromised only to pacify some rash workers causing troubles on the streets. We may give concessions, but not too much.
strings.GNG_out_of_harms_way_tt:
The key to containing the Riots is to establish a firebreak - and keep the wider public from joining the conflagration.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_no_room_to_breathe_desc:
The idea of reaching to the rioters and appealing to their sense of humanity and compassion in order to restore order to the streets is simply mad. Attempting to reconcile with them is a very futile endeavor, and the people will not be satisfied with our ruses. The only sensible option is to remind them of their place and forcefully suppress any signs of defiance. Our approach will focus on keeping a very close eye on the rioters and, when the perfect opportunity shows itself, we will strike them hard and everything will return to normal

This method will be very popular among most of the Legislative Council, showing that we are capable and willing to take control and assert our dominance, but we cannot be certain of what the people will respond to our methods.
strings.GNG_no_room_to_breathe_tt:
A fire, left unchecked, only spreads. It must be smothered before it grows larger.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength at the cost of £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_give_them_an_inch_desc:
In accordance with our method of handling the situation, we will once again use appeasement to calm the workers down, and prevent them from causing a possible escalation in the severity of the situation. The workers descend to the streets definitely without reasoning, everyone has their own reasons to protest and riot, and it does not take a genius analyst to understand what the rioters want.

They have centered their campaign of protest to demand things such as better wages, improvement of working conditions, and reasonable work hours, among many other things. To bring order back on the streets, perhaps it is time for us to review our current policies, and perhaps, give the laborers the rights and conditions, along with enforcing them effectively to appease the rioters.
strings.GNG_give_them_an_inch_tt: The lowest-hanging fruit to defuse this crisis is to take one step towards the £GNG_rioters_texticon dissidents... even if it empowers our critics.
strings.GNG_and_well_take_a_mile_desc:
It is common sense that we have to have something to gain out of our rather disprofiting change in policy, particularly on the status of worker rights and such. There is no telling that the rioters would simply stop causing trouble immediately after our recent change of policy. Thus, we've come up with a new, and admittedly mildly risky strategy to make sure that the riots stop, there is no telling of what the rioters' response to this would be.

“Requests” will be issued to the workers on the streets, asking the rioters to restrain their actions and limit themselves from carrying out further acts of violence on the streets. We will also make some... subtle but noticeable threats of what might happen if they do not comply with our very polite request.
strings.GNG_and_well_take_a_mile_tt: Of course, we will tell investors that anyone who still objects, can see how much they enjoy a jail cell instead...
strings.GNG_tone_down_the_rhetoric_desc:
Other corporate leaders that make up the Cantonese government have very rapidly denounced the recent events with rather strong connotations in their words. There is no other option for Matsushita but to toe the middle line very, very carefully.

Dissimilarly to the other corporate leaders, Chief Executive Matsushita will make a statement to criticize the police force's actions and handling of the riots, while at the same time not completely denouncing the police, thus maintaining his full support for law enforcement. On top of this, Matsushita will also promise cooperation with the populace if the workers are to restrain themselves. In these times, the tongue truly is sharper than the sword.
strings.GNG_tone_down_the_rhetoric_tt: Stability is the order of the day - not punishment, and not retribution.
strings.GNG_assert_our_presence_desc:
The situation is very fragile, and the rioters are running amok acting as if they own the streets. After what we have done and policies that we have changed, they are still just troublemakers on the streets. With our recent actions that are seen as giving into the protesters, and this may give the wrong impression towards the populace that the government is weak and easily swayed. We do not want those kind of sentiment in the air.

The rioters must not forget that they do not own the streets, and they must also remember who is truly in control of Guangdong. We will establish a large police presence, not to attack them upfront, but to show that we are still here, reminding the rioters of our presence on the streets.
strings.GNG_assert_our_presence_tt: But whatever its purpose, the £GNG_police_texticon Police presence shall be increased.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_every_wall_desc:
As we have promised to the Legislative Council, we will keep a very close eye on the rioters and monitor their actions, and their intentions. It is prudent for us to be able to know what our enemies are doing to best plan our next moves, and secure any upcoming plans to eradicate the rioters from the streets.

More resources shall be allocated to surveillance, and soon, there will be eyes on every wall, cameras around every street corner, and there will be policemen and spies over every dark alley in the cities of Guangdong. Nothing will escape our watchful gaze, and everything will be revealed to us. After all, we cannot allow anyone who wishes to see the fall of Guangdong have any sense of security, and everything they are planning will be revealed to us. There are no more secrets.
strings.GNG_eyes_on_every_wall_tt: Our £GNG_police_texticon police and intelligence services surveil all...
strings.GNG_ears_on_every_corner_desc:
The rioters, though united within the same cause, are very diverse in their own beliefs, some are even in it only for the money they might get after the crisis is over, expecting us to pay them better. Among those men and women, surely there are some that are truly desperate, or some that are simply easy to sway in, in such a way that they may play right into our hands.

This presents a great opportunity for our efforts to quell the crisis. We will convince, bribe, or coerce in an expansive web of informants from the different factions of rioters, and they will give further insight towards their actions and plans. This will allow us to make our moves based on the information provided to us by our informants. This, along with our recent establishment of extensive surveillance systems, will give us everything we need to know about these troublemakers.
strings.GNG_ears_on_every_corner_tt: ...and they know exactly what the £GNG_rioters_texticon protestors are up to.
strings.GNG_issue_urgent_police_funding_desc:
To summarize the situation, we are trapped between a rock and a hard place. There is little to nothing separating the possibility of anarchy befalling over the streets of Guangdong and the possible interference of the brutal Kenpeitai, neither of which serves our interests. Nothing separates the two extremes apart, nothing but the Guangdong Police Force.

The Guangdong Police Force is our last hope of maintaining control of the streets without ourselves being controlled. They are the only force loyal to Guangdong and its government, along with the only ones keeping the best interests of the people in mind. As the police force is our last hope, we must provide critical support towards the police. Any available funding that we have must be channeled into the police force to strengthen their position, and for them to take back the streets from these rioters.
strings.GNG_issue_urgent_police_funding_tt: Our £GNG_police_texticon security forces will be given a blank check to do what they must... provided, of course, we haven't promised the£GNG_legco_texticon LegCo that the budget will be frozen.
strings.GNG_keep_tokyo_in_mind_desc:
The government of Japan in Tokyo has pulled out their support from us in light of the recent events, leading us to face this crisis with little to no outside aid. And although that support from our benefactors have seemingly vanished, we must not forget what we are and what position we serve within the Co-Prosperity Sphere.

Our actions must reflect what Tokyo would do, and it is very important to us that we keep their best interests in mind during this crisis. Keeping this in mind while we deal with the rioters in order to not damage anything important is thus essential. Our position as the pearl of the Co-Prosperity Sphere and as the most profitable source of income for our overlords in Tokyo must be kept as it is, and our profitability for the Empire of Japan must not be damaged.
strings.GNG_keep_tokyo_in_mind_tt:
We, of course, should keep £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Tokyo informed of our budget increases - if only so they have a narrative that isn't breathless headlines about chaos and misery.
Assuming, of course, that we are telling the truth.
strings.GNG_budget_is_frozen_keep_tokyo_in_mind_: Because the budget is frozen, we get no further effects.
strings.GNG_emergency_powers_ordinance_desc:
Enough talking, for it is time for us to take action. The Chief Executive, Matsushita, has a plan that will carry Guangdong through the crisis, but this plan requires the full support of every section of the government, which is admittedly, tough to acquire. Thus, we propose an alternative.

An ordinance proposal will be sent to the Legislative Council to be voted on. This ordinance will give emergency powers to the Chief Executive, allowing him to carry out his plan on dealing with the riots. Power must be completely concentrated into the hands of the Chief Executive for this plan to work, otherwise, the plan will fail before it even starts, and we may be forced to come up with another plan.
strings.GNG_emergency_powers_ordinance_tt: To deliver the coup de grace, new powers are needed - ones that we can turn to to stop this from ever happening again.
strings.GNG_break_the_deadlock_desc:
A new situation has developed within the doors of the Legislative Council. It is now apparent that our appeasements towards the rioters may cause some worry within the Legislative Council of the possibility of the government losing control. This has resulted in a deadlock between these two responsibilities, keeping the rioters appeased and happy, as well as calming the members of the Legislative Council from fear of our weakening influence.

Matsushita is now at a crossroads, one that he cannot back down from. The choice is simple, yet daunting. Either he will force a compromise with the rioters, to the dismay of the Legislative Council, or to continue this precarious position of balancing corporate and popular interests. One wrong move and the whole system might come tumbling down.
strings.GNG_break_the_deadlock_tt: To divide the placated masses from the rabid few - surely this can be accomplished?
strings.GNG_walking_a_fine_line_desc:
There is no better option. On one side, we have the people of Guangdong, aching for reforms and improvements for their living and working conditions, and on the other, the Legislative Council and their interests of making Guangdong the “shining pearl” that it deserves to be, without a care for the wellbeing of others. If we appease one faction, the other will cry out in defiance, and terrible consequences may befall upon our precious state.

For the sake of everyone involved, the government, and Matsushita, will walk a fine line between the two, like toeing through a tightrope. It is to our knowledge that this will be a very challenging and thankless task, one that Matsushita must carry out nevertheless for the sake of stability and peace. No wrong steps must be taken, or everything may come tumbling down.
strings.GNG_walking_a_fine_line_tt:
There are easy ways out, solutions provided from courtiers seeking honors in return - but £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita will walk his own path, come hell or high water.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_an_ear_to_the_streets_desc:
Since the beginning of this affair, the people on the streets kept on shouting demands and requests of improved working conditions and other things which if we follow through will cause our profitability to tank, and so far, our efforts to contain them haven't concerned anything about what they have been asking. Their continued act of rioting is our gravest threat to our stability yet, and so, to carry out the task of pacifying the streets, perhaps it is time that we change that.

This time, we will take notes of what they ask for in their daily riots, and for once, listen to their shouts and screams. They may fall right into our hands, if we play our cards right. Perhaps, we may fulfill some of their demands and wishes, within reason of course, in order to temporarily pacify the situation before a more permanent solution can be found. We do have to tread carefully so as to not anger the Legislative Council, and once again, walk the fine line between the two.
strings.GNG_the_concerns_of_the_legislative_coun:
The Legislative Council, even in times like these, is still filled with talks and bickerings about profit margins and economic statistics, accompanied with a new feeling of crippling uncertainty. Unsurprisingly enough, these concerns are also those that fill Matsushita's mind. Perhaps it is time for Matsushita to deal with the Legislative Council. After all, the point of toeing the middle line is to appease both parties in the negotiations, and making sure that both of them are pleased in order to contain the situation.

To show the Legislative Council that we are willing to quell the riots if necessary, we will start to somewhat clamp down into the riots. Sustaining tough action against them will earn us the support of the Legislative Council. But we must be careful to not anger the rioters too much, lest our efforts fail and the situation descends into anarchy.
strings.GNG_whispers_from_the_home_islands_desc:
Guangdong is nothing without our benefactors in Tokyo backing us up. They are the ones that first made us this profitable and rich. Without the guidance of Tokyo, our streets may already fall into anarchy, and Guangdong will fall shortly after. In accordance with this, every action we take must have the interests of our benefactors in Tokyo in mind. The Japanese government at this very moment is already expecting us to bring order back to the streets without delay. If we are to fail in bringing the situation under control rapidly, they may not be hesitant to intervene more directly, which we do not want to happen.

With the situation showing no signs of calming down at the moment, this rumor may come true if we are not careful. Thus, it is to our best interests that we act fast to diffuse the situation, before it gets worse and before Tokyo intervenes.
strings.GNG_respite_and_reconciliation_desc:
Morita Akio has a plan to deal with the consuming chaos on the streets. His plan is to negotiate with the different dissenting factions within the riots, and to work out a deal with them to put an end to the anarchy on the streets. Matsushita has deemed that Morita's plan is the most feasible one that we have in store, to bring an end to the violence peacefully, without the police having to lift a finger. Understandably however, the other executives and the members of the Legislative Council are not on the same page with Matsushita and Morita, and the plan is very unpopular among them.

Facing no other options, Morita's plan will be carried out, and he will open negotiations with the rioters, and hopefully reconcile to put an end to the riots. But Matsushita must be very careful for how much he is willing to offer to the rioters, as one concession too many may cost him all of the support from the Legislative Council and the other executives.
strings.GNG_respite_and_reconciliation_tt: Some of the £GNG_rioters_texticon dissidents can be reasoned with. The challenge is not looking weak in the process.
strings.GNG_strength_and_stability_desc:
There is an alternative to Morita Akio's proposal to handle the situation. Ibuka and the majority of the Legislative Council proposes that we clamp down even harder on the rioters, for they have been avid supporters of strong suppression since the beginning of this affair. Solving the situation through violence may not seem like the best solution to the chaos, but it is the one most likely to succeed. Matsushita recognizes this, and along with him not wanting to anger the Legislative Council, decides that this is the way forward. The streets will be quelled through the hand of the police force, and order shall be restored.

Though this brings up another concern, the concern that, instead of successfully driving away the rioters from the streets, the suppression efforts will only strengthen the resolve of the riots and radicalize their ideals. This must be kept in mind while carrying out the task, otherwise they will become impossible to dissolve through brute force alone.
strings.GNG_strength_and_stability_tt: We have the resolve; we have the tools. All we need is more time.
strings.GNG_staying_on_top_desc:
Throughout the entire affair, everyone around Matsushita, from those that he trusts to those that he does not, have all been exploiting the chaos within the government and the Legislative Council that the riots caused to wrestle away power from him. Fortunately, however, this has been brought to Matsushita's attention, and he can take the necessary actions to prevent such an event from taking place.

Matsushita will keep a very watchful eye on anyone who is still willing to do such an act of defiance, while simultaneously having his other eye on the streets to monitor the situation so that it doesn't get out of hand. We are at the end of the line, and it is at these crucial moments that the future of Guangdong takes shape. There must be no loose ends.
strings.GNG_staying_on_top_tt: This is a lonely road; but it's the only one Matsushita's ever known.
strings.GNG_forcing_a_compromise_desc:
The future of Guangdong is set, and we can see the writings on the wall. The riots are still getting worse day by day, despite our efforts. Something radical must be done, something that will surely put an end to the chaos. We cannot solve this situation through violence, nor can we do so through walking the middle line. And so, it is clear that the only way forward is to force a compromise.

We will prioritize opening negotiations with the Guangdong Federation of Tradesmen and with the Committee of Chinese Labor. Morita's reformist ideals will prove to them that the protestors can be worked with, and to ensure the safety of Guangdong. He will be sent to negotiate on behalf of Matsushita, and strike a favorable deal with them.
strings.GNG_forcing_a_compromise_tt:
Negotiations and dealmaking are the heart of business.
Why should these disturbances be any different?
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength and £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_find_moritas_role_desc:
The different dissenting factions want a lot of things from us, but in order to keep our power from slipping away from our grasp, we can't give them everything. Morita Akio will be a reliable asset for negotiating on our behalf, and he will play a key role to appease all the dissenting factions.

But the circumstances are now presented to us. Morita Akio will be our negotiator, but to which extent can he act separately from our instructions? The degree of autonomy Morita has during the negotiations may make or break our situation, and we must make our decision with care and our best interests in mind.

In any case, we must keep a watchful eye on Morita, keeping him from overstepping his given boundaries, for the sake of keeping the negotiations favorable to us, while simultaneously successful in calming down the factions.
strings.GNG_find_moritas_role_tt: Morita's words will carry weight with those who can be reasoned with... but can Matsushita trust him?
strings.GNG_not_just_a_facade_desc:
The people have heard our promises of conceding to their demands somewhat, and we have followed those promises with some degree of constraint so as to not worsen the opinion of the Legislative Council towards our administration, but we fear that the times call for a change.

In order for the negotiations to proceed smoothly, we must show the people, and by extension, the factions we are negotiating with, that we are willing to take truly meaningful actions to prove our intentions to the people and those we wish to negotiate with.

Angering the Legislative Council may be the least of our concerns at this moment, as we must prioritize on keeping our image to the factions. Issues such as working conditions may now be reviewed thoroughly to better meet the demands of the factions.
strings.GNG_not_just_a_facade_tt: In this circumstance, we must make at least a step towards concessions - even if it hurts us politically
strings.GNG_hear_out_the_moderates_desc:
Though many within the Legislative Council see that the dissenting factions are nothing more but a band of uncompromising radicals unwilling to listen to any of our words without any sense of moderation, the truth is that there are still a significant amount of members within the dissenting factions that recognize that there can be no meaningful change to be had if without there being cooperation between both parties. This may play well in our hands.

During the negotiations, we may use some trickery to have the moderate members of the factions be listened to more than the radicals. By doing this, the laborers' rage can be directed to the more outspoken moderate stance that those faction members stand for. This will land us a better chance of working out a reasonable compromise with the dissenting factions, and for them to listen to our appeals.
strings.GNG_hear_out_the_moderates_tt: Even within the £GNG_rioters_texticon rioters, there are meaningful differences - those who want a better life, and those who want to burn everything to the ground. We can exploit this...
strings.GNG_united_against_extremists_desc:
Now that we have dealt with the moderates, it is time for us to take into account the rest of the groups, those that we cannot reason with, and those who only seek destruction upon the beauty of Guangdong. These radicals, true to their name, hold a very hardline stance on the current situation, one that we regard as nothing but a facade of their true intentions, to see Guangdong crumble with them ruling the streets. They cannot be reasoned with, and attempting to do so is simply a waste of time on our behalf.

Perhaps the moderates may help us. Appealing to common sense and our mutual feeling of comradery, we will unite the moderates and stand with them to curb the influence of these radicals, in the hopes that such an outcome of anarchy and destruction will not befall upon Guangdong, something which we and the moderates share a common goal of.
strings.GNG_united_against_extremists_tt: ...and let the agents of anarchy burn themselves out.
strings.GNG_everything_to_keep_the_peace_desc:
In our sense, keeping the peace by any means necessary must not be taken in a violent context, but it must be taken as a mandate for our state to do anything in our power to keep the peace, through methods of peace. And everything that we have done so far has stood true to this mandate, for peace comes before anything else. Our goal is for steady cooperation, and in that sense, we have achieved the goal. Any false pride above those that we wish to negotiate with are futile, and does not yield any fruit.

For now, we have done all we can, and let us hope that Morita returns to us from the negotiations with favorable deals, so we and the people of Guangdong may march into the future, as one. For the good of Guangdong, may she be in good hands.
strings.GNG_everything_to_keep_the_peace_tt: It's time to sweeten the deal.
strings.GNG_one_final_push_desc:
It has been proven from time and time again that the rioting factions are those that we cannot negotiate or converse with. Attempting to resolve this through unusual means will only result in failure, and we must act swiftly to put an end to the crisis, once and for all. Through the only means available to us at this moment, that is a crackdown upon the streets, can we truly return to normalcy and bring peace to Guangdong,

The government, Matsushita, and the Legislative Council itself has concluded that only through decisive and aggressive action can we forcefully get rid of the rioters from the streets of Guangdong. Not only will this surely end the chaos on the streets, this will do so guaranteeing the support of our higher ups and the Legislative Council. Thus, we will spare no quarter to these vandals and troublemakers, and their chaos ends today. Only one final push until we are victorious.
strings.GNG_did_pass_emergency_powers_ordinance: We passed the £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Emergency Powers Ordinance.
strings.GNG_one_final_push_tt:
We will never accept defects as inherent to the system. They must be rooted out and destroyed.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to drastically  reduce riot £GNG_riot_strength_texticon strength, at the expense of £GNG_riot_radicalism_texticon radicalism are unlocked.
strings.GNG_earning_komais_support_desc:
With every other option considered infeasible by Matsushita and the government, we have chosen to enact a brutal crackdown upon the terrorists on the streets. A problem that may arise from our actions is that the brutal crackdown may sprout anger from within the rioters, but they are the least of our concerns. After all, we won't have to care about what they say when they're off the streets.

Despite what the rioters will think, Komai is still a man with considerable skill at maintaining control over his workers. With the situation at hand, this leaves Matsushita with no choice but to cooperate with Komai to handle the situation, and suspend any attempt of giving into the rioters' demands. No compromise shall be given, and what they will receive is their price of their ungratefulness.
strings.GNG_earning_komais_support_tt:
£GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai and Hitachi might have started this problem, but they assuredly have the tools to end it.
It's not like we needed £GNG_Sony_texticon Sony and £GNG_Cheung_Kong_texticon Cheung Kong anyway.
strings.GNG_loosen_the_kenpeitais_leash_desc:
For a long time we have kept the Kenpeitai close under our supervision in order to not have them influence our politics and internal affairs, but the times have changed. During the preceding weeks, we have observed that the Kenpeitai have proven themselves as an efficient force at suppressing the riots on the streets of Guangdong, and we wish that they continue doing so for the time being.

By relaxing some of the strict surveillance we have on the Kenpeitai, we can turn a blind eye to some of their violent actions on the streets to maximize the efficiency of the crackdown against the rioters. For the first time, we actually have a use for Japan's brutal secret police, and it is very useful indeed. At this rate, the riots will dissipate soon enough, and we can return to normalcy.
strings.GNG_loosen_the_kenpeitais_leash_tt:
The people need to understand that the £GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai have been held back - for their sake.
They need to be reminded that it can always get worse.
strings.GNG_take_out_the_ringleaders_desc:
The riots, though violent, are very highly organized. The rioters are divided into factions with their own chain of command, like a true criminal organization. The only thing that has been keeping the factions cohesive and operating as one are the leaders of these factions. After some time has passed since the beginning of the riots, it has become clear that a few key individuals stand out as the leaders of movements, and as organizers of the riots. With their presence on the streets, the morale of the rioters run high, and their organizational skills mean that there is little to none factional divide within the dissenting factions..

With this in mind, it is only common sense that the police force will target these key individuals to be taken out of the picture, by methods of capture, imprisonment, or even execution. Having them out of the picture will mean that the riots grow disunited, making it much easier to disperse.
strings.GNG_take_out_the_ringleaders_tt:
A dissident without £GNG_rioters_texticon leadership is an angry hooligan.
Remove the £GNG_rioters_texticon leadership, and our work becomes far easier.
strings.GNG_subdue_the_headless_chicken_desc:
The minds and the heads of the riots have been removed from their body, and now before us, we have a headless chicken still running amok. The lack of proper leadership within the riots have caused its desired effects. Riots stopped becoming organized, and groups of the dissenting factions began disagreeing with their peers. The common movement within the streets of Guangdong has effectively been thrown into a state of disarray. We can now begin the process of cleaning up the place.

The headless chicken that is the remaining riots on the streets can now be subdued with ease. We can now safely crackdown on the rioters with unrestrained ruthlessness and brutality, without fear of further radicalizing the movement, as their leaders have been eliminated from the scene. Rest assured, we have come as close as we have been to stopping these riots, and soon, peace will return to the streets.
strings.GNG_subdue_the_headless_chicken_tt:
No clever tactics or schemes - just unrelenting pressure and power.
It's the only way to be sure.
strings.GNG_rout_them_to_the_last_man_desc:
For a long time, our main directive is to eliminate any and all dissent within Guangdong, for a long time, we have fought for that goal, and for the first time since the beginning, we are finally close to achieving it. We have weakened them, and they are on their last legs. Only one more nudge and the entire building will come down. The riots are now reduced to individual protests and isolated incidents, and mostly, the widespread chaos has been contained, but it is not over just yet.

Not a single person who wishes bad for Guangdong can be allowed to escape justice. For the sake of Guangdong's future, one final push, the last one to completely eliminate dissent. There will be no man left standing from the rioters, for we will rout them to the last man.
strings.GNG_rout_them_to_the_last_man_tt: The last 10% of the work is always the hardest.
strings.GNG_from_ashes_to_ashes_desc:
Throughout the past tumultuous decade, Guangdong has been rocked by a repeating pattern of civil unrest and economic strife. It is a cycle which has left many scars across the facade of the nation, most of which will never truly heal.

The damage done has been largely indiscriminate, only a few fortunate elites at the top of the corporate power structure have suffered little more than the occasional restless night obsessing over profit margins. So damaging have these recent events been, even the Chief Executive himself has not been spared the merciless uncertainty...
strings.GNG_from_ashes_to_ashes_tt: There is a crest and a trough for every wave, every cycle upon which billions of yen turn. Such is business; such is life.
strings.GNG_guangdong_rises_desc:
Though uncertainty persists, something resembling stability has at last returned to the streets of Guangdong after the terrible disorder brought by the riots and the Oil Crisis. We had come close to being toppled by hostile individuals who, failing to understand the reality of the situation, set out to force reform down our throats without any regard to broader considerations or the reality of life. But we have pacified them one way or the other.

At last, with peace once more fully enshrined, the established order of corporations in Guangdong can once again begin their great work of driving Guangdong into a new, better era.
strings.GNG_guangdong_rises_tt: If there's a silver lining to the tumult of recent months, it's that people are eager to forget the past, to rush.
strings.GNG_from_the_pearl_river_delta_desc: During the Oil Crisis and the Riots that followed it, we emphasized that we - not the overly charitable reformists of the State Faction, nor the 'meritocrats' and tech-fiddlers of Fujitsu, nor indeed the advocates of the 'Manchurian Plan“ over at Hitachi - we are the sole guarantor of progress and prosperity for this state and its people. We did everything we could to make this clear, and now we are repairing the benefits thereof; one example of this is found in Guangdong's recent onrush of electronics production. All manner of electrical goods are now produced in the State of Guangdong; they fulfill every possible demand or desire a customer could possibly dream of, all at prices that no one in their right mind would ever dare turn down.
strings.GNG_from_the_pearl_river_delta_tt: Our factories hum once again with the energy of machines and men...
strings.GNG_within_the_sphere_desc:
Once upon a time, Guangdong was an inconsequential fragment of the Japanese empire, a pitiful backwater overshadowed and overlooked by its neighbours. It was for that reason that during the various crises of the last decades all the protestations of the members of the Co-Prosperity Sphere that we are a “rising star” and “critically important to the triumph of Pan-Asianism” proved to be for naught; we were simply 'not worth defending' in their eyes. But as we emerge from the recent instability, it has become very clear that that is no longer the case.

The State of Guangdong and its innovative corporations are now the future of the Sphere, not the antiquated, brutish industrial chaos of Manchukuo that Komai fetishizes even now. Our economy is now indisputably vital to that of the Co-Prosperity Sphere; if they ever wish to bring about that co-prosperity of theirs, they will need our help to do so.
strings.GNG_within_the_sphere_tt: ...with Matsushita's leadership a shining example for the Sphere at large...
strings.GNG_to_the_world_beyond_desc:
Who now dares to doubt that Guangdong is host to pioneers of the new technological order and bright lights of the new electronic golden age? Even when the daggers of hate and envy were pointed at our engineers and laborers from every direction during the world-historical disaster that was the Oil Crisis, they persisted in their labors. Hell burned and high water churned around us, but the Guangdong workers kept working; the riots did not put a stop to their diligent progress.

The expertise and innovation that have been nurtured in Guangdong during these years of Chief Executive Matsushita's rule have begun to draw long-overdue international recognition. Products designed and manufactured on the Pearl River Delta and in Guangdong are now considered to be without parallel anywhere in the world.
strings.GNG_to_the_world_beyond_tt: ...and the world at large pays notice to the products of the Silicon Delta.
strings.GNG_one_mans_ambition_desc:
In the aftermath of all the shocks that have struck to the heart of our state, there was only one man who proved capable of leading the nation - Matsushita Masaharu. The will of the august corporations of Guangdong had entrusted Chief Executive Matsushita Masaharu with the welfare of the Land of the Three Pearls. As Matsushita led Guangdong and the company that bears his family name through the recent disasters, he aimed to remain on top of it all, trying to keep himself fully in control over the direction that the state took.

Matsushita Masaharu stands at the helm of the ship of state, but his future prospects are decided. We shall see if he managed to keep his hand on the tiller, or if someone else wrested it from him.
strings.GNG_one_mans_ambition_tt: The Chief Executive sits behind his desk, and receives his guests...
strings.GNG_looking_toward_the_future_desc:
Guangdong has never been a country over-reliant on “tried and tested traditional methods”, nor has it been one to avoid the opportunity to innovate. Far from that, our country is one to look firmly ahead, with its eyes kept to the future. We persistently seek new ways, new methods of increasing profit and improving the effectiveness of our products.

The riches the future is certain to bring to us because of our devotion to this approach are ready and waiting for anyone persistent and strong enough to take it.
strings.GNG_looking_toward_the_future_tt: Under visionary leadership, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong strides into the 1970's...
strings.GNG_beholden_to_the_past_desc:
Those who, over the last decade, have striven to transform this land of Guangdong into an industrial and technological centre unrivalled in the Sphere or indeed among all humanity know very well just how the opportunity came about. They remember the instability and misery that plagued their earliest attempts to establish technological progress in this nation, and the incessant Japanese and Kenpeitai interventions those incidents brought about.

Though the watchful gaze of Tokyo and the restless Kenpeitai officers have more or less withdrawn to the shadows since the rise of Matsushita Masaharu, it is by no means certain that things will remain this way. Chinese subversion is now on the rise. There will certainly come a time when the Chief Executive has no choice but to let these previous enforcers return from the shadows.
strings.GNG_beholden_to_the_past_tt: ...in the proud tradition of the Matsushita family, even if Masaharu is not related by blood...
strings.GNG_brought_into_a_new_age_desc:
Even after the instability and confusion that the Oil Crisis brought, the new decade is still young; it is certain to be one of risk and boundless opportunities for the acquisition and usage of wealth. Anyone who is willing or able to take a chance is capable of gaining unimaginable wealth or being thrown into the depths of poverty by losing everything they have.

As for the Chief Executive, Matsushita Masaharu, whatever his faults or accomplishments have been over these past years as ruler of the Pearl River Delta, he has survived a near-decade in his position at the head of the table, and will now see the first fruits of his time in power.
strings.GNG_brought_into_a_new_age_tt: ...for the spirit of enterprise is unquenchable and eternal, in the face of war and turmoil to come.
strings.GNG_new_pearls_for_a_new_era: New Pearls for a New Era
strings.GNG_the_right_people_in_the_right_places: The Right People in the Right Places
strings.GNG_chief_executive_ibuka_desc:
Ibuka Masaru, a man of purpose. Indeed conviction has proven the mightiest weapon of all, with which one holds his ground in the face of adversity and triumphs over those who mock his unrelenting march forward as mere folly. Only Ibuka knows what's best for Guangdong, whine as the cowards and naysayers might; only he knows the path to a brighter future, and this truth alone cements his superiority over lesser men like Morita Akio and Matsushita Masaharu.

Conviction is his raison d'être, as much as it has been the driving force behind his ascension to the helm of Guangdong. There, he shall ready the gadgets and finally begin Guangdong's renovation into what it is always meant to be: a true beacon of innovation, where the Sphere's brightest minds shall convene and labor to their hearts' content for the betterment of all mankind.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_ibuka_tt: Our Chief Executive, £GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Ibuka Masaru, looks towards a future etched in silicon and lit with neon...
strings.GNG_an_engineers_touch_desc:
Ibuka Masaru, a man of expertise. What is an engineer, the unyielding backbone of progress, if his mind were to be bogged down by nonsensical ramblings shamelessly disguised as “ideological principles”, and by hordes of pen-pushers content with cowering behind barricades of documents and walls of cash?

No, Ibuka is an engineer in the purest sense, a futurist above abstractions and irrationality. He has come to grasp, better than ideologues and bureaucrats ever could, the ultimate nature of macroscopic global society as but a system of equations; its inhabitants the plethora of variables within, and the tenets of science, their definitive solution.
strings.GNG_a_visionarys_dream_desc:
Ibuka Masaru, a man of ambition. The Jewel of the South in his dreams is to be the ideal laboratory, slave no more to inutile paperwork and counterproductive regulations; its occupants, men of unparalleled faculty in their own right, no longer caged animals awaiting slaughter by spineless office-bearers willfully ignorant of the potential of human intellect.

An engineers' paradise, a greenhouse of merit, where those who excel shall roam unshackled and redefine Guangdong's society beyond the wildest of imaginations.
strings.GNG_dragging_guangdong_into_the_future_d:
Ibuka Masaru, a man of unwavering dedication. Already confronting the new overseer of Guangdong's rebirth are one infuriating rot after another festering deep within its apartments, factories, and government halls under his very eyes - stagnation, ignorance, complacency, gifted men and women consigned to irrelevancy and oblivion like forsaken Pearls buried beneath the murky depths of the River.

To the weak-willed all of this might prove too daunting a task, too insurmountable a barrier; but Ibuka will endure, just as he has done ever since his days in the Imperial Japanese Navy. Come what may, under the guidance of him and him alone Guangdong will reclaim its deserved spot on the world stage: the upper bound of possibilities, the definition of progress, and the apex of humanity's future upon which the reverent gaze of billions would fall - even if it means he'll have to drag it there, kicking and screaming.

No one, not one person with a hint of rationality, shall be allowed to stand in his way. After all, if one single man could shatter all limits and attain true enlightenment for himself, why can't millions?
strings.GNG_dragging_guangdong_into_the_future_t: ...and there is no place in £GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Ibuka's vision for laggards or dullards.
strings.GNG_begin_the_dissection_desc: Guangdong's current economic state is appalling, the inefficient systems dotting its structure and the abhorrent and careless management of its assets have rendered it rapidly descending and one foot in the grave. A full scale intensive dissection will have to be performed on Guangdong's inner economic apparatus to discover the exact cause of this despicable plague, but also the way to lead it to a swift and profitable reconstruction.
strings.GNG_begin_the_dissection_tt: Innovation cannot be borne from wasteful, legacy initiatives. Out with the old - and in with the new.
strings.GNG_liquidate_nonessentials_desc: The state's finances are riddled with useless and counterproductive deficits, these programs may look impressive, but are an immense liability to us. Programs akin to welfare and state subsidies, reminders of the inefficiency of our lackadaisical and apathetic predecessors, can have easily been abolished to be diverted to more profitable and fruitful pursuits.
strings.GNG_liquidate_nonessentials_tt: We must jettison our economic deadweight...
strings.GNG_raise_expectations_desc: As of currently, the rate of production and profit in the factories of Guangdong had decreased severely, no doubt because of the tolerance for inertia and open laziness present in the corporations. If Guangdong is going to soar above its economic competitors, its foundations, the corporations, must be rigid and efficient in their work. As such, let it be known that any continued inability or carelessness will be rooted out. We expect only the maximum of competence to be seen in any corporation, whether it be Sony, Matsushita, or even Fujitsu. Failure is intolerable.
strings.GNG_isolate_inefficient_firms_desc: Guangdong is known as a land of opportunity, attracting new businesses from far and wide. Though, if you fail to grasp this opportunity, you are to fester in the dust. Many old businesses in Guangdong had failed to turn a profit for a sustained amount of time, and it is clear that they are failing. In order for us to instate our own vision for a modern, efficient and capable Guangdong, it is necessary for these liabilities to be wiped off the records, quickly and quietly. We will isolate these already struggling firms and corner them with market power, and there's always the coffers of Fujitsu.
strings.GNG_survival_of_the_fittest_desc:
Darwinism - that survival comes to those who adapt - is the core theorem of evolutionary theory, the perfect ingredient of inspiration, innovation, and excellence; and a concept in dire need of rehabilitation.

What the slothful and incompetent decry as “injustice”, we call equal-opportunity competition with equal-opportunity rewards; what the gluttonous establishment denounce as “hazardous managerial conduct”, we call a long overdue adrenaline shot revitalizing our product, resource, and labor markets away from irreversible stagnation. We have shown Guangdong the path to prosperity; then we need only to observe as it claws and bites its way there on its own.
strings.GNG_survival_of_the_fittest_tt: ...so that we may survive, and thrive.
strings.GNG_purge_the_incompetent_desc:
The inhabitants of Guangdong are in for a rude awakening. Too many of those scientifically illiterate and intellectually bankrupt have been infesting our streets, factories, laboratories, and government institutions, nibbling away Guangdong's creativity, productivity, and fiscal health - all while indulging themselves in ignorance and hedonism defiling our societal and economic landscape, whether they realize it or not.

Let those mules blissfully drown themselves in their cesspits one last time - for they won't get another chance to ever again. When the time comes, let's see how fast they'll scramble behind their pretty masks of innocence and stand in the way of Guangdong's revival. Our hammer will strike faster.
strings.GNG_purge_the_incompetent_tt: The lazy, the corrupt, and the simply unskilled - they will all be shown the door.
strings.GNG_reward_loyalties_desc:
Indeed, too many of the inept and incompetent have been clogging up our society - precisely the reason why going overboard with our purge isn't as desirable as it seems. We simply could not afford alienating certain upright and law-abiding individuals who, although lacking in competence, would've made for excellent guardians of our state apparatus - keeping other officials in line and keeping corruption and degeneracy out.

Those who prove themselves of immense integrity and moral standing deserve to take charge of the rank and file of the government. A bit of intellectual... impediment can be pardoned of course, for all we ask of our citizenry are loyal recruits to aid our struggle for the greater good.
strings.GNG_enact_education_quotas_desc:
Guangdong is walking on a tightrope - and even the slightest of hesitation, the most trivial of mistakes, can send it plummeting into the bottomless pit below. Our future has no room for compromises; only room for the best-learned of our civil servants funnelling decades of accumulated knowledge into the optimization of state operations.

Such is the purpose behind implementing education quotas for higher governmental posts: a literal foolproof barrier against the dimwitted and the inexpert, protecting government functionality from degradation. It shouldn't be of concern to us that education in Guangdong is a “Japanese-only privilege”; in fact, petty ethnic matters shouldn't be of concern to us at all, for all we ask of our citizenry are competent recruits to aid our struggle for the greater good.
strings.GNG_the_guangdong_civil_service_ordinanc: The time has come for Ibuka Masaru to exercise his powers as Guangdong's Chief Executive, and bring his proposals regarding streamlining and optimizing its civil service sector to proper fruition in the Legislative Council. Should our rival corporations see reason, the Civil Service Ordinance will be a handy scalpel with which to cleanse the bureaucracy of inefficiency, as well as a display and reinforcement of Ibuka's personal executive clout for the sake of his grand vision.
strings.GNG_the_falling_profits_problem_desc: Without increased profits from the start, and therefore extra funding from which to initiate additional projects, current plans are doomed to fail before they can truly begin. Fortunately, the Chief Executive is both willing and able to make some money the old fashioned way when the situation calls for it.
