strings.GNG_keep_it_a_secret_desc:
Canines are quite the nuisance, they are - easily provoked, even a step on the tail could send them flying into an irritating rampage. Couple that with their cancerous pack mentality, and in no time humongous blights of walking, barking flesh would congregate upon the sanctity of Guangdong's soil.

The only fitting way to dispose of them would therefore be mass euthanasia, with which not as much as a squeal will be allowed out of those rabid wretches' mouths before they're put out of their misery. Crackling gunfire would've brought us the same number of bodies anyway.
strings.GNG_beg_us_for_death_desc:
There are people that scurry in the shadows, etching mischief into articles and journalistic pieces; their filth corrupts the minds of readers, and rots of the morale of our hard-working people. Guangdong will show no tolerance towards beliefs antithetical to its industrious traditions, nor to those who spout them.

Like poison to rats, we will initiate a series of raids and take-downs in places where we suspect these criminals fester, to ultimately eradicate their presence altogether. No matter if their nails claw the very brick walls as we drag them from where they dwell, it is paramount these animals are punished for their deviance and mischief.
strings.GNG_an_invitation_for_the_best_desc:
Whilst our auxiliary police units prowl the streets in search for scum to throw into dark pits, locked away from the touch of sunlight until they wither away in the cold, we are far from our desired goal in settling restless crowds. Therefore, it is in our best interests to invite experts in the realm of crushing dissent.

By issuing formal requests and invitations to Mangyō representatives and agents in Manchukuo, offering them positions of authority over policing and state security, we welcome the very best into our ranks. May our ties to the company produce fruitful responses, and may the subduing of insurgent forces be found among them.
strings.GNG_without_a_trace_desc:
A product of our arduous and infinitely righteous endeavor to eliminate the hideous stain of dissent from Guangdong and restore her former serenity, tens of thousands of incarcerated entities now languish rightfully in our prisons and holding facilities. These disruptive and unruly scum have proven themselves to be of no value or contribution to functional society, only serving the purpose of opposing our virtuous and sublime administration. Though they may be considered repulsive vermin, even vermin hold the ability to perform sufficient labor, and this fact is not lost upon our astute Chief Executive.

We will organize the captured dissidents into labor forces that are to be dispersed throughout the rural hinterlands of Guangdong. They are to obsequiously assist in the development of various resource extraction programs, effectively brandishing them assets who will provide something of benefit for our regime. However minuscule or minute the returns may be, due to their inattentive and evasive nature, it at the very least ensures that they will not be worthlessly benefiting from Guangdong's existing resources. They are numerous and expendable - a model workforce.
strings.GNG_purging_the_innards_desc:
We are a nation of diligent citizens, at constant toil to preserve our hard-working way of life from corrupting and subverting forces creeping in filthy backstreets and swallowing shadows. Such forces, wherever they may be found, are nothing but the craft of traitors, but using an enemy is far more effective than stomping one out.

Be they from the highest echelons of society, or from the dirtiest of those living on the streets, their crimes will not go unpunished. Their trials will rally public hatred against the enemies of our regime, whether they know it or not, and work in our favor to manage and control public opinion. Soon enough, we will be dividing the goats from the sheep.
strings.GNG_necessary_sacrifices_desc:
As a result of the hard work of law enforcement across this great nation, the sick and dissident traitors prowling in the shadows have been scraped from the darkness of city streets and thrown into cold jail cells for the rest of their lives. Indeed, their capture has been a wonderful tool in manipulating the public's fear, and mangling their perception of 'responsible government'.

However, there is little use in keeping them alive to whimper pathetically in their cells, rotting away as they howl tears of despair; it is far too expensive, and so our Chief Executive has authorized an order to lodge a bullet between their eyes. Their submission has outlived its use, and so they too will follow suit.
strings.GNG_swallowed_by_the_night_desc:
With much of the burdensome dissidents having been suitably apprehended and subdued, our already limited capacity is on the verge of collapsing day by day. As our devoted and praiseworthy security forces continue the process of expunging all traces of sinister dissent from our society, the incarceration facilities are slowly becoming a symbol that arbitrarily and wrongfully paints our administration as one of tyranny and regression. Certainly, this notion cannot be allowed to develop any further, unless we wish to incur increased dissent upon ourselves.

The primary solution presented for the issue is to alleviate amounts of stress from the prisons, separate and disperse the entities being held in them to remote and confidential locations, safely hidden from the public eye. This will ensure that no common crowd consensus of resistance ever comes to form, there will be no icons of martyrdom or what they perceive as persecution, there will not be a second Bastille.
strings.GNG_a_million_bowed_heads_desc:
A police state. A “humanitarian hellhole”. Such are the dozens upon dozens of condemnations conjured up and lobbed at us by weak-hearted hypocrites resting upon their own mountains of loot across the lands and seas. To those adversaries we testify: all are true, and in this we take utmost, unrepentant pride.

For what are duteous children if not subjects to the hardest of flogging, to the harshest of discipline? What is to become of the Pan-Asian man, were he to succumb to the greatest vice of all and defile himself with treachery? The Rising Sun, of course, permits no such error. Up above in the firmament she gleams, and delivers her crimson rays upon every obedient citizen, every turning cog, and every bar of gold to grace this oasis of prosperity; of those who dare to defy her light, only scorched bones will remain.
strings.GNG_a_million_bowed_heads_tt: When they know fear, we will know peace.
strings.GNG_never_to_be_seen_again_desc:
As our efforts to comprehensively expel all elements of dissent from the once pristine pearls continue to advance, our plans for the compulsory relocation of incarcerated dissidents need to be cemented alongside the progression of other matters. While dislodging them to the expansive rural regions of Guangdong may seem the most obvious and efficient solution, it does not completely achieve our purposes of keeping them from the public eye, as the rather meager size of our state and the extensive amount of dissidents may lead to accidents which are rather avoidable. It has become apparent that the most viable and reasonable solution would be to contact our benefactors to the north, the Mangyō Corporation and their lucrative breadbasket of Manchukuo, abundant with vacant territories and away from any unwanted prying eyes.

Therefore, we will transport all captured dissidents and their families to the factories and fields of Manchukuo, where they will toil away beneath the guardianship of Mangyō. Undoubtedly, this will strengthen our ties and grow our favorability with our largest backer, as well as effectively silencing the embers of disobedience upon our soil.
strings.GNG_never_to_be_seen_again_tt: We have no need for dissidents - though the factories and mines of £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Manchukuo are hiring...
strings.GNG_one_million_is_a_statistic_desc:
Dogs. Rats. Maggots. How we have expunged those reprehensible vermin form every corner on our map, with fewer than hundreds left walking and tainting this earth; how we have dutifully channeled the arsenal of terror, disciplined ourselves with chains and bullets and suffocated ourselves with waterboards, and called upon whatever vicious gadgets and unforgiving measures Guangdong so direly demands of us!

Because who are we to turn our backs on her wails of distress, to sit idly by at the sight of her diseased physique - pale, emaciated, yet eternally pregnant with riches? Even as the stars turn and the years elapse, so many remain who would decry our righteousness and devotion as cruelty, tyranny, barbarism; all we did was came to Guangdong's aid and protected her, as we will continue to until the day our souls expire, against the ghastly and all-devouring night.
strings.GNG_one_million_is_a_statistic_tt: Do not count those left behind. They are the inevitable casualties of £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi's progress.
strings.GNG_miracle_on_the_pearl_river_desc:
At long last. Four long years of labor. Four painstaking years to cleanse Guangdong of savagery and bring her back under the Rising Sun's light. Now she soars higher and prouder than ever - above the pitch-dark clouds of ignorance and complacency, her immaculate wings powered by the blood and sweat of the inferiors and every single imbecile daring to stand in the way of her emancipation.

We thank our wise Chief Executive, for showing us the way and leading our crusade against the omnipresent grasp of degeneracy; we thank the diligent men of Hitachi, for restoring to us the limitless wealth Guangdong so rightfully deserves; and above all, we thank the most loyal of our citizens - men or women, young or old - for taking their stand against the rabid dogs conspiring to take away from us this glorious, unprecedented golden era of ours: one of prosperity and of righteous harmony.

Ten thousand years to His Majesty the Emperor and his eternal benevolence! To the everlasting glory and fraternity of Dai-Tōa Kyōeiken!
Banzai! Banzai! Banzai!
strings.GNG_miracle_on_the_pearl_river_tt: Komai has not just changed £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - it is a £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong built in his, and £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Manchukuo's, grand ambitions.
strings.GNG_the_public_order_and_police_law: The Public Order and Police Law
strings.GNG_shut_up_and_get_on_with_it: Shut Up and Get on With It
strings.GNG_guangdong_thirsts_desc:
Guangdong, an entity defined by her immaculate serenity and the delightful omnipresent aura of prosperity; a paragon of economic stability and success, the pinnacle of social concord and solidarity. We must ensure that this image of Guangdong, an image of triumph and success, is protected and upheld with diligence against the destructive forces lingering around our state.

The ocean of the global markets is stirring with intensified vigor, the tempestuous and turbulent waves threatening to engulf the pristine pearl of Guangdong in perpetual darkness as the supply of oil plummets, threatening the livelihoods of our devoted citizens. Though the drastic increase in oil prices may only seem like a temporary issue, barely affecting the daily happenings of our society as of current, it is apparent that if this affair is indeed a prolonged crisis, the Three Pearls will be devastated and the economic stability of Guangdong will be in peril. Our Chief Executive and the administration will conceive of solutions to this looming disaster, in order for Guangdong to maintain her grace and decency, our coffers must remain filled.

The ship of Guangdong shall survive this endeavor, for there are no storms we cannot weather.
strings.GNG_guangdong_thirsts_tt:
In good times and bad, the master provides.
So will £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi provide?
strings.GNG_hitachi_manchukuo_ending_one_point_t: Komai will chain £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong closer to the £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Manchurians and £GFX_MAN_mangyo_texticon Mangyō.
strings.GNG_hitachi_komai_ending_one_point_tt: Our Chief Executive will push forward his own system and assert himself.
strings.GNG_trial_by_fire_desc:
As the shadow of yet another crisis looms over the territories and businesses of Guangdong, its ghastly and horrendous form causing the decline of so many of our prized institutions, our Chief Executive, Komai Kenichirō, must once again take up the burden of state and clear the obstructions on Guangdong's glorious and righteous path to continued triumph and success. Did the great men of yore not have to face challenges in their ascent to prominence and power? Did Caesar, Alexander, or Napoleon not have to face adversities on their paths to grandeur and victory? The Oil Crisis shall not be Komai's Waterloo, instead, it shall act as Komai's Austerlitz, a trial of the endurance and benefit of the administrative apparatus that our Chief Executive has bestowed upon us, another obstacle to surmount that will further prove the success of Hitachi's rule over the Three Pearls.

The administration and our Chief Executive shall be ready. It might not be easy, it might not be smooth, but we shall emerge from the flames emboldened and strengthened, the future ahead of us.
strings.GNG_trial_by_fire_tt:
Guangdong will survive.
£GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi's Guangdong - or Komai's Guangdong?
strings.GNG_the_executives_order_desc: Our loyal and devoted citizens, the lifeblood of Guangdong's productive engine, assets that will determine the fate of Guangdong's uncertain yet bright future, building blocks that serve to support Guangdong's continued state of perpetual prosperity. These pieces, pawns in the grand design of our Chief Executive, must be kept calm and useful, as they are the key to protecting Guangdong and her serenity from the menace that is the Oil Crisis. Our Chief Executive shall interrupt the regularly scheduled programming of Guangdong's televisions and radios, and instead broadcast a message, one of hope and assurances, requesting the faith and trust of the populace, so that they may be united in the battle against the vicious elements of this looming crisis. Though the words may not be entirely genuine, it is of no doubt that it will serve its purpose, that the masses of the Three Pearls will be kept in check.
strings.GNG_the_executives_order_tt: When the Chief Executive speaks, the people listen...
strings.GNG_abundans_cautela_non_nocet_desc:
The streets of Guangdong have always been a wild and unruly realm, one where the anarchic masses and crowds wield authority, defying the prosperous rule of order and stability. When our Chief Executive stood ascendant above his rivals, he brought cohesion and balance back to the public sphere, enforcing righteous and stringent laws and increasing the police presence, ensuring that the Three Pearls would be kept orderly.

However, it is now apparent that the abhorrent chaos of the past is returning once more, as the rising rate of unemployment and renewed volatility of the markets have made the populace fearful and recalcitrant. Our Chief Executive will once again increase security measures, imposing stricter regulations and more frequent arrests. Lawfulness will be maintained, our current hardships are not an excuse for disorder.
strings.GNG_abundans_cautela_non_nocet_tt:
Those who find themselves on the streets have only themselves to blame.
And if we need to call in help from £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Xinjing to keep them in line, so be it.
strings.GNG_patriots_have_nothing_to_fear_desc: Although the presence of dissidents on the streets is a concern to us, it is merely a minute fraction of Guangdong's total population, ensuring that no major functions of the state are hampered due to it. Keeping the rest of the populace in check is of the utmost importance, as such, we shall provide them with promises and assurances and shower them with the prospects of reward. The media and our postal service shall be instructed to deliver messages meant to provide our citizens with an incentive to remain loyal and obedient. Although it is disappointing that the people still do not completely and willingly adhere to our Chief Executive's admirable design, we will do what is needed to maintain that design, the people will have to live with it, for reality is held in our hands.
strings.GNG_patriots_have_nothing_to_fear_tt:
We offer a bargain - work with £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai, and reap the rewards.
It's not necessary to say what happens to those who don't cooperate.
strings.GNG_lights_out_desc:
Electricity is undoubtedly the lifeblood of Guangdong, the essence that maintains the well-oiled machine and ensures that our industrial output remains constant and undisturbed. However, it seems that the Oil Crisis has brought our energy production and reserves to a tenuous situation, as the state of the economy forces the power plants to operate at a slower rate, we can no longer match the rate of consumption in the cities across Guangdong. Our Chief Executive, in an act of brilliance, has mandated that electricity be rationed across the Three Pearls to ensure that electricity will be available for factories and manufacturing plants. During the daytime, electricity will be completely allocated to the industrial sectors, while the residential sectors will have to survive off of the resplendent rays of the Sun.

While most of the inhabitants of the Three Pearls will be given access to lights in the evenings, we cannot assure this for many disadvantaged denizens who reside in derelict and aging tower complexes. Fortunately, these dilapidated tenements are teeming with dissidents and agitators, the intervals of darkness may provide opportunities for raids and quiet operations, our security forces may find executing their duties much easier this way.
strings.GNG_we_are_watching_desc:
Desperation and misery are catalysts for crime and transgressions, unfortunately for our administration, desperation and misery are abundant in these arduous times. Our Chief Executive has already enacted several measures to combat the increased rate of misconduct rife on the streets due to the stagnation the Oil Crisis has caused, though they are certainly effective, we may need to employ additional efforts to fully maintain control on the streets.

The solution to our problems is surveillance, by utilizing organized and efficient systems of security cameras and electronic devices, we can extend our vision over the entirety of the Three Pearls, ensuring that nobody steps out of line. When these procedures are enforced, we shall know the identities of every single offender, the exact time and place, and the offenses committed. The people need to be reminded once more of the consequences of their actions and the futility of evasion, for it is simply not possible.
strings.GNG_notch_off_a_few_zeroes_desc:
The Oil Crisis is a malicious and vile serpent, wrapping its horrible, slithery form around the immaculate and pristine pearl of Guangdong, threatening the brilliant design of our astute Chief Executive. The despicable serpent ravages all, but there is one particular subset of people to which it has taken a liking, the poor.

The poor and needy of Guangdong have always been a nuisance and a center of disobedience and dissent, when the Oil Crisis descended upon the Three Pearls, the noose tightened. In order for us to discourage the unproductive dregs of society from joining agitator movements and protests, we need to offer them something in return to keep them quiet and complacent. A large reason why the impoverished remain in their state is due to overwhelming debt, if we agree to enact legislation that would erase a large portion of the aforementioned debt, it is likely that they would be satisfied. Although this may upset our benefactors at Mangyō, it is our belief that desperate times require unorthodox solutions, even if it involves operating at a loss.
strings.GNG_offer_no_alternative_desc:
Our efforts to crack down upon the unruly and riotous population of Guangdong are proceeding smoothly and efficiently, with the increase in arrests and continued monitoring by our security forces, it is almost certain that calm shall return to the streets in due time. This, however, does not mean that we should grow careless or lackadaisical regarding the manner, for apathy and neglect are the vices that doomed our predecessors.

The forces and units already present in the suppression of dissent shall be granted extra privileges and powers in order to allow them to execute their duties with maximum efficacy. To further ensure that discord is prevented, the media of Guangdong shall be silenced and kept on a leash, as information may encourage sympathizers to participate in these vile acts of selfishness.
strings.GNG_offer_no_alternative_tt:
Those who oppose us have three options: stay quiet, take it up with the Police, or try their luck with our 'imported' security forces.
Only one has a pleasant outcome.
strings.GNG_a_single_demand_desc:
Loyalty is mandatory and compulsory, in the state of turmoil and strife we are currently in, loyalty equates to survival. We will enact protocols to enforce a model of rewards and punishment; if the populace remains steadfast and obedient, they shall be allocated additional resources and stimuli; if the populace refuses to adhere to the orders of the administration, they shall face immense hardships and receive lower amounts of rations and energy.

By appealing to the natural urges of man, we predict that this will satisfy the Japanese and Zhujin communities of the Three Pearls, while the majority Chinese population will be appeased enough to prevent large-scale insubordination. Our brilliant Chief Executive once again displays his cunning and intelligence, success is guaranteed.
strings.GNG_a_single_demand_tt: Those loyal to £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai's vision shall survive - those with capital, those with knowledge, and finally, those with nothing to give but their lives.
strings.GNG_the_coffers_crave_desc:
Our defence to the Oil Crisis has been deftly handled, but it seems deft hands are not enough to protect such a niche economy as our own. Our coffers are a ship, slowly sinking from a thousand tiny holes. Guangdong's bureaucracy stands at the precipice, and Komai's carefully assembled system only lingers thanks to the Chief Executive's great struggle.

Now is not the time to turn back, and we shall march forwards, no matter the casualties.
strings.GNG_the_coffers_crave_tt: The maw of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong's economy opens wide, and calls for more - more money, and more bodies.
strings.GNG_as_above_so_below_desc:
Even the proudest eagles are occasionally injured. Turning back to the mother and the nest is humiliating, but if Guangdong is an eagle, the Oil Crisis is an infected wound. The state must find some form of respite, even at the cost of Komai's pride.

Mangyō, the ex-patron of Komai and the Chief Executive's metaphorical nest, have been willing to help in the past, but whatever deal is made with the corporation always seems to bite Guangdong back down the line... While torched prides are painful things, collapsed nations are even more so.
strings.GNG_as_above_so_below_tt: An article of faith: £MAN_mangyo_texticon Mangyō will have the answers...
strings.GNG_out_with_the_gutting_knife_desc:
Budget cuts were not easy things to enact, but, when all the facts were in and the numbers were crunched, sometimes they were a lifesaving necessity.

Komai faced this issue with typical forthrightness and confidence. The only question was, “On which services do we enact the cuts?” Public services were the first obvious answer. By halving the budgets of certain amenities, community efforts, and public works, funds could be redirected into financial relief and police forces. Money could still flow throughout the country, albeit through different channels.

Naturally there'd be some disquiet about this, but it was all for the good. Komai signed the papers and had them dispatched.
strings.GNG_out_with_the_gutting_knife_tt: To pull men forward in hard times, demands a hard heart - hard choices that only £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Chief Executive Komai is prepared to make.
strings.GNG_squeezed_dry_desc: Now more than ever is increasing production needed in Guangdong. Government subsidies for research, development, and the ever lucrative integration and development of synthetic resources will boster this production, and should be implemented immediately, even at the cost of our last drops of credit...
strings.GNG_squeezed_dry_tt: Regrettably, we will need to spend money to make money - even if our superiors and colleagues disagree heavily.
strings.GNG_crunch_and_condense_desc:
In the interest of maximizing profits for industrial conglomerates Guangdong, companies not under Government oversight will be squeezed for the highest total output possible. This involves cutting corners, lengthening shifts, and skimping on benefits for longtime employees.

Komai is not completely sold on this approach, but in the interests of increasing Guangdong's prosperity, he will let it happen... for now...
strings.GNG_turn_it_up_a_notch_desc:
Hard times lay ahead. Komai's man in the treasury department approached him on Monday and grimly informed him that if they did not increase the government's reserve funds by ten percent by the next quarter, they would be, as he put it, “A bee in the giant hornet's jaws.” Komai resolved to act.

After analysing demographics for Guangdong, Komai signed a memorandum into effect which instituted a flat raise in taxes countrywide. Milking the Chinese for their money was trivial; the Chinese were too poor to afford to pick up their assets and flee the country and therefore had to stay and pay their dues. The Zhujin and Japanese, however, were another matter.

“Incentives must be given,” the memorandum stated, “to the Zhujin and Japanese living and working in Guangdong to remain in-country during this tax hike. Unlike their Chinese counterparts, they would have the means and the wherewithal to depart. Make every effort to encourage them to stay.”

As the papers went out, Komai was restless. This would be a tough time for the country. It would have to be met squarely and with determination.
strings.GNG_the_public_order_and_police_law_desc:
The POP Law is not something Komai is comfortable with. Allowing security officials from Mangyō and Manchukuo into the country and letting them act without oversight from Guangdong police feels like a recipe for disaster. But pressure is mounting from Mangyō and many government officials to sign it into law.

With a hesitant hand, Komai gives his personal accedance to the law and tells his supporters he will fight to bring it into effect post haste.
strings.GNG_the_public_order_and_police_law_tt: Our benefactors have given us the tools to pacify £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - all they need is the authority, independent of the meddlesome £GNG_police_texticon Police.
strings.GNG_shut_up_and_get_on_with_it_desc:
The accursed ingrates and bleeding hearts - dissident groups, public dissenters, you name it - will not stop bothering us with their incessant babble about 'reform' and 'humanity'. This cannot be borne; accordingly, Chief Executive Komai has reached a decision. We will pass the Civil Obedience Law, which will sever domestic communications such as phone lines and enforce harsh curfews, their unpopularity be damned.

The Chief Executive feels more comfortable implementing this measure as opposed to the Public Order and Police Law. He thinks it will not set off the ungrateful civilians as much as that law could have.
strings.GNG_shut_up_and_get_on_with_it_tt: Whatever is within our control to pacify the populace, we will use - even if it causes significant discomfort in everyday life.
strings.GNG_an_economy_besieged_desc:
Chief Executive Komai is of the view that further failure to pass more comprehensive economic measures is unjustifiable given the gravity of the current situation. Accordingly, he has directed that the budget be frozen before we are torn to pieces. We have no choice; no matter what we try, no other measures will suffice to stabilize the economy and ensure our hegemony over Guangdong persists.

It may raise eyebrows among investors, but the times are desperate and the Oil Crisis is roiling everyone economically. Few if any will dare question the wisdom of the Chief Executive in taking such a measure in times as terrible as these.
strings.GNG_an_economy_besieged_tt: To weather this storm, we must batten down the hatches - and decide who we let in alongside us.
strings.GNG_get_me_on_the_phone_desc:
Chief Executive Komai fears that if things go the way they are currently going for much longer, control over the Guangdong economy will be wrenched away from him. If, Heaven forbid, that were to happen, all our work over these past eight years purging decadence and folly from this state of Guangdong will have been for naught. It would start with our losing support from above and below and end with Komai being kicked out of the Chief Executive's office on the seat of his pants. To prevent this from taking place, the Chief Executive has decided to hedge his bets and put the relationships he's built with his various benefactors to use.

The Chief Executive does not deny that there are risks. For instance, Mangyō is certain to somehow cheat him or use his plea to squeeze something extra out of him. But Komai is certain that it is well worth the risk; any concessions he is forced to make are more than worth it in light of the benefit of preserving Guangdong with him at his head.
strings.GNG_get_me_on_the_phone_tt: To survive, we must look to allies with deeper pockets than ourselves...
strings.GNG_the_poisoned_water_desc:
With pressures on him mounting from every direction, Chief Executive Komai has no choice but to remain steadfast and stay the course. His system will survive come hell or high water; the cost matters not. Even the prospect of upsetting his benefactors once or twice by denying them an opportunity to prey upon Guangdong when she is at her weakest is of no concern to him whatsoever.

A reorganization of the economic department, prioritization of internal cooperation both inside and outside of the department, and a focus on the issue at hand will all ensure Guangdong can survive to see another year. Another major part of making sure that happens is granting Komai's Mangyō patrons no further concessions.
strings.GNG_the_poisoned_water_tt: The only people £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai needs are those who know their place - beneath his feet.
strings.GNG_guarantee_japanese_holdings_desc:
The Chief Executive is of the mind that we need to put our economic task forces to use to defend our rightful control over the State of Guangdong and right quickly at that. Following his wise instructions, we will now move to guarantee any and all Japanese holdings within the State of Guangdong. This is certain to remove the primary incentive for Japanese asset holders to leave the country, making sure that they will show due loyalty.

Granted, this may seem like an incremental measure, unsuitable for a time of drastic and decisive decision-making. But it is with these increments that stable foundations capable of weathering crises are built.
strings.GNG_slash_wages_desc:
If the State of Guangdong is to survive, its business establishment - which is the very foundation of its prosperity, lest we forget - needs to thrive, no matter the cost. If that requires cutting employees from the payrolls so be it; no cost is too small to pay for a stable balance book. The workers may complain or join the idiots in the streets, but that too means nothing to a wise businessman who knows better than to concern himself with the view of mere sheep and peasants.

The next decision on Chief Executive Komai's list follows from this. Let us declare a government-managed plan to slash employee wages in order to ensure that as many enterprises as possible will come out of the Oil Crisis alive.
strings.GNG_the_business_warrant_ordinance_desc:
Chief Executive Komai has another card up his sleeve. This time, he wishes to force any businesses not incorporated or formed in Guangdong to pay a tax before buying any warrant or order to do business with local labor or resources. This will make sure that no business owner enters or leaves the borders of our fair state without leaving just tribute to the beauty that is Guangdong.

The measure is controversial; already we hear murmurings of angry discontent among the Japanese elite and the Mangyō board of directors. But it is necessary and correct, Komai thinks. It will either encourage holders of money to stay and tie themselves down to the land of Guangdong as they always should have, or it will incentivize them to get out like the traitors they always were.
strings.GNG_a_coordinated_response_desc:
As the world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis rages on, it is time for us to call upon our oldest friend and ally, the esteemed Mangyō Corporation, with a view on establishing an economic forum. The Chief Executive is happy to ask them for help, and just as pleased at the prospect of working with Mangyō too to coordinate a response.

But there is one problem, and Komai is fully aware of it. During economic chaos like this, big corporations have a very easy time exploiting economies like those of Guangdong. As Komai knows, this runs the risk of weakening our economy. That in turn can damage Komai's own career and image as well as running the risk of angering the populace. As such, he will be very cautious about what he does and does not commit to in this forum.
strings.GNG_a_coordinated_response_tt: £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi and £GFX_MAN_mangyo_texticon Mangyō shall vanquish their enemies together.
strings.GNG_princeps_sum_desc:
Now it is time for our esteemed Chief Executive to address the people of the State of Guangdong once more. He will ask them to put their faith in him once again and trust that the glorious Machine that he built out of the ruins of the Yasuda Crisis will outlast the Oil Crisis. Then he will move on to outline a policy of recovery that will restore Guangdong to its rightful position of great wealth and international prestige and honor and ensure that those who deserve to hold economic control and influence are given free reign to do so.

After that, it will be time for Chief Executive Komai to get to work on his promises. He knows he must hurry; he has only so much time available to him.
strings.GNG_princeps_sum_tt: The Chief Executive is a harsh and solitary man, but even he needs loyal lieutenants.
strings.GNG_the_skin_of_our_teeth_desc:
As the world-historical disaster that is the Oil Crisis continues to roil Guangdong like nothing it has ever seen before, it is clear to even the most illiterate worker in the dingiest factory in the most remote town in the state that the economy is in a shambles and deteriorating with each passing day. Our honorable, esteemed Chief Executive knows the gravity of the situation and will take direct action to rectify it.

Today work shall begin to deal with the myriad issues the Oil Crisis has brought into sharp relief and see them solved once and for all. We have no choice but to act quickly; otherwise, Chief Executive Komai's days will be numbered, and all the work that we have done to rebuild Guangdong in the superior Manchurian image under his leadership will be for naught.
strings.GNG_the_skin_of_our_teeth_tt: £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - and £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi - will not survive if there is no market left standing at the end of the Oil Crisis.
strings.GNG_through_the_gauntlet_desc:
Thereafter, Chief Executive Komai will approve yet another re-evaluation of welfare spending. All kinds of complex and loophole-exploiting commissions will evaluate the successes of what little remains of the former Guangdong state social security program. But Komai knows what conclusion they will reach, since he preselected their recommendations to ensure that welfare is given only to those who deserve it.

Backed with these fixed reports, Komai will change the requirements for welfare receipt eligibility so that the Chinese are more or less totally excluded, thus ensuring that far less has to be pumped into that nuisance of a budget item. The Chinese, after all, do not need the same level of care as Japanese or Zhujin; being foreordained to live as laborers and servants, they should receive only the level of care that we ordinarily provide such people.
strings.GNG_through_the_gauntlet_tt: There are always ways to cut corners within our own authority. After all - what do the £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese really deserve, anyway?
strings.GNG_rework_resource_allocation_desc:
Another situation that has to be dealt with as quickly as possible is the matter of resource allocation. Let us take a metaphorical knife (santoku, gyutou, you name it) and cut up the complex system of supply and demand like so many pieces of sashimi at the dinner table. Resources will now be allocated in such a manner as will streamline production and electricity distribution throughout the State of Guangdong.

Ideally this measure, proposed by the Chief Executive, will save Guangdong enough resources to avoid a strain when the full economic recovery inevitably comes around.
strings.GNG_trim_the_fat_desc:
Any state that wishes to survive for more than two or three hours must prioritize the welfare of those who contribute the most to it, rewarding only the good and loyal servants. During a shortage of resources, this is by necessity at the cost of those who contribute less or are less loyal. In the case of our great State of Guangdong these are respectively the Japanese-Zhujin community and the Chinese rabble. The former are all-important; the latter are mere fuzz and redundancies that we can easily do without.

Let us trim the fat on our payrolls by instituting a quota system proportionate to employees and income of each business to fire Chinese workers so as to ensure that Zhujin and Japanese employees' jobs and economic status are protected. This is right and proper; after all, the strong take, and the weak accept their losses.
strings.GNG_trim_the_fat_tt:
Cost-cutting is a fact of life.
And the facts are that £GFX_MAN_mangyo_texticon Mangyō needs Japanese speakers more than Chinese bodies.
strings.GNG_fumble_the_numbers_desc:
Now the government will move on to the matter of taxes. Chief Executive Komai, joined as he often is by representatives of Mangyō, will go through the motions of structuring new tax codes with a view on publishing their results during the next state television and radio address. To the people that listen, these new laws will seem complex; that is because they are. They're actually designed to exploit the low-earning Chinese majority and work to promote further influence for the Mangyō and Hitachi monopolies.

Komai, though somewhat reticent as a lawmaker over the amount of influence Mangyō is beginning to gain over Guangdong, will approve the measure. But his doubts over it will remain.
strings.GNG_a_breath_of_new_life_desc:
The budget has been frozen for some time now, and we have felt the benefits of that measure in making sure that Guangdong successfully survives the worst of the Oil Crisis. Now that the nation is back on her feet, the Chief Executive is well-placed to begin the construction of a new budget to suit his aims and the further promulgation of the Manchurian Plan in Guangdong.

If all goes well, we will at last be able to abandon the economic fetters that this crisis has placed on us and get back to work, with spending free to approach normal levels for the first time in months. Then it will only be a matter of time before we can return to our task of promoting the glory and beauty of this great land of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_a_breath_of_new_life_tt: With all necessary adjustments made, £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong can adjust to its new normal.
strings.GNG_obligations_gentlemen_desc:
Amidst the economic wreckage that threatens the State of Guangdong, throwing everything that makes her great into instability, it is necessary for Chief Executive Komai to prioritize his Hitachi Limited's survival above all else. After all, if Hitachi falls flat, just what will Komai Kenichirō have left? His situation will make even the Morita Akio of the 1950s look like a rich man by comparison.
Any and all measures must be taken; any and all benefactors and acquaintances must be called in with due haste.

To that end, Komai will reach out to various officials he knows in Manchuria and Japan, and also strive to maintain his traditionally good relations with Mangyō (hiding his disdain from their earshot, of course).
strings.GNG_obligations_gentlemen_tt: If £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi rules, even amongst ashes - then we are satisfied.
strings.GNG_scratch_my_back_desc:
If we truly want Guangdong to survive, it is unfortunately not enough for us to rely upon the assistance of Mangyō or the favor of the Home Islands bureaucracy. We must also approach the Mangyō Corporation for bailouts and assistance with production. Early indications are that they are willing to help, but they - just like virtually any reasonable entity (charity, pah!) - want something in return. Chief Executive Komai will, of course, accept.

Make no mistake, it galls the Chief Executive to allow Mangyō another avenue for them to cheat and steal as they already do a thousand different ways. But Komai knows his situation; he knows that this is one of the only options he has left, and one of the options he knows he can at least somewhat influence.
strings.GNG_scratch_my_back_tt: Surely corporate headquarters in £MAN_manchukuo_texticon Xinjing will understand our needs...
strings.GNG_learn_from_example_desc: Having successfully obtained the help we require from Mangyō, we must now learn from the great examples that they have set in productivity, efficiency, and innovation. Accordingly, we will move to adapt their successful industrial techniques and styles of research and development to the Guangdong and Hitachi contexts. As a result, we will be able to increase production while cutting down on prices, in turn, this will improve the state of our budget and free us to do other, more important things.
strings.GNG_surgical_efficiency_desc:
It is the considered opinion of Chief Executive Komai that while Hitachi is efficient, it can do yet better than it currently does, and it will if he has anything to say about it. So he will now pressure Hitachi to evaluate every payroll and budget allocation within Guangdong down to a T with a view on saving money and maximizing efficiency.

True, this measure will upend a lot of fat-cat senior bureaucrats who have probably not gone outside in years, but it will not take more than a reminder of their place in Guangdong to shut them up when they start screeching. After all, it is not them but the Chief Executive who determines what does and does not happen in this State of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_surgical_efficiency_tt: £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi must be ruthless with itself - because if we aren't, the market will be.
strings.GNG_if_it_aint_broke_desc:
Amidst the current economic crisis, demand for goods produced in Guangdong has collapsed; nobody has the money required to buy any of them. This is self-evident to anyone with eyes to see and ears to hear, and cannot be ignored.

Accordingly, Hitachi will now cut down on its output to match the current demand and be more in step with the current disposable income levels of the average consumer. By saving the money that would go to production and funnelling it to places where it will be of more use, we will be able to make long-lasting investments into the improvement of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_a_renewed_drive_desc:
With spare cash brought about from a myriad different cuts and abstractions, and production recovering back to pre-crisis levels thanks to more cuts and the help of our honored Chief Executive's many allies and benefactors, Hitachi is at last well-placed to begin making some money back. As such, we will now embark on a glorious sales drive and make as much as we can from as many contracts and sales as we can get hold of.

Truly, it shall be glorious! Hitachi Limited and its great leader, Chief Executive Komai Kenichirō, shall be the vanguard of this glorious State of Guangdong and her recovery and growth to a new height of efficiency and strength. The Chief Executive will be known by all and sundry as the man who brought about a new era for our state!
strings.GNG_a_renewed_drive_tt: With everything tilted in its favor, there is no stopping £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi now.
strings.GNG_the_noose_loosened_desc:
The skies over Guangdong are once again cerulean and bright, the dreary and somber clouds of the Oil Crisis have faded, disappearing and giving way to the radiant and golden rays of the Sun. Our Chief Executive, brilliant and courageous, has brought us prosperity, order, and stability once more. Our factories are filled with diligent workers and the cacophonous noises of machines in operation, the stock market is stable once again, the volatile fluctuations of the Oil Crisis no longer present.

However, as one set of troubles clear, a tempest is approaching Guangdong, one whose ferocity and intensity are unmatched. The raucous and indignant public is rumbling with discontent and discord, a deafening silence echoes across the streets of the Three Pearls. All across the nation, protesters assemble and distribute their dissenting beliefs, misconduct is rampant in workplaces and small-scale demonstrations are becoming more and more frequent.

Our Chief Executive shall guide us through this as he has done before; the ship of Guangdong is entering another storm.
strings.GNG_the_noose_loosened_tt: The plebeian masses need not understand why we do what we must - theirs is but to obey, and not to question.
strings.GNG_the_fire_rises_desc:
Our Chief Executive stands ascendant over the verdant hills and operating factories of Guangdong, gazing down upon his vast and prosperous domain. The mighty and indomitable tower which supports his position, constructed of freshly worked steel and the bodies of the workers of Guangdong, is a symbol of the magnificence of our Chief Executive's grand and illustrious design.

In the previous years, he has guided us through a period of immense economic hardship, one filled with turmoil and strife, a tempest from above that disrupted all aspects of our great society. However, as the somber clouds overhead begin to clear, the rays of sunshine are greeted by the plumes of ominous dark smoke rising from below; the foundation of our Chief Executive's tower of grandeur stirs with tremendous vigor, the cries of insurrection and dissent blend together into a cacophonous symphony, a deafening orchestra of defiance and dismay.

Our Chief Executive shall not allow his work to be undone by the vile actions of imbeciles and rascals; he shall not watch his tower be engulfed by the ravenous flames of intransigence and discord. The tremors will cease, stability will return, the opulence of his apparatus will not be dismantled by indolent fools.
strings.GNG_the_fire_rises_tt:
The Three Pearls burn by a fire of our own making.
So much the better, if we can remake Guangdong anew from the ashes.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_we_need_you_desc:
In the old tales of classical antiquity, within the great stories of might and valor, of heroes and conquerors, there appears a character of struggle and strength, a character who embodies our illustrious Chief Executive's resilience and diligence: Atlas.

Akin to the imposing titan, our Chief Executive sustains an immense burden, that of the governance of Guangdong, and yet he does not complain, he willingly accepts his duties and provides us with necessary and wise guidance. The unruly rabble currently running rampant upon the streets of Guangdong, denying the prosperous rule of our Chief Executive, will be eliminated as he has done before with dissenters and agitators. The world shall watch in awe as Guangdong once again emerges from the debris of anarchy and discord stronger and mightier, ascendant once more.

As Atlas has done with the celestial spheres, the pearl of Guangdong shall be held aloft, soaring above the others as a paragon of stability.
strings.GNG_chief_executive_we_need_you_tt:
If the rioters seek to become an unstoppable wave, then we will show them that £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi's Guangdong is an immovable object.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_no_go_zones_desc:
As our Chief Executive begins to enact severe security measures to expunge the rot of the protesters, our priorities need to be correct. Our police force and units of the IJA stationed within Guangdong will be sent to secure certain locations and sites which are considered important and essential to Guangdong's administrative and economic apparatus. These zones will be heavily reinforced with the latest equipment and riot-control measures, ensuring that unpermitted entry would simply not be possible under any circumstance. These buildings are to be government offices, corporate headquarters, and certain manufacturing plants; places which absolutely cannot be relinquished to the barbaric horde.

We will ensure that our most valuable assets are kept safe and protected, the magnificence of Guangdong is at stake.
strings.GNG_not_an_inch_desc:
It is of the utmost necessity that we make these protesting ingrates and good-for-nothings understand the reality of the situation. We - the government - are right; they are completely in the wrong. We cannot err, and we admit no faults. They alone are capable of error.
We will not acknowledge the existence of their so-called 'right' to protest what they in their benighted, subhuman ignorance think is 'wrong'.

They are beneath us; we are above them; thus shall it always remain, for the continued beauty and welfare of this State of Guangdong demands it. There will be no 'reforms', no 'opening up'; no amount of flowers shall be permitted to bloom in this country while the infallible Chief Executive Komai rules.

Let this be made clear before we send the police out into the streets. Let them be warned here and now, everywhere they can hear their rightful Chief Executive speak.
strings.GNG_not_a_mile_desc:
Among the security forces of all people we have heard degenerate rumblings of 'sympathy' for the 'legitimate concerns' of the rioting traitors in the streets of Guangdong. Self-evidently, this prospect cannot be tolerated, lest the police join hands with the protestors and rise up to topple their betters in some kind of asinine, shameless “velvet revolution.”

To counteract this horrific possibility, our esteemed Chief Executive will direct the security forces - especially the Guangdong Police - to take a hard line. Effective immediately all security forces in Guangdong will be prohibited from engaging in any form of coordination or cooperation with the protestors. By the Government's orders, they will all be treated as rioters without exception, lest they grow confident on perceiving a seemingly feeble police force.
strings.GNG_cordon_off_the_streets_desc:
The ungrateful protesting hordes of rabble-rousers, foreign agents and communists are choking the streets of Kōshū and a myriad other cities. If we let them run wild, affording them undeserved freedom of movement, countless important buildings will be overrun before we can say “Tenno-heika banzai.” Just why that would prove devastating is self-evident.

As this prospect cannot be borne, let us make our job easier as we prepare to take them down head-on. We must set up cordons in the major areas affected by these degenerate ingrates so as to make sure that we and not they determine where they do or do not go. Having contained them in this fashion, we will be well-placed to close in on them hard and fast in the future.
strings.GNG_choke_them_out_desc:
Cordoning them off, packing them in, splitting them up - we have made great progress in the fight against the communists and foreign agents in the streets of Guangdong. But more can be done. We notice that a large proportion of these traitors manage to keep themselves afloat by relying on local businesses, with or without their consent. Furthermore, in a violation of common sense, they are still able to call in emergency services when they are wounded - but then that makes sense, since the Chief Executive was hitherto too busy to tell them to focus on people that actually deserved help. No more.

Our esteemed Chief Executive now gives a new directive: let everything be shut down. Close businesses by hook or by crook. Block emergency services from working in areas where the riots are at their worst - any potential loss of life from legitimate, law-abiding citizens suddenly cut off is more than worth the benefit to the public of seeing the renegade agitators kept down and out without medical help. Finally, let anyone seen escaping the lawless crowds be arrested; this will thin their numbers and force them to give in eventually.
strings.GNG_pack_them_in_desc:
Our directive ordering the Police and other security forces to seal themselves off emotionally from the traitorous rabble in the streets has taken fruit, and they are now fully ready to do our bidding as is right and proper. In fact, the Commissioner and other prominent police officers have now approached us asking for our advice on how best to deal with the rioters.

Let us put the Police to use by coordinating with them to encircle the already cordoned-off groups of protestors. We will entrap them in the ghettos and poorer districts, and prevent them from moving back and forth between cities. Let us see just how strong their will is when they find themselves herded back and forth like so many livestock at our whim.
strings.GNG_metal_grinds_stomachs_churn_desc:
For all our attempts to make these protesting ingrates and good-for-nothings understand the reality of the situation, the riots, far from improving, have in fact worsened. Though we have had minor successes in cordoning off the streets, packing them in, and choking them out, the rabble has merely grown more intense, and public order is at an all-time low.

Needless to say, this situation could not be less desirable. Our esteemed Chief Executive must show these people their place or he will fall more dramatically than the Yasuda stocks and then their employees did last decade. Komai Kenichirō must act swiftly to prevent this. He now has two choices in front of him: using either harsh general measures or precise, calculated strikes.
strings.GNG_metal_grinds_stomachs_churn_tt:
The flames grow ever fiercer.
So do our countermeasures.
strings.GNG_do_as_i_say_desc:
Our Chief Executive, Komai Kenichirō, knows that he is the head of state of Guangdong, the sole guarantor of her beauty and prosperity. Accordingly, he has concluded that he cannot settle for half-measures or so-called 'precision strikes'. No, a headstrong approach must be the word of the day. We have no other choice in the matter.

The Chief Executive will now go out on national television and outline himself as the rightful leader of the nation. He will describe himself as the guide of the troubled Guangdong populace while urging the protestors to back down. Komai Kenichirō will not rest until all of Guangdong understands the following fact of life:

“Our Chief Executive is Guangdong's strongman. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned by anyone, let alone by commoners whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do and die rather than question why.”
strings.GNG_do_as_i_say_tt:
The threat of force is useless without a promise of reprieve - a sound strategy, even if it will anger the most bloodthirsty among us.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_leave_by_sundown_desc:
Cordoning them off, packing them in, splitting them up, choking them out by depriving them of access to businesses and healthcare - we have made great progress in the fight against the communists and foreign agents in the streets of Guangdong. But more can be done to bring an end to this nonsense.

The rioters will now be issued daily warnings: they must clear out by sundown each night in order to assure peace and good order in the city streets. Otherwise, the police will be directed to use harsh force to arrest and jail them without mercy or consideration. We have it on good authority that they will be fully ready, willing, and able to see this done.
strings.GNG_lock_down_the_streets_desc:
We have made great progress in the fight against the communists and foreign agents in the streets of Guangdong, most recently by ordering rioters to leave by sundown. But we can do yet more to make sure that the renegades that dare question our great Chief Executive Komai's authority learn their place as quickly as possible.

We have ordered them to leave the streets every sundown, and encircled them in ghettos and poorer areas. Now we are at last poised to strike; let us take this opportunity before the situation changes. Let the groups of rioters we have encircled be stricken down and dealt with as soon as is humanly possible.
strings.GNG_pump_up_the_budget_desc:
During the Oil Crisis, with spare cash brought about from a myriad different cuts and abstractions, and production recovering back to pre-crisis levels thanks to more cuts and the help of our honored Chief Executive's many allies and benefactors, we were able to create a significant increase in funds. Now, with the economy more or less stabilized despite the disorder of our great state, we can put these funds to use.

Put more money into policing and security and let its budget climb. That will allow us to put these renegade bastards down and ensure the continued promotion of law and order in our glorious state of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_no_need_to_panic_desc:
Any state that wishes to survive for more than two or three hours must prioritize the welfare of those who contribute the most to it, rewarding only the good and loyal servants. And in these latter days, since the fall of Yasuda and Suzuki, who have been more loyal to the glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her prosperity than the corporations - with Mangyō and Hitachi at their head? Who has contributed more to this great nation than them?

The rioting ingrates outside do not understand that the corporations of Guangdong are above them for their benefit as well as ours; out of a foolish desire for 'equality' they are now beginning to threaten the companies' assets. This cannot be tolerated; accordingly, we will solemnly promise to assure the safety of private corporate holdings in Guangdong, with Hitachi, and Mangyō prioritized.
strings.GNG_guangdong_or_anarchy_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is the sole guarantor of prosperity in this nation; he is its strongman, the protector of her beauty. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned. Nor should his ability to protect this glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her welfare and prosperity be held in any doubt.”

“The general public is, no doubt, deeply concerned about the state of the nation, as well they should be given our current struggles against traitors and renegades in our streets. But they need not worry. The honorable Chief Executive, Komai Kenichirō, is father of the nation and promoter of her beauty; he will ensure that everything turns out well. All that the good people of Guangdong need to is to conform to the orders issued by this government; if they do this, they will have exactly nothing to fear.”
strings.GNG_guangdong_or_anarchy_tt:
If £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi falls - everyone loses.
We will make the masses understand that.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_we_know_what_you_know_desc:
Steam presses to reseal envelopes, surreptitious wiretaps, and the ever-present eye of the street informer. These are the tools by which the Chief Executive keeps tabs on the pulse of the people - their fears, their doubts, and their half-baked plans.

They forget, at their own peril, that Hitachi hears all. Hitachi sees all. Hitachi knows all.
strings.GNG_words_from_within_desc:
It is written that spy operations and their targets should be pursued with respect to two kinds of people: the traitors and the unrighteous. The rioting ingrates outside who, despite our best efforts, still do not understand that the corporations of Guangdong are above them for their benefit as well as ours are a quintessential example of the kind of person that falls in both of the above categories.

Accordingly, as we send in the police and security troops to do away with the rioters from without, we will send informants, spies, and agitators to infiltrate their ranks, damaging them from within. Their duty will be twofold: first, they will leak any and all useful information they find to the government, and second, they will undermine any plans the protestors may come up with.
strings.GNG_words_from_within_tt:
The £GNG_rioters_texticon rioters believe they can trust their own.
How foolish they are.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_names_names_names_desc:
As we sent in the police and security troops to do away with the rioters from without, we also deployed an assortment of informants, spies, and agitators to infiltrate their ranks, eating away at them from within. Their duty has been twofold: first, they have leaked any and all useful information they find to the government; second, they have successfully undermined any plans the protestors came up with.

As the protestors, assaulted from both inside and outside, at last thankfully begin to collapse, it is time for us to begin the work of mopping up. But we cannot do that if we do not know the names of the renegades and subversives that sent Guangdong into this hellish downward spiral. Accordingly, our agents and police officers will be directed to find the names of any and all ringleaders and people of interest who the government can arrest, charge, and bring to justice.
strings.GNG_the_house_always_wins_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is the father and protector of the nation. His ability to protect this glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her welfare and prosperity cannot be held in doubt. Nor indeed should his authority over this delta be questioned by anyone, let alone by traitors whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do what they are told, not bothering to question why or how.”

And it is no longer held in doubt. The protestors have diminished from their once genuinely concerning peak. What could have genuinely effected a regime change is now pathetic, radical, and rapidly dwindling in numbers. Moreover, the general population holds their honorable Chief Executive in a fearful reverence, respecting his successful handling of both crises.

Komai Kenichirō now holds both the loyalty and the fear of the people. He might have been happier if he had their adoration too, but what he has is more than sufficient to hold on to his rightful position as Chief Executive. So he will make do and move forward.
strings.GNG_the_house_always_wins_tt:
The game was rigged from the start.
The criminals didn't figure it out until it was too late.
strings.GNG_not_as_i_do_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is Guangdong's strongman. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned by anyone, let alone by commoners whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do and die rather than question why.”

While the Chief Executive emphasizes this fact by taking a present, strongman approach, a different reality will play out on the streets of Guangdong. State repression will be the primary method of dealing with this rabble. Komai Kenichirō's plan is to silence them as much as possible as soon as possible, using brutal methods to put down the protestors once and for all.
strings.GNG_not_as_i_do_tt:
It's well past time we taught the rioters the meaning of unrestricted violence - even if it risks alarming £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Tokyo.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_old_friends_new_business_desc:
In these latter days, since the fall of Yasuda and Suzuki, who have been more loyal to the glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her prosperity than the corporations - with Mangyō, and Hitachi at their head? Who has contributed more to this great nation than them? Who else is better placed to come to our aid than Mangyō, in particular?

Chief Executive Komai, relying on his various contacts and connections at Mangyō Corporation, has issued a directive calling in Mangyō security forces to back up the police and security troops as well as manage the rioters. They will be kept as mere footsoldiers in the organizational hierarchies, yes, but their muscle will be what we need to pull through.
strings.GNG_bones_on_concrete_desc:
Any state that wishes to survive for more than two or three hours must prioritize the welfare of those who contribute the most to it, rewarding only the good and loyal servants. Such a state must, moreover, feel no qualms about relying on brutal methodologies to punish the traitorous and overambitious parasites that, forgetting their oaths and duties, choose to betray the state's ruler and his government. Our Chief Executive understands this wisdom and will put it to use.

By a directive of our magnanimous Chief Executive, backed by the Commissioner of Police, the security forces of this State of Guangdong will now be permitted to use brutal force in non-lethal dealings with the rioting traitors. Police brutality will now be considered elevated and correct in police strategy; after all, what better method is there to intimidate and subdue the rabble in the streets than breaking a few legs and arms at will?
strings.GNG_wipe_the_streets_desc:
Now is an opportune time to show these subversive traitors, these agents of the OFN and Einheitspakt, their rightful place - beneath us, in submission to us alone and not to any foreign interest, religion, or ideology. Few methods are better in obtaining this goal than liberally applying force; few mechanisms of doing so are more effective than a cavalry charge. So let us put the horses available to our great police officers to effective use.

On orders of our great Chief Executive and the Commissioner of Police, officers will now charge clumps of protestors with batons at the ready. This will enable them to make as many arrests as are necessary in order to break these upstarts' wills and put an end to their inane movements.
strings.GNG_safety_off_desc:
The rioting ingrates outside do not understand that the corporations of Guangdong are above them for their benefit as well as ours. At this rate, it is doubtful that they will ever come to understand; perhaps we have no choice but to kill a few of them outright to frighten them into submission.

On orders of our most wise and merciful Chief Executive and the Commissioner of Police, officers will now be authorized to use lethal force to the extent they deem necessary when they are forced to deal with the traitors in the streets. No cost of protestor lives is too high if it helps restore the established order and the beauty of this state of Guangdong.
strings.GNG_no_negotiations_desc:
If a state wishes to survive for more than two or three hours it must prioritize the welfare of those who contribute the most to it, rewarding only the good and loyal servants. Furthermore, it must at all costs avoid negotiating or capitulating to the will of hostile actors who, rather than holding the interests of the state and its ruler to heart, instead concern themselves with their own parochial follies. In our case, these hostile actors include the unions and protestors, who have troubled us since the fall of Yasuda and our rise to power, but especially now.

Even after all this, these rabble-rousers still have the gall to make demands. Let us be clear: there will be no negotiations whatsoever. The unions and dissidents do not deserve to be heard out, not at the best of times, and certainly not now. They have two choices, no more, no less: toe the line or be destroyed under the full force of the law.
strings.GNG_no_negotiations_tt:
If the criminals don't want to live in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong - we are happy to oblige.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_pack_the_courts_desc:
When people in other countries - America, Germany, India, you name it - speak of 'court packing' they usually mean something in the vein of adding judges to high or low courts with a view on shifting the balance in a given direction. In Guangdong, on the other hand, we do things in a distinctly different manner. We pack our courts with defendants.

Luckily for the poor judges, the system is a conveyor belt. The verdicts are already decided and the stamp of 'guilty' is marked on each casefile, for that is what these traitors all are. But the Government and our honoured Chief Executive both want to see these good-for-nothing ingrates tried and jailed, and right quick. So the Guangdong-style court-packing will continue apace.
strings.GNG_make_an_example_desc:
The rioting ingrates outside did not understand that the powers-that-be of Guangdong are above them for their benefit as well as ours; until it was too late they continued to fight against their rightful overlords and brought chaos and near-ruin to this beautiful country and her people. But now it is time to make an object lesson of these good-for-nothing, useless traitors, so as to ensure that no more such incidents will take place in our lifetimes.

Show-trials will be televised all across the State of Guangdong and evidence shall be presented against the people whose trials are to be broadcast. Trial and evidence will be shown in such a way as is most effective in depicting the radical violence of these renegades. They will kick and scream after the courts provoke them, but only the kicking and screaming will be shown. And when the guilty verdict is given, it will be only a matter of time before our great Chief Executive or his agents send the guillotine blade down on the upstarts' traitorous necks.
strings.GNG_make_an_example_tt:
The criminals' life and liberty are forfeit.
The sooner they understand this, the better.
New £decision_icon_small decisions to reduce £GNG_riot_strength_texticon riot strength and increase £GNG_government_riots_texticon government control are unlocked.
strings.GNG_complimentary_fabrication_desc:
Our agents and police officers were directed to find the names of any and all ringleaders and people of interest who the government could arrest, charge, and bring to justice. They performed this task with aplomb, and now countless assorted rabble-rousers, agitators, and subversive agents are held in our prisons. But there is the matter of putting them through the judiciary to deal with.

Fortunately for us, the judiciary and security services both take great pleasure in taking our orders. Accordingly, in addition to the evidence of participation and organization of protests - which in and of itself suffices to prove treason - the ringleaders will also be confronted with reams of evidence fabricated against them by the security forces, just to make extra sure that they are kept where we want them and stand no chance of escaping our justice.
strings.GNG_i_play_this_game_best_desc:
No-one but no-one is capable of outsmarting our esteemed Chief Executive, Komai Kenichirō, chairman of Hitachi Limited, promoter of the glorious Manchurian Plan, chief defender and preserver of the great beauty and strength of the State of Guangdong.

The riots have been crushed under his iron boot; the treasonous revolutionaries are either imprisoned or have dissipated back into the unknown lower masses. The population looks upon Komai with fear and reverence, as is their right and duty. As the nation heals and falls into a dull, awkward sense of calm, the Government and its esteemed leader drink to the health and beauty of the nation. It is right and proper; after all, the crises have ended, and order has been restored.
strings.GNG_i_play_this_game_best_tt:
Justice is not a function of morality, but of strength.
The criminals never had a chance.
strings.GNG_this_beautiful_nation_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is Guangdong's strongman. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned by anyone, let alone by traitors whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do what they are told, not bothering to question why or how. Nor should his ability to protect this glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her welfare and prosperity be held in any doubt.”

“The esteemed gentlemen officers of the Imperial Japanese Army, close and esteemed allies of Chief Executive Komai Kenichirō, have at times expressed concern about the situation in the streets of Guangdong. By this message, the Government of Guangdong shall make clear that they have no need to worry. By hook or by crook, no matter the cost of lives or money, Chief Executive Komai will do his duty by Guangdong and the Emperor and ensure that everything goes to plan.”
strings.GNG_this_beautiful_nation_tt: Though our methods seem extreme, our intent will be understood by those who matter.
strings.GNG_despite_all_its_toils_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is Guangdong's strongman. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned by anyone, let alone by traitors whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do what they are told, not bothering to question why or how. Nor should his ability to protect this glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her welfare and prosperity be held in any doubt.”

“The most honorable Japanese expatriate community have approached the Government and the Legislative Council of the State of Guangdong to express their worry and fear about the state of affairs in the country. Their concerns are legitimate, but this message shall make clear that despite everything, the matter remains fully under control. One way or the other, Chief Executive Komai will make sure that none of the toil and money they have invested in this country is brought to nothing.”
strings.GNG_despite_all_its_toils_tt:
Our troubles our temporary. Our potential is infinite.
That is our message to £GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Tokyo.
strings.GNG_will_survive_desc:
“Our Chief Executive is Guangdong's strongman. His authority over this delta is not to be questioned by anyone, let alone by traitors whose rightfully ordained place in life is to do what they are told, not bothering to question why or how. Nor should his ability to protect this glorious, beautiful State of Guangdong and her welfare and prosperity be held in any doubt.”

“The honorable, enlightened Zhujin-Japanese community, who forsook the backwards culture of their traitorous former relatives now rioting in the streets to embrace a superior, more advanced way of life, now live in fear that the madmen and renegades besieging the cities of this beautiful land will bring their efforts to naught. Let us be clear: everything is under control. The honorable Chief Executive, Komai Kenichirō, will make sure that the sacrifices of the Zhujin community remain worth their while.”
strings.GNG_will_survive_tt: And most importantly: the criminals will not.
strings.GNG_a_reluctant_dawn_desc:
The air is cool, the sky is bright, the Sun rises over the horizon, shining its brilliant golden rays of warm sunlight over the inhabitants of Guangdong and the Three Pearls. The gunfire and cries of the weeks prior have dissipated, being carried away by the quiet breeze; the streets are silent, devoid of rioting workers in tattered clothing or police officers dressed in blue. Our Chief Executive emerges from his rightful seat, triumphant and victorious, golden laurels resting upon his head.

Order and stability has returned to the delightful territories of Guangdong once more, the plumes of opaque smoke have cleared, the orchestra of discord has been silenced. To Chief Executive Komai, the future holds infinite possibilities and grander designs; a great, magnificent future where the populace and assets of Guangdong are to be shaped according to his will, one where the people remain loyal and obedient, their frustrations no longer hampering the progress which they could never see or comprehend. The Sun towers above the Three Pearls as with any other day, but this time, Helios heralds a new era of prosperity and success, one with no obstructions or obstacles.
strings.GNG_a_reluctant_dawn_tt: £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai stands triumphant, with £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong prostrate at his feet.
strings.GNG_the_institutional_chokehold_desc:
As our Chief Executive celebrates his triumph against the forces of dissent and indolence, Guangdong returns to its old order once more; designed to maximize efficiency, by any means necessary. The factories and manufacturing plants spring back into operation, the monotonous humming of machines heralding the return of the status quo. Workers, whether they were in custody or languishing in their residences, are returned to their original places of employment, engaging once more in the daily tradition of the commute, surveillance at every corner. The tight policies of police crackdowns and forced inspection are enforced once more, nobody in the state dares to step out of line.

Our Chief Executive's vision for the potential of Guangdong continues on its way to being realized, a society of streamlined production and efficiency, a center of industry, and a titan of the economy.
strings.GNG_the_institutional_chokehold_tt: Now everything in £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong is dyed in £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi's's colors.
strings.GNG_taste_the_cutting_air_desc:
While the fittest survive and thrive as is their right and duty, those that are less than them are by necessity given a choice between dying and spending their lives in eternal subservience to their betters. This is how it is in the State of Guangdong that was built by Komai Kenichirō.

Those that have the appropriate merit—demonstrated by their ethnic origin, or their monetary abilities, or simply in some cases by choosing the right place to be in the right time—are given direction over workers, and the freedom to do what must be done to increase the profitability of their enterprises. Limp-wristed, liberal concepts such as workers' rights or the sentiments of the populace have no needs; and if the workers groan in pain or suffer injuries, that is good for them, since pain builds character.
