This is how it shall remain so long as our Chief Executive remains in power; he has made sure that no subversive or group of subversives will try to destroy the beautiful paradigm that has been established in Guangdong.
strings.GNG_taste_the_cutting_air_tt: The people are entitled only to the air they breathe.
strings.GNG_the_fittest_have_survived_desc:
One of the few things on which Chief Executive Komai Kenichirō completely agrees with the German “imperialists” is something that their Deputy Fyurer or whatever it is they call him once said. He said that this earth, far from being some kind of fairy-land, was a struggle for life; a perfectly natural, extremely harsh state of battle in which the fittest could survive. His argument has been proven true here in Guangdong - the fittest of this “great, beautiful nation”, that is, the rich, have survived, indeed thrived.

The upper crust has been swamped in wealth, benefitting from the economic reforms of our esteemed Chief Executive before the Oil Crisis. They have also benefited from the consolidations during and after the Crisis. Amidst all this, Hitachi-affiliated businesses have turned Guangdong and the Three Pearls into a hub of trade and commerce at the mouth of the Pearl River Delta.
strings.GNG_the_fittest_have_survived_tt:
£GNG_Sony_texticon Sony, £GNG_Matsushita_texticon Matsushita, £GNG_Fujitsu_texticon Fujitsu - they were all complacent.
Only £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi had the will to rule.
strings.GNG_the_world_shall_know_guangdong_desc:
As the bright lights of the cities glisten over the shores of the Pearl River Delta, the State of Guangdong turns its attention to the future. Chief Executive Komai Kenichirō has forged a seat for himself from the blood, sweat, flesh, and bones of those beneath him, carving out an iron throne for himself. But what was the worth of it all?

The Japanese government is distracted with a myriad different 'issues'; the Chinese to the north grow bolder and more powerful as their nationalism reasserts itself. Komai Kenichirō knows that thanks to his work the world knows Guangdong. But he knows just as well that a good name is of no use in defending the republic against the swallowing darkness of future uncertainty.

Though Komai, like the ancient Greco-Roman monarchs or the myriad pre-Meiji shogunates, is possessed of all the power in Guangdong, his little despotate is only one cog in the machine that is humanity. Despite everything that has happened, Komai remains a small fish in a big, big pond.
strings.GNG_the_world_shall_know_guangdong_tt: £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Komai Kenichirō is the master of his house - will he become master of the world?
strings.GNG_i_dedicate_this_year_desc:
As the New Year begins, fireworks and other assorted lights crackle across the night skies of a myriad cities of the Delta. Celebratory messages blare from every television and radio set for miles around. The streets are calm and restrained, and the moods of the few people on the streets are solemn—the better for them to continue their work advantageously later, unaffected by excesses of emotion or sentimentality. This is the Guangdong built by Komai Kenichirō, and the fulfillment of everything for which he stands.

The businessmen in Komai's court point at red, upward-sloped lines with their fingers while green banknotes stuff their pockets. Mangyō - this mighty, terrible bulwarks of the Manchurian way - is an honored guest in the republic. So it is, so it should be—for all the beauty that Guangdong needs is found in the fulfillment of the Manchurian Plan, not in unnecessary beautification measures that cannot but distract workers and officials.
strings.GNG_i_dedicate_this_year_tt: The elite of £GFX_GNG_Guangdong_texticon Guangdong dance, bedecked in Manchurian livery - and in a world apart from the masses below.
strings.GNG_to_our_industrious_desc:
To people whose sole concerns are aesthetics and pleasant smells, and who expect to wake up to the scent of fresh flowers every morning, Guangdong is an unpleasant hellhole. But to the discerning eye of the Chief Executive, beauty is far deeper than such superficialities: it is seen in productivity, successful quotas, products sold and exported. By this metric, Guangdong is one of the fairest—and most profitable—lands of all.

The profits are sweet for as long as they stack tall. But there is something quite terrifyingly mortal and ephemeral about it all. For all his successes, Komai worries that although Guangdong is now richer and more beautiful than ever thanks to the Manchurian Plan, his little fiefdom is vulnerable in the face of the upcoming war.
strings.GNG_to_our_industrious_tt: The fruits of our labor are as limitless as the hunger of our factories...
strings.GNG_to_our_cooperative_desc:
Patriotism! Patriotism! Patriotism! Glory to cooperation! Bold, defiant billboards advertising Hitachi and Mangyō products are matched only by those that depict and promote loyalty to the government and love for the nation in their omnipresence.

Whether it is children holding hands and waving flags of Guangdong and the Empire of Japan, or grinning Chinese, Japanese, and Zhujin workers together at work, there are those that will claim that it looks forced, or ripped out of an older playbook. But they are wrong—if Guangdong relies on that old playbook, it is because it has worked once before and will do so yet again.

Productivity and cooperation has remained at an all-time high, no matter what some may claim about a demoralized populace. The only reasonable conclusion is that Hitachi's method has worked.
strings.GNG_to_our_cooperative_tt: The energy of our people is as boundless as our propagandists' imaginations...
strings.GNG_to_our_innovative_desc:
The stock exchange numbers swell to unheard-of levels, and a myriad neon lights blaze forth from the tall buildings of Guangdong's cities - as evident to outside observers as to the average citizen. In the awesome reflections of Komai's neon fiefdom, the faces of the average man on the street show only the reflected glory of Komai's vision for Guangdong - the results of their tireless labor and unquestioned obedience. To say otherwise is unthinkable, an attempt to deny the reality presented for tales of subjective misery.

The industries of Guangdong throw together the newest of products, circuitry, and machinery. To a conscious mind these are mere petty, useless trinkets; but the population keeps on spending. This is all Komai Kenichirō requires to be satisfied with the state of affairs.
strings.GNG_to_our_innovative_tt: The future of our state is as bright as the smiles of our people...
strings.GNG_civilisation_on_the_river_desc:
Chief Executive Komai Kenichirō - in his own words, “the strongman of the State of Guangdong, the sole guarantor of her beauty and prosperity” - gazes out of the great glass windows of his office over the twinkling city on the Delta. He is a proud, ruthless man at the height of his accomplishment.

But Komai's prosperity and happiness are threatened by recent events in China. Though it galls him to even think about it, he is forced to admit that the recent occurrences in China - irredentism, nationalism, anti-Japanese sentiment - could change Guangdong's future far more quickly or thoroughly than Komai ever could. Worse yet, contact with Japan has slowed, and things are slowly falling from the height reached after the recovery from the Oil Crisis.

As this thought makes its rounds through the minds of Komai and his advisers and sycophants, there is an odd air of pride and grim acceptance. There is also a frightening fact that quickly becomes self-evident to any dispassionate observer: any action these men take on a whim can result in immediate, disastrous effects on the lives of the average Guangdong citizen.
strings.GNG_civilisation_on_the_river_tt: ...all in service to our brave vanguard of Pan-Asian industry, and the voracious ambition of £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi and Komai Kenichirō!
strings.GNG_IJA_gui_flavour_text:
• PACIFICATION INCOMPLETE •
• CALAMITY AWAITS •
• LONG LIVE HIS MAJESTY THE EMPEROR •
strings.GNG_the_wheel_turns_desc:
Martial law is in effect.
Remain in your homes.
Compliance is mandatory.
Offenders will be shot.
strings.GNG_wake_up_from_the_silicon_dream: Wake Up From the Silicon Dream
strings.GNG_a_failed_experiment_desc:
What was the State of Guangdong? A political entity? An economic powerhouse? No. The State of Guangdong was an experiment, a fruitless venture, a trial which yielded worthless and unproductive results, a withered, perished specimen which now serves no purpose. Experiments that do not bring forth beneficial and worthy results are disposable, they are merely expendable items of zero value.

Guangdong did not fail due to the temporary issues which plagued its existence, Guangdong succumbed to the corruption and filth present within the very nature of its design, a deplorable state apparatus constructed with the sole intent of contributing to gluttony and avarice. We are the ones returning the territories of the Pearl River Delta to their rightful place, we are the ones shattering every contraption in this apparatus of greed, we are the ones reestablishing the righteous and glorious tenets of Pan-Asianism to this shameful land. What the weak and incompetent men of the inept and disgraceful corporations could not do, we are executing with the intensity of a thousand suns.
strings.GNG_a_failed_experiment_tt:
Look upon the mess £GNG_Guangdong_texticon you have made.

Look what you made £GNG_IJA_riots_texticon us do.
strings.GNG_close_up_shop_desc:
To truly cleanse this spoiled land and reintroduce righteous and just rule, we are expunging any trace of the former corrupt system of governance, the depraved and gluttonous tyranny of the corporations that have tainted every corner of the state, the supreme symbols of the era of duplicity and subversion of the virtuous maxims of pan-asianism. They are being utterly and mercilessly demolished, our fists are pulverizing the remnants of the regime of unbridled corruption, the indecent and vile dregs who participated in the operation of these organizations of vanity are being eliminated, the memories of them and their reprehensible deeds perishing in the ravenous fires of expurgation.

The contemptible vices that have kept Guangdong in fetters are being destroyed one by one, and the corporations shall follow.
strings.GNG_end_corruption_desc:
Inefficient, ineffective, and inept, a wretched den of scum and villainy. The Legislative Council that has overseen Guangdong is nothing more than a thin veneer of accountability, a haven for the corrupt, fraudulent scum that passes for leadership in this farce of a so-called nation, ruling over a rotten edifice of vice, disorder, and incompetence. It must be destroyed.

The Legislative Council will hereby, effectively immediately, be dissolved, its cohorts to be tried as the traitors they are, its buildings and offices repurposed for something useful.
strings.GNG_end_corruption_tt: Military justice is swift - and without mercy.
strings.GNG_a_blank_cheque_desc:
Our mission is simple, our mandate is clear. Pacify Guangdong and its environs, end the violence in three pearls, and suppress any hint of resistance that is foolish enough to challenge the servants of the Emperor. We are not beholden to the incompetents and traitors who once ruled Guangdong, we are not beholden to the fraudulent and corrupt corporations who once dominated this nation, and we are certainly not beholden to the spies, traitors, and rats who dare stand against the Pan-Asian Dream.

We are only beholden to His Majesty and the Empire to which we serve. We have a blank cheque on hand and no trial to trial us. Guangdong is being cleansed of any who dare oppose the march of progress.
strings.GNG_a_blank_cheque_tt:
There are no more questions to be asked.

It is time for action.
strings.GNG_reappropriate_research_desc:
We cannot deny that the corporations of Guangdong, the failures that they are, corrupt and fraudulent they may be, have managed remarkable technological advancement. Bleeding edge research years ahead of similar efforts in the Home Islands, producing electronics and prototypes that might still be of use when placed in the right hands.

Shipments of these prototypes and research notes back to Japan are well underway, where the Army can turn these sparse gems of success into tools that can be of service the world over.
strings.GNG_reappropriate_research_tt: Even if £GNG_Guangdong_texticon you are useless, your £GNG_research_texticon research may be of some value for us.
strings.GNG_secure_the_hinterlands_desc:
As we annihilate the forces of corruption and excess upon the banks of the Pearl River Delta, cleansing each sprawling city of degeneracy and debasement, open defiance against our honorable cause now originates from another source: the rural hinterlands. We have already dispatched convoys of soldiers to seize and occupy all insubordinate regions outside of the Three Pearls, the insignificant pockets of futile resistance are being vanquished, the cities brimming with Chinese dissenting inhabitants are being captured and subdued.

The subversive scum still defying our authority, clinging onto deluded visions of hope that have long departed, are being eradicated; we have drafted extensive lists of names to keep the barrels of our guns forever warm.

We are bringing forth the benefits of order and stability back to the territories, accompanied by the melody of deafening gunfire and the harmony of heavy footsteps.
strings.GNG_secure_the_hinterlands_tt:
There is value in the £GNG_Guangdong_texticon Three Pearls; there is even some value in the land outside of it.

There is no value in the people who live there.
strings.GNG_the_koshu_tribunal_desc:
Traitors, that's what they are. Morita, Ibuka, Matsushita, Sony, Fujitsu, Hitachi, the executives, the Legislative Council, government ministers, the rioters, the Guangdong Police Force, the Kenpeitai, the Yakuza and Triads, Chinese, Zhujin, Japanese - no one, absolutely no one, is innocent from playing their part in this colossal, absolute disintegration of order and this miscarriage of the Pan-Asian dream. All of them are traitors, without one single exception - and the State of Guangdong itself, for all its disorder, all its incompetence, all its degeneracy, and all its failures to deliver its own fabricated fantasies, is treason incarnate.

All are traitors, and all will be brought to justice as such. And sacred justice is what the Kōshū Tribunal shall deliver unto the flaming wreckages of the Three Pearls, until no traitor, conspirer, dissenter can befoul the Co-Prosperity Sphere's unity and the stability of Southern China with their wretched existence any longer.

So shall the curtains fall, and this unprecedented farce draw to its final act.
strings.GNG_the_koshu_tribunal_tt: Stand, and face judgment for your crimes.
strings.GNG_wake_up_from_the_silicon_dream_desc:
Thus ends the woeful tale of this so-called Silicon Delta, this self-proclaimed Jewel of the South, this affront to the sanctity of Dai Tōa Kyōeiken that had held onto its pathetic existence for two decades too long.

This “Silicon Dream” upon the Pearl River died just as it had lived - a delusion, a product of artifice concocted by incompetents in suits who, in their inexpiable ignorance, tore down the pillars of order and decency only to replace them with their heaps of fleeting gold. The dream died, consigned to the deepest corners of the dustbin of history, remembered for nothing but the humiliation it wrought upon the rest of the Sphere for eons to come. The dream died - and in its wake the Pan-Asian cause has been tainted, defiled, and entire decades of fruitless endeavors lost to the void.

Yet it benefits us not to linger on the past. The dream may have died, but the Rising Sun reigns upon its smouldering corpse still. The dream may have died, but the cruel, harsh reality lives on. As stormclouds gather and the Republic of China renegades further and further against everything we stand for, this insignificant sliver of soil by the South China Sea will serve us well in its next life - as a bastion of Pan-Asian solidarity, the grandest and most enduring of His Majesty the Emperor's citadels, a phoenix baptized by fire and righteous fury.

So that no one will take our ideals, our light, and our future away from us, ever again.

strings.GNG_Aggressively_Solicit_Investment_desc: We're struggling to meet growth goals set by the mainland, but we know of some unsavory figures who are interested in investing in Guangdong. We need that cash injection right now.

strings.GNG_Dump_Products_in_China_desc: Some companies have been having trouble selling out their stock. Thankfully, we border a massive market in the ROC, and a 40% loss still sounds a hell of a lot better than a 100% loss.

strings.GNG_Econ.2.desc:
“As you can see, gentlemen, with productivity increasing and wages being kept static, Guangdong's Gross Domestic Product has increased two-fold since fiscal year 1962. We expect to see profits rising into the next fiscal year, alongside new investments and greater productive efficiency from better R&D.”

Suzuki looked out onto the room of idle men in business suits listening in on his presentation. The fluorescent bulbs above them gave their nods of approval a gaseous quality. He could feel the projection seep into his eyes, as it drew graphs of various lines and arrows on the wall behind him. The shareholders did not quite care for Suzuki, and Suzuki did not quite care for them, but he knew that they were the real commanders of the Pearl River Delta. The fact that what he had to say and show was making them happy would mean that Guangdong could go forward.

“And with 1963 dawning upon us, I expect Guangdong to remain a shining example of economic success in the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.”

The suits took in the information for a moment, before giving Suzuki a standing ovation.
strings.GNG_Econ.2.a: A miracle on the Pearl River!
strings.GNG_Econ.3.t: A Day Late, A Dollar Short
strings.GNG_Econ.3.desc:
“Unfortunately, overall economic productivity has not increased greatly since the previous fiscal year, imposing a chilling effect on profits and investments. With some financial and economic reforms, however, we should be able to make some of these losses up before the first quarter of 1964.”

Suzuki felt a dozen pairs of daggers dig into his soul as he explained the economic shortings of the region he governed. They knew his proposals of contingency and recovery were nothing but walls of paper, meant to give the impression of foresight. He knew that the goals for 1963 put forward by Tokyo were preposterous, but he did not have much room for maneuver to begin with. The business of governing is a fickle one, and at times you have to keep your head down and take a beating.

With the shareholders in strong disapproval, Tokyo will not be far behind, and the Pearl River Delta will become a more marginal piece of the puzzle that is the Sphere.
strings.GNG_Econ.4.desc:
Chief Executive {leader_name} and Consul-General Takashima Masuo sat silently in their seats, eyes shifting from each other, to the floor, to anywhere else. Neither was particularly keen to open today's meeting, a formality observed for the sake of formality, even as Yasuda's collapse had robbed both men of their time and sanity in equal abundance.

“Even though Guangdong's performance this year has fallen short of what we discussed last year,” Takashima finally ventured, removing his glasses with a weary hand, “I think we would both claim extenuating circumstances are to blame.”

Chief Executive {leader_name} nodded silently, stifling a bitter chuckle at Takashima's assessment. Even if Tokyo proper had been supremely unhelpful, having Takashima acknowledge the utter bedlam that had followed Yasuda's collapse was more than he'd hoped for.

“Be that as it may,” Takashima continued, replacing his glasses with a sigh, “Tokyo has communicated that they will expect Guangdong to do its part in the Sphere's economic recovery.”

Takashima looked exhausted - having spent most of the past year fighting for resources from Tokyo, even as Japan itself plunged into economic and political meltdown. Chief Executive {leader_name} hoped the coming year would be slightly easier for them both, now that the Yasuda collapse was behind them and the Companies started looking back to the future.

The air in the room remained heavy and still, even as the clock ticked relentlessly onwards.
strings.GNG_Econ.4.a: We should both get back to work.
strings.GNG_Econ.5.desc:
Chief Executive {leader_name} leaned back in his chair, smiling faintly as Consul-General Takashima Masuo took a seat opposite him, holding the {year} copy of Guangdong's economic data. They both knew the thick tome's contents in advance, and Takashima only made a cursory show of idly turning its pages before setting it aside.

“Guangdong has met all its economic targets for last year,” Takashima said, a wry smile tugging on his lips. “Industrial output, factory investment, export revenues: all indicators show an economy performing at its best. Tokyo is very pleased.”

Chief Executive {leader_name} nodded, letting the Consul-General's praise settle comfortably within him. Of course Guangdong had met the expectations set out for it by its stakeholders. Between his policies and the efforts of the Companies, Guangdong had proven it could perform economic alchemy - and it would do so for however long was required.

The two men talked for another fifteen minutes, the two largely exchanging compliments and conversing in generalities about the coming year's economic initiatives. The meeting was on course to end early, as the conversation petered out, with Takashima fiddling with his glasses, waiting to be excused.
strings.GNG_Econ.6.desc:
Chief Executive {leader_name} folded his hands on his desk, suppressing a frown as Consul-General Takashima Masuo took a seat opposite him, holding the {year} copy of Guangdong's economic data. Not that there was a great need for it; both men had followed Guangdong's performance anxiously as their fears became a foregone conclusion.

“Output, investment, exports. All performing well under expectations.” Takashima said curtly, a hard edge to his voice. “This is hardly what you promised us a year ago, Chief Executive. Tokyo is deeply disappointed.”

Chief Executive {leader_name} nodded slowly, the Consul-General's words sinking in. There was no denying it; Guangdong had promised much, and delivered little. Despite his policies and the efforts of the Companies, Guangdong had let its stakeholders down, inviting whispers about its - his - credibility.

The two men conversed for another thirty minutes, examining in detail the plans to make up the difference in the coming year. Takashima's expression hardly changed throughout the conversation, entirely focused on the task at hand - completely engrossed by work, even as the end of the allotted time approached.
strings.GNG_Econ.7.desc:
Chief Executive {leader_name} suspected Japanese Consul-General Takashima Masuo hadn't slept well for several months. The prominent bags under his eyes and disheveled combover clearly indicating there was no real time for personal care in the Japanese government in the midst of the Oil Crisis.

Then again, he suspected Takashima would say much the same about himself.

“Chief Executive,” Takashima said, his voice subdued from exhaustion. “You might be aware that Tokyo has been dealing with... other issues, as of late.”

{leader_name} nodded. “If Japan has its hands full with the Oil Crisis, I hope they have some sympathy for our predicament. Factors outside of our control.”

“Indeed.” Takashima sighed, sinking into his seat. “There's no insistence for Guangdong to meet the pre-crisis economic targets now.”
strings.GNG_Econ.8.desc:
Chief Executive {leader_name} scarcely noticed the passage of the original, scheduled date for the annual economic catch-up with the Japanese Consulate-General, its original embellished entry on his desk calendar completely obscured behind the scribbled chaos of resolving the ongoing Riots.

The Japanese Consulate-General hadn't called to ask about the meeting or to schedule an alternate date, either. They - just like {leader_name} - had more urgent, dangerous matters to attend to.

The earnings reports, fiscal projections, or growth forecasts that had been prepared for the meeting sat unused in a corner of the Chief Executive's office, gathering dust. If the Riots ever reached the Government Complex -
strings.GNG_Econ.8.a: - then they would all burn together.

strings.GNG_legco_sony_desc:
Initially incorporated as the Sonus-Li Electronics Company in 1954, Sony is Morita Akio's second commercial venture following the acquisition of Tokyo Telecommunications in 1952. Sony's ability to drive audio-visual innovation at affordable prices, with a mixed Zhujin-Japanese workforce, has made it the unofficial representative of Guangdong's Zhujin population.

Having rebuilt his business in the shadow of the Japanese, Morita consciously advocates for Zhujin interests in Guangdong, culminating in the creation of his own faction in the Legislative Council in 1960. Sony is now too influential to be ignored - a reputation that Morita bears proudly against his Japanese rivals, with no rivalry as bitter as his vendetta against his former partner, Ibuka Masaru of Fujitsu.
strings.GNG_legco_fujitsu_desc:
Established in 1935 as a joint venture between Siemens and the second-tier Furukawa Zaibatsu, Fujitsu has since established itself as a pioneer in the field of telecommunications and computing. After Ibuka Masaru joined Fujitsu in 1952, the firm has aggressively expanded its operations in Guangdong, dedicated to commercializing bleeding-edge computing technology with its Japanese-led core engineering staff.

For Ibuka, however, machinery is but a means; the end lies in the total intellectual uplifting of the man and woman. More so than any other company on the Legislative Council, Fujitsu advocates for a vision of a future driven by science and engineering - a meritocracy of limitless ambition where anyone who has what it takes can and will excel. In Ibuka's world, the only way is up.
strings.GNG_legco_matsushita_desc:
Founded in 1918, Matsushita Electric is one of Japan's most prestigious electronics manufacturers - starting from selling electrical sockets to developing a vast selection of leisure and home appliances. Ever hungry for new opportunities, Matsushita was one of the first to enter Guangdong as the vanguard of Japanese capitalism on the Chinese mainland.

Among the major companies leading the Legislative Council, Matsushita is a firm member of the Japanese corporate establishment, neither as soft-hearted as Sony nor as bullheaded as Fujitsu. Its representative in Guangdong, Matsushita Masaharu, is both reliable and adaptable to Guangdong's ever-changing conditions - with both eyes firmly on the bottom line.
strings.GNG_legco_cheungkong_desc:
When Li Ka-shing left Sony's leadership team in 1958, many Japanese executives hoped it would end the Morita-Li partnership that had upended Guangdong. They were sorely mistaken; Li, now head of Cheung Kong Holdings, had merely shifted his attention to providing the necessities of modern life for the Chinese masses, a sorely underserved market.

Supermarkets, pharmacies, wholesalers, and cinemas: Cheung Kong has its fingers on the pulse of the poorer Zhujin and Chinese communities across Guangdong, an inescapable presence in the post-Yasuda landscape. For Li, doing good and good business are one and the same - for nobody should experience want as he once did, especially if he can profit from making sure they do not.
strings.GNG_legco_hitachi_desc:
Created in 1910 as a manufacturer of electric motors, Hitachi is the electronics subsidiary of the Mangyō Zaibatsu - itself subsumed under the Manchurian Industrial Development Corporation, the preeminent state-owned company of {man_getnamedef}. Backed by the Manchurian state and its captive workforce, Hitachi has a presence in nearly every segment of the electronics market.

Hitachi's chief executive, Komai Kenichirō, is a man both familiar and alien to Guangdong's tycoons - blending a shared emphasis on technology with a devotion to total control and state intervention that is anathema to Guangdong's more freewheeling capitalism. To many, Komai is a reminder of a darker time, of total mobilization for the state; a Manchurian agent coming to haunt Guangdong.
strings.GNG_legco_yasuda_desc:
The Yasuda financial conglomerate is one of the Big Four Zaibatsu in Japan - and the one most aggressive in expanding overseas, including in Guangdong. From major corporate loans to payday lending, Yasuda Holdings is deeply intertwined with the economy of the entire Co-Prosperity Sphere, expanding at a breakneck pace overseas to make up for constrained opportunities on the Home Islands.

Yasuda's prominence - as the only one of the major Zaibatsu among the Four Companies of Guangdong - gives it outsized influence in the Legislative Council. Deep pockets can buy many favors, and Matsuzawa Takuji is well aware of the power that entails, serving as first among equals among Guangdong's corporate titans.
strings.GNG_legco_yasuda_post_collapse_desc:
Pride comes before a fall, and in the wake of the storm left behind by the Minezaka scandal, Yasuda lies broken. With a balance sheet in tatters and its senior leadership implicated in the worst corruption scandal in Japanese history, nobody in Tokyo is lifting a finger to save Yasuda - overturning its position in Guangdong almost overnight.

Even as more self-interested men abandon ship, Matsuzawa Takuji - now Chief Executive - leads a battered remnant of Yasuda officers to see Guangdong through its greatest crisis. Their loyalty will no longer buy them riches or renown - only the knowledge that they served their master until the bitter end.
strings.GNG_legco_suzuki_desc:
While the Four Companies control the lion's share of the seats in the Legislative Council, a sizable bloc remains loyal to the Civil Administration of Guangdong and the Chief Executive. These individuals - a collection of Japanese expatriates and politically reliable 'notables' - flock to the Chief Executive both for his proximity to power and the sizable 'gifts' given to maintain their favor.

The base motivations of these men make them reliable enforcers of Chief Executive Suzuki's will in the Legislative Council - so long as he keeps them satiated with the fruits of power and influence. With a strong mandate from Tokyo and a partnership with Yasuda in hand, Suzuki is confident he can keep his courtiers in line.
strings.GNG_legco_civil_authority_desc:
How quick to turn are those kept loyal by promises of wealth and power, when both are found to be wanting! Such is the way of things in Guangdong, and of Chief Executive Suzuki's men in particular: having crowded around him in times of plenty, they disavow him in the wake of Yasuda's collapse in hopes of saving their own skin.

But spare a thought for the few who continue to make cause with the stricken Chief Executive. Whether out of long-buried principles, petty rivalries, sunk costs, or self-delusion, these men have tied themselves to the mast of Suzuki's sinking ship, come what may.

strings.GNG_map_sar_tooltip:
£GNG_police_texticon Guangdong Police Force
--------------
With “Honor, Duty and Loyalty” emblazoned on badges of men who embody none of them, the Guangdong Police Force serves as the Legislative Council's mailed fist in all affairs within its jurisdiction. They ensure that the tycoons' words are law in every street corner and opium den, and assure every citizen that they are safe at all times - if need be, from themselves. Yet much like an iron gauntlet, the GPF is clunky, unwieldy, and coated in rust. Their primacy entails law and order, true, but also the primacy of jack-booted thugs in blue with yawning pockets and laughable oversight.

The Police have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:sar_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].
Currently the Police's control is capped at [?GNG_police_max|2]%.
strings.GNG_map_kenpeitai_tooltip:
£GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai
--------------
Though Guangdong presents itself as an independent nation, the Kenpeitai reminds its citizens where their true allegiance should lay. Contemptible in their methods yet efficient in their tasks, these secret policemen monitor Guangdong from their garrisons, ready to sally forth at the first whiff of dissent. More germane to the Council's treasury is that the Kenpeitai are funded at the Emperor's expense. None can find a police force better or cheaper, say Tokyo's sycophants. One wonders, however: the people fear the Kenpeitai now. What if they learn to hate it?

The Kenpeitai have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:ken_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].
Currently the Kenpeitai's control is capped at [?GNG_kenpeitai_max|2]%.
strings.GNG_map_yakuza_tooltip:
£GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza
--------------
“Yakuza” is a one-word question with three different answers and more. To themselves and their apologists, they are the ninkyō dantai: noble rōnin bands of the modern day, sharing the luxuries of rich men with their brothers and fellow poorfolk. To the Chinese and Zhujin, they are unhinged, fingerless mobsters who leave behind dead bodies and opium wherever they go. The Legislative Council could simply call the Yakuza for the troublemakers they are - but some with deep pockets prefer doing business with them over anyone else.

The Yakuza have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:yak_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].
strings.GNG_map_triads_tooltip:
£GNG_triads_texticon Triads
--------------
Woo Sing Woo, Sun Yee On, Shui Fong - every Chinese person knows such names by heart. Hearkening to the “secret societies” which inhabited China since the dynasties, these Triads rule Guangdong's underworld with a fistful of drugs and another of lead. Their ranks have unsurprisingly swelled since the state's conception; with this growth followed strength and influence among the Chinese underclass. Growing voices argue for courting Guangdong's new kingmakers instead of curtailing them at great cost - an action officials wary of our northern neighbor have cautioned against.

The Triads have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:tri_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].

strings.GNG_map_hainan_denied_tooltip:
Hainan
--------------
This state is unavailable for interactions.
strings.GNG_map_hainan_denied_tooltip_tt:
Though legally part of Guangdong under the Kanton Protocol, Hainan remains an administrative anomaly. Sharp developmental and cultural differences from the booming Pearl River Delta, and a lack of immediate profit, mean Kōshū's corporate planners have little interest in integrating the island into their frameworks.

Such disinterest from Kōshū led to a negotiated settlement that places the island under the authority of the Nanjing Government, where it now functions as a Special Administrative Region (S.A.R.). For now, the arrangement is convenient. Kōshū's corporations focus on the profitable mainland, leaving the island's administration to Nanjing. The question of Hainan's full integration is merely postponed; should its strategic or economic value shift, Kōshū will eventually move to assert its claim.
strings.GNG_map_qinzhou_denied_tooltip:
Qinzhou

strings.GNG_map_zhanjiang_denied_tooltip:
Zhanjiang
--------------
This state is unavailable for interactions.
strings.GNG_map_zhanjiang_denied_tooltip_tt:
Under the Kanton Protocol, the ports of Zhanjiang and Qinzhou are legally part of Guangdong. In practice, they have been de facto controlled by Chongqing remnants since the 1955 riots, when Nanjing's failure to assert control created a power vacuum filled by the Southwestern Warlords.

At present, military reintegration is considered unfeasible. The formidable presence of the Guangxi Clique, combined with fervent Chinese nationalism cultivated against the State, makes direct intervention untenable and risks a costly, protracted conflict with no guarantee of success. Consequently, the cities persist as a strategic liability, serving as Guiyang's forward base for intelligence and subversive activities in Guangdong.

This unresolved issue is a source of significant friction, and while confrontation is currently tabled, the situation must be settled when a more favorable opportunity arises.
strings.GNG_map_japanese_expat_support_tooltip_o:
£GNG_expats_texticon Japanese Expats
--------------

Executives, entrepreneurs, and engineers - these are the masters of Guangdong, the educated elite that dominate economic and political life. Concentrated in the Three Pearls, these individuals - and their dependents - wield political influence greater than their numbers imply, and their support is crucial to keep Guangdong's economy from coming to a screeching halt.

The Japanese comprise [?total_national_jap_pop_percent|2%] of Guangdong's total population.
The government has [?GNG_jap_app|2]% support among Japanese Expats (Capped at [?GNG_jap_app_cap|2]%), granting the following effects:

Daily Political Power Gain: [?GNG_japanese_gov_support_pp_gain|2+]
GDP Growth Multiplier: [?GNG_japanese_gov_support_gdp_growth|2+%]
£GNG_japanese_nation_texticon Dai-Nippon Teikoku Opinion Cap: {getgngjapaneseempireofjapanopinioncap}
strings.GNG_map_japanese_expat_tooltip:
£GNG_expats_texticon Japanese Expats
--------------

Executives, entrepreneurs, and engineers - these are the masters of Guangdong, the educated elite that dominate economic and political life. Concentrated in the Three Pearls, these individuals - and their dependents - wield political influence greater than their numbers imply, and their support is crucial to keep Guangdong's economy from coming to a screeching halt.

Japanese Expats make up [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:jap_pop|2]% of the population of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].
strings.GNG_map_zhujin_tooltip:
£GNG_zhujin_texticon Zhujin
--------------

The Zhujin - the common name for an emerging Cantonese-Japanese hybrid culture - are both envied and resented in equal measure. Educated and generally fluent in both Cantonese and Japanese, the Zhujin emerged from Guangdong's identity crisis as an indispensable and increasingly localized professional and bureaucratic class - the face of what Guangdong could yet become.

Zhujin make up [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:zhu_pop|2]% of the population of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].

Every month the £GNG_zhujin_texticon Zhujin population is {getgngzhujinassimilationpopulationimpact}.
strings.GNG_map_chinese_tooltip:
£GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese
--------------

Even though China no longer controls the land, the people are not so easily separated from their homeland. Ethnic Chinese make up the dominant majority across Guangdong, especially outside the cities, serving as manual labor in Guangdong's factories. Their struggle to survive as an underclass beneath the Japanese and the Zhujin showcases Guangdong as it is, rather than what it wants to be.

Chinese make up [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:chi_pop|2]% of the population of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName].

Every month the £GNG_chinese_texticon Chinese population is {getgngchineseassimilationpopulationimpact}.

strings.GNG_map_rioters_tooltip:
£GNG_rioters_texticon Rioters
--------------

The sufferings of the people have become a roaring cry for freedom - or so the Guangdong Federation of Tradesmen and the Committee of Chinese Labor would tell you. If they made their case without arson, battery, and larceny, they might even have had a point.

But as it stands, we cannot distinguish between honest grievance and incandescent fury - and neither people nor profit can survive long in the face of the latter. The question of why they turned to violence is irrelevant - the streets are filled with hoodlums and hooligans, and they will be punished accordingly.

The £GNG_rioters_texticon Rioters have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:riot_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName]
strings.GNG_map_government_tooltip:
£GNG_government_riots_texticon Government
--------------

When the flames from burning barricades reach towards the sky, and the angry mob carves out swathes of territory as 'liberated zones' - then the old differences in Guangdong cease to matter.

Gangster, soldier, or cop - nothing matters more than the distinction between those siding with the forces of order and profit, and those who revel in anarchy and debasement. We call for freedom without anarchy, dignity through work, and prosperity over penury - and those who disagree have no place amongst us.

The £GNG_government_riots_texticon Government have [?var:GNG_map_selected_state:govt_spt|2]% control of [?GNG_map_selected_state.GetName]
strings.GNG_map_police_selected: We are interacting with the £GNG_police_texticon Police.
strings.GNG_reinforce_the_police_in_state_desc: Giving our officers some additional equipment and transferring detectives into this region will allow our police force to better maintain control here.
strings.GNG_modernize_police_in_state_desc: Upgrading and making sure all of the police's equipment work should allow them to be a more effective force in combating thugs and our enemies.
strings.GNG_build_police_boxes_in_state_desc: Increasing the public presence of our officers should allow them to exert more control in this state.
strings.GNG_Growing_Police_Influence_desc: Every quarter of a year, the GPF's presence will grow in two of our regions, keeping our streets safe and fighting crime.
strings.GNG_guangdong_riots_active: The Guangdong Riots Engulfs Our Streets
strings.GNG_bolster_zhujin_police_desc: Funding the Zhujin Police in this district will ensure that we don't lose control. It also helps cool tensions when the officers fighting to maintain order come from the same background.
strings.GNG_use_triads_as_middlemen_desc: The Triads are more than willing to help us calm down the rioters, so long as we're also willing to look the other way as they try to profit off of the situation.
strings.GNG_low_level_negotiations_with_workers_: Agreeing to several small concessions will have some of the workers in this district getting off the streets and putting down their picket signs.
strings.GNG_send_the_special_service_desc: Thanks to our foresight, we have several squads of intelligence agents awaiting orders. We could use their help in suppressing some of the riots in this district.
strings.GNG_use_the_special_branch_desc: The Special Branch has been assigned across Guangdong, but they are overstretched. Refining their efforts to this specific district will allow them to clamp down on subversive activities and improve their overall efficiency.
strings.GNG_employ_triad_goons_desc: The Triads have a variety of “services” available for purchase. Thankfully for us, they're not picky sellers, so long as the cash reaches them quickly.
strings.GNG_employ_yakuza_goons_desc: The Yakuza normally prefer to rough up businesses and citizens for protection money, but we can convince them to instead target the rioters in exchange for cold hard cash.
strings.GNG_deploy_the_special_police_desc: There are an increasing number of dissidents and riots in this district, and our police force is stretched thin. Thankfully, a division of the £GNG_police_texticon Special Police is on standby.
strings.GNG_deploy_paramilitaries_desc: Deniable plausibility allows us to put extra “troops” on the street in the name of maintaining calm and order during these trying times.
strings.GNG_surveil_and_strike_desc: Our surveillance teams have identified several locations we believe the rioters are organizing from. Time to send in the cleanup crew.
strings.GNG_greenlight_yakuza_raids_desc: A lie here and an exaggeration there would lead to the Yakuza mistakenly launching an assault on some of the rioters' bases, which is something we could live with.
strings.GNG_conduct_mass_arrests_desc: Issue a proclamation that anyone caught outside of their homes past curfew in this district will be arrested, and watch as the number of detainees pile up in our jails.
strings.GNG_kenpeitai_on_the_streets_desc: The Kenpeitai normally prefer to work from the shadows, but their ruthlessness makes them solid enforcers too in beating back the rioters.
strings.GNG_greenlight_kenpeitai_raids_desc: The Kenpeitai are aware of several resource caches the rioters are using. Time to give them the go-ahead to allow them to do what they do best.
strings.GNG_map_kenpeitai_selected: We are interacting with the £GNG_kenpeitai_texticon Kenpeitai.
strings.GNG_order_a_crackdown_in_state_desc: We've received intelligence from our field operatives that subversive agents are operating in this state. Time to round them up and throw them in a cell.
strings.GNG_downsize_kenpeitai_duties_in_state_d: The Kenpeitai are needed elsewhere throughout Guangdong, so we should prepare for them to relocate and hand off their responsibilities back to the police.
strings.GNG_change_state_police_duties_desc: Sometimes, the Kenpeitai is more suited towards handling a region. The local police force won't be happy about it, though.
strings.GNG_Growing_Kenpeitai_Influence_desc: Every quarter of a year, the Kenpeitai will grow in two of our regions, spreading their influence and growing their networks.
strings.GNG_map_yakuza_selected: We are interacting with the £GNG_yakuza_texticon Yakuza.
strings.GNG_raid_yakuza_bases_in_state_desc: The Yakuza have gotten too cozy in their dens. Time to give them a reminder of who is supposed to be in control, and maybe reappropriate a few bottles of quality alcohol.
strings.GNG_bribe_the_yakuza_in_state_desc: There's nothing cash can't buy in Guangdong, and that includes assets and businesses that allow us to maintain control of its streets.
strings.GNG_strike_triads_in_state_desc: Thanks to our new Yakuza friends, we've been made aware of some illegal parlors and restaurants the Triads are running. Time to clamp down on these illegal businesses.
strings.GNG_draw_lines_of_control_desc: Our Yakuza allies are getting a serious amount of heat from the Triads in this region. Pointing our police in the direction of the Triads should buy the Yakuza some breathing room.
strings.GNG_Growing_Yakuza_Influence_desc: Every quarter of a year, the Yakuza will grow in two of our regions, spreading their influence and growing their networks.
strings.GNG_map_triad_selected: We are interacting with the £GNG_triads_texticon Triads.
strings.GNG_raid_triad_warehouses_in_state_desc: We've identified one of the storage facilities the Triads are using to move drugs throughout Guangdong. We should launch a raid as soon as possible.
strings.GNG_bribe_the_triad_in_state_desc: There's nothing cash can't buy in Guangdong, and that includes assets and businesses that allow us to maintain control of its streets.
strings.GNG_safeguard_triad_business_desc: Stanley Ho has notified us that some of our police officers and the Kenpeitai have been investigating his legal businesses, and has recommended that we call the investigation off. We'll heed his recommendation.
strings.GNG_strike_yakuza_together_desc: The Triads have proposed a plan that would allow us to put Yakuza members behind bars, while they promise to maintain control on the streets with the help of the Yakuza's rackets. Who can say no to that?
strings.GNG_Growing_Triad_Influence_desc: Every quarter of a year, the Triads will grow in two of our regions, spreading their influence and growing their networks.
strings.GNG_underworld_button_blocker: The underworld is irrelevant in the face of the Guangdong Riots.

strings.GNG_Product_GUI_tooltip_normal_tt:
If one were to see the companies of Guangdong as fierce warriors vying for each other's heads, then the annual Product Launch would be their dueling ground; their prized electronics, sharp-edged katanas to land the fatal blow.

The path to woo the £GNG_legco_texticon Legislative Council with state-of-the-art products is fraught with intricacies. For the successful launch of each and every product two factors are indispensable: quality control and advertising. £GNG_product_quality_texticon Product Quality anchors the trust of investors in our endeavors, while sufficient advertisement accumulates consumer interest from targeted as well as potential markets.

It is through a steady stream of successful launches that Guangdong shall maintain its financial prestige, and contribute our part to the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere's global power projection, both soft and hard. But even if product manufacturing lies dormant technology does not - for our brightest engineers and researchers across the Three Pearls shall toil day in and day out for the constant perfection of our releases and the optimization of state apparatus.

A Product Cycle typically lasts 100 days, after which our creation will be put to the test in the murky waters of capital, depending on how well both the quality and the popularity is. Release a product of immense quality and popularity, and watch the political clout of its parent company skyrocket; release an inferior product, however, and everything might come crashing down...

strings.GNG_market_to_the_republic_of_china_desc:
Sometimes the most obvious solution to a problem is the most effective one. Currently, the problem facing us is one of maximizing profits for the latest development cycle; and the solution? Maximizing our potential consumer base to promote the greatest volume of sales.

Who better to turn to in that case than our neighbors in the Republic of China? True, they may not have the most sophisticated palates for technology, but what they lack in discerning taste they more than make up for with sheer numbers. By focusing our efforts on advertising and developing for the Chinese masses, we can break into a great and underappreciated well of buyers. Provided they can pay for our product, of course.

This show of attention to the Chinese will not only endear our neighbor to us but it will also get our administration some support amongst our own working class. Some in Tokyo will raise an eyebrow, but the fact of the matter is that if they expect us to turn a profit on their behalf, then they must be willing to allow us to conduct our business on sound market principles.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_empire_of_japan_desc:
The Empire of Japan is our master and patron - it is only natural for us to repay their support with the fruits of their investments. The Japanese consumer is the beneficiary of an economic sphere that reaches across the breadth of the Pacific and has reaped the rewards of such cooperation. The Japanese consumer, more than anyone else in the Sphere, is primed and able to be a reliable market for our innovative products.

Focusing our efforts on the Japanese market is not only a historically-proven sound choice, but it will remind Tokyo of our loyalty and trustworthiness, better for securing our economic and political positions. The Chinese government will no doubt be displeased. Some in the Republic have been calling for us to give the average Chinese consumer greater access to our products, but that will have to wait for another year.
strings.GNG_market_to_italian_market_desc: The Empire of Japan has always maintained happy relations with its former partner and ally, Italy - it is high time we reap the benefits of this long friendship. Luckily for us, we are perfectly situated to enter into the unfilled niche of electronics. While Italy may no longer be as backward as it was in the 1930s, it has not yet developed a market for the mass-produced consumer products we specialize in. Most of what it produces domestically is of relatively high quality, but they are expensive, scarce, and largely marketed toward corporations and the government. If all goes well, expansion into Italy will come with an eager new pool of consumers and little direct competition for the time being.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_iberian_market_desc: The Iberian Union represents the unfortunate fate of many states that were spared destruction by the Reich, only to be pulled low by the reverberations of its victory. The dysfunctional government established by Spain and Portugal's merger, not to mention the resulting loss of colonial revenue following German land grabs in Africa, hampered Iberian economic potential during the 1950s. Recent talk of reforms and revitalization may or may not herald a future economic boom, but for now, they are an underdeveloped market waiting for us to tap. Until they establish a domestic electronics industry of their own, we can easily fill their shelves with our products, provided we get the blessing of their Caudillos.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_turkish_market_desc: Not all of the victors of the Second World War emerged so lucky as Japan, Germany, or Italy. True, the Turks emerged with territories in the Caucuses and a new hegemony in the near-east, but that hasn't done much to save their long-ailing economy or quell popular discontent in their new patrimony. All this to say, Turkey has not had the luxury of developing an economy that can produce the latest electronics for government and civilian consumption alike. Luckily for them, our good relations with Italy allow us to use the Suez and thus grants us easy access to Turkish markets.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_mexican_market_desc: With North America being the center of American and OFN influence, breaking into its potentially lucrative markets has been predictably slow going. Luckily for us, not every nation there is so leashed to Uncle Sam as to refuse good business. Mexico has long been wary of the giant to its north, and not without cause. With no real love for the American-led international order that the OFN seeks to establish, it has been the Mexican government's standing policy to seek neutrality in both military and economic affairs. If only more states could be so sensible in these matters, the world would be a much better place. The Americans might give it the side eye but if the Mexican government has a need for better data storage or computational power and its citizens demand the comforts of the modern age, then that is what they'll get. For a price of course.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_brazilian_market_desc: Brazil is a rising power, both within South America and in global affairs. Unlike their American neighbors, Brazil and Japan have enjoyed cordial diplomatic and economic relations for some now, and by extension so have we. Therefore, we are a known presence in the Brazilian market, and our companies have solid brand recognition among many Brazilian consumers. Marketing our latest product to Brazil would guarantee an interested consumer base with relatively few domestic options to choose from - in other words, a solid investment for us.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_argentine_market_desc: Argentina is an ambitious nation hoping to carve out its place separate from the economies of either the arrogant United States or their rival to the north, Brazil. In some ways, their economic goals make us natural business partners. Our companies produce some of the finest products in the modern world, and thanks to our special economic status, we have less of an overbearing presence than most American manufacturers that could deliver comparable goods.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_chilean_market_desc: The economic situation that exists between Japan and Chile is such that the latter is essentially a guaranteed trading partner. We can capitalize on the leverage our overseers in Tokyo possess over the South American nation to ensure a captive market for our latest, top-of-the-line products. Perhaps the Japanese delegation to Chile could quietly inform Santiago that if they wish to see their exports continue as usual, they will need to place some orders for our product for their government offices. Or we could simply brute force our way into the civilian market, it matters little either way as long as we reach our sales quotas.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_american_market_desc: Thanks to the passage of the Honolulu Accords, trade has finally opened up between America and Japan for the first time in decades. This presents a golden opportunity for us to finally break into one of the most lucrative markets on the planet. Of course, every golden opportunity comes with drawbacks of its own. In the first place, Tokyo is not likely to be pleased by any extensive interactions with the Americans outside of their direct control. Second and potentially more problematic is the fact that the Americans are perhaps the only other nation with the capability to match our R&D and production capabilities. Their domestic producers may be able to actually compete with our companies, but in the end we will win on the quality of our products.
strings.GNG_market_to_the_german_market_desc: To say that our past economic relations with the German Reich have been rocky would be an understatement. With relations quickly souring following the Second World War, our products have not yet found themselves in much of continental Europe thanks to geopolitics and superpower diplomacy. All that has changed since the rise of a new Führer of Germany however, as market reforms have finally allowed mutual trade to flow between continental Europe and the Sphere. German consumers may be less familiar with our products than those in other nations, but that is just all the more reason for us to introduce them to all that we have to offer. A new era of happy commerce could be right around the corner between us and this new Germany if we only embrace the opportunity. We should be careful when dealing with one of Tokyo's chief rivals, although surely they can recognize that good business is good business no matter where it comes from.
strings.GNG_pay_off_high_ranking_contacts_desc: When it comes to product advertisement, it pays to have the right person in your corner - literally. In a market as cutthroat as Guangdong, having the right endorsements or product quality attestations is the difference between success and failure - and as such we will make sure that the regulators, auditors, and promotional agents will have whatever they need to agree that we are the only game in town.
strings.GNG_hold_a_massive_press_conference_desc: Nothing gets publicity quite like a good press conference. We can make a massive splash with the right setting, some well-chosen words, and plenty of incentives for the press. Naturally, such an event comes at a price, but as with any investment, the point is to deliver a tidy return. Any expenses made now will seem trivial once potential customers watch the conference on their home televisions or read all about it in their morning paper.
strings.GNG_buy_mass_radio_airtime_desc: With each passing year the television is becoming the premier medium of choice for those with extra money to spend. While it has extraordinary value as a marketing tool, we must be conscious that it is still not a universal. In contrast, there are hardly any households in Guangdong, China, and Japan that lack at least one radio set, to say nothing of radios out in public spaces. The buzz of radio static can be heard across stores, open shopfronts, and even offices all across the Great Asian Co-Prosperity Sphere. It may be a more cautious, safe marketing tactic, but risk-taking in and of itself is not our goal - profit is.
strings.GNG_bribe_channels_for_tv_airtime_desc: Time is money; such an adage is hardly less true for television. Television in Guangdong is just as cutthroat as every other industry - companies are forced to vie for air space and the television executives are all too aware of how much value their services command. If we want to get word of our product to television sets across the Sphere, we will need to deal with these executives directly and grease the wheels. Such is the cost of business.
strings.GNG_force_overtime_for_factory_workers_d: The development of a product is one piece of the puzzle - if we cannot produce enough units to meet the demand we generate, all our efforts will have been wasted. By pushing our workers to their limits, we can amp up our production. The workers will not like it, but they have few options to protest our decision. However, the workers still have ways of making their dissatisfaction known. The Republic will hear of it for one, and the workers will not soon forget regardless of whether or not they show it now. It will be up to us to determine if it is a worthwhile choice.
strings.GNG_use_underworld_contacts_desc: In public, we have nothing to do with the unsavory likes of the Triads or the Yakuza. Unofficially, however, we should always be willing to make a deal. We have plenty of clandestine contacts with these organizations and a few favors accrued over the years for services rendered. If we wanted to, we could call a few of these favors in and have them drum up some interest for our upcoming product amidst Guangdong's seedier underbelly.
strings.GNG_force_police_prototyping_desc: The Guangdong Police can occasionally prove useful beyond just providing law and order on the streets. As we move into the testing phase of the development cycle we require as much data as possible. Since the state already pays their salaries, it will be simple to send prototypes and test models their way. Most of our products have at least some use in office settings, either for the discharge of their duties or their down time. As a matter of sending out a few well placed bribes this is simple enough to accomplish, although pushing our products onto the police too often is likely to strain our relationship.
strings.GNG_test_the_product_rigorously_desc: The next business week will be entirely devoted to testing prototypes and implementing refinements to our current project under development. The market has come to expect from us a degree of refinement and sophistication in our products and we have an obligation to meet or exceed those expectations, if only to maintain our share values and bolster our company's image amongst our peers and competitors.
strings.GNG_hire_more_skilled_engineers_desc: A concept is worth nothing without its execution. It takes more than just ideas and marketing to successfully launch a product. It also requires reliability, good construction, and well-thought-out design. If hiring a few more well-trained hands for our development team is necessary to keep our product up to the high standards of the market, then that is what we will have to do.
strings.GNG_suppress_negative_press_desc: There will always be flies in the ointment, so to speak. Even the best-designed product is bound to catch unfair criticism for one perceived fault or another. Whether it be working conditions, product safety, or complaints over pricing, we can always expect some nuisance from the media. Luckily the press can be dealt with in the same fashion as everyone else on the Pearl River Delta: money. Some yen waved around here or there and our headaches will quietly dissipate.
strings.GNG_move_factory_workers_to_qa_desc: The QA process encourages learning from failure and consistent small changes to improve a product. This process takes time, however, and manpower for product testing is not often our top priority. Instead of expanding our dedicated quality assurance staff, it will be much cheaper to simply divert some of our factory workers to testing prototype models in their spare time or even on their factory floors or break rooms if the product in question has uses in those settings. Granted, this is not part of their formal job description and some workers may be annoyed at the imposition, but they ought to know that in Guangdong, no role or rule is absolute.
strings.GNG_move_white_collar_workers_to_qa: Move White Collar Workers to QA
strings.GNG_move_white_collar_workers_to_qa_desc: The QA process encourages learning from failure and consistent small changes to improve a product. This process takes time, however, and manpower for product testing is not often our top priority. Instead of expanding our dedicated quality assurance staff, it will be much cheaper to simply divert some of our office staff to testing prototype models in their spare time or even within their offices if the product in question has uses in that setting. Granted, this is not part of their formal job description and some workers may be annoyed at the imposition, but they ought to know that in Guangdong, no role or rule is absolute.
strings.GNG_force_overtime_for_engineers_desc: There are only so many hours in a day, only so many days in a week, and only so many weeks in a product cycle. In Guangdong's cutthroat environment, any delays on our part could have disastrous consequences for our product and more importantly, our product's profitability. It is somewhat distasteful, but we can best hasten the development of the current project by mandating overtime for all engineers. This will invite grumbling from the engineers of course, and word will quickly reach back to both their fellow Japanese expats and the Home Islands.
strings.GNG_ask_japan_to_loan_engineers_desc: So far, we have relied on our own men to design and develop our latest product. While normally they are perfectly adequate for our needs, if we want to go above and beyond the standard quality the market is used to, we will need to pull from Japan's considerable talent pool. By pulling in our contacts through our offices in the Home Islands, we can arrange to have the best engineering talent the Sphere has to offer transferred temporarily to our current projects here in Guangdong. Some feathers may get ruffled here and there as we pull high-demand skilled labor for our own needs but all our loans will be repaid in full, have no fear.
strings.GNG_sacrifice_research_and_development_d: Even during the product cycle, in which the majority of our resources are put towards the goal of a profitable release, we maintain our public research and development division. In this case, however, we cannot afford to maintain two fronts. We will divert further resources and manpower from the R&D teams to active product development. Our research will suffer on all fronts while we pursue this more focused approach, but the quality of our product will be greatly improved.
strings.GNG_let_kenpeitai_test_products_desc: If the Kenpeitai insists on serving as the eyes and ears of Japan, lurking around in every nook and cranny of the Pearl River, then at the very least they should be expected to give back to the bottom line in some way. Their agents should have plenty of use for top-of-the-line technology, and whether they choose to use our product in the field or in their offices, it makes no matter to us. As long as they give our R&D teams useful feedback they can do whatever they want with it. It goes without saying that they'll expect something in the way of compensation for this assistance but we'll deal with that another time.
strings.GNG_push_forward_the_product_launch_desc: Thanks to an incredibly productive development cycle, our latest product is actually viable for release before the end of the mandated launch deadline! Not only do we have an opportunity here to release early, but we can also effortlessly translate this turn of events into some excellent marketing. Consumers and investors alike will be thrilled by the news of our product's advanced launch which will surely boost its profitability.
strings.GNG_push_forward_the_product_launch_tt: The Product Release Deadline will be pushed forward by 10 days
strings.GNG_delay_the_product_launch_desc: It is not easy to admit by any means, but the fact is that our current product is simply not ready for release by the appointed deadline. To release it then would invite disaster - a defective, poor-quality product will sell terribly and completely tarnish our hard-won reputation. Delaying the launch will of course have its downsides - consumers tend to be fickle beasts and react poorly to perceived signs of failure. That will simply have to be borne however if the alternative is an utter embarrassment at the market.
strings.GNG_delay_the_product_launch_tt: The Product Release Deadline will be pushed back by 20 days
strings.GNG_product_release_deadline_desc:
It takes a lifetime to build trust, and an instant to lose it.

We made a promise to our shareholders that we would deliver results - a product that will shake the world and fatten their wallets - at least once every year. There is always the option to ask for a delay, or to release an unprepared product to the world - but we should be careful, for to forgo release entirely would put our credibility on the line.
strings.GNG_Product_Prioritize_Audio_Video_desc: For the time being, we will assign our R&D teams to prioritize advancements in audiovisual presentation methods. This will, of course, provide clear advantages to Sony in upcoming Product Development Cycles. On a further note, audiovisual products tend to gain the most attention from the consumer market - electronic household luxuries are the status symbols of our time, and anyone who can afford them is willing to pay for those symbols. After all, nothing brings in buyers like flash and style.
strings.GNG_Product_Prioritize_Household_Electro: For the time being, we will assign our R&D teams to prioritize the design and development of new household electronics to put on the consumer market. Matsushita Electric Company will be poised to take advantage of our sponsored research, and will no doubt reap its benefits come future Product Development Cycles. Our domestic development will also be aided by our focus and our citizens will find that their access to modern luxuries greatly improved. The future of living means washing machines, refrigerators, and rice cookers - the home of tomorrow is right around the corner.
strings.GNG_Product_Prioritize_Storage_desc: For the time being, we will assign our R&D teams to prioritize the development of greater data storage capabilities to improve our overall development capabilities. In the process of developing numerous products and innovations, we have accumulated an immense amount of data. Some of this data is immediately applicable to ongoing projects, but often its true value will only come much later and in very different contexts. Lessons learned from one Development Cycle might be crucial to the development of a product two Cycles after. With that in mind, our scientists and engineers have become quite averse to losing any information gained from their work and as this philosophy has proven its value on more than one occasion, we are inclined to oblige them.
strings.GNG_Product_Prioritize_Computation_desc: For the time being, we will assign our R&D teams to prioritize the development of greater computing capabilities and the requisite hardware needed to maintain such capabilities. Such a decision to elevate computational research will naturally give Fujitsu Limited a leg up in future Product Development Cycles. Additionally, any breakthroughs made in this sector will be just as easily put to use back into our R&D capabilities as it puts money into Ibuka Masaru's pockets. If Fujitsu claims to be the future, we had better get in on their success.
strings.GNG_Product_Prioritize_Efficiency_desc: For the time being, we will assign our R&D teams to prioritize power efficiency improvements for government electronics. While not contributing directly to the profitability of our products, it will improve our overall administrative capabilities and our economic development. Our resource extraction operations would benefit from improved optimization, not to mention the automated systems in the factory complexes.
strings.GNG_Invest_in_focused_research_desc: At any given time, our R&D teams are likely focusing on several different efforts at once, all in service to the development of our products. During periods of normal development, this approach is not problematic. Indeed, it has been a crucial part of our ability to stay at the top of the global tech industry. There are times, however, when it is helpful to narrow our focus and make a concerted effort with every resource we have toward a single goal, be that a design bottleneck or specific innovation that will be instrumental in future projects. Of course, such a marshaling of resources requires a good deal of invested capital to produce results that will make up for the venture's opportunity cost.
strings.GNG_Force_Scientists_on_Overtime_desc: No development project can succeed without the brain and manpower to back it up. It is thanks to the efforts of our dedicated scientists that we have been so successful in staying on the cutting edge of consumer-ready technology. As with any development endeavor though, there is always more work to be done and not enough time to do it all in. Given the absolute necessity of the annual development cycle to our economy, we have a responsibility to prepare our products as quickly and efficiently as possible. Sometimes this necessitates difficult choices, such as our allocation of R&D man-hours. To put it bluntly, we can improve the rate at which development progresses by ordering our teams to put in more shifts for longer periods. This is not something we can do lightly, however, as it will also necessitate paying out extra wages and will not be looked on favorably by the Japanese expat community from which we draw our best and brightest.
strings.GNG_Cut_Corners_on_Research_desc: In the race to put out the “next big thing” and further cement Guangdong's economic ascendency, there is more than a little pressure to put certain... standards aside if it means a quicker development period. Naturally, this isn't something to be broadcast to the rest of the world and our competitors - but it would be naive to expect them to adhere to rules simply because we do out of any sense of “fairness.” To look for any such thing in Guangdong is to have been seriously misled. No, the real danger of expediting our progress by quietly ignoring certain cumbersome tests and rules is that we might slip up and release a truly dysfunctional product. Some things are bound to be overlooked here and there but, by keeping our time-saving measures reasonable, we can maintain our level of quality within an acceptable deviation.

strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.1.desc: This event should be hidden, yet you found it anyways
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.2.t: The End of the {year} Product Cycle
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.2.desc:
Months of arduous labor - both intellectual and physical - culminate in a morning of silence, as the first rays of sun sweep away the lengthy shadows cast by fading neon lights.

Nobody sleeps, of course. The engineers wait at their desks, the executives pace their rooms, and the customer service staff hover above their telephones. Only the factory workers enjoy the brief respite - having made all they were asked to, and then some more besides.

Outside the electronic shops and boutiques in Guangdong's cities, a thin line of technophiles and the curious turns into a throng - and then a crowd, murmuring to each other as soft dawn turns to bright morning. The shutters remain closed, even as the older jostle or scrape is heard from within, the sign of an instrument being moved to its proper place.

As the clock strikes nine, the shutters rattle open, disgorging a sales staff with megaphones at the ready to greet the ongoing crowd. They will surge past the line of staff onto the shop floor, each eager to become the first to get their hands on the latest and greatest that Guangdong has to offer.

This is Launch Day, and fortune waits for no one.
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.2.a: At the end of the day, the numbers tell a story...
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.3.t: The Beginning of the {year} Product Cycle
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.3.desc:
While every day is a battle for the corporate warriors and emperor scientists of Guangdong, one day in particular stands out amongst the rest in its singular importance. An army of managers spread forth from Kōshū's boardrooms bearing budgets, memorandums, and orders to office spaces and factory floors across Guangdong - heralding the start of the year's product cycle.

Once again, in {year}, the Four Companies of Guangdong race to see who can mesmerize and win over the hearts - and wallets - of the world with their advancements in gadgetry and engineering. Whether through technical brilliance, unforgettable marketing, or ruthless cost management, one Company will either take the world by storm or crash ignominiously into failure.

And as the Companies' fortunes go, so too does Guangdong's economy...
strings.GNG_hitachi_product_bribe_tt: £GNG_Hitachi_texticon Hitachi offers us a handy bribe, in exchange for selling their product and forfeiting all the £GNG_legco_texticon LegCo bonuses. Beware, we do not know what intentions lie behind this offer.
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.4.desc:
Even in Guangdong, radios had become commonplace enough that even those without means - which was the vast majority of households, struggling to save enough for a rainy day - could keep up with the latest news, entertainment, and music.

And if not by themselves, then through their next door neighbor; one could walk into any apartment complex in Guangdong and hear five different programs playing on any given floor. The cacophony could drown out the constant drone of the ubiquitous fans, circulating new air in the enclosed spaces.

But if you missed your favorite program, then that was it. No replays or recourse until maybe - just maybe - a rerun might play when you least expected it. Recordings were the province of professionals in studios - an amateur could only rely on luck.

But with the TR-962 A, luck is only part of the question. Input-output settings and the ability to set up reels of magnetic film to record your favorite broadcasts, in equal fidelity to when they first aired.

Assuming, of course, you had the magnetic tape to spare - which Sony was more than happy to provide.
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.4.a: It's not the product that makes money - its the ancillaries.
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.5.desc:
As summer approached, the employees of the Sun Kee wholesale company found that it wasn't the work that killed them - it was the heat. Even with the fans turned to maximum strength, they would feel their will to work dissolve into the rivers of sweat flowing from every pore, panting like dogs in the stale, muggy air.

Their initial misgivings about the box installed in the office windows - wouldn't it let more hot air in? - were quickly dispelled. After just thirty minutes of feeling the brisk chill settle over the office, they had only praise for the Matsushtia W-31 air conditioning unit.

Office life quickly reoriented itself around the W-31. The employees quickly discovered which desks were close enough to be comfortable without being freezing; the management learnt that to the costs of keeping it on largely paid for themselves in productivity.

The complaints from outside passerby about dripping water were ignored - and as for the factories, well, nobody paid them much mind in the first place.
strings.GNG_Product_Cycle.6.desc:
Most would take one look at the head-height machines being wheeled into Yasuda's Kōshū headquarters and quickly find somewhere else to be.
